## R4. SARFAESI enforcement

**Purpose.** Enforce security interests in immovable property and hypothecated movables under Chapter III of the SARFAESI Act 2002 and the Security Interest (Enforcement) Rules 2002, for eligible tenants only, with a hard gate before every irreversible step and an evidence file that survives a s.17 challenge.

**Capabilities:** eligibility gate; enforcement workflow and Rules 3, 8 and 9 day-count engine; redemption cut-off; e-auction connector; s.13(9) consent record; possessed-asset feed (CIR para 21); evidence bundles (R15.7); surplus and shortfall routing.

### R4.1 Eligibility gate

Run per account and per secured asset on entry to the track and again on every material event (payment, classification change, IBC event, court order, transfer, valuation). Output: `eligible`, `blocking_reasons[]`, evidence snapshot hash. The gate extends the R1.4 SARFAESI row.

| # | Test | Rule | Source | If failed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Secured creditor entitled to enforce | Bank, co-operative bank, AIFI, ARC; HFC registered under NHB Act s.29A (notified financial institution); NBFC only with total assets ≥ ₹100 crore | SARFAESI s.2(1)(m)(iv); S.O. 856(E), 24 Feb 2020; HFC notification of 17 Jun 2021 [VERIFY: HFC gazette number] | Block; route to R5/R8 |
| 2 | NBFC debt threshold | Secured debt ≥ ₹20 lakh; not applicable to HFCs (*Virendra Rathore v. Tehsildar*, MP HC, 22 May 2024) | S.O. 652(E), 12 Feb 2021 | Block |
| 3 | NPA | Borrower-level NPA in the tenant's books when the s.13(2) notice issues | s.13(2); IRACP paras 23, 51 | Block |
| 4 | CERSAI registration | Registration ID and date for the asset | s.26D | Block, no override |
| 5 | Not excluded | Lien (a); pledge of movables (b) → R10; aircraft (c); vessel (d); conditional sale, HP or lease without a security interest (e); unpaid seller (f); CPC s.60 exempt property (g); financial asset ≤ ₹1 lakh (h); agricultural land (i); dues below 20% of principal plus interest (j) | s.31 | Block; route per asset |
| 6 | Agricultural land | Nature and use when the security was created, not the revenue entry alone [VERIFY: *Pappireddiyar* (2018) and current SC position] | s.31(i) | Block pending opinion |
| 7 | Not time-barred | R1.5 limitation engine (Art.62, 12 years, for money charged on immovable property) | s.36 [VERIFY: SC position on Art.62] | Block |
| 8 | Shared security | Secured creditors holding ≥ 60% by value of the outstanding on a record date agree; binds all | s.13(9); R13 | Block until recorded |
| 9 | No moratorium or stay | No IBC s.14, s.54E or s.101 moratorium over the asset owner; no court or DRT stay | IBC; R6.7; R9 | Freeze |
| 10 | Parties complete | Every borrower, co-borrower and guarantor-mortgagor; legal heirs where a party has died | s.2(1)(f); Rule 3(4); R1.9 | Block notice |

Only tests 6 and 10 may be overridden, by the Head of Legal with maker-checker and a recorded opinion. For co-lent loans, whether s.13(9) applies is unsettled; default is to require the 60% record [interpretation: unsettled; confirm with counsel].

### R4.2 State machine and day counts

Calendar days with the first day excluded (General Clauses Act s.9) unless a step says working days; M1 holiday calendar of the place of the act.

| State | Entry gate and content | Exit and timer | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|
| DEMAND_ISSUED | Dues frozen as at a stated date by component; assets as described in the security document; s.13(13) restriction and s.13(8) redemption note; one notice per borrower and guarantor-mortgagor; amounts reconciled to the ledger | Dispatch by Rule 3(1) modes (R3) | s.13(2), s.13(3); Rules 3(1), 3(4), 3(5) |
| DEMAND_SERVED | Evidenced service per party; on avoidance, affixation plus 2 newspapers (one vernacular) | Cure: 60 days from the last party's service [REC: default; dispatch-based variant configurable] | s.13(2); Rule 3(1) |
| REPRESENTATION_OPEN | Representation received before any s.13(4) measure | Reasoned reply within 15 days of receipt; s.13(4) blocked until dispatched | s.13(3A) |
| SYMBOLIC_POSSESSION | Appendix IV notice delivered and affixed; movables: panchnama (App. I) and inventory (App. II) with two witnesses | Publication in 2 newspapers (one vernacular) within 7 days; website entry, updated monthly | Rules 4, 8(1)–(2); CIR para 21 |
| S14_PENDING | Physical possession resisted | Application with the affidavit declarations in the s.14(1) proviso; order targeted in 30 days, extendable to 60 (directory: *C. Bright*, SC 2020); R9 matter | s.14, s.14(1A) |
| PHYSICAL_POSSESSION | Order executed or peaceful handover | Inventory of contents; occupant and tenancy check (post-notice tenancy void: s.13(13); *Boon Realtors v. Julien Educational Trust*, Cal HC DB, June 2026) | s.13(13), s.17(4A) |
| VALUED → RESERVE_FIXED | Approved valuer's report; reserve fixed by the Authorised Officer with the secured creditor, rationale recorded | — | Rule 8(5) [VERIFY: current "approved valuer" definition] |
| SALE_NOTICE | 30-day notice to every borrower; App. IV-A in 2 newspapers (one vernacular); affixed; terms on the tenant's website; platform listing | Redemption ends on the date of publication | Rules 8(6)–(7); s.13(8); *Celir LLP v. Bafna Motors* (SC, 21 Sep 2023); *M. Rajendran v. KPK Oils* (2025 INSC 1144, 22 Sep 2025) |
| AUCTION_SCHEDULED | Earliest date: later of service and publication + 30 clear days [interpretation: conservative]; re-sale needs ≥ 15 days' notice | — | Rule 9(1) |
| AUCTION_HELD | Highest bid ≥ reserve; below reserve only with written consent of the borrower and the secured creditor | Confirmation | Rule 9(2) |
| CONFIRMED | — | 25% (including EMD) the same day or the next working day | Rule 9(3) |
| BALANCE_DUE | 25% received | Balance on or before the 15th day from confirmation; written extension agreed with the purchaser, maximum 3 months; otherwise FORFEITED and re-sale | Rule 9(4)–(5); *M.R. Vasumathi v. Authorized Officer* (SC, CA 1606/2026, 9 Jun 2026) |
| CERTIFICATE_ISSUED | Price received in time | App. V certificate; registration and state stamp duty; delivery; encumbrances discharged where agreed | Rules 9(6), 9(7), 9(9) |
| APPROPRIATED | Proceeds received | Costs, charges and expenses → dues → residue to the persons entitled (R12 rows 11–13) | s.13(7) |
| SURPLUS_PAYABLE / SHORTFALL | Residue or balance known | Surplus after a CERSAI and encumbrance check (no statutory day count; default 7 working days [REC]); shortfall by s.13(10) application (Rule 11, App. VI) or suit (R5) | s.13(7), s.13(10) [VERIFY: forum for an un-notified NBFC] |
| CLOSED / WITHDRAWN / STAYED | Paid, settled (R8), court order, moratorium | CERSAI satisfaction or modification; website removal; document release (RBC para 35) | CIR para 21; RBC para 35 |

- **Redemption:** for defaults or NPAs on or after 1 Sep 2016 the right ends on publication of the sale notice, which is one composite notice; the Rule 9(1) gap does not revive it (*M. Rajendran*). Accounts with an NPA date before 1 Sep 2016 go to counsel before publication.
- **Movables (Rules 4–7):** perishables may be sold at once (Rule 4); valuation (Rule 5); 30 days' notice with App. II-A publication, 15 days for a re-sale (Rule 6); App. III certificate (Rule 7); custody per R10.8.
- **Borrower remedies (defensive matters in R9 with the R9.4 deadlines):** s.17 application within 45 days of the s.13(4) measure, decided in 60 days and at most 4 months (s.17(1), (5); *IOB v. Radhey Infra*, SC, 7 Oct 2025); s.18 appeal within 30 days with pre-deposit of 50% of the lesser of the amount claimed and the amount determined, reducible to 25% (*Narayan Chandra Ghosh* (2011) 4 SCC 548); writs (oppose on alternative remedy, *United Bank of India v. Satyawati Tondon* (2010) 8 SCC 110); civil suits barred by s.34 save fraud or action wholly without jurisdiction. All DRT pleadings are e-filed (from 23 Jun 2025).

### R4.3 Documents and evidence

The file assembles itself as steps complete and exports as the s.14 annexure and s.17 defence bundles (R15.7): eligibility snapshot; security documents and CERSAI certificate; COB classification record (IRACP para 19); certified statement of account with an electronic-record certificate (BSA 2023 s.63 [VERIFY section]); notices and the R3.5 service register; representation and reply; possession papers, inventories, geotagged media, cuttings, website captures; s.14 papers; valuations and reserve note; bidder KYC, EMD, bid log with hash, consents, UTRs, written extensions; certificate, delivery memo, appropriation statement, surplus or shortfall letters.

### R4.4 Controls

- Hard gates in R4.1–R4.2; the API returns the failing rule and citation.
- Authorised Officer designated by the Board with rank and delegation recorded (Rule 2 [VERIFY: rank equivalence for NBFCs]); only that officer signs (R3.3).
- Possession only by the Authorised Officer, without force; police help only under a s.14 order.
- Bidder exclusion list (tenant staff, agencies, valuers and related parties) [REC]; valuation not older than 6 months at sale notice and two valuations above a Board threshold [REC].
- *Vasumathi* monitor: balance clock with T−5 and T−1 alerts; certificate generation blocked without timely payment or a signed extension.
- e-auction only on BAANKNET or a contracted platform with audit logs and bid-log export [VERIFY: NBFC access to BAANKNET and its API].

**Data captured.** `sarfaesi_case`, `sarfaesi_eligibility_check`, `representation_13_3a`, `possession_record`, `valuer_assignment`, `reserve_price_decision`, `sale_notice`, `auction` (extended), `sale_confirmation`, `sale_certificate`, `proceeds_appropriation`, `s13_9_consent`; notices and service via R3 entities; matters via R9.

**Configuration.** Eligibility profile; Authorised Officers; newspaper master by district and language; valuer panel and refresh policy; reserve and re-sale reduction policy; EMD percentage; auction platform adapter; surplus SLA; cure-timer basis; templates per state and language (R3).

**Events.** `RecoveryStrategyChanged` (mechanism `SARFAESI`), `LegalNoticeIssued` (`S13_2`, `S13_3A_REPLY`, `APPX_IV`, `APPX_IV_A`), `NoticeServiceUpdated`, `AssetRepossessed` (symbolic or physical), `CollateralValuationUpdated`, `LitigationCaseOpened` (s.14, s.17, s.13(10)), `OrderRecorded`, `AuctionScheduled`, `AuctionConcluded` (sold, failed, forfeited), `RecoveryReceiptPosted`, `CollateralReleased`, `RecoveryCaseClosed`.

**Tests (R4).**
1. No CERSAI ID → blocked without override; gold pledge → routed to R10 (eligibility thresholds are tested in R1).
2. Borrower served 4 Jan 2027, guarantor-mortgagor 8 Jan 2027 → cure ends 9 Mar 2027; a s.13(4) measure dated 9 Mar is rejected, 10 Mar accepted.
3. Representation received 20 Feb 2027 → reply due 7 Mar 2027; s.13(4) blocked until the reply's dispatch is recorded.
4. Symbolic possession 15 Mar 2027 → publication by 22 Mar 2027; s.17 window ends 29 Apr 2027.
5. Sale notice served 28 Jan and published 1 Feb 2027 → earliest auction 4 Mar 2027.
6. Confirmation 4 Mar 2027 → 25% by 5 Mar, balance by 19 Mar; balance on 22 Mar without a written extension → certificate blocked, forfeiture task opened.
7. Redemption tender after publication, NPA date 10 Jan 2020 → rejected (*M. Rajendran*); NPA date 10 Jan 2016 → counsel task.
8. CIRP admitted against the corporate borrower before the certificate → R4 frozen at the next COB (*IOB v. RCM Infrastructure*, SC 2022).
9. Proceeds ₹1.10 crore, costs ₹4 lakh, dues ₹96 lakh → surplus ₹10 lakh to the persons entitled after the CERSAI check.

## R5. Civil and tribunal remedies

**Purpose.** Obtain and execute money decrees and equivalent titles where self-help (R4, R10), cheque remedies (R7) or ADR (R8) are unavailable or insufficient, using only forums the tenant may lawfully use.

**Capabilities:** forum rules extending R1.4; pre-suit review; s.12A pre-institution mediation; ordinary, commercial and Order XXXVII suits; DRT track for eligible tenants; execution of every executable title; attachment, garnishee and salary attachment; guarantor actions; state revenue recovery (configurable).

### R5.1 Forum rules

- **DRT:** only banks as defined in RDB s.2(d) (including multi-State co-operative banks; other co-operative banks [VERIFY]) and FIs notified under RDB s.2(h)(ii); an NBFC or HFC only with a recorded gazette notification (default false); debt ≥ ₹20 lakh (S.O. 4312(E), 6 Sep 2018); a SARFAESI notification does not carry over (*Tata Motors Finance v. Naushad Khan*, Bom HC 2023; *Aditya Birla Finance v. Anjali Nag*, Del HC 2024). Where false, the track is hidden with the reason.
- **Commercial suit:** loan recovery by a banker or financier is a commercial dispute; specified value ≥ ₹3 lakh (CCA s.2(1)(c)(i)); s.12A pre-institution mediation first unless urgent interim relief is genuinely sought, judged from the plaint (*Patil Automation* (2022) 10 SCC 1, prospective from 20 Aug 2022; *Dhanbad Fuels* (SC, 15 May 2025); *Novenco v. Xero Energy* (2025 INSC 1256)). Barred where RDB s.18 applies (RDB-eligible lender, claim ≥ ₹20 lakh) and for matters within SARFAESI s.34.
- **Order XXXVII:** suits on written contracts, negotiable instruments and guarantees for a debt or liquidated demand, in courts where the Order applies (including commercial courts).
- **Government or public-officer defendants:** 2 months' notice (CPC s.80); no execution for 3 months after decree (CPC s.82).
- **Revenue recovery:** state statutes (e.g. UP 1972, Rajasthan 1952, Kerala, Tamil Nadu) only where the tenant class is notified; disabled by default; per-state record of statute, notification, form, authority and counsel sign-off [VERIFY per state].
- **Defensive forums** (Permanent Lok Adalat under LSA s.22C, consumer commissions, writs) are R9 matters and blockers in R1.

### R5.2 Suit state machine

`PRE_SUIT_REVIEW → [S12A: PIMS_APPLIED → MEDIATION → SETTLED | NON_STARTER_REPORT] → SUIT_FILED → SUMMONS_SERVED → {O37_TRACK | ORDINARY_TRACK} → DECREE → EXECUTION (R5.3) → SATISFIED → CLOSED`

| Step | Timer | Basis | Data |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pre-suit review | Before limitation end less a buffer | R1.5 | Cause of action, jurisdiction (defendant residence, cause of action, exclusive-jurisdiction clause), suit valuation, court fee, urgency note |
| s.12A mediation | 3 months, + 2 months by consent; limitation excluded meanwhile | CCA s.12A(3); PIMS Rules 2018 | DLSA reference, sessions, report |
| s.12A settlement | Signed by parties and mediator; status of an arbitral award on agreed terms | CCA s.12A(5); A&C s.30(4) | Settlement, stamp, R8 compliance schedule |
| O.XXXVII appearance | 10 days from service of summons | O.XXXVII r.3 | Date |
| Leave to defend | 10 days from service of summons for judgment | O.XXXVII r.3 | Application, order |
| Written statement (commercial) | 30 days; hard cap 120 days | CPC O.VIII r.1 as amended by the CCA | Filing date; forfeiture flag |
| Interim protection | Any time | CPC O.XXXVIII r.5, O.XXXIX, O.XL | Dissipation grounds, order |

**DRT track (eligible tenants):** `OA_FILED (e-DRT) → SUMMONS → WRITTEN_STATEMENT → INTERIM_ORDERS → FINAL_ORDER → RECOVERY_CERTIFICATE (s.19(22)) → RO_EXECUTION → CLOSED`; DRAT appeal 45 days with 50% pre-deposit of the debt determined, reducible to 25% (RDB ss.20–21); appeal against a Recovery Officer's order 30 days (s.30); Limitation Act applies (s.24).

### R5.3 Execution engine

- **Titles:** civil or commercial decree; consent decree (RSA para 100); arbitral award after the s.34 window, no automatic stay (A&C s.36); s.74 conciliation settlement; s.12A settlement; Lok Adalat award (LSA s.21); DRT recovery certificate. A Mediation Act settlement is not a decree until s.27 is notified (R8.4).
- **Workflow:** `TITLE_RECORDED → ASSET_DISCOVERY → EXECUTION_FILED → ATTACHMENT | GARNISHEE | SALARY_ATTACHMENT | ARREST_APPLICATION | RECEIVER → SALE → PROCEEDS → SATISFACTION_RECORDED → CLOSED`.
- **Forum:** awards in the court where assets lie (*Sundaram Finance v. Abdul Samad* (2018) 3 SCC 622); decrees by transfer under CPC s.39 where needed.
- **Limitation:** 12 years from the decree (Art.136), alerts at T−365, T−180 and T−90.
- **Asset discovery:** R2.4 sources; judgment-debtor examination and asset affidavit (CPC O.XXI r.41; *Rahul S. Shah v. Jinendra Kumar Gandhi* (2021) 6 SCC 418).
- **Modes:** attachment and sale (O.XXI rr.43–54, 64–66; court-sale deposit 25% and balance in 15 days, rr.84–85); attachment of debts and garnishee (rr.46, 46A–46I); salary within the exempt limit (CPC s.60(1)(i)); bank accounts; arrest only on evidence of means (CPC s.51; O.XXI rr.37–40); receiver (O.XL).
- **Payments out of court** are certified to the executing court (CPC O.XXI r.2); the R12 posting opens the certification task automatically.

### R5.4 Guarantor and co-obligor actions

Liability is co-extensive and immediate on demand; the lender need not exhaust remedies against the borrower (ICA s.128; WD para 10). Invocation through R3; limitation from the demand (R1.5); guarantors joined in the same suit so the decree runs jointly and severally; refusal despite means → WD screening (WD para 10(4)); a personal guarantor to a corporate debtor may also be pursued under IBC Part III (R6.3).

**Controls.** No DRT without the gazette record; no suit where RDB s.18 bars it; s.12A bypass only with a counsel note on the *Novenco* factors; no filing after limitation unless rebased under Limitation Act s.18 or s.19 (R1.5); execution needs a current title and a satisfaction ledger reconciled to R12.

**Data captured.** `suit_preparation`, `s12a_mediation`, `executable_title`, `execution_proceeding`, `attachment_order` (property, debt, salary, bank, garnishee), `out_of_court_payment`, `guarantee_invocation`, `revenue_recovery_request`.

**Configuration.** Court and forum master with pecuniary limits; state court-fee calculators; s.12A rules; O.XXXVII courts; DRT flag; revenue-recovery state table; execution strategy templates; counsel panels (R11).

**Events.** `RecoveryStrategyChanged`; `LegalNoticeIssued` (pre-suit demand, CPC s.80, guarantee invocation); `ADRReferralCreated` and `ADROutcomeRecorded` (s.12A, provider type `LSA_PIMS`); `LitigationCaseOpened` (`CIVIL_SUIT`, `COMMERCIAL_SUIT`, `ORDER_37`, `DRT_OA`, `EXECUTION`, `REVENUE_RECOVERY`); `HearingScheduled`; `OrderRecorded`; `LitigationCaseUpdated`; `RecoveryReceiptPosted`; `LitigationCaseClosed`.

**Tests (R5).**
1. Un-notified NBFC, claim ₹50 lakh → DRT not offered; commercial suit offered with s.12A first; claim ₹2.5 lakh → ordinary civil court without s.12A.
2. s.12A reference with a 2-month consented extension → limitation end moves by the whole mediation period.
3. Urgent-relief bypass without a counsel note → filing blocked.
4. O.XXXVII summons served 3 Feb 2027 → appearance due 13 Feb; summons for judgment served 1 Mar → leave application due 11 Mar 2027.
5. Decree dated 15 Mar 2027 → execution limitation 15 Mar 2039 with alerts.
6. Borrower pays ₹2 lakh directly during execution → O.XXI r.2 certification task opened.
7. Revenue-recovery request for a state whose flag is false → rejected with the configuration reason.

## R6. Insolvency (IBC) claims and proceedings

**Purpose.** Use the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code 2016 as a creditor (s.7, personal-guarantor proceedings, claims, CoC votes, plan and liquidation tracking, PPIRP) and propagate any moratorium to every other track at the next COB.

**Capabilities:** effective-dated rule pack; s.7 readiness and filing; IU (NeSL) records; Part III workflow; claims; CoC votes; plan and distribution tracking; PPIRP support; cause-list watcher; moratorium propagation.

### R6.1 Rule pack (IBC (Amendment) Act 2026, Act No. 6 of 2026)

Assent 6 Apr 2026; most provisions in force from **26 May 2026** (S.O. 2625(E), 22 May 2026). Each rule carries `status` and `effective_from` [VERIFY: any later commencement notification before go-live].

| Provision | Rule | Status |
|---|---|---|
| s.7(5) | NCLT "shall" ascertain default and admit or reject within 14 days; must admit where default exists, the application is complete and no disciplinary proceeding is pending against the proposed RP; reasons for delay; 7 days to cure defects; IU record sufficient proof | In force |
| s.12A | Withdrawal with 90% of the CoC, only between CoC constitution and the first invitation for resolution plans [VERIFY: reported 30-day disposal] | In force |
| s.28A | Sale of a guarantor's asset needs prior CoC approval | In force |
| s.30(2) | Dissenting financial creditor gets at least the lower of its liquidation value and its s.53 share of plan proceeds | In force |
| ss.34A, 52, 54 | CoC may replace the liquidator by 66%; secured creditor's election within 14 days with a cost contribution; liquidation 180 + 90 days | In force |
| s.53 | Secured status only to the value of security relinquished; government dues 2 years, no secured priority; statutory charges outside "security interest" | In force |
| s.54A(2)(e) | PPIRP approval threshold 51% (was 66%) | In force |
| s.61(6); ss.64A, 183A | NCLAT disposal in 3 months; penalty ₹1 lakh to ₹2 crore for frivolous proceedings | In force |
| s.96(4) | No interim moratorium against a personal guarantor to a corporate debtor | In force |
| Avoidance | Look-back from the filing date; creditors may apply if the RP does not | In force |
| CIIRP (Ch. IV-A, ss.58A–58K); group insolvency (Ch. VA); cross-border (s.240C) | — | **Not in force**: flags hard-off |

Baseline: threshold ₹1 crore (S.O. 1205(E), 24 Mar 2020); CIRP 180 + 90 days, 330-day cap (*Essar Steel*); CoC 66% for plan approval and RP replacement, 51% otherwise; PPIRP threshold ₹10 lakh, 120 days.

### R6.2 s.7 application

- **Eligibility:** financial creditor; corporate debtor that is not a financial service provider; default ≥ ₹1 crore; within Art.137 (3 years from default, *B.K. Educational* (2018)), rebased by s.18 acknowledgments including balance sheets (*Laxmi Pat Surana* (2021); *ARC v. Bishal Jaiswal* (2021)); no existing moratorium.
- **Readiness pack** (built from SMA-2 for corporate accounts flagged by R1): IU record of default and authentication status; Form 1 (AAA Rules 2016); proposed IRP's Form 2 consent and disciplinary check; Board authority; financial contracts; certified statement of account; chronology of debt (CIRP Regulations as amended 18 Sep 2023 [VERIFY: regulation number]); bench by registered office.
- **States:** `READY → FILED → DEFECTS_NOTIFIED (≤ 7 days) → ADMITTED | REJECTED | WITHDRAWN → ICD → PUBLIC_ANNOUNCEMENT → CLAIM_FILED → COC_CONSTITUTED → RFRP_ISSUED → PLAN_VOTED → PLAN_APPROVED | LIQUIDATION_ORDERED → IMPLEMENTATION | LIQUIDATION → CLOSED`.
- **Timers:** admission target 14 days from filing with escalation at day 10 and overdue flag at day 15; CIRP 180/270/330 days; appeal 30 + 15 days (s.61); s.12A window.

### R6.3 Personal guarantor (Part III, at the NCLT)

- The NCLT is always the forum for personal guarantors to corporate debtors (s.60(1); *SBI v. Mahendra Kumar Jajodia*, SC 2022).
- `DEMAND_SERVED (14 days, PG Rules) → S95_FILED → RP_APPOINTED → RP_REPORT (≤ 10 days, s.99) → ADMISSION (≤ 14 days of report, s.100) → S101_MORATORIUM (180 days) → CLAIMS → REPAYMENT_PLAN | BANKRUPTCY → CLOSED` [VERIFY: PG Rules form numbers].
- No interim moratorium on filing (s.96(4)); approval of the debtor's plan does not discharge the guarantor (*Lalit Kumar Jain v. UoI* (2021) 9 SCC 321).

### R6.4 Claims, CoC votes and plans

| Item | Rule | Data |
|---|---|---|
| CIRP claim | Form C (Form CA for a class) with proof by the last date in the public announcement (14 days from IRP appointment) | Principal, interest to the ICD, charges, security, guarantees, set-off, hash |
| Late claim | Up to the later of 90 days from the ICD and the RFRP date; reasons after 90 days; RP verifies up to 7 days before the vote | Reason note |
| Assignment | Report within 7 days (CIRP Regulations, 2023 amendment) [VERIFY: regulation number] | Transferee, R13 link |
| Liquidation | Claim as at the liquidation commencement date; s.52 election within 14 days | Election, realisation plan |
| CoC vote | One record per agenda item: voting share, internal approval (DoA, recusal), decision, rationale, time, e-vote evidence; thresholds 66% (plan, RP replacement, liquidation), 51% (others), 90% (s.12A), 66% (s.34A) | Signed record |
| Plan tracker | Applicant's s.29A declaration; upfront and deferred amounts; instruments valued under RSA paras 139–156; s.30(2) floor check on dissent; milestones; monitoring committee; breach to R9 | Plan version |

Each lender of a co-lent or consortium claim votes its own admitted claim; alignment clauses bind only if the agreement says so [interpretation]. On plan approval, claims not in the plan are extinguished against the debtor (*Ghanshyam Mishra* (2021)); the residue goes to R12 and recovery continues against guarantors.

### R6.5 Liquidation waterfall (s.53, with the 2026 explanations)

| Rank | Claim |
|---|---|
| 1 | CIRP and liquidation costs |
| 2 | Workmen's dues for 24 months, pari passu with secured creditors who relinquished security (secured only to the value relinquished) |
| 3 | Other employees' dues for 12 months |
| 4 | Financial debts of unsecured creditors |
| 5 | Government dues for 2 years (no secured priority), pari passu with secured creditors' unpaid amounts after enforcement |
| 6 | Remaining debts |
| 7 | Preference shareholders |
| 8 | Equity shareholders or partners |

The calculator estimates recovery and reconciles each distribution. Liquidation auctions are on BAANKNET for notices from 1 Apr 2025 (IBBI circulars); where the tenant realises its own security under s.52, R10 runs the sale and R6 records the distribution and any shortfall claim.

### R6.6 PPIRP for MSME corporate debtors

Record MSME status, default ≥ ₹10 lakh, the tenant's share, its approval under the 51% threshold of unrelated financial creditors (s.54A(2)(e)), base-plan terms, the 120-day clock (plan within 90 days), the s.54E moratorium and any conversion to CIRP.

### R6.7 Moratorium propagation

The NCLT cause-list watcher matches borrower, guarantor and group CINs each morning; a hit raises `RiskSignalRaised`; an admission order updates every track at the next COB.

| Event | Frozen | Continues | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|
| Application pending | Nothing; senior review before any SARFAESI sale step | All, with risk flag | *IOB v. RCM Infrastructure* (SC 2022): a sale not complete before the ICD fails |
| CIRP admitted | R4, R5, R8, R10 against the corporate debtor and its assets; set-off [VERIFY] | Guarantor actions (s.14(3)(b); *SBI v. V. Ramakrishnan* (2018)); s.138 against directors (*P. Mohanraj v. Shah Brothers Ispat* (2021) 6 SCC 258) | IBC s.14 |
| PPIRP commenced | As for CIRP | As for CIRP | s.54E |
| PG application filed | Nothing | All | s.96(4) |
| PG application admitted | All actions on that guarantor's debts | Actions against others | s.101 |
| Liquidation order | Suits against the debtor without NCLT leave | s.52 realisation | ss.33(5), 52 |
| Plan approved | Claims beyond the plan | Guarantors | *Ghanshyam Mishra*; *Lalit Kumar Jain* |

**Accounting.** Plan proceeds, instruments and distributions post through R12 row 25 (instruments under RSA paras 139–156 and Ind AS 109; deferred consideration per policy [VERIFY: auditor sign-off]); admitted cases are reported to CICs as suit-filed (CIR para 12(7)).

**Controls.** Filing by a Board-delegated officer; IU record authenticated before filing; confidentiality undertakings for CoC papers; votes cast only by the authorised representative; cause-list hits acknowledged within one business day.

**Data captured.** `ibc_proceeding`, `iu_record`, `ibc_claim` (versions), `coc_meeting`, `coc_vote`, `ibc_resolution_plan`, `s52_election`, `liquidation_distribution`, `moratorium_order`, `cause_list_hit`.

**Configuration.** NCLT bench master [VERIFY: bench jurisdiction map — Chandigarh bench for Punjab, Haryana, HP, J&K and Ladakh; Uttarakhand to Allahabad; no Pune or Aurangabad bench]; CoC DoA; claim-update triggers; recovery-estimate models.

**Events.** `LitigationCaseOpened` (`IBC_S7`, `IBC_S95`, `CIRP_CLAIM`, `LIQUIDATION_CLAIM`, `PPIRP`), `HearingScheduled`, `OrderRecorded` (admission, moratorium, plan, liquidation), `LitigationCaseUpdated` (claim admitted, vote cast), `RiskSignalRaised`, `RecoveryStrategyChanged` (freeze or release), `AuctionScheduled`, `AuctionConcluded`, `RecoveryReceiptPosted`, `LitigationCaseClosed`.

**Tests (R6).**
1. Default ₹90 lakh, or a corporate debtor that is an NBFC → s.7 blocked.
2. Default 3 Feb 2023 with a balance-sheet acknowledgment signed 30 Jun 2024 → limitation 30 Jun 2027 [interpretation: *Bishal Jaiswal*].
3. Filed 1 Feb 2027 → admission target 15 Feb 2027; escalation 11 Feb; overdue flag 16 Feb.
4. IRP appointed 10 Mar 2027 → claim due 24 Mar 2027; a claim on 20 Jun 2027 with the RFRP issued 15 Jul 2027 → accepted as late with reasons.
5. CIRP admitted → R4, R5 and R8 actions against the debtor frozen at the next COB; the s.138 matter against two directors stays active.
6. PG s.95 filed → no freeze; admitted → all actions against that guarantor frozen.
7. A CIIRP workflow request → rejected: "provision not in force".

## R7. Cheque and mandate dishonour (s.138 NI Act; s.25 PSS Act)

**Purpose.** Turn every qualifying cheque or e-mandate dishonour into a time-compliant notice and, where policy allows, a complaint, with an evidence pack drawn from M7 and communications that stay factual.

**Capabilities:** instrument registry; return-reason qualification; day-count engine; bulk notices (R3); complaint pack and jurisdiction resolver; *Sanjabij Tari* procedure support; s.143A and s.148 tracking; compounding linked to R8; director-liability data; court-cluster operations.

### R7.1 Inputs and qualification

**From M7 (immutable):** cheque number, date, amount, drawer account, drawee branch, payee branch where deposited for collection, purpose (EMI, PDC, SPDC, security); NACH/ECS UMRN, sponsor and destination banks, debit date and amount; presentation record; return memo or NPCI return code with timestamp; date the information reached the tenant.

| Return reason | s.138 (cheque) | s.25 PSS (e-mandate) |
|---|---|---|
| Insufficient funds; exceeds arrangement | Yes | Yes (the only s.25 grounds) |
| Account closed | Yes (*NEPC Micon v. Magma Leasing* (1999) 4 SCC 253) | No |
| Payment stopped by drawer | Generally yes, case-dependent [VERIFY: counsel-approved mapping] | No |
| Signature mismatch | Case-dependent (*Laxmi Dyechem v. State of Gujarat* (2012) 13 SCC 375) [VERIFY] | No |
| Technical (mandate not registered, bank error) | No: re-present or correct | No |

A security cheque presented after the instalment fell due qualifies (*Sampelly Satyanarayana Rao v. IREDA* (2016) 10 SCC 458); time-barred debts do not (R1.5).

### R7.2 Day-count engine

| Step | Rule | Basis | Golden test |
|---|---|---|---|
| Presentation | Within validity (3 months); re-presentation within validity allowed, each dishonour plus notice a fresh cause of action | s.138 proviso (a); *MSR Leathers v. S. Palaniappan* (2013) 1 SCC 177 | Cheque dated 1 Nov 2026 → present by 31 Jan 2027 [interpretation: conservative] |
| Information received | Date the return memo or file reaches the tenant | s.138(b) | 5 Jan 2027 |
| Demand notice | Within 30 days of receiving information | s.138(b) | Last day 4 Feb 2027 |
| Service | Speed post with PoD, courier and email through R3 (WhatsApp barred by the 7A.0.6 guard-rail although courts have accepted it, *Rajendra v. State of UP*, All HC 2024); deemed service on refusal or "unclaimed" at the correct address | *C.C. Alavi Haji* (2007) 6 SCC 555 | Delivered 10 Feb 2027 |
| Payment window | 15 days from receipt | s.138(c) | Ends 25 Feb 2027 |
| Cause of action | Next day | — | 26 Feb 2027 |
| Complaint | Within one month, excluding the first day; condonable for sufficient cause | s.142(1)(b) and proviso; *Econ Antri v. Rom Industries* (2014) 11 SCC 769 | Last day 26 Mar 2027; filing on 29 Mar drafts a condonation application |
| Jurisdiction | Court where the payee's branch of deposit is | s.142(2)(a); s.142A | From M7 |
| Trial | Summary; reasons to convert; evidence on affidavit | s.143; *In re Expeditious Trial* (SC, 16 Apr 2021) | — |
| Interim compensation | Up to 20%, discretionary; paid within 60 days, + 30 | s.143A | — |
| Appeal deposit | ≥ 20% of fine or compensation | s.148 | — |

**s.25 PSS Act:** the same notice, payment, complaint and trial steps apply to an electronic funds transfer dishonoured for insufficiency or exceeding the arrangement; the mandate, UMRN and NPCI return file replace the cheque and memo.

### R7.3 *Sanjabij Tari v. Kishore Borcar* (2025 INSC 1158, 25 Sep 2025)

- Mandatory synopsis, generated with the complaint.
- Summons by ordinary modes plus dasti, email, WhatsApp and other electronic modes under the BNSS, with an affidavit of service; the tenant supplies verified contacts from M3 (court-issued service is not a tenant communication).
- Summons may carry a court QR or UPI link; payment of the cheque amount closes the case; the tenant reconciles its receipt to the court's confirmation.
- No pre-cognizance summons under BNSS s.223; a Delhi HC Larger Bench reference on the s.223 proviso (18 Mar 2026) keeps this configurable per court [VERIFY: outcome].
- s.143A applied for at the first opportunity.
- Compounding costs on the cheque amount: nil before defence evidence; 5% after defence evidence and before judgment; 7.5% in revision or appeal before the Sessions Court or High Court; 10% before the Supreme Court [VERIFY: payee of costs]. The R8 settlement screen shows the cost at the current stage.

### R7.4 Complaint pack and accused

- **Pack:** verified complaint; Board resolution or power of attorney; synopsis; original cheque or mandate record; return memo or NPCI file; notice and service evidence; electronic-record certificate (BSA 2023 s.63 [VERIFY section]); statement of account; agreement and KFS; affidavit evidence (s.145).
- **Accused (s.141):** the company must be arraigned (*Aneeta Hada v. Godfather Travels* (2012) 5 SCC 661); directors named only with specific averments that they were in charge of and responsible for the business at the time (*SMS Pharmaceuticals v. Neeta Bhalla* (2005) 8 SCC 89); officer data from MCA as at the offence date; under an IBC moratorium, natural persons only (*P. Mohanraj*).

### R7.5 State machine

`INSTRUMENT_RETURNED → QUALIFIED | NOT_QUALIFIED → NOTICE_ISSUED → NOTICE_SERVED | SERVICE_FAILED → PAYMENT_WINDOW → PAID | CAUSE_OF_ACTION → POLICY_DECISION (ticket, product, prospects) → COMPLAINT_FILED → COGNIZANCE → SUMMONS_SERVED → S143A_ORDERED → TRIAL → COMPOUNDED | CONVICTED | ACQUITTED | WITHDRAWN → APPEAL (R9) → CLOSED`

A settlement in R8 closes a pending complaint only by a compounding or withdrawal order recorded by the court [interpretation: RSA para 100 speaks of recovery proceedings; record the court's order in every case].

**Controls.** Users cannot extend timers; a missed notice deadline closes the instrument as `TIME_BARRED_NOTICE`; communications factual, with no threat of arrest, police action or exposure, and a description of the criminal process only where an instrument was actually dishonoured (R15.1; RBC para 100); PDC/SPDC custody register with dual control; unused instruments returned and mandates cancelled on closure (RBC para 17); interim compensation held as refundable (R12 row 26); volume filing by court cluster with one evidence pack per complaint.

**Data captured.** `negotiable_instrument` (cheque or mandate, custody, validity end), `instrument_return` (reason code, information date, qualification), `dishonour_track` (notice, service, window, cause of action, complaint last date, condonation flag), `accused_person` (role, s.141 basis, DIN), `compounding_cost_calc`.

**Configuration.** Return-reason mapping (counsel-approved); filing policy by product, ticket and DPD; templates per language; court clusters; counsel allocation (R11); compounding authority (R8 matrix).

**Events.** Consumes Part 5.2 `PaymentBounced`; emits `LegalNoticeIssued` (`S138`, `S25_PSS`), `NoticeServiceUpdated`, `LitigationCaseOpened` (`S138`, `S25PSS`), `HearingScheduled`, `OrderRecorded` (summons, s.143A, conviction, compounding), `SettlementApproved`, `RecoveryReceiptPosted`, `LitigationCaseClosed`.

**Tests (R7).**
1. The R7.2 golden dates are reproduced exactly.
2. NACH returned "account closed" → s.25 not offered; a cheque returned "account closed" → s.138 offered.
3. Cheque presented after validity → flagged stale; no notice.
4. Venue resolves to the court of the payee's branch of deposit, not the drawee branch.
5. Compounding cost on a ₹2,00,000 cheque: ₹0, ₹10,000, ₹15,000 and ₹20,000 by stage.
6. Company accused admitted into CIRP → complaint continues against named directors; company stage `STAYED`.

## R8. Settlement and ADR (negotiation/OTS, conciliation, mediation, arbitration, Lok Adalat; Equator and other providers)

**Purpose.** Resolve defaulted accounts by agreement or by an enforceable neutral outcome, within the Board's settlement policy and the RBI rules, through Equator Resolution first and any certified provider on the same contract, using arbitration only where the appointment will survive enforcement scrutiny.

**Capabilities:** settlement policy engine, NPV calculator and approvals; negotiation log; consent-decree and restructuring routing; arbitration gates; conciliation; Mediation Act features behind flags; Lok Adalat batches; provider abstraction; outcome compliance; hand-off to R5.

### R8.1 Settlement policy engine (RSA paras 16, 86–100)

The policy is a versioned object linked to its Board approval (M19). It applies to all NBFCs including those below ₹500 crore (RSA para 157); for HFCs only paras 86–138 bind (RSA para 5), which do not include para 16, so the para 16 approver rule is applied to HFC tenants as policy [REC].

| Element | Rule | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| Policy content | Conditions precedent (minimum ageing, collateral deterioration); graded staff accountability; permissible sacrifice by category after realisable value; realisable-value methodology | RSA para 16(1)–(4) |
| Approver | At least one level above the sanctioning authority; anyone who sanctioned the loan excluded in any capacity; related-party recusal | RSA para 16(5)(i); CRM para 13J |
| Fraud and wilful defaulters | Board approval in every case; without prejudice to criminal proceedings; penal measures continue; fraud debarment runs 5 years from full payment of the settlement; LWD removal only after full payment | RSA paras 16(5)(ii), 97–98; FRM para 35; WD para 13 |
| Discretion | Not a borrower's right | RSA para 87 |
| Contingent claims | May be agreed but not recognised on balance sheet; recognition makes it restructuring | RSA para 88 |
| Payment period | Over 3 months, or any part settlement, is restructuring | RSA paras 89–90 |
| Pending proceedings | Settlement subject to a consent decree from the forum | RSA para 100 |
| Cooling period | Board-set, floor 12 months; technical write-offs per Board | RSA paras 95–96 |
| Reporting | Quarterly to the next higher authority; MD & CEO or Board-committee approvals to the Board; para 94 content | RSA paras 93–94 |
| CIC | Report settlements with reasons; "settled" only for waivers due to financial inability; wrong debits and contested charges as "disputed" | CIR paras 12(2), 12(4) |

- **Calculator:** NPV of the offer against the realisable path for each permitted mechanism (R1 estimates of time, cost and recovery); sacrifice by component (penal charges, interest, principal, costs); band check by product, DPD and amount. Bots and Udofin may present offers only inside the pre-approved band (R15.3).
- **Negotiation log:** every offer and counter-offer, channel, participants, recording or transcript reference (none for mediation) and the policy-check result at that moment (extends the R2.5 log).
- **States:** `SETTLEMENT_REQUESTED → PROPOSAL_DRAFTED → POLICY_CHECKED → APPROVAL_ROUTED → APPROVED | REJECTED → OFFER_ISSUED → ACCEPTED (eSign) → [CONSENT_DECREE_REQUIRED → DECREE_RECORDED] → PAYMENT_PLAN_ACTIVE → COMPLETED | BREACHED → CURE_PERIOD → REVIVED → CLOSED`.
- **On completion:** NOC; release of security (property documents within 30 days, RBC paras 35–39; gold within 7 working days, RBC paras 58, 69); CIC update; LWD removal where due; CERSAI satisfaction; cooling-period block in the M4 BRE; R12 row 19.
- **Shared exposures:** each lender approves its own share under its own policy; the servicer issues one joint offer only when all approvals exist (R13.2). A DLG provider has no approval right.

### R8.2 Arbitration gates

R1.4 decides arbitrability: blocked for banks and notified FIs with RDB claims ≥ ₹20 lakh (*Vidya Drolia*, SC, 14 Dec 2020), for in-rem mortgage enforcement (*Booz Allen* (2011) 5 SCC 532), under an IBC moratorium, and not compellable while a consumer complaint is pending (*Emaar MGF v. Aftab Singh* (2019) 12 SCC 751). Where it is permitted, four gates apply and none can be overridden.

- **Gate A — consent basis.** Either the loan agreement version on the account pre-names Equator or another independent institution (clause, version, execution and stamp proof stored; appointment by such an institution is not unilateral, *Sundaram Finance v. Hanuman Prasad*, Raj HC, SBCWP 17398/2024, 2026), or the borrower gives written post-dispute consent naming the institution (eSign or OTP, IP, timestamp, full text shown, explicit decline path). Otherwise the referral is blocked and the engine offers a s.11 petition (R9) or other routes; referral to a provider not pre-agreed is unilateral in substance and the award a nullity (*L&T Finance v. Jai Paras Material Store*, Cal HC, EC-COM 218/2026, 14 May 2026).
- **Gate B — no unilateral appointment.** The tenant, its counsel, agencies and Udofin cannot nominate, shortlist, rank or veto a neutral, or force a choice from a tenant-curated panel (*CORE v. ECI-SPIC-SMO-MCML (JV)*, Constitution Bench, 8 Nov 2024; *Perkins Eastman v. HSCC* (2020) 20 SCC 760); a s.12(5) waiver needs an express post-dispute written agreement (*Bharat Broadband* (2019) 5 SCC 755). The API has no "preferred neutral" field.
- **Gate C — independence evidence.** For each appointment the provider returns the pool snapshot, filters, random seed and selection log; the neutral's 3-year count of this tenant's matters against the configured cap (Fifth Schedule items 22 and 24); the Sixth Schedule disclosure signed before acceptance; a Seventh Schedule conflict check; and the fee basis (published schedule, paid to the institution or neutral, never through the tenant's counsel, no outcome-linked fee). In *Shikha Ghosh v. Axis Bank* (Del HC DB, FAO(COMM) 91/2025, 30 Sep 2026) an arbitrator who handled 4,155 of a bank's cases and was paid through its lawyer produced unenforceable awards; the bank and RBI must file affidavits by 16 Nov 2026, next date 17 Nov 2026 [VERIFY: outcome and any RBI direction before go-live].
- **Gate D — service.** The s.21 request goes to every known address and email through R3 with delivery evidence; no deemed service without evidence or a documented reasonable inquiry (A&C s.3; *Sedhram Nilkanth Muglikar v. M.R. Makhare*, Bom HC, 2026).

**Timelines (R9 alerts):**

| Step | Limit | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| Commencement | Receipt of the s.21 request (limitation anchor) | A&C ss.21, 43 |
| Failure to appoint | s.11 petition after 30 days, within 3 years | s.11(4)–(5); *Arif Azim v. Aptech* (2024 INSC 155) |
| Challenge to neutral | 15 days from awareness | s.13(2) |
| Pleadings | 6 months from the arbitrator's notice of appointment | s.23(4) |
| Award | 12 months from completion of pleadings; + 6 by consent; then court | s.29A |
| Fast track | 6 months, on documents, by written agreement | s.29B |
| Award form | Written, signed (eSign valid), reasoned, dated, place stated; post-award interest 2% above the current rate unless the award says otherwise | s.31, s.31(7)(b) |
| Stamping | Duty due on signing; stamp the same day | Stamp Act Sch. I Art.12 or state law; *URC Construction v. AAI* (Del HC, 1 Sep 2026) |
| Correction | 30 days; additional award 60 days | s.33 |
| Challenge | 3 months + 30 days from each party's receipt | s.34(3) |
| Enforcement | As a decree after the window, in the civil court where assets lie; no automatic stay | s.36; *Sundaram Finance v. Abdul Samad* (2018) 3 SCC 622 |

- **Enforcement risk:** High Courts are split on whether an executing court may refuse an award by a unilaterally appointed arbitrator (refusal: *Mahavir Prasad Gupta v. GNCTD*, Del HC DB, 31 May 2025, and *L&T Finance*; contra: *Sundaram Finance v. S.M. Thangaraj*, Mad HC, 27 Jan 2025). Legacy awards with unilateral appointments are flagged `ENFORCEMENT_RISK` and executed only after counsel review; legacy loans with unilateral or no-institution clauses enter a post-dispute consent campaign (UR2) or the s.11 route [REC].
- **Interim relief:** s.9 (proceedings within 90 days, s.9(2)); s.17 tribunal orders; emergency-arbitrator orders only under institutional rules (*Amazon v. Future Retail* (2022) 1 SCC 209).

### R8.3 Conciliation (default enforceable settlement route)

Part III of the A&C Act stays in force until Mediation Act s.61 and the Sixth Schedule are notified.

`INVITED (s.62) → ACCEPTED | DECLINED | DEEMED_DECLINED (30 days' silence, s.62(4)) → CONCILIATOR_APPOINTED → SESSIONS → SETTLEMENT_SIGNED (s.73: signed by the parties, authenticated by the conciliator) → STAMPED [VERIFY: state article] → COMPLIANCE → CLOSED | NON_SETTLEMENT`

The settlement has the status of an arbitral award on agreed terms (s.74 with s.30), executable under s.36. Confidentiality (s.75); no proceedings during conciliation except to preserve rights (s.77), so limitation keeps running and protective filing stays open; the conciliator cannot later arbitrate (s.80). RSA checks apply: instalments over 3 months make it restructuring (para 89); where a proceeding is pending, the settlement is also filed there for a consent decree (para 100).

### R8.4 Mediation

S.O. 4384(E) of 9 Oct 2023 brought into force only ss.1, 3, 26, 31–38, 45–47, 50–54 and 56–57 of the Mediation Act 2023; the Mediation Council of India was established on 27 Aug 2026; no notification was found for ss.4–25 or 27–30 [VERIFY: egazette before go-live].

| Provision | Feature | Status |
|---|---|---|
| s.5 pre-litigation mediation (voluntary) | Pre-litigation workflow | Not notified: flag off |
| s.8 (appointment in 7 days); s.18 (120 + 60 days); ss.19–20 (settlement, optional registration); s.28 (challenge 90 + 90 days) | Clocks and records | Not notified: built, flag off |
| ss.22–23 confidentiality, no recording | Recording hard-disabled in any mediation session | Applied now as policy [REC] |
| s.27 enforcement as a decree | Executable title | **Not notified**: a mediated settlement is a contract only |
| s.30 online mediation with written consent | Consent capture | Not notified: consent captured anyway [REC] |
| CCA s.12A pre-institution mediation | R5.2 | In force |

Until s.27 is in force, a mediated outcome is converted into a s.73/74 settlement, a s.12A settlement or a consent decree before it is treated as enforceable.

### R8.5 Lok Adalat

- **Law:** pending and pre-litigation matters (LSA ss.19–20); the award is a deemed civil-court decree, final and not appealable (s.21); no statutory cap; RBI's ₹20 lakh ceiling (RBI/2004-05/95, 3 Aug 2004) binds banks and AIFIs only.
- **Calendar:** National Lok Adalats 2026 on 14 Mar, 9 May, 12 Sep and 12 Dec [VERIFY: nalsa.gov.in]; maintained per state and district; DRT Lok Adalats only for DRT-eligible tenants.
- **Batch:** T−45 to T−30 select (exclude fraud or WD without the Board protocol, IBC moratorium, deceased without legal representatives; apply the R8.1 band); T−15 submit in the DLSA or SLSA format; per-account delegation letter signed one level above the sanctioner; LSA notice plus the tenant's RBC-compliant SMS or email; sitting; certified award uploaded; schedule (restructuring flag over 3 months); breach → execution (R5.3); no settlement → re-queue.
- **Permanent Lok Adalat:** a borrower forum for notified public-utility services up to ₹1 crore; once invoked, the court route is barred (s.22C) → R9.

### R8.6 ADR provider abstraction and Equator

**Contract** (Integration Specification): processes, appointment model with Gate C evidence, service proof, eSign and e-stamp, hearing modes, fees, data role, API or CSV/SFTP transport, SLAs. A provider is enabled only after `ConnectorCertified`, including an independence test pack. Equator is the first certified provider; others (for example Presolv360, Sama, Jupitice, CADRE, Webnyay) connect through adapters, CSV where no API exists.

| Provider state | Canonical event | Finbyx action |
|---|---|---|
| Referral sent | `ADRReferralCreated` | Referral pack frozen and hashed |
| Screening result; withdrawn, terminated, stayed, mandate extended | `ADRCaseStatusChanged` | Fix, reroute or update the track |
| Notice dispatched or delivered | `NoticeServiceUpdated` | Proof per channel |
| Post-dispute, online-mediation or fast-track consent; decline | `ADRConsentRecorded` | Gate A satisfied or route closed |
| Neutral appointed with disclosure | `ADRNeutralAppointed` | Gate C checked; challenge clock |
| Hearing scheduled | `ADRHearingScheduled` | R9 calendar; Udofin link (UR2) |
| Settlement proposed outside the mandate | `ADRCaseStatusChanged` | Routed to R8.1 approval |
| Settlement signed, award signed or stamped, non-settlement | `ADROutcomeRecorded` | Title recorded; s.34 clock or schedule |
| Payment or breach against the outcome | `ADROutcomeComplianceUpdated` | R12 posting; `SettlementBreached`; enforcement hand-off |

- **Documents:** referral pack (agreement with clause and stamp proof, KFS, certified statement of account, recall and s.21 notices with proofs, settlement mandate with floor, tenor, waiver limits and expiry, authority letter); outputs (disclosures, orders, minutes except for mediation, eSigned and e-stamped settlement or award in PDF/A, non-settlement report, closure certificate); the provider keeps originals, Finbyx certified copies and hashes.
- **Payments:** only through links or virtual accounts into the tenant's own account (CF para 10(2)–(3)); Equator and Udofin never receive borrower money; neutral fees paid by the tenant under the provider's schedule; any recovery of ADR costs from the borrower needs a KFS-disclosed charge or explicit consent (RBC para 29(5)) [VERIFY: interaction with penal-charge rules].
- **Outcome compliance:** schedule tracking, reminders (UR1 where permitted), breach detection, cure notice, then R5 with an enforcement pack (certified outcome, stamp proof, service proofs, s.34 status) or R8.1 for a revised settlement.

**Controls.** Gates A–D; R8.1 matrix with sanctioners excluded; a settlement cannot reach `COMPLETED` while R9 shows a pending matter without a consent decree; mediation recording disabled; cooling-period block in M4; monthly neutral-concentration review by Compliance.

**Data captured.** `settlement_proposal` (dues snapshot, offer, sacrifice by component, NPV, policy version, restructuring flag), `settlement_approval`, `settlement_schedule`, `settlement_breach`, `adr_case`, `arbitration_clause_version`, `adr_consent`, `neutral_appointment`, `adr_outcome`, `lok_adalat_batch`, `lok_adalat_entry`; v1.3 `settlement`, `consent_decree`, `cooling_period` reused.

**Configuration.** Policy versions and bands; approval matrix; clause library (institution and alternate, seat in the borrower's state by default [REC], online hearings, fast track, consumer carve-out); providers and caps; Lok Adalat calendars and DLSA formats; stamp rules by state.

**Events.** `SettlementRequested`, `SettlementOfferIssued`, `SettlementOfferAccepted` (consumed; eSign or OTP acceptance), `SettlementApproved`, `SettlementBreached`, `ADRReferralCreated`, `ADRConsentRecorded`, `ADRNeutralAppointed`, `ADRHearingScheduled`, `ADRCaseStatusChanged`, `ADROutcomeRecorded`, `ADROutcomeComplianceUpdated`, `NoticeServiceUpdated`, `LitigationCaseOpened` (s.9, s.11, s.34, s.36), `RecoveryReceiptPosted`, `RecoveryCaseClosed`, `PolicyAttested`.

**Tests (R8).**
1. Four monthly instalments → restructuring tag before approval; three instalments within 3 months → no tag.
2. Approver who sat on the sanctioning committee → blocked; fraud-classified borrower → routed to the Board.
3. Pending civil suit → settlement cannot complete until a consent decree is recorded.
4. Fresh loan application 11 months after completion → BRE declines on the cooling period.
5. Clause names no institution and no post-dispute consent → referral blocked with the *L&T Finance* reason.
6. Neutral at the tenant's cap → excluded; provider response without a selection log → appointment rejected.
7. Award received 10 Apr 2027 → 3 months end 10 Jul 2027, condonable outer limit 9 Aug 2027; execution blocked until 10 Aug 2027 unless counsel records a decision to file after 10 Jul [interpretation].
8. Award not stamped within the state window → enforcement pack blocked pending impounding and duty.
9. Mediation-as-decree requested → disabled ("Mediation Act s.27 not in force"); conciliation offered.
10. Lok Adalat batch excludes a borrower under moratorium and a deceased borrower without legal representatives.

## R9. Litigation and proceedings tracker

**Purpose.** One record of every proceeding the lender brings or defends, in every forum, linked to the recovery case, ADR, accounting and provisioning.

### R9.1 Forums and matter types

- **Forums:** civil and commercial courts (including Order XXXVII and execution); DRT and DRAT; NCLT and NCLAT; High Courts (writs, appeals, s.11 and s.34 petitions); Supreme Court; criminal courts (s.138 and s.25 complaints, FIRs); consumer commissions (e-Jagriti, live from 1 Jan 2025); RBI Ombudsman and CMS; arbitral tribunals; Lok Adalats and Permanent Lok Adalats; Equator and other ODR providers; revenue-recovery authorities; s.14 CMM or DM proceedings.
- **Offensive matters:** s.14 applications, DRT original applications (where eligible), suits, s.138 complaints, IBC s.7 and s.95 applications, Form C claims, arbitration claims, execution petitions, s.13(10) shortfall applications.
- **Defensive matters:** borrower s.17 applications (45 days from the s.13(4) measure; DRT decides in 60 days, maximum 4 months, SARFAESI s.17(5), enforced in *IOB v. Radhey Infra*, SC, 7 Oct 2025); writs; consumer complaints (an arbitration clause does not bar them, *Emaar MGF v. Aftab Singh*, (2019) 12 SCC 751); PLA applications; s.34 challenges to awards; police complaints against agents; RB-IOS complaints; CPGRAMS.
- Counter-litigation links: every defensive matter links to the offensive track it attacks (`linked_matters[]`).

### R9.2 Data model

- `matter`: case and account links, role (petitioner or respondent), mechanism, forum (type, state, district, bench, court number), case type and number, CNR or diary or filing number, filed on, claim and relief, status and stage, next date and purpose, judge or bench, counsel and opposing counsel, stay (flag, order, scope, expiry), outcome (type, amount, date), costs awarded, recovery to date, provisioning and contingent-liability link.
- `hearing`: date, bench, item number, purpose, attended by, minutes, next date, adjournment reason and party, costs imposed.
- `order`: date, type (interim, final, decree, award, RC, dismissal), PDF, OCR text, AI summary with a `human_verified` flag, extracted directions converted to tasks.
- `deadline`: source (rule pack, order, manual), due, owner, escalation chain, status.

### R9.3 Court-data synchronisation

- **Source hierarchy:** (1) official eCourts open APIs for institutional litigants, applied for through the e-Committee or a High Court [VERIFY: NBFC eligibility for institutional credentials]; (2) licensed CNR-based court-data vendors through the connector SPI [VERIFY: vendor coverage of DRT and DRAT]; (3) counsel portal updates; (4) manual entry with upload.
- DRT: all RDB and SARFAESI pleadings are e-filed since 23 Jun 2025 (DRT/DRAT Electronic Filing (Amendment) Rules 2025), but no public API is known; NCLT, NCLAT, Supreme Court and RBI CMS likewise. Status comes from vendors or counsel.
- Conflicting next dates: show both, prefer counsel for the next date and the official source for orders, raise a task. Each morning, match cause lists against open matters; a missing expected listing raises an alert.

### R9.4 Hearing calendar and deadlines engine

- Calendars by counsel, forum, officer and region; conflict detection (two matters, one counsel, same time in different cities).
- **Deadline rules (rule pack, each cited):** s.17 reply and the DRT's s.17(5) outer limit; SARFAESI s.18 appeal 30 days with 50% pre-deposit of the lesser of claim and amount determined (reducible to 25%); RDB s.20 appeal 45 days with s.21 deposit; RDB s.30 appeal 30 days; NCLAT appeal 30 + 15 days (IBC s.61); s.7(5) NCLT decision within 14 days with 7 days to cure defects; CIRP 330-day cap; Form C by the public-announcement date; s.34 challenge 3 months + 30 days (A&C Act s.34(3)); s.33 correction 30 days; s.29A mandate 12 months after completion of pleadings; consumer complaint 2 years (CPA 2019 s.69) and appeal 45 days (CPA 2019 s.41); SLP 90 days [VERIFY: Supreme Court Rules 2013 O.XXII r.2(1)]; written statement in commercial suits capped at 120 days; Order XXXVII appearance and leave to defend 10 days each.
- **Watch items:** *Shikha Ghosh v. Axis Bank* (Del HC DB, 30 Sep 2026; RBI affidavit due 16 Nov 2026, next hearing 17 Nov 2026) on bulk unilateral arbitration; the Delhi HC Larger Bench reference on BNSS s.223 and s.138 (18 Mar 2026).

### R9.5 Orders, documents and counsel portal

- Orders synced or uploaded, OCR'd and summarised by AI; directions become tasks only after human confirmation (M20). Certified copies tracked. E-filing bundles prepared (searchable, paginated, bookmarked, split to portal limits) [VERIFY: portal size limits by forum]. All documents in M16 with hash and legal hold.
- Counsel portal: assigned matters only; next date, purpose and minutes; orders and drafts; instruction requests; fee notes against the R11 schedule. Instructions to file, settle, concede or appeal are recorded with approver and time.

### R9.6 Costs, outcomes, contingent liabilities and alerts

- Fee budget per matter and stage with variance alerts.
- Outcomes drive R12: decree amounts to a memo legal-claim ledger (no NPA income until realised, IRACP para 38); costs awarded recognised on realisation; deposits (SARFAESI s.18, RDB s.21, NI Act ss.143A, 148) tracked with interest per order.
- Defensive matters with monetary exposure assessed quarterly as probable, possible or remote, feeding provisions and disclosures (Ind AS 37).
- Alerts: next date within 7 days without an update; order without tasks; adjournments over a threshold; stay expiring; appeal or execution limitation.
- Integration: an R8 or Equator referral creates a matter that `ADRCaseStatusChanged` and `ADROutcomeRecorded` update; s.9, s.11, s.34 and execution proceedings on an award are linked court matters; an IBC admission order puts R1 on moratorium hold.

**Data captured.** Matters, hearings, orders, deadlines, stays, deposits, costs, outcomes, contingent-liability assessments, source and conflict log.

**Controls.** Matter cannot close without an outcome and an order; any settlement in a pending matter requires a consent-decree task (RSA para 100); AI summaries cannot create tasks until verified; counsel edits are versioned.

**Configuration.** Forum masters, matter types, stage lists per forum, alert offsets (tighten only), vendor sources and polling schedules, contingent-liability thresholds.

**Events.** Emitted: `LitigationCaseOpened`, `LitigationCaseUpdated`, `HearingScheduled`, `OrderRecorded`, `LitigationCaseClosed`, `LegalHoldChanged` (hold applied or released on a matter). Consumed: `ADRReferralCreated`, `ADRCaseStatusChanged`, `ADROutcomeRecorded`, `ADROutcomeComplianceUpdated`, `LegalNoticeIssued`, `GrievanceRaised`, `LoanTransferred`.

**Tests (R9).** A s.17 application against a possession taken on 1 Jun creates a 45-day window ending 16 Jul and links to the SARFAESI track; a CNR sync showing a different next date from counsel raises a conflict task; a final order cannot close a matter while a deposit refund is pending; a consumer complaint against an account with an arbitration clause is accepted as a defensive matter; an IBC admission order freezes the SARFAESI track in R1.

## R10. Repossession, valuation, auction and sale

**Purpose.** Take, hold, value and sell or invoke each type of security lawfully, apply proceeds correctly and return any surplus.

**Capabilities:** asset routing; vehicle repossession; gold and silver auctions; pledge and lien invocation; deposit set-off; receivable notices; liquidation-auction tracking; custody registers; platform adapters; surplus and shortfall handling.

### R10.1 Asset routing

| Asset | Route | Engine |
|---|---|---|
| Immovable property | SARFAESI if eligible, else decree execution | R4; R5 |
| Plant, machinery, stock | SARFAESI Rules 4–7 if eligible, else contract or court receiver | R4; R5 |
| Vehicles | Contractual repossession within RBC para 26 and *Hari Dutta Sharma*; SARFAESI movables where eligible and chosen by policy | R10.2 |
| Gold and silver (pledge) | ICA s.176 under RBC paras 60–66 and CF para 40; outside SARFAESI (s.31(b)) | R10.3 |
| Securities and demat MF units (pledge); SOA MF units (lien) | ICA ss.176–177; depository or RTA invocation | R10.4 |
| Fixed deposits | Contractual lien and set-off | R10.5 |
| Book debts, receivables, TReDS units | Notice to account debtors; assignment; TReDS settlement | R10.6 |
| Assets in IBC liquidation | Liquidator's sale or s.52 realisation | R10.7; R6 |

### R10.2 Vehicles

The agreement must contain an enforceable clause on notice period, waiver circumstances, procedure, final chance to repay before sale, redelivery and sale (RBC para 26). In *Hari Dutta Sharma v. State of UP* (2026 LiveLaw (SC) 942, SC, 16 Sep 2026) a forcible 1 a.m. seizure without the contractual 7-day notice or a signed possession memo conferred no right of repossession and violated Articles 14 and 21; the Court awarded ₹10 lakh compensation, closed the loans, ordered refund of the sale price with 6% interest and directed RBI to enforce compliance.

`DEFAULT → PRE_REPOSSESSION_NOTICE → NOTICE_PERIOD_ELAPSED → ASSIGNED → REPOSSESSED → YARD_INTAKE → PRE_SALE_NOTICE (final chance) → REDEEMED | VALUED → SALE → FORM_36 → TRANSFER_TO_BUYER → APPROPRIATED → SURPLUS | SHORTFALL → CLOSED`

- **Hard gates:** no assignment until the contractual notice period has elapsed after evidenced delivery; agent carries ID, authorisation letter and notice copy (RBC paras 95–96); no seizure outside 08:00–19:00 [REC: aligned to RBC para 100]; no force, no seizure with occupants inside; police intimation per state practice [VERIFY].
- **Possession memo and inventory:** odometer, condition, contents (personal belongings returned against receipt), geotagged media, signatures of the agent and the person in charge or two witnesses; copy to the borrower the same day; insurance from repossession; storage charges only as disclosed in the KFS.
- **Re-registration:** the financier applies in Form 36 for a fresh certificate, with the registering authority's Form 37 notice to the owner (MV Act s.51(5); CMVR r.61); Form 35 only on closure (*Shahrukh Saleem*, All HC, 4 Jul 2023); then transfer to the buyer [VERIFY: Forms 29/30 sequence and state Vahan practice].
- **GPS and telematics:** only where disclosed in the agreement and consented to; location only; no remote immobilisation unless contract and law allow [VERIFY: whether RBC paras 100S–100T on financed devices reach vehicle immobilisers]; a GPS fix never replaces notice at the recorded address.
- **Sale:** independent valuation (two for commercial vehicles above a threshold [REC]); e-auction (e.g. SAMIL, MSTC) or sealed dealer bids, at least three [REC]; no staff or agency bidders.

### R10.3 Gold and silver

`DEFAULT_OR_MATURITY → REPAYMENT_NOTICE (acknowledgment kept) → [UNTRACEABLE → PUBLIC_NOTICE → 1 MONTH] → ADVERTISED → VALUED → RESERVE_FIXED → AUCTION_1 (physical, same district) → SOLD | FAILED → AUCTION_N → STATEMENT → SURPLUS_REFUNDED | SHORTFALL → CLOSED`

| Rule | Implementation | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| Notice | Adequate notice through available means to the borrower or legal heirs; copy and acknowledgment kept; period set by policy | RBC para 60 |
| Untraceable | Auction only one month after a public notice | RBC para 60 |
| Publicity | At least 2 newspapers: one regional-language, one national daily | RBC para 61 |
| Auctioneer | Trained employee or empanelled auctioneer, with surprise visits and internal audit | RBC para 62 |
| Current value | Actual purity; lower of the 30-day average close and the previous day's close (IBJA or a SEBI-regulated exchange); nearest-purity adjustment; metal value only | CF paras 40–42 |
| Reserve | ≥ 90% of current value; ≥ 85% after two failed auctions | RBC para 63 |
| Venue | First auction physical in the lending branch's district; then adjoining district or online | RBC para 64 |
| Bidders | Tenant and related parties barred | RBC para 65 |
| After auction | Full details to the borrower; surplus within 7 working days of receipt of full proceeds; shortfall per agreement | RBC para 66 |
| Discrepancy | Reconcile to the assay certificate; compensate | RBC paras 50, 68 |
| Release on closure | Same day, maximum 7 working days; ₹5,000 per day of attributable delay | RBC paras 58, 69 |

The reserve calculator stores the feed inputs and refuses an auction below the floor for that attempt; GST on auction sales is configured with tax counsel [VERIFY].

### R10.4 Securities (LAS and LAMF)

- **Monitoring:** daily valuation on T-1 bhavcopy or AMFI NAV, drawdowns frozen if data is over one business day stale [REC]; listed shares held by a tenant with assets ≥ ₹100 crore: 50% LTV at all times, shortfall made good within 7 working days (CF para 106(1)); others on Board haircuts; primary-gold-backed units barred (CF para 35(2)).
- **Margin call:** `MarginCallRaised` with shortfall, options and deadline; cure by payment or top-up (`MarginCallCured`); Udofin may present and capture a top-up (UR1).
- **Pre-invocation notice:** reasonable notice to the pledgor under the pledgee's undertaking in the pledge form required by the SEBI circular of 5 Feb 2026 (implementation by 6 Apr 2026) and ICA ss.176–177; the notice log is a hard gate.
- **Invocation:** the pledgee's DP instructs; the depository notifies both sides and records the pledgee as beneficial owner (D&P Regulations 2018 reg 79(8)); locked-in securities cannot be invoked; SOA MF liens are invoked through the RTA or MF Central, redeeming to the tenant [VERIFY: operating guideline and contracting route].
- **Sale:** Board disposal policy (market, VWAP over a period, block deal) with SEBI SAST and PIT checks; `CollateralInvoked`; surplus refunded; shortfall to R5 or R8.

### R10.5 Loan against fixed deposit

Lien marked at origination with every joint holder's consent; on default, a set-off notice with full particulars of remaining claims and retention conditions (RBC para 17); premature closure only where the agreement allows; a third-party bank deposit is invoked through the lien letter; net proceeds appropriated and surplus refunded; set-off against a corporate debtor under moratorium held for counsel [VERIFY].

### R10.6 Book debts, receivables and TReDS

- **Book debts:** identify account debtors (GST data, ledgers, M5); notice to pay the tenant's account; under an assignment, payment to the borrower after notice is at the debtor's risk (TPA ss.130–131) [interpretation: for hypothecation without assignment, enforce through SARFAESI or court].
- **Factoring:** assignment registered with CERSAI under the Factoring Regulation Act 2011; claim against the account debtor.
- **TReDS:** an accepted factoring unit binds the buyer, who pays the financier on the due date and cannot set off disputes; no recourse to the MSME seller; the platform files the assignment with CERSAI (TReDS Directions 2026, RBI/DPSS/2026-27/406, 23 Jun 2026); default → demand on the buyer, platform settlement-failure process, then R5.

### R10.7 IBC liquidation auctions

As a realising secured creditor (s.52) the tenant sells under R4 or R10; otherwise it tracks the liquidator's BAANKNET listings (IBBI mandate for notices from 1 Apr 2025), EMD and s.29A declarations of any bidder it introduces, results and distribution (R6.5).

### R10.8 Valuation, surplus, shortfall and custody

- **Valuers (R11):** registered valuers by asset class (Companies (Registered Valuers and Valuation) Rules 2017 where applicable); conflict declaration per assignment; rotation; market, realisable and distress values; age limits; two valuations above a threshold.
- **Surplus:** identify persons entitled (CERSAI and encumbrance search, subsequent charge-holders, joint owners, heirs); notice; payment only to a verified account; unclaimed surplus stays a liability; SLA 7 working days for gold (RBC para 66), policy default 7 working days elsewhere [REC].
- **Shortfall:** computation statement to the borrower; recovery continues through R5, R7 or R8; limitation recomputed (sale proceeds are not the borrower's acknowledgment [interpretation]).
- **Custody:** yard, vault and warehouse registers with chain of custody, insurance and ageing; exceptions raise `ComplianceIssueRaised`.

**Controls.** Notice gates; field-app (M22) ID and authorisation checks before a repossession can be recorded; geofenced, time-stamped evidence; no related-party or staff bidders; reserve floors; surplus SLAs; dual control over vault and yard releases; R15 conduct rules.

**Data captured.** `repossession` (extended), `vehicle_reregistration`, `custody_location`, `custody_movement`, `gold_auction` (extended with price inputs, attempt, venue), `margin_call`, `pledge_invocation`, `setoff_action`, `account_debtor_notice`, `liquidation_auction_watch`, `valuer_assignment`, `shortfall_statement`.

**Configuration.** Notice periods by product; repossession windows; yards and vaults; valuer panels; auction platforms; gold price feed; securities disposal policy; surplus SLA.

**Events.** `LegalNoticeIssued` (pre-repossession, gold auction, pledge invocation, set-off, account-debtor), `NoticeServiceUpdated`, `AssetRepossessed`, `CollateralValuationUpdated`, `MarginCallRaised`, `MarginCallCured`, `CollateralInvoked`, `AuctionScheduled`, `AuctionConcluded`, `RecoveryReceiptPosted`, `SurplusRefunded`, `CollateralReleased`, `RecoveryCaseClosed`.

**Tests (R10).**
1. Vehicle: 7-day notice delivered 1 Feb 2027 → assignment blocked until 9 Feb 2027; repossession logged at 22:15 → rejected; memo without signatures → cannot reach `REPOSSESSED`.
2. Gold: 30-day average ₹7,000/g and previous close ₹6,900/g for that purity; net weight 50 g → current value ₹3,45,000; reserve ≥ ₹3,10,500; after two failures ≥ ₹2,93,250.
3. Gold: first auction outside the branch district → blocked; related-party bidder → rejected; full proceeds Friday 5 Mar 2027 → surplus due 16 Mar 2027 (no holidays assumed).
4. LAS: shortfall Monday 1 Feb 2027 → cure deadline 10 Feb 2027; invocation without a notice log → blocked.
5. LAFD: joint deposit without the co-holder's lien consent → set-off blocked.
6. Surplus with a subsequent charge on CERSAI → paid to the charge-holder by priority, not the borrower.

## R11. Counsel, agency and vendor management

**Purpose.** Empanel, allocate, pay, score and audit every external party used in recovery, with the RE retaining responsibility for all of them (OUT para 17).

### R11.1 Vendor types and empanelment

| Vendor type | Empanelment requirements |
|---|---|
| Advocates and law firms | Enrolment and practice verification; forum experience; conflict declaration; fee schedule approved; engagement letter |
| Recovery agencies and agents | Due diligence; police verification (RBC para 94; para 100H from 1 Jan 2027); IIBF Debt Recovery Agent certificate (para 100I: from 1 Jan 2027, existing agents within one year); code-of-conduct undertaking (RBC para 99); authorisation letter and ID (paras 95–96); website list (RBC para 97; updated within 7 days, para 100K) |
| Valuers | Approved or registered valuer status for SARFAESI valuations (Rule 8(5)) [VERIFY: current definition of "approved valuer" in the 2002 Rules]; independence declaration; rotation rules |
| Auctioneers and e-auction platforms | For gold: employee or empanelled auctioneer with safeguards (RBC para 62); platform terms, EMD handling, bid-log export |
| Field investigators | FI-only mandate (R2.3); identity and police verification [REC] |
| Print-to-post and dispatch vendors | Data-protection terms; tracking integration |
| ODR and ADR providers (Equator and others) | Published rules and fees; independent appointment engine; per-lender concentration caps; no fees paid through the lender's counsel; no outcome-linked fees (Fifth Schedule items 22 and 24 to the A&C Act; *Shikha Ghosh v. Axis Bank*, Del HC DB, 30 Sep 2026) |
| Repossession yards and custodians | Insurance, inventory and access controls |

- Every vendor sits in the outsourcing register with a materiality assessment (OUT para 36) and a contract with the OUT para 34 clauses, including audit rights (para 34(vii)). Group entities (Equator, Udofin as agent, Infrabyx field apps) also follow OUT paras 45–51 (Board policy, arm's-length SLAs, customer told which entity serves them).
- **Group professional and advocate directory (v1.5):** advocates, law firms, valuers, investigators and other professionals may be sourced from the Infrabyx Operations Hub directory (OH9) through the Integration Specification (`ProfessionalEmpanelled`, `ProfessionalSuspended`, `MatterAllocated`). The directory is a sourcing list only: the tenant still runs its own empanelment, conflict check, engagement letter and fee approval under R11.1–R11.5 and remains responsible (OUT para 17). Directory entries carry only the information Bar Council of India Rules Part VI, Chapter II, Rule 36 permits an advocate to publish (name, address, contact details, enrolment number and State Bar Council, enrolment date, qualifications, areas of practice): no ratings, success rates, "top" labels, fees, testimonials or paid placement. The tenant's R11.4 scorecards stay inside the tenant and never flow back to the Hub. ADR neutrals are appointed only by the ODR institution (R8.6), never allocated from the directory. Litigation is opened only after the R1.4 mechanism-selection engine routes a case to it.

### R11.2 Allocation rules

- Rule-based allocation by forum, mechanism, geography, language, product, ticket, capacity, conflict status and performance; round-robin within a tier; champion–challenger for agencies.
- **Eligibility gate before every allocation:** certificate current, police verification current, authorisation letter valid, website listing live, no open conduct incident above a severity threshold, capacity available.
- Allocation to an agency triggers the borrower intimation (R3) before first contact; recall or change triggers immediate intimation (paras 100M–100N from 1 Jan 2027; RBC para 95 now).

### R11.3 Fees, invoices and taxes

- Fee schedules by vendor, forum and stage; success-linked agency fees only within policy (incentives must not induce harsh conduct, para 100Q from 1 Jan 2027).
- **GST reverse charge** (Notification 13/2017-Central Tax (Rate)): Sl.2 advocates; Sl.3 arbitral tribunal; Sl.8 recovery agent to a bank, FI or NBFC [VERIFY: ITC treatment under the tenant's s.17(4) option].
- **TDS** under Income-tax Act 2025 s.393(1), which replaced s.194J from 1 Apr 2026 (10% professional, 2% technical, threshold ₹50,000) [VERIFY: against the official text].
- Agency fees paid by the RE, never netted from borrower receipts (CF para 10(5)). Invoices: match to schedule and stage → maker-checker → R12 posting with matter and loan tags → payment.

### R11.4 Performance scorecards

- **Counsel:** hearings attended, adjournments sought, time to disposal by forum, success rate, recovery per ₹ of fee, timeliness of updates.
- **Agencies:** resolution %, ₹ collected to ₹ allocated, PTP-kept %, roll-back %, complaints per 1,000 accounts, out-of-window attempts (target zero), recording coverage %, script QA score, unauthorised third-party contacts, certificate currency.
- **Valuers and auctioneers:** valuation variance to realised price, turnaround, failed-auction rate.
- **ODR providers:** turnaround by stage, set-aside rate, enforcement yield, neutral-workload concentration.

### R11.5 Conflicts

- Conflict check at empanelment and at each allocation: counsel acting for the borrower or a related party; valuer related to the borrower or bidder; auctioneer related to the lender (RBC para 65 bars the NBFC and its related parties from bidding in gold auctions); neutral appointed by the same party twice in 3 years (Fifth Schedule item 22).

### R11.6 Audits

- Audits by internal or external auditors, or pooled audits of common providers (OUT paras 37, 76–78); annual review of each provider's condition (OUT para 38); agency audits and penalties (paras 100E–100F from 1 Jan 2027); findings tracked to closure; repeated breaches suspend the vendor.
- Exit: plan and data return or destruction (OUT paras 43–44); borrowers told immediately of agency termination; website updated within 7 days.

**Data captured.** Vendor master, certificates and expiries, verifications, contracts and clauses, allocations, fee schedules, invoices with RCM and TDS, scorecards, conflict checks, audits and findings.

**Controls.** Allocation blocked on any failed eligibility check; invoices blocked without matter and stage; no payment to an ODR provider routed through counsel; expiring certificates alert at 60 and 30 days and block on expiry.

**Configuration.** Vendor categories, empanelment checklists, fee schedules, scorecard weights, allocation rules, audit frequency.

**Events.** Emitted: `ConnectorCertified` (for provider connectors), `EvidenceSubmitted` (audit evidence to GRC). Consumed: `CollectionActivityLogged`, `FieldVisitLogged`, `GrievanceRaised` (complaints naming an agent).

**Tests (R11).** Allocation to an agent without an IIBF certificate is warned before 1 Jan 2027, blocked from 1 Jan 2027 for agents engaged on or after that date, and blocked from 1 Jan 2028 for agents engaged earlier; an advocate invoice of ₹1,00,000 posts RCM GST and TDS correctly; terminating an agency queues borrower intimations for all its live allocations; an ODR fee payment to a law firm account is rejected.
