## R12. Recovery accounting and finance

**Purpose.** Post every recovery event in Finbyx's own ledger (M10) correctly under Ind AS 109 and the IRACP floor, keep written-off dues alive in sub-ledgers, keep money that is not the borrower's repayment (DLG, CGTMSE, partner shares, trust collections) off the loan, and export and reconcile daily.

**Capabilities:** appropriation engine; posting rules; memo legal-claim, recoverable-cost, technical write-off (TWO) and post-write-off ledgers; DLG, CGTMSE, co-lending, servicer-trust and ARC postings; provisioning hooks; exports; reconciliations.

### R12.1 Principles and appropriation

- Finbyx is the book of record; external systems receive exports only (M10). Postings come from events through versioned rules; manual journals need maker-checker and a reason code; every line carries `{loan_id, lender_share, recovery_case_id, matter_id, mechanism, channel, product, branch}`.
- Ind AS 109 and IRACP run in parallel; any shortfall of the allowance against IRACP goes to the impairment reserve (IRACP paras 34–36).
- Borrower cash is posted the same day (CF para 10(5)); rows 15–18 and 24 are not borrower repayments.

| Context | Default appropriation | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| Standard account | Costs → charges → penal charges → interest → principal [REC] | Contract prevails; else ICA ss.59–61 |
| NPA account | Principal-first or interest-first, chosen per product and applied uniformly [REC] | Income only on realisation (IRACP para 38) |
| SARFAESI proceeds | Costs, charges, expenses → dues → residue to persons entitled | SARFAESI s.13(7) |
| Gold auction proceeds | Per agreement (no RBI order) | RBC para 66 |
| Co-lending escrow | CLA clause, then each lender's own policy | TDCR para 117 |
| Settlement and IBC receipts | Settlement letter; plan or s.53 statement | RSA paras 86–100; IBC ss.30, 53 |
| Acquired stressed loans | Acquisition cost first | TDCR para 76 |

### R12.2 Posting rules

| # | Event | Debit | Credit | Sub-ledger | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Account becomes NPA | Interest income (unrealised) | Interest and charges receivable | Loan; interest suspense | IRACP para 38; Ind AS stage 3 interest on net carrying amount (Ind AS 109 para 5.4.1(b)) |
| 2 | Contractual interest on an NPA | Memo | Memo | Legal-claim | Feeds notices, claims, decrees |
| 3 | Borrower receipt on an NPA | Bank | Loan components per R12.1 | Loan | Interest and charges are income on realisation |
| 4 | Counsel bill | Legal expense; RCM GST input | Vendor (net); TDS payable; RCM GST payable | Matter; vendor | RCM Notif. 13/2017-CT(Rate) Sl.2; TDS Income-tax Act 2025 s.393(1) Table Sl.6(iii).D(b), formerly s.194J (R11.3) [VERIFY: official text] |
| 5 | Recovery-agent fee | Collection expense; RCM GST input | Agency (net); TDS; RCM GST | Agency | RCM Sl.8; never netted from borrower receipts (CF para 10(5)) |
| 6 | Tribunal or institution fee | Legal expense; RCM GST input | Provider; RCM GST | ADR case | RCM Sl.3 [VERIFY: institution versus tribunal invoicing] |
| 7 | Recoverable cost, standard account | Loan charges receivable | Recoverable-cost clearing | Loan | Only if agreement and KFS provide (RBC para 29(4)–(5)); never penal (RBC para 30) |
| 8 | Recoverable cost, NPA | — | — | Shadow cost | No income until realised (IRACP para 38) |
| 9 | Costs recovered | Bank | Recovery of legal expenses | Shadow cost | On realisation |
| 10 | Bidder EMD | Bank | EMD payable | Auction | Forfeited deposit credited to the loan [interpretation: Rule 9(5); auditor sign-off] |
| 11 | Sale proceeds | Bank | Sale-proceeds suspense | Case | Cleared by row 12 |
| 12 | Clearing of proceeds | Sale-proceeds suspense | Costs recovered; loan; surplus payable | Loan; surplus | s.13(7); surplus after the CERSAI check |
| 13 | Surplus paid | Surplus payable | Bank | Surplus | Unclaimed surplus stays a liability |
| 14 | Shortfall | — | — | Loan | Stays open; R5 or R8; limitation recomputed |
| 15 | DLG invocation receipt | Bank (or cash, FD or BG appropriated) | DLG received | DLG | Not credited to the loan (CF para 25(2)); never reinstated (para 25(4)); ECL recomputed (IRACP para 36C) [VERIFY: Ind AS presentation] |
| 16 | Recovery after DLG invocation | Bank | Loan; DLG provider payable | Loan; DLG | Sharing per contract (CF para 25(3)) |
| 17 | Co-lending escrow receipt | Escrow bank | Own-share loan; partner payable | Per-lender account | TDCR paras 116–117 |
| 18 | Servicer collections on transferred or securitised loans | Bank (trust) | Collections held in trust | Servicer | Remit after receipt; no commingling (TDCR para 30; SEC para 95) |
| 19 | Settlement completed | Bank; ECL allowance for the waiver | Loan (gross) | Settlement | Waiver posted on completion only; contingent claims off balance sheet (RSA para 88) |
| 20 | Technical write-off | ECL allowance | Loan (gross) | TWO (full dues by component) | Ind AS 109 para 5.4.4; no waiver (RSA para 91); partial TWO on original exposure (para 92) |
| 21 | Recovery after write-off | Bank | Bad debts recovered (P&L); DLG or CGTMSE payable | TWO; post-write-off | RSA para 94(4) reporting |
| 22 | Transfer to an ARC | Bank; investment in SRs; provision utilised | Loan (gross) | ARC transfer | Below NBV: shortfall to P&L (TDCR para 80); above NBV: reversal only as cash exceeds NBV (para 81) |
| 23 | SR revaluation | Investment provision | Investment in SRs | SR | Lower of NAV value and NBV (para 82); over-10% cap (para 83); ₹1 after GoI guarantee (para 84(3)); loss at end of resolution period (para 85) |
| 24 | CGTMSE claim receipt | Bank | CGTMSE claim received | CGTMSE | [VERIFY: presentation]; later recoveries remitted (row 21) |
| 25 | IBC plan or liquidation receipt | Bank; instruments | Loan | IBC claim | RSA paras 139–156; residue to row 20 or write-off [VERIFY: deferred consideration] |
| 26 | Interim compensation (NI Act s.143A) | Bank | Compensation refundable | Matter | Refundable on acquittal (s.143A(4)); applied to dues on conviction or compounding [interpretation] |

Rows 3, 9, 12, 16, 17, 19, 21 and 25 emit `RecoveryReceiptPosted` and refresh the dues view used by notices, settlements and claims.

### R12.3 Taxes, provisioning and exports

- **Taxes:** reverse-charge GST and TDS on counsel, agency and tribunal fees per R11.3; GST valuation of goods repossessed from unregistered borrowers (CGST Rules r.32(5)) and gold-auction GST [VERIFY]; TDS by purchasers of immovable property under the Income-tax Act 2025 [VERIFY: section]; stamp duty on sale certificates borne by purchasers.
- **Provisioning (M10):** any event changing expected recovery (possession, valuation, sale, settlement approval, IBC plan, DLG invocation, ARC sale) requests an ECL re-estimate; IRACP class and ageing stay COB-driven (IRACP paras 19, 21–27); settlements over 3 months and part settlements are tagged restructuring (RSA paras 89–90) and classified under RSA paras 53–55; DLG reflected in ECL only where integral, recomputed after invocation (IRACP paras 36A–36C).
- **Exports (R14.4):** Tally Prime vouchers by XML over HTTP (port 9000) or JSON through the local connector; SAP S/4HANA OData journal entries, BAPI or IDoc where required [VERIFY: customer landscape]; Zoho Books; CSV, XLSX, JSON, XML, PDF/A. Batches are numbered, signed and idempotent.
- **Daily reconciliations:** recovery sub-ledgers to GL; bank and escrow (three-way for co-lending); servicer trust accounts to remittances; surplus ageing; legal expense to R11 invoices; DLG cover, invocations and shares; CGTMSE claims and remittances; TWO sub-ledger to the RSA para 94 report; decree satisfaction to receipts (O.XXI r.2). Breaks open a task at T+1.

**Controls.** Versioned posting rules with approver and effective date; closed periods locked; validator blocks DLG and CGTMSE receipts from loan principal accounts and surplus from income; manual recovery adjustments need Finance and Recovery sign-off.

**Data captured.** `appropriation_policy`, `posting_rule`, `memo_claim_entry`, `recoverable_cost_entry`, `two_ledger_entry`, `post_writeoff_recovery`, `dlg_recovery_share`, `interim_compensation_holding`, `export_batch`; v1.3 `journal`, `posting`, `reconciliation_run/break` reused.

**Configuration.** Appropriation policies; CoA mapping; tax rules; export targets and mappings; reconciliation tolerances.

**Events.** Consumes `AuctionConcluded`, `SettlementApproved`, `ADROutcomeComplianceUpdated`, `CollateralInvoked`, `LoanTransferred`, `CoLendingSplitConfirmed`, Part 5.2 `DLGInvocationSettled`; emits `RecoveryReceiptPosted`, `DLGRecoveryShared` (row 16, CF para 25(3)), `ReconciliationBreakRaised` (daily reconciliation breaks), `ControlTestResultPublished` (reconciliation results, R15.8).

**Tests (R12).**
1. Every rule produces a balanced journal (property test over random event sequences).
2. DLG receipt ₹50,000 on dues of ₹2,00,000 → borrower dues stay ₹2,00,000; cover reduced; no reinstatement on later recovery.
3. TWO of ₹5,00,000 → GL loan nil, TWO sub-ledger ₹5,00,000 plus memo interest; recovery of ₹1,00,000 → P&L and TWO reduced.
4. Settlement of ₹6,00,000 on dues of ₹10,00,000 → ₹4,00,000 waiver posted only on the final receipt.
5. ₹10,000 escrow receipt under an 80:20 CLA → ₹8,000 partner payable, ₹2,000 own loan.
6. ARC sale of an NBV ₹55 lakh loan for ₹40 lakh cash plus SRs → shortfall to P&L per paras 80–82 after SR valuation.
7. An export batch sent twice to Tally → one set of vouchers.

## R13. Shared-exposure recovery (co-lending, transferred and securitised loans, ARC sale, consortium/ICA)

**Purpose.** Recover loans in which several regulated lenders, investors or ARCs have an interest, so that each acts only within its rights, money reaches the right account, classification and reporting stay consistent, and each party gets the data it needs.

**Capabilities:** shared-exposure registry; CLA recovery matrix; escrow and trust validators; classification-sync monitor; per-share approvals; s.13(9) and ICA vote engines; servicer reporting; stressed-loan and ARC sale workflows; party feeds.

### R13.1 Registry

One record per arrangement: type (CLA, assignment, novation, participation, securitisation, ARC transfer, ARC as recovery agent, consortium, multiple banking); parties and shares; lender of record; servicer; security trustee; agreement version and `cla_regime` (TDCR paras 2 and 96 define "existing CLAs" by different dates [VERIFY: legal view for CLAs signed 6 Aug–28 Nov 2025]); recovery matrix; information SLA; escrow or trust account; DLG arrangement. R1.4 reads it before offering any mechanism.

### R13.2 Co-lending (TDCR Part B)

| Rule | Implementation | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| CLA allocates servicing and recovery to the REs or their agents | Recovery matrix per CLA | TDCR para 104 and Explanation |
| Single point of interface in the loan agreement; change only after prior intimation; CLA details in the KFS | Interface field and change workflow; KFS Part 2 item 5 check | TDCR paras 105–106 |
| All flows through one bank escrow controlled only by the co-lenders; appropriation per agreement | Validator rejects any LSP signatory; R12 row 17 | TDCR para 117; CF para 10(1) Note |
| Separate borrower account per lender | Dual sub-accounts | TDCR para 116 |
| Borrower-level SMA/NPA applied by the other lender; shared near-real time, latest by end of next working day | `ClassificationSynced` with as-of date; breach → `ComplianceIssueRaised` | TDCR para 124; IRACP para 23 |
| Each lender reports its own share to CICs | Per-share CIC file | TDCR para 122 |
| DLG only from the originating NBFC, ≤ 5% of loans outstanding under the CLA | Separate CLA DLG ledger, not the CF para 24 ledger | TDCR paras 111, 123 |
| Onward or inter-se transfer only under Part A with mutual consent | Transfer gate | TDCR para 125 |
| Service continues if the CLA ends | BCP runbook | TDCR para 119 |

| Action | Decides | Executes | Gate |
|---|---|---|---|
| Reminders, calls, visits | Servicer RE | Servicer or its appointed agent or LSP | RBC paras 95–100; CF para 9(6) |
| Settlement | Each RE for its own share, own Board policy | Servicer issues one joint offer | RSA paras 16(5), 89, 100 |
| SARFAESI on shared security | Secured creditors ≥ 60% by value | Designated RE's Authorised Officer | s.13(9) [interpretation: applicability to CLAs] |
| Suit, s.138, arbitration | Each lender of record for its share, or jointly | Panel counsel | Consent decree where pending (RSA para 100) |
| Sale of the loan | Mutual consent | Part A process | TDCR para 125 |
| DLG invocation | Partner RE | — | Within 120 days overdue; 5% CLA cap (CF para 27; TDCR para 123) |

[interpretation] Classification sync also reaches each RE's other exposures to the same borrower (IRACP para 23); confirm with counsel.

### R13.3 Transferred and securitised loans

- **Own-share recovery:** each party may resolve or recover its own economic interest without the other's consent (TDCR para 19(2)); security held in trust needs a documented, binding invocation mechanism, which R4 and R10 read first (para 21).
- **Servicer:** written arm's-length agreement; no fee deferral or waiver; limited duration; replaceable by the transferee; no remittance before collection; collections in trust (TDCR para 30); certified MIS and audit access (paras 41–42); no change of terms without a restructuring test (paras 14, 23).
- **Participation:** the transferor stays lender of record and runs recovery [interpretation]. **Assignment or novation:** borrower notice and new payment instructions (TPA ss.130–131); `LoanTransferred`, `ServicerChanged`. Reps and warranties: replacement within 30 days, each replacement or damages payment notified to RBI DoS (paras 24, 52(4)).
- **Securitisation:** the servicer bears no loss beyond its own default, negligence or fraud, remits only after receipt, holds collections in trust without commingling and remits all cash flows, failing which it is treated as a liquidity facility (SEC paras 95–96); facility providers, servicers included, must be regulated by at least one financial-sector regulator (SEC para 80), so an unregulated Infrabyx entity may act only as a technology sub-contractor [interpretation]; material risk change notified within 14 days (para 22); replacement provisions (para 70); third-party servicer data certified by auditors, preferably annually (para 109); Annex I MHP/MRR disclosure (paras 112–113). Recovery on securitised NPAs runs under the servicing agreement, with proceeds to the SPE trust account.

### R13.4 Stressed-loan transfers and ARC sale (TDCR Part A Ch. IV)

`BOARD_REVIEW (para 56) → VALUATION (two external at ≥ ₹100 crore, para 57) → FRAUD_AND_WD_CHECKS (FRM para 54; WD para 14) → SALE_ROUTE (e-auction, para 59; bilateral + Swiss challenge, para 60) → BUYER_GATES → TRANSFER → POST_TRANSFER → CLOSED`

| Gate | Rule | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| Mode and buyer | Assignment or novation only; permitted transferee or ARC; not s.29A-disqualified; for fraud accounts not the promoter group | TDCR paras 12(14), 54, 58 |
| Swiss challenge | Mandatory after bilateral negotiation where lenders' aggregate exposure ≥ ₹100 crore, and for any ICA exit of all lenders; Board mark-up; if the winning bid is declined, provide the higher of the challenger discount and the IRACP provision | TDCR paras 60, 89–92 |
| Price | Cash only to non-ARCs; derecognise on full consideration; no contingent price | TDCR paras 65–66 |
| Fraud accounts to ARCs | Reporting, monitoring, complaints and proceedings pass to the ARC; staff accountability stays | TDCR para 78; FRM para 54 |
| After transfer | CIC duty with a credit-institution transferee; cooling period ≥ 12 months; surplus share booked only when realised; SR valuation (R12 row 23); loan-transfer database entry | TDCR paras 61, 68, 79, 82–85, 94 |
| ARC as fee-based recovery agent | Loan stays on books; realisations credited to it | TDCR para 88 |
| Acquired stressed loans | Hold ≥ 6 months; recoveries first reduce acquisition cost | TDCR paras 74, 76 |

Pending matters: substitution applications (R9), IBC claim transfer report (R6.4), CERSAI charge assignment, CIR para 21 website update.

### R13.5 Consortium, multiple banking and ICA

- All specified lenders sign the ICA within the 30-day Review Period (RSA paras 10(13), 31); specified lenders are commercial banks, AIFIs, deposit-taking NBFCs and non-deposit NBFCs with assets ≥ ₹500 crore, excluding HFCs (RSA para 10(15)).
- **Vote engine:** a decision passes with ≥ 75% by value of total outstanding facilities (fund and non-fund) **and** ≥ 60% of signatories by number; it binds all; dissenters receive at least liquidation value (RSA para 32). An NBFC may still start legal proceedings (RSA para 29).
- Additional provisions only where aggregate exposure ≥ ₹1,500 crore: 20% if not implemented within 180 days from the end of the Review Period, + 15% at 365 days from its start (RSA paras 45–48).
- CRILC monthly for exposures ≥ ₹5 crore and weekly default reports (RSA paras 20–21); project-finance credit events to all members (RSA para 107).
- The s.13(9) test (60% by value) is computed separately from the ICA test; every member displays possessed assets (CIR para 21(1)(xi)).

### R13.6 Data shared per party

| Party | Receives from the tenant | Sends to the tenant | SLA |
|---|---|---|---|
| Co-lender | Classification changes, escrow allocations, recovery actions, settlement proposals, legal stage | Its classification changes, approvals, CIC confirmation | Classification by end of next working day (TDCR para 124); daily three-way escrow file |
| Transferee or investor | Collections, remittances, certified MIS, recovery status | Servicer replacement, instructions within its rights | Monthly certified MIS (TDCR para 41) |
| SPE or trustee | Collections, waterfall inputs, trigger status, Annex I data | Payment instructions | Servicing agreement; 14-day material-change notice (SEC para 22) |
| ARC | Loan and legal file, fraud-reporting duties, CERSAI assignment | Surplus-share reports (TDCR para 79), SR NAV | Data room; quarterly NAV |
| Consortium members | Lead-lender notices, votes, s.13(9) consents, possessed-asset data | Votes, consents | Signed records |
| DLG provider | Invocation notices, recovery-share statements | Cover within the fixed set | Part 5.2 DLG events; monthly disclosure (CF para 28) |
| Udofin (as LSP) | Status-level legal stage, settlement status, allocation | Activity, PTPs, settlement requests | UR5, consent-scoped |

**Controls.** Escrow and trust validators; per-share approvals before a joint settlement; signed, immutable vote records; sync breaches raise `ComplianceIssueRaised`; no action outside a party's matrix role; transfer database entry before closure.

**Data captured.** `shared_exposure`, `recovery_matrix_rule`, `share_approval`, `servicer_remittance`, `trust_account`, `ica_vote`, `substitution_task`; v1.3 `cla_*`, `loan_transfer`, `arc_transfer`, `swiss_challenge`, `security_receipt` reused.

**Configuration.** CLA matrices; servicing agreements; vote thresholds (statutory values locked); reporting SLAs; counterpart endpoints.

**Events.** `CoLendingSplitConfirmed`, `ClassificationSynced`, `LoanTransferred`, `ServicerChanged`, `RecoveryStrategyChanged`, `SettlementApproved` (per share), `RecoveryReceiptPosted`, Part 5.2 `DLGInvocationRaised` and `DLGInvocationSettled`, `LitigationCaseUpdated` (substitution), `ComplianceIssueRaised`.

**Tests (R13).**
1. CLA escrow with an LSP signatory → rejected.
2. Partner marks the borrower NPA at COB Wednesday 3 Feb 2027 → originator applies NPA as of 3 Feb by 23:59 Thursday 4 Feb 2027, else a compliance issue opens.
3. CLA DLG of ₹6 crore on ₹100 crore CLA outstanding → rejected (cap ₹5 crore); CF DLG ledger unaffected.
4. ICA shares 50, 20, 15, 10 and 5%: first, second and fourth vote yes → 80% by value and 3 of 5 → passes; first two only → fails.
5. Shared security 65% bank, 25% NBFC, 10% NBFC → the 25% NBFC alone cannot act under s.13(4); bank plus the 10% NBFC can.
6. Bilateral sale with ₹120 crore aggregate exposure → Swiss challenge mandatory; ₹80 crore → policy; ICA exit of ₹40 crore → mandatory.
7. Servicer remittance before collection → blocked; securitisation servicer role given to an unregulated entity → rejected.

## R14. Recovery analytics, registers, reporting and exports

**Purpose.** Produce the registers inspectors and auditors ask for, the KPIs management runs on, the regulatory and Board inputs, and every export format the tenant needs.

### R14.1 Registers (system-maintained; updated on the triggering event; produced on demand)

| Register | Key contents | Corrections to the Udolex templates |
|---|---|---|
| NPA classification and provisioning | Account, product, dues by component, DPD, class, NPA date (immutable), provision, CRILC flag, WD status, mechanism and stage, recoveries, limitation date | Limitation per claim type and article (R1.5), not a flat 3 years from last payment; sub-standard up to 12 months (IRACP) |
| Legal proceedings | Matter, forum, numbers, filing date, counsel, stage, next date, claim, recovery, counter-litigation, deadline watch | Adds ADR and defensive matters |
| Recovery-agent assignment | Account, agency, agent, IIBF reference, authorisation, intimation proof, contact log, recording reference, complaints, outcome | No RBI "3 attempts a week" rule (policy only); recordings at least 6 months or until disposal if sub judice (para 100P) |
| Grievance and complaint (recovery) | Reference, channel, nature, agent named, deadlines, response, outcome | Linked to M15 clocks (IO, RB-IOS 2026) |
| OTS and compromise settlement | Dues, settlement amount, sacrifice, approver level, NPV test, fraud or WD flag, schedule, restructuring flag, consent decree, CIC reporting, cooling-period end | RSA paras 16, 89–100 replace the "June 2023 framework"; 12-month minimum cooling period for every settlement (para 95), not "5 years for WD"; WD name stays on the LWD until full payment (WD para 13) |
| Technical write-off | Original exposure, amount written off, continuing enforcement, recoveries | Claim retained (RSA para 91); quarterly recovery reporting (para 94) |
| CGTMSE claim | Scheme, guarantee cover, NPA date, lock-in end (18 months), legal-action date, claim lodged, first instalment (75% of eligible amount), recoveries remitted | Replaces the "12 months from NPA" deadline [VERIFY: current claim-lodgement deadline and ₹10 crore ceiling] |
| SARFAESI possessed assets (website) | Annex IV columns; possession date on or after 25 Sep 2023; symbolic and physical | Monthly update; removal on sale or full settlement (CIR para 21) |
| Notices outward and proof of service | Per R3.5 | — |
| s.138 and s.25 instruments | Instrument, return memo, notice, service, complaint, stage | — |
| Auction and sale | Asset, valuation, reserve, notices, bids, deposits, confirmation, certificate, surplus or shortfall | Rule 9 deposit and balance deadlines |
| Surplus refund | Surplus amount, entitled persons, CERSAI check, paid date | Gold surplus within 7 working days (RBC para 66) |
| Wilful defaulter and large defaulter | Cases, committees, notices, orders, Annex I and II submissions | WD paras 5–6, 11–12 |
| Fraud | Dates of occurrence, detection and classification; SCN; FMR; LEA report; debarment clock | FRM paras 4, 6, 35, 40, 43 |
| ADR | Referral basis (clause or consent), provider, neutral, stages, outcome, compliance | — |
| Legal hold | Scope, reason, owner, release | — |
| DLG recovery share | Invocation, post-invocation recoveries, shares | Never credited to the loan (CF para 25(2)) |

### R14.2 KPIs (definitions fixed; targets set by the tenant — Udolex targets are indicative only)

| KPI | Formula |
|---|---|
| Roll rate | Accounts moving to the next bucket ÷ accounts in the bucket at period start |
| Cure rate | Accounts returning to 0 DPD ÷ accounts in the bucket |
| NPA slippage | New NPAs ÷ standard book at period start |
| Recovery rate | Amount recovered ÷ outstanding at case opening, by mechanism, product, vintage and bucket |
| Cost to recover | Total recovery cost (legal, agency, valuation, publication, internal allocation) ÷ amount recovered |
| Time to recover | Days from case opening (or NPA) to resolution, by mechanism and forum |
| Case ageing | Open cases by days since opening and since last action |
| PTP kept rate | PTPs honoured ÷ PTPs taken |
| Right-party contact rate | Contacts reaching the borrower ÷ attempts |
| Legal success rate | Favourable outcomes ÷ disposed matters, by forum |
| ADR outcome rates | Settled, awarded, set aside, enforced |
| Conduct KPIs | Out-of-window attempts, complaints per 1,000 accounts, recording coverage, agent certificate currency |

### R14.3 Board, RBI and CIC inputs

- Quarterly settlement and write-off report with the RSA para 94 splits, including recovery on written-off accounts (RSA paras 93–94).
- CRILC monthly for exposures ≥ ₹5 crore and the Friday weekly default report (RSA paras 20–21); WD Annex I and II monthly to all CICs by SFTP (WD paras 11–12); FMR (FRM para 43).
- CIC status: suit-filed, settled (only for waivers for financial inability, with reason and amount) and disputed (CIR paras 12(2), 12(4), 12(7)).
- Board and RMC packs: proceedings tracker, settlement register, agency conduct, contingent liabilities, limitation-risk list.

### R14.4 Exports and report designer

- **Formats:** CSV (RFC 4180), XLSX, JSON (schema-versioned), XML, PDF and PDF/A-2b; Tally Prime XML over HTTP (port 9000) through the local connector agent; SAP S/4HANA (OData Journal Entry APIs; BAPI or IDoc where required) [VERIFY: per customer landscape]; REST API and webhooks; scheduled SFTP extracts with checksums; court e-filing bundles.
- Every export carries a logged manifest (filter, as-of date, row count, SHA-256, requester) and a masking profile by recipient type.
- **Report designer** over the governed semantic layer (M17) with row-level security, schedules and Board-pack templates.

**Controls.** Registers derived from source records, never hand-edited; manual corrections only through the source record with maker-checker; regulatory files validated against schemas before submission.

**Configuration.** Register columns (add only), KPI targets, segment dimensions, export schedules and recipients, masking profiles.

**Events.** Emitted: `ReturnStatusUpdated`, `EvidenceSubmitted`. Consumed: all recovery, litigation, ADR and settlement events.

**Tests (R14).** NPA date cannot change after first setting without a classification-correction workflow; a settlement paid over four months shows the restructuring flag in the OTS register; a possessed asset sold is removed from the next monthly website file; a Tally export of recovery postings imports with STATUS 1 in a test instance; a PDF/A export validates as PDF/A-2b.

## R15. Conduct, compliance and evidence controls

**Purpose.** Make every recovery action lawful by design, prove it with evidence, and feed LawDocsComply or any third-party GRC tool automatically.

### R15.1 Contact-policy engine

- `canContact(account, party, channel, purpose, timestamp)` runs before every outbound attempt by staff, diallers, voicebots, field app, agencies and Udofin; every evaluation is logged, denials included; missing inputs fail closed.
- Rules (effective-dated packs, R2.6): party of record only (third parties only for `LOCATE`); contact window; sensitive-occasion blackouts; Board-policy frequency caps; stop on valid payment, PTP not yet due, same-subject dispute or grievance, stay or moratorium; agent eligibility (R11.2); no anonymous numbers; pre-approved content with sender and grievance-officer details; vernacular (RBC para 10); prohibited-phrase lint (arrest, police, public exposure, false consequences; para 100Z from 1 Jan 2027); channel consent and DND (TRAI TCCCPR; para 100AB).

### R15.2 Call recording and retention

- Record all recovery calls (outbound, and inbound to numbers the NBFC provided) with disclosure; log time and count (para 100P from 1 Jan 2027; recommended now).
- Retain at least 6 months, or until disposal where sub judice (hold set automatically when a linked matter or complaint is open); QA sampling with human review of adverse AI scores.

### R15.3 AI and voicebots

- Disclose at the start that the caller is an automated assistant for the lender (and LSP, if any), with grievance details; "talk to a human" at any turn [REC; FREE-AI Committee report, 13 Aug 2025].
- Offers only within the R8 pre-approved band; no threats; no mention of criminal action except an accurate s.138 description where a cheque was dishonoured; payment only into the RE's account.

### R15.4 Grievance linkage

- Every recovery-conduct complaint (direct, RB-IOS 2026, CMS, CPGRAMS, consumer commission, social media) links to the case, agent and contact attempts; same-subject contact pauses per policy; the evidence pack is auto-assembled.
- Internal Ombudsman and RB-IOS handling per M15; disputes heard at the next higher level (RBC para 7(2)); compensation for non-compliant recovery (paras 100E–100F from 1 Jan 2027).

### R15.5 DPDP and data controls

- Purpose tags on recovery data (servicing, recovery, legal claim, locate) with the legal basis recorded where consent is not the basis (DPDP Act s.17(1)(a) legal claims; s.17(1)(f) defaulter financial information). `ConsentWithdrawn` stops consent-based processing (marketing, AA monitoring) but not legal-basis processing, and the borrower is told why.
- `DataPrincipalRequest` answered within M15 and DPDP clocks, excluding records under retention or hold; breaches via `SecurityIncidentNotified`; minimum data to agents (para 100O); India-only storage.

### R15.6 Wilful-defaulter, fraud and settlement tracks

Full rules are in Part 8A.20 (WD), 8A.14 (FRM) and 8A.18 (RSA); R15 runs them as case state machines with these hard clocks and gates:

- **WD:** screen NPAs ≥ ₹25 lakh; classify within 6 months of NPA (WD para 6); show-cause reply 21 days, representation 15 days, hearing without a lawyer, reasoned order naming committee members (para 5); committee-composition validator; guarantor refusal routed here (para 10); pre-transfer gate (para 14); penal clocks (para 7(3)); monthly Annex I and II files (paras 11–12).
- **Fraud:** three dates captured (FRM para 4); show-cause reply at least 21 days and a reasoned order (para 6; *SBI v. Rajesh Agarwal*, SC 2023); FMR within 14 days of classification (para 43); law-enforcement report mandatory at ₹1 lakh or more (para 40); no sale to lenders or ARCs before the investigation ends (para 54); 5-year debarment from full repayment or settlement (para 35).
- **Settlement guard-rails (executed in R8):** approver one level above the sanctioner, sanctioners excluded; Board approval for fraud and WD (RSA para 16(5)); over 3 months or part settlement is restructuring (paras 89–90); consent decree where proceedings are pending (para 100); cooling period at least 12 months (para 95); applies to NBFCs below ₹500 crore too (para 157).

### R15.7 Evidence packs and audit trail

- One-click evidence packs: s.14 affidavit annexures (notice, service, non-payment, CERSAI, NPA), s.17 defence bundle, s.138 complaint bundle (instrument, return memo, notice, service, BSA 2023 s.63 certificate for electronic records), RB-IOS response, ADR referral pack, auditor and RBI inspection packs.
- Hash-chained audit trail (M19) covering who, what, when, where and before and after values for every recovery action, configuration change and override.

### R15.8 LawDocsComply and third-party GRC feeds

- Through the Specification's GRC connector (LawDocsComply, MetricStream, IBM OpenPages, ServiceNow IRM, Archer; OSCAL export where mapped), Finbyx consumes `ObligationPublished` (paragraph-referenced obligations, e.g. `RBI/2026-27/230#100P`) and emits `ControlTestResultPublished` (contact-window compliance, recording coverage, IIBF currency, WD six-month deadline, FMR and s.13(3A) timeliness), `EvidenceSubmitted` (hashed evidence with aggregate counts and masked sample IDs, never raw PII), `ComplianceIssueRaised`, `ReturnStatusUpdated` (WD files, FMR, CRILC) and `PolicyAttested`.
- Switch, not rebuild: the same events feed the embedded compliance module (M14) when LawDocsComply is not used.

### R15.9 Regulatory change management

- Each rule pack has an owner, sources, status and effective dates; scheduled cut-overs (Third Amendment on 1 Jan 2027) run as dated releases with regression tests.
- Watch-list with review dates: RBI response in *Shikha Ghosh* (after 17 Nov 2026); Mediation Act notification of ss.4–25, 27–30 and 39–44 (s.26 is in force); IBC CIIRP, group and cross-border commencement; DPDP Rules phasing (Rule 4 from 13 Nov 2026; Rules 3 and 5–16 from 13 May 2027); state anti-coercion laws; CGTMSE circulars; RBI CIMS return changes.
- Every regulatory change produces an impact list (rules, templates, registers, tests) and a CCO sign-off before activation.

**Data captured.** Contact-policy evaluations, recordings and QA scores, AI transcripts, complaint links, purpose and basis tags, WD and fraud case records, settlement policy checks, evidence packs, GRC event log, rule-pack versions and sign-offs.

**Controls.** Fail-closed contact policy; guard-rail validation on configuration; maker-checker for rule-pack activation; automated control tests with exceptions raised as `ComplianceIssueRaised`.

**Configuration.** Frequency caps, blackout calendars, prohibited-phrase lists (add only), QA sampling rates, retention above the minimum, GRC destination and mappings.

**Events.** Emitted: `ControlTestResultPublished`, `EvidenceSubmitted`, `ComplianceIssueRaised`, `ReturnStatusUpdated`, `PolicyAttested`. Consumed: `ObligationPublished`, `ConsentWithdrawn`, `DataPrincipalRequest`, `SecurityIncidentNotified`, `GrievanceRaised`, `GrievanceEscalated`, `SettlementRequested`.

**Tests (R15).**
- A call scheduled at 18:30 for a microfinance borrower on 15 Dec 2026 is denied; the same call on 15 Jan 2027 follows the post-amendment pack.
- An agent without a valid authorisation letter is denied contact.
- A recording linked to an open RB-IOS complaint survives the 6-month purge.
- A WD case without an order at NPA + 6 months raises `ComplianceIssueRaised`.
- A fraud classification on day 0 without FMR by day 14 raises an issue.
- `ConsentWithdrawn` for marketing does not stop a s.13(2) notice.
- The contact-window control test publishes `ControlTestResultPublished` with population, exceptions and an evidence hash.

## R16. Product recovery playbooks

**Purpose.** Give every Part 6 product a default, tenant-configurable recovery playbook that sequences mechanisms lawfully for its security, borrower type and conduct rules, so that R1 can propose a strategy and R2–R13 can execute it.

**Model.** `playbook` (product, version, effective dates, approval) → ordered steps (trigger by DPD or event, action, mechanism, R3 template, owner, SLA, gates) → permitted mechanisms (re-evaluated per account by R1.4) → asset handling → ADR suitability → accounting notes → conduct pack (contact windows, visit rules, state overlays). Tenants may tighten statutory parameters but not loosen them; a lint rejects any version that breaks a floor; champion–challenger variants run only after the R1 compliance check.

| Family (Part 6 #) | Default sequence | Mechanisms | Key rules and timelines | Assets | ADR fit | Accounting |

| MSME and business (3), CGTMSE | SMA monitoring → resolution test (RSA paras 13–15) → recall → SARFAESI if secured and eligible → book-debt notices → guarantors → IBC s.7 or PPIRP for corporates → CGTMSE claim | All, incl. IBC for corporate debtors | CGTMSE: guarantee live on NPA date; 18-month lock-in; first instalment 75% after legal action, waived ≤ ₹10 lakh [VERIFY: ceilings and lodgement deadline] | Stock, receivables (R10.6); mortgage (R4) | Medium | CGTMSE ledger (R12 rows 21, 24) |
| LAP (4) | Recall → s.13(2) → possession → auction → shortfall suit | SARFAESI if eligible, suit, settlement, IBC for corporates | s.31(i) check; post-notice tenancy void (s.13(13)); documents released in 30 days, ₹5,000/day if late (RBC paras 35, 39 for personal loans; policy for business LAP) | R4 | Settlement high; arbitration low (in-rem) | s.13(7); surplus ledger |

**Playbook notes [REC].** Run the R4 gate at SMA-2 for LAP and home loans so CERSAI, title and agricultural-land defects are fixed before NPA, and offer a settlement before any sale notice on a primary residence; mark the CGTMSE portal by the quarter after NPA; build the IBC readiness pack (R6.2) from SMA-2 for corporates; release timers for gold and property documents run independently of recovery.

**Controls.** Lint against floors (contact windows, notice periods, gold reserve, no SARFAESI for pledges, no DRT for un-notified tenants, Gate A for arbitration, microfinance visit rule); approval of each version; every executed step records the playbook version.

**Data captured.** `recovery_playbook`, `playbook_step`, `playbook_lint_result`.

**Configuration.** Per tenant, product, branch and segment; effective dating; variants; state overlays.

**Events.** `RecoveryCaseOpened` (playbook version), `RecoveryStrategyChanged`, `PolicyAttested`.

**Tests (R16).**
1. Every default playbook passes the lint; a microfinance step calling at 18:30 before 1 Jan 2027 fails.
2. A gold playbook with a SARFAESI step fails; an LAP playbook offering the DRT to an un-notified NBFC fails.
3. A personal-loan arbitration step without Gate A fails.
4. Shortening a vehicle notice period applies only to agreements whose clause permits it.
5. A co-lent settlement step without a partner-approval gate → the R13 overlay inserts it before the step can run.

# PART 7B — REGULATORY RETURNS, SUPERVISORY PORTALS AND CREDIT BUREAU SUBMISSIONS

**Purpose.** Turn Finbyx's ledger, loan, exposure, fraud and KYC data into every return, report and bureau file that the tenant's regulators and the credit information companies (CICs) require, on time, reconciled to the books and with a complete evidence trail. Finbyx prepares, validates, reconciles, packages and evidences. **Authorised humans in the regulated entity (RE) approve and file.** This Part replaces the build content of M13; M13 becomes a pointer to this Part, and its return table, Part 8A.2 (CIR), Part 8A.34 (SR) and Part 8A.36.2 remain the regulatory source rows that the RR1 registry loads.

**Applicability.**

- **Full scope:** NBFCs in every layer and category under the RBI (NBFC – Supervisory Returns) Directions, 2026, RBI/DoS/2026-27/466, DoS.CO.DSG.60/33.01.001/2026-27, **31 July 2026** (SR). The owner's reference to "28 Nov 2025" for this instrument is superseded (that is the date of the DoR prudential set); log it in `docs/regulations/errata.md`.
- **HFCs:** excluded from SR (SR para 3); returns go to NHB [VERIFY: NHB list and portal]; HFCs still report to CICs (CIR para 3).
- **Indicative packs ([VERIFY] row by row):** commercial banks, UCBs, StCBs/DCCBs, ARCs, IFSCA Finance Companies and Finance Units, credit co-operative societies (Registrar returns, not RBI).
- **Never a filer:** Udofin or any LSP. The RE reports DLA loans to CICs (CF para 17) and DLAs on CIMS (CF para 18); Udofin supplies DLA facts (Udofin UP3).

**Direction and requirement codes used.** SR, CIR, CF, RSA, WD, FRM, KYC, ALM, CON, CRM, INV, CYB, MSD, GOV, CMP, SA, AUD, SEC, TDCR, BR, MISC, RBC (existing); `CICRA`, `CIC-AMD`, `CICD`, `CB-SR`, `UCB`, `HFC`, `ARC`, `NABARD`, `IFSCA-FC`, `PMLA`, `SARFAESI`, `ITA25`, `MSCS`, `SCS`, `SRO-MFIN`, `RBIOS26`, `IO26`, `DPDP`, `TRAI`, `CERTIN`, `FEMA` (Part 8A.37). REQ-IDs follow Part 8A.0.1 (`REQ-SR-21`, `REQ-CIR-10(2)`, `REQ-CICRA-21(3)`, `REQ-CIC-AMD-19(1)`).

**Terminology.** "CIC" alone means a credit information company. Core investment companies are written out or coded `CICD` (RBI (Core Investment Companies) Directions, 2025). `CIC-AMD para n` cites the RBI (Credit Information Companies) Directions, 2025 as amended by the Amendment Directions, 2025, RBI/DOR/2025-26/119, DoR.FIN.REC.No.326/20.16.056/2025-26 (the CIC-side rules); the lender-side amendment of CIR is RBI/DOR/2025-26/117, DoR.FIN.REC.No.324/20.16.056/2025-26.

**Data owned.** Return registry, element dictionary, cell maps and lineage, validation rule packs, return runs and packages, acknowledgements, revisions, supervisory query register, portal-user alias register (aliases only, never credentials), bureau format packs, bureau submissions, rejections, DQI, disputes and compensation, CRILC, WD/LD and FMR outputs, revision assessments, and reporting settings (RR9). Source data (GL, loans, borrowers, collateral, exposures, fraud cases) stays owned by M3–M12 and Part 7A; this Part reads it through governed snapshots.

**Events (Integration Specification v1.1, sections 6.15, 6.18 and 6.19).** Emits `ReturnDue`, `ReturnGenerated`, `ReturnValidated`, `ReturnApproved`, `ReturnFiled`, `ReturnRevised`, `ReturnStatusUpdated` (existing), `BureauFileGenerated`, `BureauFileSubmitted`, `BureauRejectionReceived`, `BureauCorrectionRequested`, `BureauCorrectionCompleted`, `ControlTestResultPublished`, `EvidenceSubmitted`, `ComplianceIssueRaised`. Consumes `PeriodClosed` and `FinancialStatementsApproved` (Part 7C), `LoanDisbursed`, `LoanClosed`, `AssetClassificationChanged`, `LoanTransferred`, `GrievanceRaised` (category CREDIT_INFORMATION) and `ObligationPublished`. LawDocsComply (through the M14 GRC connector) or embedded M14 consumes every return and bureau event. Return packages and bureau files travel only by document reference, never inside an event. **The Operations Hub receives only `ReturnDue` and `ReturnFiled`, as status metadata (return code, legal entity, period, due date, status, acknowledgement reference), and only where the tenant opts in** (setting `share_return_status_with_hub`, default off, RR9.1). It never receives amounts, package contents, bureau events or borrower data.

---

## 7B.0 Design principles and filing boundaries

1. **Prepare, never file.** Finbyx generates, validates, reconciles, packages and evidences; an authorised RE user submits on the portal (RBI, NABARD, IFSCA, FIU-IND, CERSAI/CKYCR, income-tax, MCA, GST) and records the acknowledgement.
2. **No credentials, no scripting.** No regulator-portal user IDs, passwords, OTPs, DSC PINs, cookies or tokens are stored or proxied; no RPA or scraping [REC; SR para 19 places user administration with the NBFC]. A portal-user alias register records only who filed.
3. **Machine-to-machine only where documented for the entity class.** CIMS system-to-system collection from an ADF server is documented for banks, **not assumed for NBFCs or UCBs** [VERIFY: Sankalan help documents]; the adapter stays behind a flag until RBI's written confirmation is attached. CIC SFTP is a documented machine channel (RR6).
4. **The Direction prevails over the RBI web list** (RR1.4).
5. **Online only.** Email is a filing only as an RBI-advised contingency, followed by online re-submission (SR para 18).
6. **Versioned data, not code.** Definitions, templates, rule packs and bureau formats are effective-dated, because RBI may add or withdraw returns at any time (SR para 25); every filing stays pinned to the versions it used [REC].
7. **Reconcile and trace.** No approval without TB reconciliation (SR para 14) and cell lineage (SR para 15).
8. **Privacy and residency.** Return and bureau files are PII: stored in India, encrypted, access-logged, retained per AC7, never emailed.

**Filing boundary matrix.**

| Filing | Finbyx does | RE user does | Channel |
|---|---|---|---|
| RBI returns (SR para 21) | Template fill, validation, reconciliation, package, clock, ack capture | Maker uploads, checker submits on CIMS; ack recorded | CIMS upload or web form |
| DNBS10 (SAC) | Auditor data pack, clock | Statutory auditor files with the NBFC-created login (SR 21 item 7) | CIMS |
| Cyber incident | Incident record, 6-hour timer, draft | Files on DAKSH | DAKSH |
| Applications | Pack, checklist, query tracking | Submits and answers on PRAVAAH | PRAVAAH |
| FIU-IND reports | XML via FIU utilities | Principal Officer uploads | FINGate 2.0 |
| CKYCR, CERSAI | Upload files, 10/7/30-day clocks | Authorised user uploads | CKYCR, CERSAI |
| SFT, FATCA/CRS | Form 165/166 data files | Designated director uploads | Income-tax portal |
| CIC files | Build, validate, encrypt, SFTP from a tenant-controlled host, ingest responses | CIC nodal officer approves each cycle | CIC SFTP |

### Acceptance tests

- A static scan and runtime test find no storage field, secret reference or HTTP client configured for any regulator-portal domain (`*.rbi.org.in`, ENSURE, FINGate, CERSAI, income-tax portal); the build fails if one is added.
- The ADF/S2S adapter returns `channel_not_confirmed` unless the tenant's confirmation evidence is attached and a second approver has enabled the flag.
- An email-contingency filing without an RBI-advice attachment cannot be saved; one with it opens an `ONLINE_RESUBMISSION_PENDING` task that stays open until an online acknowledgement is recorded.

## RR1. Return registry and applicability engine

**Purpose.** One data-driven registry of every return, report, certificate and bureau file the tenant must produce, with legal basis, applicability, timing, format, channel and signatory, resolved per legal entity from its regulatory profile.

### RR1.1 Registry model

`regulator` → `portal` → `return_definition` → `return_version` → `return_due_instance` → `return_run`.

- `regulator` (RBI-DoS, RBI-DoR, RBI-FED, NHB, NABARD, FIU-IND, CERSAI, CBDT, IFSCA, MCA, GSTN, CRCS, state Registrar, CIC) and `portal` (CIMS-SANKALAN, DAKSH, PRAVAAH, ENSURE, IFSCA, FINGATE2, CKYCR, CERSAI-CR, IT-REPORTING, CIC-SFTP, EMAIL-CONTINGENCY; URL, channels, help-document URL and fetch date).
- `return_definition`: `code`, `name`, `rbi_return_id`, `legal_basis[]` (e.g. `RBI/DoS/2026-27/466#21.5`), `applicability_rule` (RR1.3), `periodicity`, `reference_date_rule`, `due_rule` (`+15D`, `+21D`, `WED_NEXT_WEEK`, `+5WD_FROM_AUDIT_REPORT_CAP_31DEC`, `+1M_FROM_SA_APPOINTMENT`, `+14D_FROM_CLASSIFICATION`, `IMMEDIATE`, `+6H_FROM_DETECTION`), `holiday_calendar`, flags (`nil_return_required`, `audited`, `solo_or_group`, `contains_pii`, `ad_hoc`), roles (RR3.5), `format_version` (template hash, schema, UCRF version), `channel` (WEB_FORM, TEMPLATE_UPLOAD, XML_UPLOAD, S2S, SFTP, EMAIL_CONTINGENCY, PDF), `record_limit`, `status`, effective dates, `change_log` (source URL, fetch date, approver).
- Any format or rule change creates a new `return_version`; old versions are closed, never edited.

### RR1.3 Applicability engine

**Inputs (entity regulatory profile, M1 and Part 8A.25):** legal form; regulator class; layer and the date and source of layer classification; category flags (`nbfc_mfi`, `core_investment_co`, `p2p`, `spd`, `factor`, `aa`, `mgc`, `nofhc`, `hfc`, `idf`, `ifc`); `deposit_taking`; `public_funds`; `customer_interface`; standalone, last-audited and group asset size; `has_dla`; `has_overseas_investment`; `fraud_frm_applicable`; `listed`; `ifsc_unit`; `cooperative_type`; `cic_member[]` by bureau.

**Rule form.** Each `applicability_rule` is a CEL expression (Common Expression Language, chosen for side-effect-free, typed evaluation [REC]) with a citation. Example:

```text
// REQ-SR-21(4): DNBS04A / DNBS04B
layer == "UL" ||
  (layer == "ML" && !spd) ||
  (layer == "BL" && max(assets_solo, assets_group) >= 1000000000   // ₹100 crore
   && (public_funds || customer_interface)
   && !(nofhc || p2p || aa || mgc))
```

**Evaluation.** The engine runs at onboarding, at each financial-year start, on any profile change and on any registry version change. Inputs are effective-dated: a layer or category change applies from the date in the RBI letter or the SBR test date, and an obligation starts with the first reference date on or after that date. It writes an `applicability_decision` (rule version, inputs hash, result, citation) and creates or cancels `return_due_instance` rows. Removing an obligation never deletes past instances; future ones close with reason `APPLICABILITY_CHANGED`. A per-entity applicability matrix (returns × reasons) is rendered from the decisions for the CCO and auditors.

### RR1.4 Conflict rule: RBI web list versus the Direction

**Rule [REC].** The binding Direction prevails. When the RBI list of returns, a portal help note or an FAQ differs from the Direction, the registry follows the Direction, writes a `registry_variance` (return, field, Direction text and citation, web text and URL, fetch date, decision, approver, review date) and raises a CCO task to seek clarification from RBI DoS where the variance is material. The variance list is shown on the compliance dashboard and in the evidence pack of every affected filing.

**Known variances at v1.5:**

| # | Return | Web list (23 Oct 2026) | Direction | Registry decision |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | DNBS04A/04B | BL "₹500 crore and above (at sole or group level) which are ICCs, MFIs, Factors" | BL ≥ ₹100 crore solely or at group level, with exclusions (SR para 21 item 4) | Follow SR: ₹100 crore |
| 2 | DNBS08/DNBS09 | ₹500 crore read as applying to ICCs, MFIs and Factors | SR para 21 item 5 places the qualifier after "Factors" only; RSA para 20 imposes CRILC on NBFCs within RSA scope | Default ≥ ₹500 crore for all three BL categories, union with the RSA test, tenant toggle (RR8.1) [VERIFY with RBI DoS] |
| 3 | DNBS10, DNBS13 | Lists ARCs as filers | NBFC SR covers NBFCs; ARCs file under the ARC Supervisory Returns Directions | ARC rows sit under the ARC profile (RR1.5) [VERIFY: ARC SR number and table] |
| 4 | FORM-A-SA | "Hard copy / Digital, PDF" | SR para 18 requires online filing unless prescribed; SA para 30 prescribes the form | Generate PDF; channel per SA para 30 and RBI advice [VERIFY] |

Also logged: ALM para 58 still cites the repealed 2024 Filing Directions (read as SR); LEF quarterly under SR versus CON Annex I "Return for the Month" (8A.36.2 decision kept); the superseded "28 Nov 2025" SR reference.

### RR1.5 Indicative inventories for other institution types

Rows below seed the registry with `status = ACTIVE_UNVERIFIED`. A row cannot generate a filing until a named reviewer confirms it against the primary text and sets `verified_at`. Part 7G (IP2–IP6) owns the institution profiles that switch these packs on.

**Commercial banks** (RBI (Commercial Banks – Supervisory Returns) Directions, 2026, RBI/DoS/2026-27/415; 37 returns [VERIFY each row]). Timelines (para 22): weekly by Wednesday of the following week; **fortnightly within 7 days of the 15th**; monthly 15 days; quarterly, half-yearly and yearly 21 days; audited returns 5 working days from signing. Seed rows: Form A (NDTL/CRR, RBI Act s.42) fortnightly; Form VIII (SLR, BR Act s.24) monthly; Form IX (unclaimed, BR Act s.26) annual; BSR-1/BSR-2 quarterly; CPR half-yearly (provisional by end-June/December, audited by end-September); BLR-3/BLR-7 quarterly within 15 days; RFA within 7 days of detection (**banks only; never built for NBFC tenants**); Gold Metal Loans quarterly within 7 days; FMR/FUA/FMR4-RBR; CRILC, LCR, NSFR, LEF, SLS/IRS and RBS data (para 23; [VERIFY each]).

**UCBs** (RBI (Urban Co-operative Banks – Supervisory Returns) Directions, 2026 [VERIFY: number]; RBI list rows 70–83, all CIMS template): Form I (CRR/SLR) monthly; Form B fortnightly (scheduled UCBs); RAL, ROE, RCL, RCP quarterly; RBP yearly; Form IX (assets and liabilities) and Form II (unsecured loans to directors) monthly; PSA quarterly or yearly (not salary earners' banks); Form VIII (unclaimed) yearly; Dir-I, Dir-IV, Planning-3 quarterly; CRILC for UCBs with assets ≥ ₹500 crore and exposures ≥ ₹5 crore [VERIFY: UCB RSA para 12].

**StCBs and DCCBs** (no SR Direction in the 31 Jul 2026 set; RBI list rows 64–69, CIMS template): Form I (SLR) monthly; Form II monthly; Form IX monthly; Form VIII annual as on 31 December; sectoral deposits half-yearly; Form B (StCB CRR) fortnightly. Supervisory returns to NABARD on ENSURE (RR4.4).

**ARCs** (ARC Supervisory Returns Directions, 2026 [VERIFY: number and table]; RBI (Asset Reconstruction Companies) Directions, 2025, DoR.FIN.REC.No.293/26.03.001/2025-26): DNBS07 quarterly on CIMS; DNBS10 and DNBS13 per the RBI list; returns (ARC para 151); audited balance sheet to the Regional Office within 1 month of the AGM (para 152); monthly website possession list (para 154); CERSAI and information-utility filings (paras 158–162) [VERIFY: paragraph numbers]; CIC reporting [VERIFY].

**IFSCA Finance Companies and Finance Units:** reports as IFSCA specifies, **in USD** (IFSCA-FC reg 9) [VERIFY: list, frequency, portal]; FIU-IND reporting [VERIFY]; FEMA/ECB reporting where lending into India [VERIFY].

**Credit co-operative societies** (no RBI returns): MSCS s.120 annual return within 6 months and quarterly CRCS returns (MSCS) [VERIFY]; State Act returns, e.g. Maharashtra s.79(1A) (SCS) [VERIFY per state]; late returns can disqualify directors (MSCS s.43(2)(e)–(f)) [VERIFY]; CIC reporting only as a CIC member (RR6.1).

### Acceptance tests

- Loading the SR table yields exactly 21 return definitions (the 20 items of SR para 21, with item 4 split into DNBS04A and DNBS04B); each resolves its citation to the stored SR paragraph text.
- A BL ICC with solo assets ₹80 crore and group assets ₹120 crore, with public funds, gets DNBS04A and DNBS04B; the same entity with no public funds and no customer interface does not.
- A variance row is required before a registry version differing from the cached RBI list can be activated; the activation log shows the approver.
- Changing an entity from ML to BL closes future DNBS01/DNBS03 instances with `APPLICABILITY_CHANGED`, opens DNBS02 from the next quarter-end, and keeps all past runs readable.
- A UCB pack row with `ACTIVE_UNVERIFIED` cannot reach `GENERATED`.

## RR2. Element-based data dictionary and lineage

**Purpose.** Generate returns from governed data elements, not from report queries, so that every cell is defined once, reconciled to the books and traceable to source records (SR paras 7, 12, 14–17).

### RR2.1 Data elements

- `data_element`: id, label, definition, **RBI harmonised definition reference** where one exists (https://rbi.org.in/scripts/DataDefinition.aspx, updated 17 Jun 2026, with its validation-rules/taxonomy page), unit, sign, scale (₹, ₹ lakh, ₹ crore), rounding, owner (SR para 12), effective dates.
- **Dimensions:** product; BSR sector; state, district, PIN; counterparty type; residency; ALM bucket; IRACP class; Ind AS stage; SMA status; solo or group; currency.
- One element serves many outputs: "gross advances" feeds DNBS01/02, DNBS03, DNBS04B and the notes to accounts (AC3).

### RR2.2 Source mapping to Finbyx

| Element family | Finbyx source | Aggregation |
|---|---|---|
| Balance sheet and P&L lines | GL period balances by chart-of-accounts node (M10) via the Schedule III line map (AC3) | Sum by node set; sign per element |
| Advances, asset classification, provisions | `loan_balance_snapshot`, `classification_history`, `provision_run`, `ecl_run` (M6, M10) | Sum, count, distinct borrower |
| Sectoral and geographic credit | Loan + borrower master (BSR code, district) | Sum by dimension |
| Exposure and concentration | `exposure_snapshot` (M12; fund + non-fund, borrower and group level) | Max, sum, top-N |
| Liquidity and IRS | `liquidity_run`, ALM slotting (M12, Part 8A.7) | Bucket sums |
| Capital | `capital_run` (CAP Part 8A.24; Part 7E RK3) | Ratio components |
| CRILC and defaults | `exposure_snapshot` ≥ ₹5 crore, SMA events | Borrower list |
| Overseas investment | `investment_holding` with residency (M10 item 7A; Part 7H) | Sum; NIL if empty |
| Fraud, RBR, DLA | `fraud_case`, `rbr_report`, `dla_register` | Case or line list |

### RR2.3 Cell maps and snapshots

- `cell_map`: return version → sheet and cell (or XML path, or UCRF field) → element + filter + aggregation (sum, count, max, distinct borrower, top-N) + scale and rounding (templates typically ₹ crore or ₹ lakh to 2 decimals [VERIFY per template]).
- **Snapshot:** each run reads a frozen `reporting_snapshot` (reference date, post-COB, content hash). Later back-dated postings surface as reconciliation items and, if material, a revision (RR5.3).
- **Lineage (SR para 15):** each cell stores element, query hash, snapshot id, row count and a masked drill-down to contributing records.
- **Ad hoc subsets (SR para 13):** governed query service over the exposure and loan marts; canonical test "exposure for a particular period for a specific industry cluster in a district"; outputs use the return package path (`ad_hoc = true`).
- **Data quality (SR para 17):** completeness, validity, consistency and timeliness metrics per element with thresholds, issue register and escalation.
- **Independent validation (SR para 7):** each cell-map version is approved by a reviewer outside the building team.

### Acceptance tests

- Every cell in every active template version maps to an element or is marked `NOT_APPLICABLE_FOR_ENTITY` with a reason; an unmapped cell blocks activation.
- Drill-down from a DNBS02 "gross advances" cell lists loan IDs whose sum equals the cell value before rounding.
- A posting dated before the reference date but booked after the snapshot appears in the reconciliation as a post-snapshot item and does not change the generated file.

## RR3. Return generation, validation and sign-off

**Purpose.** Produce each return as a validated, reconciled, approved and signed package.

### RR3.1 Filing state machine

`SCHEDULED → DATA_FROZEN → GENERATED → VALIDATED → RECONCILED → MAKER_SUBMITTED → CHECKER_APPROVED → SIGNED_OFF → PACKAGED → UPLOADED_BY_HUMAN → ACKNOWLEDGED → CLOSED`

Every transition is a server-side command with an idempotency key `(instance_id, run_no, command)`, writes `ReturnStatusUpdated`, and is refused (409 `invalid_transition`) from any other state. `due_at` comes from the RR5.1 instance; "lead" timers are settings (RR9.1).

| State | Entry condition | Owner | Allowed actions | Timer | Exit, failure and rollback |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `SCHEDULED` | Due instance created (RR5.1) | Return owner (maker) | Assign owner; mark `NOT_APPLICABLE` (CCO approval and reason) | Freeze target = reference date + `freeze_lead` | Freeze → `DATA_FROZEN`; an applicability change → `CANCELLED` (`APPLICABILITY_CHANGED`) |
| `DATA_FROZEN` | COB complete for the reference date; sub-ledger-to-GL breaks zero (RR3.4); for TB-based returns the period is locked or soft-closed per book (Part 7C AC2.8) | Maker | Generate; unfreeze (checker approval and reason; the old snapshot is kept) | Alert if not generated by due − `generate_lead` | Generate → `GENERATED`; unfreeze → `SCHEDULED` |
| `GENERATED` | Template hash matches `format_version`; every cell mapped (RR2.3) | Maker | Run validation; view lineage | — | No ERROR → `VALIDATED`; any ERROR → `REPAIR` |
| `VALIDATED` | No ERROR; WARNINGs listed | Maker | Run reconciliation; comment on each WARNING | — | All variances within tolerance or explained → `RECONCILED`; open break → `REPAIR` |
| `RECONCILED` | Reconciliation hash stored | Maker | Attest and submit | — | → `MAKER_SUBMITTED` |
| `MAKER_SUBMITTED` | Maker attestation | Checker | Accept each WARNING; approve; reject (reason code mandatory) | Checker SLA (default 1 working day) with reminder | Approve → `CHECKER_APPROVED`; reject → `REPAIR` |
| `CHECKER_APPROVED` | SoD check passed (RR3.5) | Authorised signatory | Sign off with step-up authentication; reject | Signatory SLA (default 1 working day) | Sign → `SIGNED_OFF` (`ReturnApproved`); reject → `REPAIR` |
| `SIGNED_OFF` | Signature recorded | System | Build package (RR3.6) | Immediate | → `PACKAGED`; any later input change voids the sign-off and starts run n+1 |
| `PACKAGED` | Package hash stored | Authorised filer | Download package; follow the guided upload checklist (RR4.1) | Alert at due − 1 working day if not uploaded | Upload recorded → `UPLOADED_BY_HUMAN`; portal down and RBI advises email → `CONTINGENCY_EMAIL` |
| `UPLOADED_BY_HUMAN` | Filer alias, time and file hash confirmed | Filer | Record portal validation result; upload acknowledgement | Reminder after 4 working hours without an acknowledgement | Acknowledgement and confirmed reference → `ACKNOWLEDGED` (`ReturnFiled`); portal rejection → `PORTAL_REJECTED` |
| `PORTAL_REJECTED` | Portal message recorded | Maker | Classify: data error or portal-side error | — | Data error → `REPAIR`; portal-side error (same file, no change) → `PACKAGED` with reason |
| `REPAIR` | Rule failure, break, rejection or reject decision | Data owner, then maker | Fix at source (never in the file); regenerate | Escalate to the CCO if repair would breach `due_at` | → `GENERATED` (same run number until `SIGNED_OFF`, a new run after) |
| `CONTINGENCY_EMAIL` | RBI advice attached (SR para 18) | Filer | Record email sent | — | → `ONLINE_RESUBMISSION_PENDING` |
| `ONLINE_RESUBMISSION_PENDING` | Contingency filing recorded | Filer | Upload online when the portal returns | Daily reminder | Online acknowledgement → `ACKNOWLEDGED` |
| `ACKNOWLEDGED` | Acknowledgement document hash and reference stored | System | Evidence completeness check | — | Complete → `CLOSED` |
| `CLOSED` | Evidence pack sealed (RR5.2) | CCO | Request revision (RR5.3) | — | → `REVISION_REQUESTED` → run n+1 from `DATA_FROZEN` |

- **Overdue** is a flag, not a state: when `now > due_at` and the state is before `UPLOADED_BY_HUMAN`, Finbyx raises `ComplianceIssueRaised` and escalates (RR5.1).
- **NIL returns:** an empty population for DNBS08, DNBS09 or DNBS13 generates a NIL return that passes every state with the same approvals.
- **Back-dated postings** after `DATA_FROZEN` never change the run; they appear as post-snapshot reconciliation items and, after `CLOSED`, open a revision assessment (RR5.3).

### RR3.2 Generation

- The filer downloads the period's RBI template and uploads it; Finbyx checks its hash against `format_version`, and a changed hash opens a template-change task (new version, cell-map review).
- Only unprotected input cells are filled; sheet names, protected cells, formulas and hidden sheets are never altered. XML or the CIMS web-form sheet is produced where that channel applies (RR4.1).
- **Deterministic and idempotent:** the same snapshot hash, cell-map version and template hash give a byte-identical file; a generate command with unchanged inputs returns the existing file (key `(instance_id, snapshot_hash, cell_map_version, template_hash)`).

### RR3.3 Validation rule DSL

Rules are versioned YAML documents with CEL expressions. Severity ERROR blocks sign-off; WARNING requires a maker comment and checker acceptance; INFO is logged.

```yaml
id: DNBS02.BS.BALANCE
return: DNBS02
version: 2026.10
severity: ERROR
assert: cell("BS", "TOTAL_ASSETS") == cell("BS", "TOTAL_LIABILITIES")
message: "Total assets must equal total liabilities"
refs: ["REQ-SR-14"]
---
id: DNBS04B.BUCKET.TIE
severity: ERROR
assert: abs(sum(cells("SLS", "OUTFLOW_B1".."OUTFLOW_B10")) - gl("LIABILITIES_TOTAL", scale="CR")) <= 0.01
refs: ["REQ-SR-14", "REQ-ALM-57"]
```

Functions: `cell`, `cells`, `element`, `gl`, `subledger`, `count_where`, `prev_period`, `pct_change`, `tenant.param`, `lookup`. Rule types: (1) schema (type, length, mandatory, catalogue); (2) intra-return arithmetic; (3) cross-return (DNBS01/02 ↔ DNBS04B outflows; DNBS03 CRAR ↔ capital run and notes; DNBS08 count ↔ ledger exposures ≥ ₹5 crore; DNBS09 ↔ week's SMA-0 events; FMR ↔ fraud register; DNBS13 ↔ investment book); (4) GL reconciliation (RR3.4); (5) period-on-period reasonableness (warnings only); (6) the portal's own validation rules (SR para 19) as a separate versioned pack.

### RR3.4 Reconciliation to the trial balance

- For each balance-sheet and P&L element: `variance = return_value − TB_value` after scaling. Tolerance for balance-sheet items is the rounding unit of the template (for ₹ crore to 2 decimals, ₹1 lakh); any larger variance must be explained in the `explained_variance` register (reason code, amount, evidence, approver) before `RECONCILED`.
- Sub-ledger to GL reconciliation for loans, provisions, borrowings and investments must be clean for the snapshot date (M10 item 3); open breaks block the run.
- The reconciliation sheet is part of the package.

### RR3.5 Maker, checker and sign-off matrix (defaults; tenant-configurable within SoD rules)

| Return family | Maker | Checker | Sign-off |
|---|---|---|---|
| DNBS01/02/03, DNBS11/12, DNBS14, PDR | Financial reporting | Head of finance | CFO |
| DNBS04A/04B, IRS, STRESS | Treasury / ALM | Head of treasury | CFO or ALCO convenor |
| DNBS08, DNBS09, LEF | Credit risk | Head of risk | CRO (or CFO where no CRO) |
| DNBS13 | Treasury | Head of finance | CFO |
| FMR, FUA, FMR4-RBR | Fraud risk unit | Head of fraud risk | Authority under the Board fraud policy (FRM; M12) |
| FORM-A-SA, GOV-14 | Company Secretary | CFO | MD/CEO |
| DLA-CIMS | Digital lending ops | Compliance | CCO certification (CF 18(4)) |
| DNBS10 | NBFC finance (data pack) | — | Statutory auditor files |
| FIU-IND reports | AML analyst | Principal Officer | Principal Officer (KYC 15) |
| CIC files (RR6) | Bureau operations | CIC nodal officer | CIC nodal officer (CIR 34(2)) |

SoD: the maker cannot be the checker or signatory for the same run; the CRO and CCO cannot be makers (GOV 21(3)–(4); CMP 27). Sign-off needs step-up authentication; a signatory's absence is covered only by a time-boxed delegation recorded in the Part 7F delegation-of-authority register, never by sharing a login.

### RR3.6 Signed package

- **Contents:** filled template or XML; `manifest.json` (entity, return, period, run and template versions, snapshot hash, file SHA-256, validation and reconciliation hashes, approvals); validation report; reconciliation sheet; lineage extract; NIL declaration where applicable.
- **Signature:** detached JWS over the manifest with the tenant's signing key in the tenant KMS [REC]. A portal DSC is applied by the signatory on the portal; Finbyx never holds a DSC or PIN [VERIFY: CIMS DSC requirement]. The upload screen shows the file SHA-256; any regeneration after `SIGNED_OFF` is a new version.

### Acceptance tests

- A DNBS02 run with an unbalanced balance sheet cannot leave `VALIDATED`; the error names the rule ID and REQ-ID.
- A WARNING without a maker comment and checker acceptance blocks `CHECKER_APPROVED`.
- A ₹2 lakh variance between DNBS02 "investments" (₹ crore, 2 decimals) and the TB blocks `RECONCILED` until an explained-variance entry is approved; a ₹40,000 variance passes as rounding.
- The same user cannot act as maker and checker on one run (403 `sod_conflict`).
- A DNBS13 run for a quarter with no overseas investment produces a NIL package that still requires sign-off.
- Altering a protected template cell (simulated) fails the template-integrity check.
- A sign-off command on a run in `MAKER_SUBMITTED` returns 409 `invalid_transition`; repeating an accepted command with the same idempotency key returns the original result.
- Regenerating a run with an unchanged snapshot, cell map and template returns the same file hash; a portal rejection classified as portal-side returns the run to `PACKAGED` without a new run number.

## RR4. Portal filing workflows (CIMS, DAKSH, PRAVAAH, NABARD ENSURE, IFSCA, FIU-IND, CKYCR, CERSAI, income-tax SFT)

**Purpose.** A guided, evidenced workflow for each portal, with the human filer in control and no credentials in Finbyx.

### RR4.1 RBI CIMS (Sankalan)

- **Portals:** CIMS Common Login (https://cims.rbi.org.in) and Sankalan (https://sankalan.rbi.org.in) (https://rbi.org.in/scripts/ReportingPlaform.aspx). Legacy XBRL, DBIE and SAARC portals close when CIMS is complete; NBFC returns left XBRL in 2024.
- **Channels** (A.P. (DIR Series) Circular No. 24, RBI/2026-27/280, 1 Oct 2026, return R012; generalised [VERIFY per return]):

| Channel | Mechanism | Finbyx support |
|---|---|---|
| System-to-system | RBI collects from the RE's ADF server | Flagged off unless RBI confirms for the entity class |
| File upload | RBI XML or XLSX template on the Data Portal | Default (RR3.6 package) |
| Screen-based web form | From the RBI .xlsx template; **2,000-record cap** | Web-form sheet; above the cap, file upload is forced |

- **Roles (SR para 19):** RBI's super-user credential lets the RE create maker and checker users. Finbyx mirrors the roles for preparation and keeps a **portal-user alias register** (portal role, employee, alias, validity); no password or OTP field exists.
- **Guided upload checklist** (one screen, each step ticked by the filer and time-stamped): open the portal in a separate browser tab (Finbyx shows the link, never embeds or automates it) → confirm entity, return, period and template version → upload the package file and compare the SHA-256 shown by Finbyx → record the portal validation result (errors pasted or attached go to `PORTAL_REJECTED`) → portal checker submits → download the acknowledgement → upload it to Finbyx, which pre-reads the reference and time for the filer to confirm. A step cannot be ticked out of order.
- **DNBS10:** the NBFC super user creates the auditor's login (SR 21 item 7); the auditor workspace (Part 7D, AU7) carries the data pack and clock; the CFO records the auditor's filing reference.

### RR4.2 DAKSH (supervisory monitoring)

DAKSH (https://daksh.rbi.org.in, launched 6 Oct 2022) is RBI's workflow application for compliance monitoring, inspection, communication, cyber-incident reporting and MIS. It is not a return portal.

| Workflow | Direction | Finbyx role |
|---|---|---|
| Cyber incident within 6 hours of detection | CYB 28, 141 (HFCs to NHB) | Incident record starts the timer; draft; DAKSH evidence; CERT-In clock separate |
| Nomination coverage (NBFC-D), quarterly | MSD 12 | Coverage report from the deposits module |
| Supervisory letters, inspection RMPs, compliance items | [VERIFY: no primary text on RMP submission] | Inbound item register (RR5.4) |
| CIC laggard lists (CICs report late CIs half-yearly, as on 31 March and 30 September) | CIR 10(2)(v) as amended; CIC-AMD 15(2) | Not a tenant filing; RR6 timeliness keeps the tenant off it |

### RR4.3 PRAVAAH (applications and authorisations)

PRAVAAH (https://pravaah.rbi.org.in; mandatory for all applicants from 1 May 2025; 108 forms) is used for applications, status tracking, query responses and decisions.

- **Application pack builder:** form, entity, documents with hashes, Board resolutions (Part 7F), checklist. Seeded uses: change in control or management incl. the 30% director change (GOV 10–11, Annex I); overseas representative office (BR 13); NBFC-AA registration; ICC-to-Factor conversion (MISC 39); IDF-MF sponsorship (MISC 63); core investment company registration within 3 months of meeting the test (CICD paras 11(7), 15–17; Part 7H IV5.6) [VERIFY: CICD paragraph numbers].
- **States:** `DRAFT → INTERNAL_APPROVED → SUBMITTED_BY_HUMAN → RBI_QUERY → RESPONDED → DECIDED → CONDITIONS_TRACKED → CLOSED`; decision conditions become M14 obligations.

### RR4.4 NABARD ENSURE (StCB and DCCB tenants)

NABARD supervises StCBs and DCCBs under BR Act s.35(6). ENSURE returns (indicative): **OSC-10 quarterly; CS-01 and CS-02 within 15 days; CSIR-01 cyber incident within 6 hours** [VERIFY: current list and formats]. Same package and evidence flow as CIMS.

### RR4.5 IFSCA (Finance Companies and Finance Units)

Reports under IFSCA-FC reg 9 in USD from the USD ledger (AC1–AC2), one tenant per IFSC unit (Part 7G, IP6) [VERIFY: return list, frequency, portal].

### RR4.6 FIU-IND (FINGate 2.0)

- **Reports:** STR, CTR, NTR, CCR, CBWTR under PML (Maintenance of Records) Rules 2005 r.3, filed per r.7 (KYC 49) on FINnet 2.0 / FINGate 2.0 (live 22 Mar 2023).
- **Timelines (PML Rules r.8) [VERIFY exact text]:** CTR, NTR, CBWTR by the 15th of the next month; STR within 7 working days of being satisfied that a transaction is suspicious; CCR [VERIFY]. Each day of delay is a separate violation (KYC 51).
- **Build:** XML from the AML case module (Part 8A.21) through the FIU-IND Report Generation and Validation Utilities [VERIFY: Reporting Format Guide version]; Principal Officer approval; STRs hidden from non-AML roles (no tipping off; no account restriction merely because an STR is filed, KYC 51); batch hash and FINGate acknowledgement recorded; Designated Director and Principal Officer intimations (KYC 14–15).

### RR4.7 CKYCR (CERSAI)

Upload within **10 days** of starting an account-based relationship and updates within **7 days** (KYC 63(1), 63(7); PML Rules r.9(1A), 9(1C)). Build: bulk file generator, response ingest (KYC identifier, errors), retry queue, identifier sent to the customer (KYC 63(6)), and the 14-digit CKYC number pushed to bureau mapping (CIR 12(10)). Breaches fail the M14 control test.

### RR4.8 CERSAI Central Registry

Security interest registered **within 30 days of creation, modification or satisfaction** (SARFAESI ss.20–26) [VERIFY: Central Registry Rules 2011 as amended, late fees]; no SARFAESI enforcement without it (s.26D). M5 `charge_registration` holds the record; RR4 adds the deadline instance, checklist, acknowledgement capture and the satisfaction trigger on closure.

### RR4.9 Income-tax reporting portal (ITA25)

- **SFT:** ITA25 **s.508, Form 165** (formerly s.285BA, Form 61A), annual, due 31 May [VERIFY: Income-tax Rules 2026]; defects cured within 30 days, corrections within 10 days (incometaxindia.gov.in, s.508); NBFC reportable-transaction list [VERIFY].
- **FATCA/CRS:** **Form 166** (formerly 61B) and NIL reports, Reporting FIs only (KYC 64) [VERIFY: rule].
- Build: year-versioned reportable rules, CBDT-schema data file, reporting-entity ID register, designated-director sign-off, acknowledgement capture. TDS statements are in AC5.

### Acceptance tests

- A CIMS web-form run with 2,001 records refuses the web-form channel and offers file upload only.
- The cyber-incident record shows a 6-hour countdown from detection time; recording the DAKSH reference after 6 hours raises a compliance issue with root cause mandatory.
- A PRAVAAH application cannot move to `SUBMITTED_BY_HUMAN` without internal approval and a Board resolution reference where the form requires one.
- An STR is not visible to roles outside AML and the Principal Officer; an attempt to view it is logged.
- A loan opened on day 0 with no CKYCR upload by day 10 fails the M14 control test on day 11.
- A loan closure with a CERSAI-registered charge opens a satisfaction-filing task due in 30 days.

## RR5. Filing calendar, evidence vault, revisions and RBI queries

### RR5.1 Filing calendar

- `return_due_instance` rows are generated 13 months ahead per entity. Weekly reference dates move to the preceding working day if Friday is a holiday (SR para 21 item 6) [VERIFY: RBI or RE holiday calendar].
- Event-driven instances: fraud classification (FMR +14 days), update (FUA immediate), cyber detection (+6 hours), SA appointment (Form A +1 month), audit-report signing (DNBS10 and all audited returns +5 working days, DNBS10 capped at 31 Dec; SR 22 Note 1, 23), DLA change, account opening (CKYCR +10 days), charge creation (CERSAI +30 days).
- Alerts at T−7, T−3, T−1 and on breach (tenants may add stages but never remove the breach alert); escalation to the CCO on breach and to the MD/CEO after 2 working days [REC]. `ReturnDue` is emitted at each alert stage to LawDocsComply or embedded M14, and to the Operations Hub as status metadata only where the tenant has opted in.
- **Working days:** the instance's `holiday_calendar` (default: RBI holidays for Mumbai plus the tenant's registered-office State calendar; Saturdays and Sundays non-working). Where a calendar-day limit ends on a holiday, the instance is due on the preceding working day [REC]; a due date is never moved later than the Direction allows.

### RR5.2 Evidence vault and acknowledgements

- Folders (Part 7J DP1.2 and Integration Specification 12.1): `05 Regulatory Returns/[regulator]/[portal]/[return code]/[period]/` and `06 Credit Bureau Reporting/[CIC]/[file type]/[period]/`, where the bureau period is the reference date and cycle code (for example `2026-07-09 W1`). Files are byte-identical to what was filed, with the validation report, sign-offs and acknowledgement alongside.
- Contents: versions, snapshot hash, file and hash, validation report, reconciliation, lineage extract, approvals, signed manifest, acknowledgement, revision history, applicable variance rows.
- **Acknowledgement capture:** the filer uploads the portal acknowledgement and confirms the reference (Finbyx may pre-read it from the PDF); `ACKNOWLEDGED` needs both.
- Retention class `REG-RETURN`: 10 years from filing [REC], never below the statutory period (AC7).

### RR5.3 Revisions

- A revision is run `n+1` with a reason code (RBI_QUERY, INTERNAL_ERROR, AUDIT_ADJUSTMENT, LATE_POSTING, FORMAT_CHANGE), trigger reference, cell-level diff, fresh validation, reconciliation, approvals and package; version n is preserved. SR has no revision paragraph; the portal's resubmission mechanism applies [VERIFY: CIMS procedure]. `ReturnRevised` is emitted on acknowledgement.
- **Revision assessment (query and revision loop):** a trigger (RBI query, audit adjustment, back-dated posting into a filed period, error found by DQ checks, `FinancialStatementsApproved` with figures that differ from filed quarterly returns) opens a `revision_assessment` listing every affected return and period with a draft cell diff computed from a fresh snapshot → the return owner proposes `REVISE` or `NO_REVISION` (with reasons; any change to a prudential-ratio cell or above the `revision_materiality` setting defaults to `REVISE`) → CCO decides → `REVISE` opens run n+1 at `DATA_FROZEN` and the full RR3.1 path → after `ACKNOWLEDGED`, the linked `supervisory_item` records the response and closes. A `NO_REVISION` decision is kept in the evidence pack with the diff.
- Audit adjustments after a quarterly filing open a revision assessment for every affected return automatically.

### RR5.4 RBI queries and supervisory requests

- `supervisory_item` register: source (DAKSH, email, letter, inspection, PRAVAAH), type (return query, SR 13 ad hoc request, RMP item, letter), linked returns, owner, due date, drafts, approvals, response reference. Ad hoc requests run as ad hoc returns with RBI's due date (SR 22 Note 2).
- A missed filing opens a compliance issue with root cause and a penalty-exposure note (SR para 24 [VERIFY: quantum under RBI Act ss.58B/58G]); late FMRs open staff-accountability review (FRM 46).

### Acceptance tests

- An FMR classified on 1 November shows due 15 November; FUA instances are due on the update date.
- DNBS10 for an audit report signed on Friday 25 Sep 2026 is due Monday 5 Oct 2026 (2 Oct is a holiday); one signed on Thursday 24 Dec 2026 is due 31 Dec 2026 (cap).
- A revision preserves version n byte-for-byte and its acknowledgement; the diff lists only changed cells.
- A run cannot be `CLOSED` without an acknowledgement attachment whose hash is stored.
- For a tenant that has opted in, the Operations Hub receives `ReturnDue` at each alert stage and `ReturnFiled` on acknowledgement, with no amount, package or borrower field; for a tenant that has not, the Hub receives nothing.
- A `FinancialStatementsApproved` event whose audited CRAR differs from the filed March DNBS03 opens a revision assessment defaulting to `REVISE`.
