## RR6. Credit bureau submission engine (consumer, commercial, MFI)

**Purpose.** Report complete, accurate and timely credit information to all four CICs in the Uniform Credit Reporting Formats, on the cadence in force from 1 Jul 2026. Extends Part 8A.2.

### RR6.1 Legal frame and scope

- **Law:** CICRA 2005, CIC Rules and Regulations 2006; CIR (349, under CICRA s.11) as amended by RBI/DOR/2025-26/117, DoR.FIN.REC.No.324/20.16.056/2025-26, **4 Dec 2025, in force 1 Jul 2026** (paras 10(2), 12(10), 15, Annex VI); CIC-side rules as amended by RBI/DOR/2025-26/119 (`CIC-AMD`). Membership of all four CICs (CIR 6); **no borrower consent needed** (CIR 11).
- **Scope:** reporting CIs per CIR 3 (Part 8A.2); banks and UCBs on their own amended CIR Directions [VERIFY: StCB/DCCB]. Credit co-operative societies report only if a CIC admits them as members [VERIFY]; otherwise the module stays off and no other lender's membership is ever used. LSPs never report (CF 17); co-lenders report their own shares (TDCR 122). MFIN members add **daily** submission (MFIN Guardrails 2.0, Directive #14) [SRO].

### RR6.2 Cadence (effective-dated; CIR para 10(2) as substituted)

| Period | Reference dates | File | Due |
|---|---|---|---|
| Until 30 Jun 2026 | 15th and month-end | Full | Within 7 calendar days |
| From 1 Jul 2026 | 9th (W1), 16th (W2), 23rd (W3) | Incremental | Within 4 calendar days |
| From 1 Jul 2026 | Month-end (ME) | Full: all active accounts plus accounts whose relationship ended since the last reference date | By the 5th of the next month |
| By agreement | Daily (DL) | Incremental | Next day (MFIN members) |

**Annex VI timetable (from 1 Jul 2026):**

| Reference date | CI shares data by | CIC rejection report by | CI correction by |
|---|---|---|---|
| 9th | 13th | 16th | 20th |
| 16th | 20th | 23rd | 27th |
| 23rd | 27th | 30th | 5th of next month |
| Month-end | 5th | 8th | 13th |

February: the "30th" rejection date falls in March; the calendar engine computes it as reference date + 7 calendar days [VERIFY: CIC practice for February]. **Do not build to the draft cadence** (7th/14th/21st/28th and a 3rd-of-month full file); the final text dropped it.

### RR6.3 Population rules

- **ME file:** every active account plus every account closed, sold, written off or otherwise ended since the last reference date.
- **W1–W3 incremental:** A opened since the last reference date ∪ B relationship ended ∪ C changed by borrower-initiated action or transaction (repayment, balance, demographic, related-party, guarantor, ownership, account type) ∪ D any interest or principal overdue. **Accounts whose only change is DPD must be reported.** Implementation: `changed_since(last_ref) OR amount_overdue > 0`, where change detection compares a canonical record hash per account and bureau.
- No repayment goes unreported, including the last instalment; closure always produces a category-B record at the next reference date (CIR 10(3)).
- Reporting continues after CoR cancellation until the loans run off (CIR 14).

### RR6.4 Routing

- Individual borrowers → Consumer; non-individual borrowers and guarantors → Commercial, with the Relationship segment for accounts opened on or after 1 Jul 2018 (beneficial-owner shareholders only) (CIR 12(8)); microfinance loans → MFI only, never also Consumer.
- Consumer and commercial co-borrowers each go in their own format (CIR 12(9)).
- Sold, purchased, co-lent and securitised accounts carry old-member fields and the relevant status codes; the servicer reports per the transfer documents.

### RR6.5 Format packs (data, never code)

**Consumer — UCRF Consumer v3.74** (4 Feb 2026, w.e.f. 1 Jul 2026; builds on v3.73 of 7 Apr 2025; the former CIBIL TUDF layout, now non-proprietary) [CIC]:

- **Record order:** Header (fixed 146 bytes; segment tag `TUDF` or, from v3.74, `CONS`; version field `12`) → per subject: **PN** name (N01) → **ID** (I01–I08) → **PT** telephone (T01–T10) → **EC** email (C01–C10) → **PA** address (A01–A05) → **TL** account (T001) → **TH** account history (H01–H48, initial load only) → **ES** end of subject (fixed `ES02**`) → file trailer `TRLR`.
- **Tag-length-value** encoding for variable segments: 2-byte field tag, 2-byte length, value (for example `0111HAREN PATEL`).
- **Header:** member user ID, short name, reporting cycle, date reported and certified (DDMMYYYY); password and authentication method become Future Use in v3.74. **Reporting Cycle codes:** DL daily, W1 (9th), W2 (16th), W3 (23rd), ME month-end, DC correction or dispute, AH ad hoc, RR rejection resubmission.
- **File name:** `[MEMBER-ID]-[DDMMYYYY]-[HHMMSS].txt`, or `.gpg` if encrypted.
- **Key TL fields:** 01–05 member, account and ownership; 08–11 dates (closed only at zero balance); 12 sanctioned (required); 13 balance; 14 overdue; **15 DPD (max 900)**; 16–20 old member and account; **21 suit-filed/WD; 22 facility status; 26 asset class**; 34–35 collateral; 38–40 rate, tenure, EMI; **41–43 written-off and settlement amounts**; 44–49 frequency, payment, occupation, income. Amounts widen to 20 in v3.74.
- **Catalogues (data):** account types 00–71; ownership 1–5; ID types incl. **09 CKYC (14 digits)**; suit-filed/WD 00–03; facility status 00–17, 99; asset class 01–05; state codes (v3.74 adds Ladakh and Foreign).
- **Validations:** PAN pattern; UID check digit; mobile starts 6–9; PIN consistent with state; DOB ≥ 16 years before reporting; date ordering; written-off amounts for statuses 02/03/04/13/15/16 and settlement for 03/04/15/16. Required-field failure rejects the record; header failure rejects the file.

**Commercial — UCRF Commercial v3.10 (Delimited)** (13 Apr 2026, effective July 2026) [CIC]:

- **Segments:** HD header → BS borrower → AS address (registered office required) / RS relationship (mandatory except factoring-without-recourse buyer trades) → CR credit facility → GS guarantor / SS security / CD dishonour of cheques → TS file closure (counts of BS and CR).
- **Encoding:** pipe-delimited fields; each segment ends with CRLF; dates DDMMYYYY; whole-rupee amounts; the characters `~` and `^` anywhere reject the whole file.
- **Transport:** **SFTP only** (since v3.8, Nov 2024).
- **File name:** `Commercial-[Cycle][DateReported][InternalRef]` with cycles DL/W1/W2/W3/ME/DC/AH/RR (naming does not cause rejection).
- **Mandatory:** BS name, constitution, business category, industry, BSR activity and at least one identifier (CIN, PAN, registration number, TIN, Udyam, CKYC); CR account number, **sanction date**, sanctioned amount, currency, credit type, balance, asset class/DPD, overdue, status, wilful-default status.
- **Catalogues (data):** legal constitution (60 co-operative society, 85 SHG, 90 individual …); relationship (55 SHG member, 70 Karta …); credit types (0100 CC … 9026 factoring without recourse); **suit-filed 05 NCLT/NCLAT**; restructuring reasons; asset class/DPD codes incl. SMA-0/1/2 and Doubtful 1/2/3 [VERIFY: full list].
- **v3.10:** "Reporting cycle" in the header; identifiers required-conditional; **written-off and settled amounts enforced from 1 Apr 2027**.

**MFI (incl. SHG) — UCRF MFI v3.3.1** (April 2026, effective 1 Jul 2026; base layout CIR Annex I Form 3) [CIC]:

- **Segments:** HDR (fixed) → GRPCRD (SHG groups only) → CNSCRD member → ADRCRD → ACTCRD → TRL (fixed). Pipe separator in v3.3.1. **Separate files for SHG and for JLG + individual** (header field 9).
- **Header:** file name tag; layout version 3.3; member ID (10); member name; branch ID (mandatory from v3.3); reported date; creation date; **system vendor identifier and version** (Finbyx writes `FINBYX` and its release version [REC]).
- **Account:** loan category T01–T08; status S04–S17 (S01–S03 removed in v3.3; S13 sold, S14 purchased, S16 calamity-restructured added; S18 also appears); frequency F01–F10; **DPD 000–999, mandatory from v3.3**; write-off reasons X01–X10 (fields 90–92 for S06); insurance L01–L10. **Fields 49 (household income), 84, 85, 86 missing → record rejected.** **CKYC own field (length 15)**.
- **File name:** `[MFI]-[CYCLE]-[DDMMYYYY]-[MEMBER-CODE]-[REF]` with cycle DL/W1/W2/W3/ME.

**Spec inconsistencies** (TH occurrences, status-17 rule, the v3.74 PIN-length note, S18) are logged as `format_issue` rows and resolved in writing with the bureau; they are never coded around. Each CIC's current specification is obtained under its member agreement before go-live.

### RR6.6 Mapping rules (enforced in the generator)

| Finbyx fact | Consumer | Commercial | MFI | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Principal or interest waived for financial inability | Status 03 settled (or 04 after write-off) with settlement amount | Account status settled with amount | S10 or S11 | Only this case is "settled" (CIR 12(4)) |
| Wrong debit or contested charge | Dispute marker; never "settled" | Dispute marker | Dispute marker | "Disputed" (CIR 12(4)) |
| IBC admission | Suit-filed 01 | Suit-filed 05 NCLT/NCLAT | n/a | CIR 12(7) |
| Wilful defaulter (ML+ only) | 02 or 03 | Wilful default 1 with date | n/a | WD 12(3) |
| Written off (full or technical) | 02 with written-off total and principal | Written-off amount (required-conditional from 1 Apr 2027) | S06 with X-code | |
| Sold to ARC or another lender | 05 sold; old member fields | Status per catalogue | S13 | |
| Restructured | Status per reason | Restructuring reason code | S08/S16/S17 | |
| Compromise settlement | Reported with reason | Reported with reason | | CIR 12(2) |
| DPD | Cap 900 | Asset class or DPD code | Cap 999 | |
| CKYC number | ID type 09 | Identifier on BS/RS | CKYC field | CIR 12(10) |
| Microfinance household income | | | Field 49; divergence reason | CF 54 |

### RR6.7 Build, transmit and acknowledge

1. **Freeze** the snapshot; **extract** (RR6.3) and **route** (RR6.4).
2. **Validate** against the version pack and the CICs' **uniform data-acceptance rules** (CIC-AMD 19(1)); ERROR records go to the repair queue with reason codes, never silently dropped.
3. **Build four outputs from one dataset**, differing only in bureau header values, file name and encryption.
4. **Approve:** the CIC nodal officer reviews counts by segment, status and DPD bucket, held-back records and variance to the last cycle.
5. **Transmit** by SFTP from a lender-controlled host (or a tenant-run agent on premises), key-based, with SFTP and PGP keys in the tenant vault (BYOK; unreadable by Finbyx staff); CIBIL consumer files may be `.gpg` and **CIBIL correction uploads are not encrypted** [CIC: TransUnion CIBIL data-acquisition note]; the encryption rule for each other CIC is a format-pack setting taken from its member specification.
6. **Record** hash, size, time and server acknowledgement; ingest status files; emit `BureauFileGenerated` (on `APPROVED`) and `BureauFileSubmitted` (on `ACK_RECEIVED`).

**State machine (one `bureau_cycle` per CIC, format and reference date):** `PLANNED → SNAPSHOT → EXTRACTED → VALIDATED → BUILT → APPROVED → TRANSMITTED → ACK_RECEIVED → REJECTIONS_INGESTED → (REPAIRED → RESUBMITTED)* → DQI_RECEIVED → CLOSED`. Missing the 4-day or 5th-of-month deadline raises a compliance issue, because CICs report laggards to RBI on DAKSH (CIR 10(2)(v) as amended).

**Exception paths:**

- **Nodal officer rejects at `APPROVED`:** reason recorded → back to `EXTRACTED` after the fix; the four bureau outputs are rebuilt together so they never diverge.
- **Transmission failure** (SFTP unreachable, key rejected): automatic retries with back-off for 2 hours, then an alert to bureau operations and the nodal officer; at due − 1 day an unresolved failure escalates to the CCO. The same file (same hash) is re-sent; a rebuild is a new `file_seq`.
- **File-level rejection** (header or trailer failure, forbidden character): the cycle goes to `FILE_REJECTED`, the whole file is repaired at source and re-sent as the same cycle code before the due date; after the due date it is still sent and the compliance issue records the delay.
- **No acknowledgement** within 1 working day of transmission: task to confirm with the CIC; the cycle cannot close without an acknowledgement or the CIC's written confirmation.
- **Partial bureau success:** each CIC's cycle is tracked separately; a failure at one CIC never blocks or re-sends the others.

### Acceptance tests

- Golden files: one consumer, one commercial and one MFI file per cycle code pass each bureau's published validator [VERIFY: validator availability per CIC] and match stored byte-level fixtures.
- An account whose only change since the 9th is DPD 31 → 38 appears in the W2 file.
- A loan closed on the 20th appears in the W3 file as category B and is absent from the next ME active set except as ended since the last reference date.
- A microfinance individual loan never appears in the consumer file.
- A record containing `~` in a commercial field is cleaned at source or held back; the file never contains it.
- The ME file for July is due on 5 August; transmission on 6 August raises a compliance issue.
- No SFTP private key is readable through any Finbyx admin API or log.

## RR7. Bureau rejections, corrections, disputes and data quality

### RR7.1 Rejection repair loop

- **Ingest** rejection reports and file-level DQI (CICs return both within **3 calendar days**, CIC-AMD 39(1)–(2), 20(1)) into one `bureau_rejection` table keyed by bureau, cycle, account and **uniform reason code** (CIC-AMD 19(2)).
- **Repair at source** (CIR 19): a task for the data owner; corrected master data flows into the next generation, never a hand-edited file.
- **Resubmit** as cycle `RR` **before or with the next reference-date file** (CIR 15 as substituted; 7 days until 30 Jun 2026), i.e. by the 20th, 27th, 5th or 13th.
- Ageing escalates after one cycle to the nodal officer and after two to the CCO. Online Maintenance corrections (uniform formats, CIC-AMD 19(1)) are mirrored as `bureau_correction` records.

### RR7.2 Data quality

- File-level DQI within 3 calendar days and CI-level DQI monthly by the 10th (weighted-average method; CIC-AMD 20(1), 20(3), Annex X), trended by segment.
- **Half-yearly DQI review**; report of issues and corrective steps to top management **within two months of the half-year end** (CIR 17), drafted by Finbyx; rejection reasons and DQI feed the half-yearly grievance RCA (CIR 34(4)).

### RR7.3 Borrower alerts

**SMS or email alert while submitting default or DPD data**, wherever contact details exist (CIR 34(1)(i)): a notification at submission, **not a pre-reporting notice**, never delaying the file. Language preference applies (RBC 10); SMS only on a DLT-registered service or transactional header and template, and any voice alert only from a 1600-series number, never a 140-series one (TRAI); template version and delivery logged per account per cycle; awareness prompts for missing contacts (CIR 34(1)(iii)).

### RR7.4 Credit-information disputes

**Intake:** borrower (branch, portal, app, email, Udofin relay), CIC-forwarded dispute, RBI Ombudsman or Internal Ombudsman reference; complaint form captures email and bank account or UPI for compensation (CIR 35(8)). Linked to M15 grievances (CIR 38(3)).

**State machine:** `RECEIVED (t0 = date first filed with the CI or a CIC) → ACKNOWLEDGED → INVESTIGATING → DECISION (ACCEPT or REJECT with a reason from the CICs' standard list, CIR 34(3)) → CORRECTION_SENT_TO_CICs (DC cycle or Online Maintenance) → CIC_CONFIRMED → BORROWER_INFORMED (rectified CIR sent) → CLOSED`.

**Clocks:**

- The CI sends corrected data to the CICs within **21 calendar days** of being informed (CIC Rules r.20(3)(c); CIR 35(2)).
- Overall resolution within **30 calendar days** of the initial filing (CICRA s.21(3); CIR 35(1)); the CIC effectively has the remaining 9 days.
- Resolution date = date the rectified CIR is sent to the complainant (CIR 35(7)).

**Compensation (CIR 35).** All dates are calendar dates; the algorithm reproduces every CIR para 35 illustration (Cases 1–7) and those cases are its golden tests.

```text
t0             = date the complaint was first filed with the CI or a CIC
days_late      = max(0, resolution_date - (t0 + 30))        # resolution_date per CIR 35(7)
if days_late == 0: no compensation
# delay attributed to each party
d_ci[i]        = max(0, ci_response_date[i] - (ci_informed_date[i] + 21))   # each CI i (CIR 35(2))
cic_elapsed    = days the CIC held the complaint:
                 CIC-registered: (ci_informed_date - t0) + (resolution_date - last ci_response_date)
                 CI-registered:  cic_rectified_cir_date - ci_response_date
d_cic          = max(0, cic_elapsed - 9)
d_fwd          = CI-registered only: resolution_date - cic_rectified_cir_date   # CI forwarding to complainant
amount_total   = 100 * days_late                            # ₹100 per calendar day
share_x        = amount_total * d_x / sum(d)                # CIR 35(4): proportionate; d_fwd is the CI's
round to paise by largest remainder so the shares sum to amount_total
pay_by         = resolution_date + 5 working days           # CIR 35(9)
```

- The CI pays its share (and, for a complaint registered with it, informs the CIC and the complainant of the total delay and each party's amount, CIR 35(6)); a CIC's share is recorded as receivable from or payable by that CIC per the member agreement.
- Credit to the complainant's bank account or UPI ID from a payout batch approved by a checker, posted to a compensation-expense GL; deviations reported to the Board or customer-service committee (CIR 18); CIR 35(12) exclusions tagged with the reason; multi-CI complaints routed to the CIC (35(5)). The complainant is told of the Ombudsman route for wrongful denial (35(10)): the RBI Integrated Ombudsman Scheme, 2026 for complaints received from 1 Jul 2026 (`RBIOS26`; the 2021 Scheme for earlier ones), and the Internal Ombudsman under `IO26` where applicable.
- Events: `BureauCorrectionRequested` on ACCEPT; `BureauCorrectionCompleted` on CIC_CONFIRMED.

### RR7.5 Nodal officer and governance

- CIC nodal officer register with email and phone; changes notified to every CIC within **5 calendar days** (CIR 34(2)(ii)); the change opens a 5-day task per bureau.
- Half-yearly RCA with annual top-management review (CIR 34(4)); quarterly Board/customer-service committee pack with dispute clocks, compensation paid and DQI.

### Acceptance tests

- CIR para 35 Case 7 golden tests: complaint with the CI on 1 Jan 2022, corrections sent 25 Jan (3 days late), CIC returns the rectified CIR on 3 Feb and the CI sends it the same day → ₹300 payable by the CI; CIC on 4 Feb, CI the same day → ₹400 (₹100 CIC, ₹300 CI); CIC on 4 Feb, CI on 5 Feb → ₹500 (₹100 CIC, ₹400 CI).
- CIR para 35 Case 4 golden test: CIC-registered complaint of 1 Jan 2022, banks B–E late by 5, 7, 9 and 11 days, resolution on 15 Feb → ₹1,500 split ₹208.33, ₹291.67, ₹375.00, ₹458.33 and CIC ₹166.67 (largest-remainder rounding; total exactly ₹1,500).
- Case 1: CIC seeks confirmation on day 11, the bank replies on day 21 of its window, resolution on 3 Feb → ₹300, all payable by the CIC.
- A rejection from the 9th cycle not resubmitted by the 20th shows as overdue and is included in the 16th-cycle file as `RR`.
- A dispute decision of REJECT without a standard reason code cannot be saved.
- A default record in the W1 file triggers one alert per borrower per cycle; a borrower with no mobile or email is counted in the "no contact" metric.
- The half-yearly DQI report for H1 (April–September) is due by 30 November and appears on the compliance calendar.

## RR8. CRILC, large-exposure, wilful and large defaulter and fraud reporting

### RR8.1 CRILC Main (DNBS08)

- **Population:** borrowers whose **aggregate fund-based and non-fund-based exposure** from the NBFC is **₹5 crore or more**, computed at borrower level across products as on month-end, with SMA status (RSA 20; SR 21 item 5). NIL return if none.
- **Applicability (8A.36.5 decision kept):** union of SR para 21 item 5 (₹500 crore qualifier read across BL ICCs, MFIs and Factors by default) and the RSA obligation (NBFC-D, NBFC-ND ≥ ₹500 crore, any Factor; RSA 7, 20–21, 158), tenant toggle, variance row (RR1.4 item 2) [VERIFY with RBI DoS].
- Project-finance credit events go in the weekly report and CRILC Main (RSA 106–107). Reported SMA status is compared with `classification_history` before sign-off, because concealment triggers accelerated provisioning (RSA 22–23).

### RR8.2 DNBS09 weekly defaulted borrowers

As at every Friday (or the preceding working day), due by the following Wednesday (SR 21 item 6, 22; RSA 21): move-in and move-out sections (PAN, name, date of default, funded, non-funded, total), computed from SMA-0 events since the previous Friday for the ≥ ₹5 crore population and reconciled with M6 classification events; NIL if none.

### RR8.3 Large Exposure Framework return (UL)

Quarterly within 21 days (SR 21 item 12) from the M12 exposure engine and Part 7E (RK5), monthly internal computation, N configurable (8A.36.2). Breaches are intimated immediately as an event-driven return and block new exposure (CON 45).

### RR8.4 Large and wilful defaulter files to CICs

- **Monthly to all four CICs by SFTP** (WD 11–12, Annexes I–II): large defaulters ≥ ₹1 crore and wilful defaulters, **suit-filed and non-suit-filed in separate files**, row-level, cycle identifier in the RBI format (e.g. `JAN24`). Removal within 30 days once outstanding falls below ₹25 lakh, and for settlements only after full payment (WD 12(2), 13). Only ML and above classify; BL keeps updating history (WD 12(3)). LWD status reported before any transfer (WD 14). Built from Part 7A R15.6 and the WD case module on the RR6 SFTP, key and evidence path.

### RR8.5 Fraud reporting

FMR, FUA and FMR4/RBR are generated from the M12 fraud module (Part 8A.14) through the RR3 pipeline, with the RR5 clocks. Generator guards: FMR category from the FRM 42 list; no uninvolved person named (FRM 47); withdrawal only with director-rank approval or a court order (FRM 48–49); group-entity frauds routed to the email pack, never CIMS (FRM 45); late filing opens staff-accountability review (FRM 46). NBFCs have **no Red Flagged Account category**; the bank RFA return (7 days, CB SR para 23) exists only under a bank profile.

### RR8.6 Bank, UCB and ARC equivalents

Commercial banks: CRILC, RFA, FMR and LEF under CB SR (RR1.5); UCBs with assets ≥ ₹500 crore: CRILC for exposures ≥ ₹5 crore [VERIFY: UCB RSA para 12]; ARCs per the ARC Directions [VERIFY].

### Acceptance tests

- A borrower with ₹3.2 crore term loan and ₹2 crore bank guarantee (non-fund) appears in CRILC Main; a borrower at ₹4.99 crore does not.
- A ₹6 crore borrower turning SMA-0 on Tuesday appears in that Friday's DNBS09 move-in section; curing on the following Monday appears in the next move-out section.
- A month with no ≥ ₹5 crore borrower produces a NIL CRILC that still needs CRO sign-off.
- A BL tenant cannot mark a borrower as wilful defaulter; the WD file still carries the history it inherited.
- An FMR naming a person flagged "not involved" fails validation.
- A wilful defaulter whose outstanding drops to ₹24 lakh on 3 March is removed in a file sent to all CICs by 2 April.

## RR9. Settings, menus and screens (workspace K — Compliance and Regulatory Reporting)

**Purpose.** Give the returns and bureau teams one place to work, with settings that cannot breach a regulatory floor. Returns screens ship with Phase 14b, bureau screens with Phase 14c. Every setting is effective-dated, changed under maker-checker and written to the audit trail; the server enforces floors whatever the UI sends (403 `floor_violation`, with the citation).

### RR9.1 Settings and options

"Floor" = regulatory or platform minimum that a tenant cannot relax (it may only tighten); "Choice" = tenant decision within the floor.

| Setting | Level | Default | Floor or choice | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Applicable returns | Legal entity | As resolved by RR1.3 | Floor: a resolved return cannot be switched off; a tenant may add voluntary or ad hoc returns | SR 21, 25 |
| CRILC BL qualifier reading | Legal entity | ₹500 crore for BL ICCs, MFIs and Factors, union with the RSA test | Choice of the CCO with a variance row, until RBI DoS clarifies | RR1.4, RR8.1 |
| `freeze_lead`, `generate_lead` | Return family | Monthly: reference date + 3 working days and due − 5 working days; quarterly: + 7 and due − 7 | Choice; the server rejects a value that leaves less than 2 working days before due | [REC] |
| Alert stages and escalation | Tenant | T−7, T−3, T−1, breach; CCO on breach, MD/CEO after 2 working days | Floor: the breach alert and CCO escalation stay | RR5.1 |
| Maker, checker and signatory roles | Return family | RR3.5 matrix | Floor: maker, checker and signatory are three different people; CRO and CCO never makers | GOV 21(3)–(4); CMP 27 |
| Checker and signatory SLA | Return family | 1 working day each | Choice | [REC] |
| Rule severity | Rule pack | As published | Floor: portal and REQ-linked rules cannot be downgraded; tenants may add rules or raise severity | RR3.3 |
| Reconciliation tolerance | Return version | Template rounding unit | Floor: may be tightened, never loosened | SR 14 |
| `revision_materiality` | Tenant | Any change to a prudential-ratio cell, or above the template rounding unit | Choice above the floor that every RBI query gets an assessment | RR5.3 |
| Holiday calendar | Legal entity | RBI Mumbai plus registered-office State; Saturday and Sunday off | Choice of State list | RR5.1 |
| `share_return_status_with_hub` | Tenant | Off | Choice; when on, `ReturnDue` and `ReturnFiled` metadata only | Integration Spec 6.18 |
| ADF or system-to-system channel | Legal entity and return | Off | Floor: on only with RBI evidence and a second approver | 7B.0 item 3 |
| Email contingency | Return | Disabled | Floor: enabled per filing only with RBI advice attached | SR 18 |
| Indicative packs (banks, UCBs, StCBs, ARCs, IFSCA, societies) | Institution profile | `ACTIVE_UNVERIFIED` | Floor: no filing until a named reviewer verifies the row | RR1.5 |
| Return evidence retention | Tenant | 10 years from filing | Floor: never below the statutory period | RR5.2; Part 7C AC7.4 |
| Portal-user alias review | Tenant | Quarterly | Choice (at least annual) | 7B.0 item 2 |
| CICs reported to | Legal entity | All four | Floor for every CI; off only for a society no CIC has admitted | CIR 6; RR6.1 |
| Daily (DL) bureau cycle | Legal entity | Off; on for MFIN members | Floor for MFIN members | SRO-MFIN |
| Transmission host | Legal entity | Tenant-controlled host | Choice: tenant host or on-premises agent; never a Finbyx-held key | RR6.7 |
| Held-back records | Format pack | ERROR held, WARNING sent and flagged | Floor: ERROR never sent and never dropped; a tenant may also hold WARNINGs | RR6.7 |
| Auto-include repaired records as `RR` | Tenant | On | Choice | RR7.1 |
| Borrower default/DPD alert | Tenant | SMS and email wherever contact exists; preferred language, else English and Hindi | Floor: cannot be switched off; never delays a file | CIR 34(1)(i); TRAI |
| Dispute compensation payout | Tenant | Auto-computed; payout batch needs a checker | Floor: pay within 5 working days of resolution | CIR 35(9) |
| Rejection ageing escalation | Tenant | Nodal officer after one cycle, CCO after two | Choice (may tighten) | RR7.1 |
| DQI alert threshold | Format | File DQI below the tenant target or 5 points below the trailing 3-cycle average | Choice | [REC] |

### RR9.2 Menu and screens

| Path | Screen | Key actions | Filters, bulk actions and exports | Visible to |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Compliance › Returns › Calendar` | Month and list views of due instances with a RAG status per entity | Open run; assign owner; mark not applicable (CCO approval) | Entity, regulator, portal, family, owner, state, overdue; bulk assign owner; export XLSX and ICS; saved views | Return makers (own families), checkers, signatories, CCO |
| `Compliance › Returns › Run` | Detail with an RR3.1 stepper and tabs: snapshot, validation (rule ID, REQ-ID, cell, explain-why text, fix link), reconciliation, lineage drill-down, approvals, package, upload checklist, acknowledgement, revisions, variances | Only the actions valid for the current state: freeze, generate, validate, reconcile, submit, approve or reject with reason, sign off (step-up), download package, record upload, upload acknowledgement, request revision | Export the evidence pack (ZIP per RR5.2) | As above; auditors and supervisors read-only (workspaces L, V, W) |
| `Compliance › Returns › Approvals` | My checker and signatory queue with SLA countdown | Approve, reject, open run | Bulk accept is offered only for NIL returns; sign-off is always one run at a time | Checkers, signatories |
| `Compliance › Returns › Registry` | Definitions, versions, applicability matrix per entity, variance register, unverified rows | New-version wizard (upload template → hash → cell-map diff → independent reviewer approval); verify a row; record a variance | Export the applicability matrix (PDF, XLSX) for the CCO and auditors | Compliance administrator, CCO; others read-only |
| `Compliance › Returns › Data dictionary` | Elements, cell maps, lineage, DQ metrics and issues | Propose element or map change (maker-checker); raise DQ issue | Filter by return, owner, DQ status; export | Data owners, compliance administrator |
| `Compliance › Returns › Portal filings` | Queues for DAKSH items, PRAVAAH applications, FIU-IND batches, CKYCR, CERSAI, SFT and FATCA/CRS | Per-portal guided checklist; acknowledgement capture | Due, state, owner; export | Per portal role; FIU-IND items only for the AML team and Principal Officer |
| `Compliance › Returns › RBI queries` | `supervisory_item` register and revision assessments | Draft response, link returns, decide `REVISE` or `NO_REVISION` (CCO) | Source, due, owner, state; export | Compliance, CCO |
| `Compliance › Returns › Dashboard` | On-time rate, overdue, next 7 days, open variances, revisions by reason, DQ trend | Drill to runs | Period, entity; export PDF for the Board pack | CCO, management (workspace M) |
| `Compliance › Credit Bureaus › Cycles` | Board of cycles by CIC, format and reference date with state, due date and counts | Freeze, build, approve (nodal officer), record transmission, view acknowledgement | CIC, format, cycle code, state, late; export | Bureau operations, nodal officer, CCO |
| `Compliance › Credit Bureaus › Cycle` | Counts by segment, status and DPD bucket; variance to the last cycle; held-back records; file hashes per CIC | Approve or reject (reason); re-send after a transmission failure | Export the count summary | As above |
| `Compliance › Credit Bureaus › Rejections` | Queue by uniform reason code with ageing | Open the source record to fix; assign | Reason, CIC, owner, ageing; bulk assign; export | Bureau operations, data owners |
| `Compliance › Credit Bureaus › Disputes` | Dispute queue with 21-day and 30-day clocks; compensation calculator; payout batches | Acknowledge, decide (standard reason), send correction, record CIC confirmation, send rectified CIR, approve payout | Clock status, channel, CIC; export | Grievance team, nodal officer; Grievance Redressal Officer |
| `Compliance › Credit Bureaus › Data quality` | File and CI-level DQI trends; half-yearly review builder | Generate the review report for top management | Segment, CIC, period; export | Nodal officer, CCO |
| `Compliance › Credit Bureaus › Formats` | Format packs, catalogues, `format_issue` list | Activate a pack version (maker-checker) | Export | Bureau operations, compliance administrator |
| `Compliance › Credit Bureaus › Nodal and alerts` | Nodal-officer register; borrower alert delivery and "no contact" list; WD/LD monthly files (RR8.4) | Change nodal officer (opens the 5-day tasks); export no-contact list for awareness campaigns | Export | Nodal officer, CCO |

- **Empty and error states** say what to do next, for example "No template uploaded for DNBS02 version 2026.10: download it from Sankalan and upload it here", "Snapshot unavailable: COB for 30 Sep 2026 has not completed", "Sign-off blocked: 2 WARNINGs not accepted by the checker".
- **Explain-why:** every block or refusal shows the rule ID, the REQ-ID with its citation and the screen that fixes it.
- **Notifications:** in-app and email for assignments, SLA breaches and alert stages, with a daily digest; reminders never contain amounts or borrower data.
- **Keyboard shortcuts** on queues and the run screen: `j`/`k` next and previous item, `a` approve, `r` reject with reason, `/` search, `g c` calendar; every action also has a button.
- **Accessibility:** WCAG 2.2 AA (contrast, focus order, keyboard-only operation, status never shown by colour alone).

### Acceptance tests

- Setting the reconciliation tolerance above the template rounding unit returns 403 `floor_violation` citing SR para 14; tightening it is accepted after checker approval.
- With `share_return_status_with_hub` off, no return event reaches the Operations Hub subscription; switching it on is logged with the approver.
- A user who is maker on a run sees no approve or sign-off button for it, and a direct API call returns 403 `sod_conflict`.
- An attempt to switch off reporting to one of the four CICs for an NBFC CI is refused with CIR para 6 cited.
- The run screen is fully operable by keyboard and passes an automated WCAG 2.2 AA check.

# PART 7C — ACCOUNTING FRAMEWORKS, FINANCIAL STATEMENTS, TAXATION AND STATUTORY AUDIT TRAIL

**Purpose.** Keep each tenant entity's books under the correct accounting framework for its type and year, run the prudential overlay alongside the statutory books, produce statutory statements and regulatory disclosures, prepare GST and income-tax outputs, connect to Tally Prime and ERPs without making them the book of record, and meet the Companies Act audit-trail, backup and retention rules. This Part extends M10 (the double-entry core stays there): AC1–AC3 extend M10 items 1, 5 and 9; AC4–AC5 extend item 6; AC6 extends item 10 and R12.3; AC7 extends the M19 audit trail. Part 8A.8 (FS) and Part 8A.17 (IRACP) remain the regulatory source rows.

**Applicability.** Every tenant legal entity: NBFCs of every layer, HFCs, core investment companies, ARCs, commercial banks, SFBs, UCBs, StCBs/DCCBs, credit co-operative societies, non-company entities (trusts, LLPs, partnerships, AIFs), IFSC units and group companies. The framework is resolved per legal entity per financial year (AC1). Banks and co-operatives are served through institution profiles (Part 7G); rows marked [VERIFY] are not used for statutory output until confirmed.

**Codes used.** FS, IRACP, CAP, AUD, SA, CYB, KYC, RSA, TDCR, MISC, RBC, SBR (existing); `IND-AS`, `CA13`, `ICAI`, `ICSI`, `CB-ECL`, `GST`, `ITA25`, `ITA61`, `IFSCA-FC`, `ARC`, `MSCS`, `SCS`, `NABARD`, `DPDP`, `SOC2`, `TRAI` (Part 8A.37). "CIC" alone means a credit information company; core investment companies are written out. Labels: [LAW] statute or rules, [REG] regulator instrument, [ICAI] professional guidance (recommendatory unless an SA, CARO or Rule 11(g) requirement), [REC] recommendation.

**Data owned.** Framework profile and decision log; book definitions and book-specific postings; prudential-overlay and Impairment Reserve runs; bank ECL runs; GL-to-statement line maps; statement, disclosure, consolidation and MCA payload runs; GST fee master, invoices, ITC election, IMS actions and return exports; TDS, TDS-receivable, tax-computation and borrower-certificate records; connector agents and export batches; the statutory audit-trail ledger, daily seals, backup and restore evidence, Rule 3(6) data and the retention schedule.

**Events (Integration Specification v1.1, section 6.20).** Emits `PeriodClosed`, `FinancialStatementsApproved`, `GstReturnPrepared`, `TdsStatementPrepared`, `InterestCertificateIssued`, `ControlTestResultPublished`, `EvidenceSubmitted`. Part 7B consumes `PeriodClosed` and `FinancialStatementsApproved` (DNBS10 and audited-return clocks); LawDocsComply or embedded M14 consumes all of them; Udofin consumes `InterestCertificateIssued` to show RE-signed certificates. Statements, returns and amounts travel only by document reference; events carry hashes and status. **The Operations Hub receives only `PeriodClosed` status metadata (legal entity, period, books locked; no balances or trial-balance hashes), and only where the tenant opts in** (setting `share_close_status_with_hub`, default off, AC8.1); it never receives `InterestCertificateIssued`, any amount or any tax data.

## AC1. Accounting framework applicability engine (Ind AS, AS, co-operative formats, IFRS for IFSC)

**Purpose.** Decide, with citations and a stored decision log, which framework, statement format, credit-loss regime and filing route apply to each legal entity in each year.

### AC1.1 Applicability matrix

| Entity | Framework | Statement format | Credit-loss regime | MCA or regulator filing |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| NBFC (incl. HFC and core investment company) in Ind AS Phase I or II | Ind AS (IND-AS r.4(1)(iii)–(iv)) | Schedule III Division III + FS Directions | Ind AS 109 ECL with IRACP floor and Impairment Reserve (IRACP 34–36) | AOC-4 NBFC (Ind AS); XBRL exempt |
| NBFC outside Rule 4 | Companies (AS) Rules 2021, to the extent not inconsistent with RBI directions (FS 10) | Schedule III Division I + FS Directions | IRACP | AOC-4; XBRL exempt |
| NOFHC; NBFC with no public funds and no customer interface; BL NBFC with customer interface but no public funds | As above | Schedule III; FS Directions not applicable (FS 8(i)–(iii)) | IRACP | As above |
| ARC | Ind AS if a Rule 4 limb applies, else AS + RBI ARC norms [VERIFY: Rule 4 limb] | Schedule III Div III or I | SR NAV valuation; ARC provisioning | AOC-4 [VERIFY: XBRL] |
| Commercial bank (SCB) | AS + RBI; Ind AS deferred "till further notice" (RBI/2018-2019/146, 22 Mar 2019) | BR Act s.29 Third Schedule Form A (Schedules 1–12), Form B (13–16) | IRACP to 31 Mar 2027; **ECL from 1 Apr 2027** (RBI/DOR/2026-27/398) | XBRL exempt "till further order" |
| SFB, payments bank, LAB, RRB | AS + RBI | Third Schedule | IRACP; outside the 2026 bank ECL Directions [VERIFY] | As banks |
| UCB | AS (ICAI Large) + RBI | Third Schedule via BR Act s.56 | UCB IRACP | Not a company; RBI and Registrar |
| StCB, DCCB | AS + NABARD | Third Schedule; NABARD formats; State Act | RBI/NABARD IRAC | Registrar; NABARD |
| Credit co-operative society (state) | State Act formats; ICAI AS where the Act is silent (SCS) | Act/Registrar format | Registrar norms [VERIFY per state] | Registrar returns (Part 7B RR1.5) |
| Multi-state credit co-operative society | MSCS Act 2002 (amended 2023) and Rules (MSCS) | Rules format [VERIFY] | Per Rules [VERIFY] | CRCS |
| Non-company entity (trust, LLP, partnership, AIF trust) | ICAI AS under the ICAI scheme for non-company entities (MSME or Large) | ICAI format or SEBI format for AIFs [VERIFY] | AS; fair value for AIFs (SEBI) | Not MCA unless LLP (Form 8) [VERIFY] |
| IFSC Banking Unit | IFRS as issued by the IASB (IFSCA, 30 Jul 2021) | IFRS, USD | IFSCA IRAC | IFSCA |
| IFSCA Finance Company or Finance Unit | [VERIFY: Ind AS or IFRS]; FU follows parent GAAP with separate books | USD balance sheet (IFSCA-FC reg 6) + governance-circular disclosures (owned-fund components, off-balance-sheet, top 5 NPAs) | IFSCA prudential | IFSCA; MCA if a company |
| Group company (non-financial, e.g. Udofin) | Ind AS (listed other than SME exchange, or net worth ≥ ₹250 crore) or AS | Schedule III Div II or I | Simplified ECL on receivables (Ind AS) | AOC-4; XBRL if triggered |

### AC1.2 Rule pack details

- **Ind AS for NBFCs [LAW]** (Companies (Indian Accounting Standards) Rules 2015, as amended 2016):
  - **Phase I, r.4(1)(iii):** periods beginning on or after 1 Apr 2018 (comparatives for 31 Mar 2018) for NBFCs with net worth ≥ ₹500 crore, and their holding, subsidiary, JV and associate companies.
  - **Phase II, r.4(1)(iv):** periods beginning on or after 1 Apr 2019 for NBFCs listed or being listed (in India or abroad) with net worth < ₹500 crore, and unlisted NBFCs with net worth ₹250 crore to < ₹500 crore, and their group companies.
  - **Net worth test:** standalone net worth on 31 Mar 2016; a later entrant uses its first audited statements; a later threshold-crosser applies from the following period (IND-AS r.4).
  - **NBFC definition (r.2(g)):** refers to RBI Act s.45-I(f) and lists 13 types incl. HFCs and core investment companies; ARCs are not listed.
  - Voluntary adoption is not available to NBFCs [VERIFY]; once on Ind AS, an entity cannot revert (r.4(2)) [VERIFY: numbering]; in a mixed group each entity follows its own roadmap but supplies Ind AS figures for the parent's consolidated statements.
- **Non-NBFC companies [LAW; VERIFY]:** Phase I from FY 2016-17 (net worth ≥ ₹500 crore); Phase II from FY 2017-18 (listed other than SME exchange, or net worth ≥ ₹250 crore); voluntary adoption allowed.
- **Banks [REG]:** Ind AS deferred for SCBs (excluding RRBs) by RBI/2018-2019/146, DBR.BP.BC.No.29/21.07.001/2018-19. The RBI (Commercial Banks – Asset Classification, Provisioning and Income Recognition) Directions, 2026, RBI/DOR/2026-27/398, 27 Apr 2026, bring ECL without Ind AS from **1 Apr 2027** for banking companies other than SFBs, PBs and LABs, plus nationalised banks and SBI (paras 2–4) (AC2.6).
- **ICAI scheme for non-company entities [ICAI]** (periods from 1 Apr 2024, superseding the March 2021 scheme): **MSME** if all hold: not listed or being listed; not a bank, FI or insurer; turnover (excluding other income) ≤ ₹250 crore; borrowings never above ₹50 crore in the preceding year; not a holding or subsidiary of a non-MSME. Otherwise **Large** (all banks and FIs are Large). MSME relaxations: AS 3, 17 and 24 do not apply; AS 18 and 28 do not apply where turnover ≤ ₹50 crore and borrowings ≤ ₹10 crore; AS 15, 19, 22 (current tax only), 28 and 29 relaxed.
- **IFSC [REG]:** IBUs use IFRS from the period starting 1 Oct 2021 if the parent already reports under IFRS, otherwise from 1 Apr 2022 (IFSCA F.No.383/IFSCA/IFSC RULE BOOK/IFRS/IRAC NORMS/1); IFSCA may allow parent GAAP case by case. USD books for IFSC companies were recommended by the 2022 IFSCA working group (recommendation only).

### AC1.3 Rules engine

**Inputs:** `legal_form`, `regulator_class`, `layer`, `deposit_taking`, `listed` (exchange, country, SME flag), `net_worth` with as-of date, group links (holding, subsidiary, JV, associate) with each linked entity's framework, `first_ind_as_year`, and for non-company entities `turnover_prev`, `max_borrowings_prev`, `is_bank_fi_insurer`, `parent_is_non_msme`.

```text
if regulator_class in {SCB, SFB, PB, LAB, RRB, UCB, StCB, DCCB}:
    fw = AS_BANK; fmt = BR_THIRD_SCHEDULE
    loss = (regulator_class == SCB and fy >= "2027-28") ? RBI_BANK_ECL_2026 : IRACP_BANK
elif regulator_class == IFSC_IBU: fw = IFRS; ccy = USD
elif regulator_class in {IFSCA_FC, IFSCA_FU}: fw = PROFILE_SETTING [VERIFY]; ccy = USD
elif legal_form == COMPANY:
    if first_ind_as_year != null: fw = IND_AS                       # sticky
    elif nbfc_type in IND_AS_RULE_2G_LIST:                           # incl. HFC, core investment co; ARC excluded [VERIFY]
        if nw_2016 >= 500cr or group_link(PHASE_I): fw = IND_AS from FY2018-19
        elif listed or 250cr <= nw < 500cr or group_link(PHASE_II): fw = IND_AS from FY2019-20
        else: fw = AS_2021                                           # no voluntary adoption [VERIFY]
    else: non-NBFC roadmap; voluntary allowed
    fmt = IND_AS ? (nbfc ? SCH3_DIV3 : SCH3_DIV2) : SCH3_DIV1
elif legal_form == COOPERATIVE: fw = ACT_FORMAT + ICAI_AS(size(entity))
else: fw = ICAI_AS; size = MSME if all(msme_tests) else LARGE
```

**Outputs per entity-year:** framework, currency, statement set, disclosure packs (FS C.1 all; C.2 ML/UL; C.3 UL), loss engines to run (IRACP always for RBI-regulated lenders; Ind AS ECL; bank ECL), CARO flag, MCA form route, s.204 secretarial-audit flag (Part 7F), IAF flag (deposit-taking or ≥ ₹5,000 crore; Part 7D), cyber chapter (CYB Ch III, IV or V), statutory-audit band (< ₹1,000 crore; ₹1,000–15,000 crore; > ₹15,000 crore; SA 11–15).

**Decision log.** Each run stores inputs hash, rule-pack version, result, citations and approver (CFO). The engine re-runs at each FY start and on any change of layer, listing, net worth or group links. A change of framework mid-year is blocked; transition to Ind AS opens a transition project (opening balance sheet, Ind AS 101 elections, comparative restatement).

### Acceptance tests

- An unlisted NBFC with net worth ₹320 crore on 31 Mar 2016 resolves to Ind AS from FY 2019-20, Division III, with IRACP and ECL engines on.
- A listed NBFC with net worth ₹40 crore resolves to Ind AS Phase II; an unlisted NBFC with ₹40 crore and no Ind AS group link resolves to AS 2021, Division I.
- An SCB resolves to IRACP for FY 2026-27 and to bank ECL for FY 2027-28; an SFB never resolves to bank ECL.
- A partnership with turnover ₹180 crore and peak borrowings ₹60 crore in the preceding year resolves to ICAI Large.
- An entity with `first_ind_as_year` set cannot be resolved to AS by any input change.

## AC2. Multi-framework ledger and prudential overlay

**Purpose.** One journal, several books: statutory books under the resolved framework, a prudential memo book for IRACP, a tax memo book, and parallel books where a transition or a group parent requires them, all reconciled.

### AC2.1 Book model

| Book | Basis | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `STAT` | Ind AS, AS 2021, ICAI AS, bank AS, co-operative Act format or IFRS (AC1) | Statutory statements, MCA filings, audited returns |
| `PRUD` | IRACP (memo): borrower-wise classification, NPA income on realisation (IRACP 38), standard, restructured and NPA provisions | Impairment Reserve test, FS 21(15) table, DNBS returns, CRAR inputs |
| `TAX` | ITA25 (memo): s.56 receipt basis for NPA interest of notified classes, s.31 deductions | Tax computation and Form 26 data (AC5) |
| `PARALLEL` (optional) | Bank ECL in parallel run before 1 Apr 2027; IFRS for a foreign parent; Ind AS transition shadow | Transition and group reporting |

- **Mechanics:** postings carry `book_set`; shared postings apply to every book; book-specific adjustments live in adjustment layers (e.g. Ind AS EIR amortisation in `STAT`, NPA interest derecognition in `PRUD`). Trial balance per book = base + layer. Periods lock per book.
- **Reconciliation:** a book-difference report explains every `STAT` vs `PRUD` difference by cause (EIR, ECL vs IRACP, income derecognition, fair value) and feeds the FS 21(15) table and DNBS03.
- **Single source:** the loan sub-ledger (M6) feeds all books; no book is re-keyed.

### AC2.2 Ind AS 109 governance gates (extends M10 item 5; FS 12(1))

- Board-approved business-model policy, policy on sales out of amortised cost and ECL methodology are recorded with version and Board date; a model or parameter change needs Board approval and a sensitivity file and cannot be back-dated to smooth profit (FS 12(1)(i)–(iii), from RBI/2019-20/170, 13 Mar 2020).
- Management overlays need Audit Committee approval (FS 12(1)(iii)); SICR rebuttal above 30 DPD needs a case file and Audit Committee minute reference and is impossible above 60 DPD (FS 12(1)(v)); a > 90 DPD account outside Stage 3 needs Audit Committee approval and feeds the disclosure count, outstanding and overdue amounts (FS 12(1)(iv)).
- **Ind AS amendments 2026** (Companies (Ind AS) Amendment Rules 2026, G.S.R. 725(E), 12 Aug 2026, mostly for periods from 1 Apr 2026) [LAW]: SPPI assessment for ESG-linked and contingent-feature loans; look-through for non-recourse and tranched assets; an accounting-policy option to derecognise liabilities settled through electronic payment systems before settlement date; new Ind AS 107 disclosures; retrospective application without restating comparatives. Implement as a rule-pack version with a product-level SPPI questionnaire and a policy election record. Ind AS 118 (IFRS 18) is under formulation; no build.

### AC2.3 Impairment Reserve floor job (IRACP 34–36; FS 12(2))

Runs quarterly (and on demand) for Ind AS NBFC tenants:

1. Compute ECL (Stages 1–3, incl. off-balance-sheet exposures and guarantees) from `STAT` and IRACP provisions (standard, restructured, sub-standard, doubtful, loss) from `PRUD`, by asset class.
2. `shortfall = max(0, IRACP_total − ECL_total)`; `appropriation = shortfall − existing_impairment_reserve` (if positive).
3. Propose the journal: Dr profit after tax (appropriation), Cr Impairment Reserve. The CFO approves; the posting is below PAT in `STAT`.
4. **Release is blocked** without a DoS permission reference attached (IRACP 35).
5. Emit FS 21(15) rows (asset classification × stage: gross carrying amount, loss allowance, net carrying amount, IRACP provision, difference) and tag the reserve as excluded from regulatory capital (never CET1) and from net NPA (IRACP 36; CAP).

### AC2.4 DLG in ECL (IRACP 36A–36C, from 13 Feb 2026)

DLG cover may be considered in ECL at every stage only if it is integral to the loan's contractual terms and not recognised separately; disclosure follows Ind AS 1; ECL is recomputed after each invocation because the cover reduces. Build: `dlg_integral` flag per arrangement with legal-review evidence; cover allocation to the covered pool; recompute on `DLGInvocationSettled` (existing event); CLA DLG ledger kept separate (TDCR 123).

### AC2.5 Capital interface

Capital tags flow to Part 7E (RK3): Impairment Reserve excluded; net unrealised fair-value gains excluded from owned funds; 12-month ECL eligible as Tier 2 within limits; lifetime ECL reduces RWA (CAP 16; RBI/2019-20/170).

### AC2.6 Bank ECL module (SCB tenants; RBI/DOR/2026-27/398)

- **Staging:** Stage 1 12-month ECL; Stages 2–3 lifetime. SICR presumed above 30 DPD; for revolving facilities, continuous excess over limit or drawing power up to 60 days; rebuttal needs Board-approved documentation (paras 25, 33–36). Stage 3 assessed per borrower, Stage 2 per facility (para 76).
- **Measurement:** book fair-valued on 1 Apr 2027 with the difference to opening retained earnings (para 19); new loans at amortised cost with EIR (para 20); legacy loans migrate to EIR by 31 Mar 2030 (paras 21, 50) with a migration tracker.
- **Floors (para 82):**

| Category | Stage 1 | Stage 2 |
|---|---|---|
| Secured retail and corporate | 0.40% | 5% |
| Unsecured retail | 1% | 5% |
| Individual housing | 0.25% | 1.5% |
| Gold loans | 0.40% | 1.5% |

  Stage 3 floors rise by vintage to 100% (vintage clock per borrower).
- **Capital (para 75):** Stage 3 ECL counts as specific provisions; Stage 1/2 ECL and overlays as general provisions toward Tier 2.
- **Transition (paras 107–110):** ECL in excess of IRACP charged to opening earnings; optional CET1 add-back factor f = 0.8, 0.6, 0.4, 0.2 for FY 2027-28 to FY 2030-31.
- **Parallel run:** at least two quarters of `PARALLEL` book before go-live [REC]. Floors never apply to SFBs, PBs, LABs, RRBs or UCBs.

### AC2.7 Other institution overlays

- **ARCs [REG]:** SRs valued at NAV within the rating's recovery range; SR yield and upside recognised only after principal is fully redeemed; SRs more than 20% below acquisition value disclosed (Master Circular RBI/2022-23/03, paras 1(2), 12–14); management fee on NAV at the lower end of the recovery range, capped at acquisition value, unrealised fees reversed after 180 days (ARC Directions 2025 paras 142–144) [VERIFY: paragraph numbers].
- **Co-operatives:** statutory appropriations from surplus (reserve fund, education fund and others) are configured per Act and by-laws [VERIFY per Act]; provisioning per Registrar, NABARD or RBI UCB norms.
- **IFSC:** USD functional and presentation currency; an INR account only for administrative and statutory expenses (IFSCA-FC reg 6); a Finance Unit's books are separate from its parent's.

### AC2.8 Period close

Extends the M10 item 9 checklist with: book-difference report signed; Impairment Reserve job approved; bank ECL floor test; DLG recompute log; intercompany eliminations prepared; tax memo book updated.

**Close state machine (per legal entity, period and book).** Each transition is a server-side command under maker-checker, idempotent on `(legal_entity, period, book, command)`.

| State | Entry condition | Owner | Allowed postings | Exit, failure and rollback |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `OPEN` | Period start | Accounts | All | Close date reached (calendar setting) → `SOFT_CLOSE` |
| `SOFT_CLOSE` | Business-date cut-off passed; COB complete | Accounts lead | Adjusting entries only, each with a reason code; operational postings dated in the period are routed to the next open period with a back-dated business date flag | Checklist complete and all reconciliations clean → `LOCK_PENDING`; a failed item stays here with an owner and due date |
| `LOCK_PENDING` | Checklist evidence attached | CFO (checker) | None | Approve → `LOCKED`; reject → `SOFT_CLOSE` with reason |
| `LOCKED` | CFO approval | System | None; corrections post in the open period as prior-period items (Ind AS 8 or AS 5) | Emits `PeriodClosed` (with `lock_version`); reopen request → `REOPEN_REQUESTED` |
| `REOPEN_REQUESTED` | Reason, impact list (returns, statements, tax filings that used the period) | CFO, with CCO concurrence where a return is affected | None | Approved → `SOFT_CLOSE` (adjusting entries only); refused → `LOCKED` |

- **Reopen floor:** a period whose audited statements are `FINAL` (AC3.1) or whose figures sit in a filed GST or TDS return is never reopened; corrections go through the current period and the return's own amendment route (GSTR-1A, correction statement). A period used by a `SIGNED_OFF` or filed RBI return may be reopened only with the CCO's concurrence, and re-locking opens a Part 7B RR5.3 revision assessment.
- **Re-lock** increments `lock_version`, recomputes the TB hashes and re-emits `PeriodClosed`; consumers treat a higher `lock_version` as superseding the earlier one.
- Late operational postings into a locked period never fail silently: the posting is accepted into the open period, tagged `back_dated`, listed on the close dashboard and, where it touches a filed return's elements, sent to Part 7B as a post-snapshot reconciliation item.

### Acceptance tests

- ECL ₹42 crore and IRACP ₹50 crore with an existing reserve of ₹5 crore → proposed appropriation ₹3 crore below PAT; with IRACP ₹40 crore → no entry and no release.
- An attempt to release the Impairment Reserve without a DoS permission reference fails.
- SICR rebuttal at 61 DPD is rejected; at 45 DPD it needs an Audit Committee minute reference.
- A bank unsecured retail Stage 2 facility with modelled ECL 3% is floored to 5%.
- A DLG invocation of ₹50 lakh on a covered pool triggers an ECL recompute; the cover balance falls by ₹50 lakh.
- `STAT` and `PRUD` trial balances differ only by items explained in the book-difference report.

## AC3. Financial statements, schedules and disclosures

**Purpose.** Produce complete, validated statutory statements and disclosures for each framework, plus the data the statutory auditor, the MCA and RBI need.

### AC3.1 Pipeline

1. Lock the trial balance per book (`PeriodClosed`).
2. Map every GL account to a statement line through a versioned `gl_line_map` per format; **no orphan accounts** (the run fails).
3. Produce balance sheet, statement of profit and loss (incl. OCI for Ind AS), statement of changes in equity, cash flow statement and notes, with comparatives (FS 19).
4. Add the regulatory disclosure packs (AC3.3) and the Schedule III datasets (AC3.2).
5. Consolidate (FS Ch IV; AC3.6).
6. Review and approve through the statement state machine below, render PDF/A, XLSX and the MCA payload, and hash all outputs.

**Statement state machine (per legal entity, financial year, book and format).** `DRAFT → TIED_OUT → CFO_APPROVED → AUDIT_COMMITTEE_REVIEWED → BOARD_APPROVED → AUDITOR_REPORT_SIGNED → FINAL → MCA_FILED_BY_HUMAN`.

- `TIED_OUT` needs every AC3.7 validation to pass; a failure returns to `DRAFT` with the rule named. Audit adjustments return the run to `DRAFT` as version n+1 and keep version n.
- `BOARD_APPROVED` records the Board meeting date and resolution reference (Part 7F); `AUDITOR_REPORT_SIGNED` records the auditor's report date and UDIN. **`FinancialStatementsApproved` is emitted once both dates are recorded**, with `framework` mapped to the Integration Specification values (`IND_AS`; `AS` for AS 2021, bank AS and ICAI AS; `COOP` for co-operative Act formats; `IFRS_IFSC`). Its audit report date starts the Part 7B DNBS10 and audited-return clocks.
- A change after `FINAL` (for example re-approval after an adjusting event) is a new version that re-emits the event with a higher version, and opens a Part 7B revision assessment for returns built on the earlier figures.
- `MCA_FILED_BY_HUMAN` records the SRN entered by the company's authorised signatory (AC3.5).

### AC3.2 Format catalogue

| Format | Basis | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Schedule III Division I | CA13 Sch III (AS) | Non-Ind AS companies incl. AS NBFCs |
| Schedule III Division II | CA13 Sch III (Ind AS, non-NBFC) | Group companies, Udofin when on Ind AS |
| Schedule III Division III | CA13 Sch III (Ind AS NBFC), G.S.R. 1022(E), 11 Oct 2018 | Ind AS NBFCs incl. HFCs and core investment companies; ratios CRAR, Tier I, Tier II, LCR |
| BR Act Third Schedule | BR Act s.29 (s.56 for co-operative banks) | Form A Schedules 1–12, Form B Schedules 13–16 with RBI notes-to-accounts directions [VERIFY: 2025 consolidated bank and UCB FS Directions] |
| Co-operative society | State Act or MSCS Rules format | Registrar formats [VERIFY per state] |
| ICAI non-company | ICAI formats (MSME or Large) | Trusts, LLPs, partnerships |
| IFRS (USD) | IASB IFRS | IBUs; IFSC units where profiled |

**Schedule III datasets (2021 amendment, in force 1 Apr 2021) [LAW]:** promoter shareholding; ageing of receivables, payables and CWIP; title deeds not in the company's name; loans to promoters, directors, KMP and related parties repayable on demand or without terms; benami proceedings; wilful-defaulter status; transactions with struck-off companies; charges not registered in time; layering compliance; schemes of arrangement; funds routed through intermediaries; undisclosed income; CSR; crypto. Each dataset has a source query and a "nil with evidence" option [VERIFY: no 2025–26 Schedule III format amendment].

### AC3.3 Regulatory disclosures (extends Part 8A.8)

The FS disclosure engine (M10 item 9; 8A.8) is extended with datasets that tie to source modules: gold and silver loans and auctions (RBC; Part 7A R10); project finance and DCCO; non-fund-based facilities; co-lending partner list and notes (TDCR 126–127); securitisation and transfers (SEC 114; TDCR 93); restructuring; sectoral and intra-group exposures; related parties and loans to directors and senior officers (FS 21(9), 21(9A), 21(11)); complaints (from M15); liquidity and LCR (from Part 7E RK4); concentration (RK5); NPA movement (from `classification_history`); IRACP vs Ind AS table (AC2.3); > 90 DPD not impaired (AC2.2). Every dataset carries a tie-out rule to its source run.

### AC3.4 CARO 2020 data pack

CARO 2020 applies to NBFCs and other companies except banks, insurers, s.8 companies, OPCs and small companies [LAW]. Finbyx assembles evidence per clause:

| Clause | Finbyx data |
|---|---|
| 3(ii)(b) | Returns and statements filed with lenders (borrowings module) vs books |
| 3(iii) | Loans, guarantees, investments; (a) and (e) do not apply where the principal business is lending |
| 3(ix) | Defaults on borrowings, wilful-defaulter status, end-use of term loans and short-term funds |
| 3(xi) | Frauds (fraud module), s.143(12) reports, whistle-blower complaints (GOV 38) |
| 3(xiv) | Internal audit reports considered (Part 7D) |
| 3(xvi)(a)–(d) | s.45-IA registration required and held; NBFI or HFC activity without CoR; core investment company status and continued compliance; number of core investment companies in the group. Includes the principal-business-criteria computation (> 50% financial assets and income [VERIFY]) (SBR 38; MISC 21) |
| 3(xix) | Ability to meet liabilities: ALM maturity profile (Part 7E RK4) |
| 3(xx), 3(xxi) | CSR unspent amounts; qualifications in group companies' CARO reports |

The NBFC Auditor's Report Directions checklist (AUD 6–12; Part 8A.15) and the exception-report register are produced in Part 7D (AU5) from the same data.

### AC3.5 MCA filing data

- **Forms:** AOC-4 and AOC-4 CFS for non-Ind AS and non-NBFC companies; **AOC-4 NBFC (Ind AS) and AOC-4 CFS NBFC (Ind AS)** for Ind AS NBFCs (notified 30 Jan 2020; substituted by the Companies (Accounts) Second Amendment Rules 2025, 30 May 2025, in force 14 Jul 2025) [LAW].
- **XBRL:** **NBFCs are exempt from XBRL filing** irrespective of whether Schedule III applies (MCA XBRL FAQs); banking companies exempt "till further order". Never generate XBRL for an NBFC; generate the AOC-4 NBFC (Ind AS) data payload instead [VERIFY: whether that form takes an XBRL instance or structured web-form data]. Non-NBFC group companies follow the XBRL triggers (listed; paid-up capital ≥ ₹5 crore; turnover ≥ ₹100 crore; or Ind AS) [VERIFY].
- **Board's report data** (Rule 8 as amended 2025: POSH complaint counts, maternity-benefit compliance statement) is supplied to Part 7F (GV3); the Rule 3(6) statement comes from AC7.
- Filing on MCA V3 is done by the company's authorised signatory; Finbyx produces the payload, attachments and checklist only.

### AC3.6 Consolidation

All subsidiaries are consolidated; any omission is logged with reasons for the auditor (FS Ch IV). AS subsidiaries of an Ind AS parent supply Ind AS figures through mapping adjustments; intercompany balances and transactions (including group co-lending, servicing fees and Udofin LSP fees) are matched and eliminated with break reports.

### AC3.7 Validations (blocking unless stated)

Balance sheet balances; cash flow reconciles to cash movement; provisions shown separately and not netted (FS 13–15); IRACP vs Ind AS table ties to the ECL and IRACP runs; NPA movement ties to `classification_history`; Annex I schedule (FS 20) ties to the balance sheet; CRAR in the notes equals DNBS03 and the capital run; every C.2 item present for ML/UL or marked not applicable with zero in both years; Schedule III datasets present or evidenced nil; comparatives present (FS 19); FS finalised within 3 months of 31 March (FS 9) — warning at 60 days.

### Acceptance tests

- A GL account without a line mapping blocks the statement run and names the account.
- An Ind AS NBFC produces Division III statements, the AOC-4 NBFC (Ind AS) payload and no XBRL file.
- CRAR in the notes differing from DNBS03 by 0.01 percentage points blocks approval.
- The consolidated statements of a group with one AS subsidiary show the Ind AS adjustment schedule and a nil omission log.
- `FinancialStatementsApproved` starts the DNBS10 and audited-return clocks in Part 7B when the auditor's report signing date is recorded.

## AC4. GST engine and return exports

**Purpose.** Apply the correct GST treatment to every fee and charge, keep ITC compliant, and produce validated return files for human filing. Extends M10 item 6.

### AC4.1 Fee master and treatment

Each `charge_definition` carries `gst_treatment`, SAC, place-of-supply rule and an evidence reference:

| Treatment | Applies to | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| `EXEMPT_INTEREST` | Interest or discount on loans, advances and deposits | GST: Notification 12/2017-CT(Rate), entry 27(a) [VERIFY: entry wording]; credit-card service charges are excluded from the exemption |
| `TAXABLE_18` | Processing, documentation, foreclosure, cheque or mandate bounce, service and other fees | 18%, SAC 9971 [VERIFY: SAC per fee; bounce and foreclosure after Circular 245] |
| `PENAL_NO_GST` | Penal charges levied under the RBI penal-charges framework (RBC 30) | CBIC Circular 245/02/2025-GST, 28 Jan 2025, relying on Circular 178/10/2022-GST; a fee labelled "penal" that does not meet RBC 30 stays taxable |
| `PURE_AGENT` | Stamp duty, registration and similar costs recovered at actuals | CGST Rules r.33 conditions recorded per charge |
| `CO_LENDING_SPREAD` | Spread or servicing fee retained by the originator under a CLA | Unresolved: the Department of Revenue rejected an industry request to remove 18% GST (Feb 2025); FIDC treats the spread as interest, the government as a servicing fee. Default `TAXABLE_18` unless the tenant records an owner decision with a written tax opinion [REC] |

- The product factory (M19, Part 6) cannot activate a charge without a treatment; a change of treatment is versioned and prospective.
- RCM on legal, recovery-agent and tribunal fees follows R11.3 and R12.2.

### AC4.2 Invoices

- Tax invoices and credit or debit notes per GSTIN, with series per registration and financial year.
- **E-invoicing does not apply** to banking companies and financial institutions including NBFCs (CGST Rules r.48(4); Notification 13/2020-CT as amended) [LAW]. The IRP adapter stays available for non-exempt group entities and Udofin (general threshold ₹5 crore AATO from 1 Aug 2023, Notification 10/2023).
- Consolidated or periodic invoice documents for financial services where permitted (CGST Rules r.54(2)) [VERIFY].

### AC4.3 Input tax credit

- **Annual election** (GST: CGST Act s.17(4) with Rule 38): either proportionate reversal under s.17(2) with Rules 42–43, or **50% of eligible ITC each month**, the other 50% lapsing. The election is irrevocable for the financial year; ITC on supplies from a registration with the same PAN is outside the 50% restriction; reported in GSTR-3B Table 4B(1).
- The election is recorded with CFO approval before the first GSTR-3B of the year and locks for the year.
- **IMS (live from 14 Oct 2024):** each inward invoice is accepted, rejected or kept pending with maker-checker; no action is deemed acceptance and drives GSTR-2B; alert before the GSTR-2B cut-off [VERIFY: cut-off date]. Purchase-register-to-2B matching with mismatch tasks.

### AC4.4 Return exports

| Return | Content | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| GSTR-1 | Outward supplies (B2B, B2C, exempt, credit/debit notes); HSN Table 12 with separate B2B and B2C tabs, 4-digit HSN up to ₹5 crore AATO and 6-digit above (Phase III from the Feb 2025 period) | JSON per the GSTN offline-tool schema |
| GSTR-1A | Amendments to the current period's GSTR-1 after filing | Only route to correct auto-filled liability |
| GSTR-3B | Summary return; Table 3 auto-populated and hard-locked from the July 2025 period; Table 4 ITC incl. 4B(1) reversal under the 50% option | Corrections only through GSTR-1A |
| GSTR-9 | Annual return | From books, GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B |
| GSTR-9C | Reconciliation statement, self-certified where AATO exceeds ₹5 crore [VERIFY] | Books-to-return reconciliation workpapers |

- **Time bar:** returns cannot be filed more than 3 years after their due date (portal validation since July 2025); the calendar flags any open period approaching the bar.
- **Filing:** an authorised user files on the GST portal with EVC or DSC, or through a GSP/ASP the tenant contracts, where the taxpayer enables API access by OTP for a time-limited session [VERIFY: GSTN developer documents]. Finbyx never stores GST portal credentials or OTPs.
- **Reconciliations:** books vs GSTR-1 by month; GSTR-3B liability vs GSTR-1; 2B vs purchase register; ITC reversal computation; RCM liability vs vendor invoices.
- **Return workflow (per GSTIN, period and return):** `DATA_FROZEN → GENERATED → SCHEMA_VALIDATED → RECONCILED → CHECKER_APPROVED` (emits `GstReturnPrepared`) `→ FILED_BY_HUMAN` (ARN and filing date recorded) `→ CLOSED`. A schema or reconciliation failure returns to `GENERATED` after a fix at source; a difference found after filing opens a GSTR-1A amendment (current period) or a next-period adjustment, never an edit of the filed package; a filing not recorded by the due date raises a compliance issue and starts the late-fee and interest computation.

### Acceptance tests

- A loan with ₹10,000 interest, ₹2,000 processing fee and ₹500 penal charge under the RBC 30 policy generates GST only on ₹2,000.
- A co-lending servicing spread without an attached opinion is invoiced at 18%.
- Choosing the 50% ITC option in April blocks any change until the next 1 April; same-PAN ITC is excluded from the 50% computation.
- No IRN request is ever made for an NBFC GSTIN; a non-exempt group GSTIN above ₹5 crore AATO generates IRN requests.
- GSTR-1 JSON passes the GSTN offline-tool schema validation; a B2C HSN row in the B2B tab fails.
- An attempt to change a filed GSTR-3B Table 3 value is redirected to a GSTR-1A amendment.

## AC5. Income-tax Act 2025: TDS, SFT, tax audit data and certificates

**Purpose.** Meet the lender's income-tax obligations under the Income-tax Act 2025 (in force 1 Apr 2026) and the Income-tax Rules 2026, and give borrowers correct certificates. Section, form and table numbers are configurable data because several are taken from secondary concordances [VERIFY: official text before each go-live].

### AC5.1 Transition and concordance

- Obligations for FY 2025-26 and earlier (including statements and certificates filed after 1 Apr 2026) use the Income-tax Act 1961 forms; obligations for tax year 2026-27 onwards use the 2025 Act. The engine selects the regime by payment or credit date and tax year [VERIFY: CBDT transition FAQs].

| 1961 Act | 2025 Act | Use in Finbyx |
|---|---|---|
| s.194A interest (and 194J, 194C, 194H, 194I, 194Q) | s.393(1) Table (e.g. Sl. 5 interest; Sl. 6(iii) professional; 6(i) contractors; 1(ii) commission; 2 rent; 8(ii) goods) [VERIFY: serials and codes] | TDS deduction codes |
| s.200(3); Form 26Q | s.397(3)(b); Rule 219; **Form 140** (quarterly; due 31 Jul, 31 Oct, 31 Jan, 31 May) | Non-salary TDS statement |
| Forms 24Q, 27Q, 27EQ | Forms 138, 144, 143 | Salary (client HRMS, Part 7F GV6), non-resident, TCS |
| Forms 16, 16A, 27D | Forms 130 (s.392 salary), **131**, 133 (s.395) | TDS certificates |
| 15G/15H; Form 13 | Form 121 (s.393(6)); Form 128 (s.395) | Declarations; lower-deduction certificates |
| s.285BA; Forms 61A, 61B | **s.508; Forms 165, 166** | SFT and FATCA/CRS (Part 7B RR4.9) |
| Form 26AS | Form 168 [VERIFY] | TDS credit matching |
| s.43D | **s.56** | NPA interest on receipt basis for notified NBFC classes |
| s.36(1)(vii), (viia) | **s.31** [VERIFY: clause; NBFC cap] | Bad debts and provision deduction |
| s.44AB; Forms 3CA/3CB/3CD | **s.63; Form 26** | Tax audit |
| s.43B; ss.269SS, 269ST, 269T | s.37; ss.185, 186, 188 | Payment-basis items; cash loan, receipt and repayment limits (MISC 24 control) |
| s.24(b); s.80C; s.80E; 80EE/80EEA/80EEB; s.115BAC | **s.22; s.123** (Schedule XV); **s.129**; s.130, s.131, s.132; **s.202** | Borrower certificates |

### AC5.2 TDS the tenant deducts

- On interest paid on deposits, NCDs and borrowings, and on payments to vendors, DSAs, agencies and advocates. Thresholds, rates and lower-deduction certificates (Form 128) are data [VERIFY: NBFC-deposit and senior-citizen thresholds carried into the 2025 Act]. Form 121 declarations captured with validity year.
- Challan creation data and challan-to-deduction matching; interest on late deposit computed.
- **Form 140** quarterly statement data file (and Forms 144 and 143 where relevant) validated with the official validation utility [VERIFY: utility name]; filing and corrections by an authorised user; **Form 131** certificates generated after the statement is processed.
- **Statement workflow (per TAN, quarter and form):** `DATA_FROZEN → GENERATED → UTILITY_VALIDATED → CHECKER_APPROVED` (emits `TdsStatementPrepared`) `→ FILED_BY_HUMAN` (token or acknowledgement number recorded) `→ PROCESSED` (processing result imported) `→ CERTIFICATES_ISSUED → CLOSED`. A processing default (short deduction, late deposit, PAN error) opens a correction-statement run linked to the original, with challan and interest recomputation; certificates are re-issued only from the corrected statement.

### AC5.3 TDS suffered on interest received

Corporate borrowers deduct TDS on interest paid to the lender. Finbyx books a per-borrower TDS receivable, matches it to Form 168 credits by TAN, period and amount, and runs a chase workflow for Form 131 certificates. A short or missing credit does **not** close the borrower's interest receivable; it stays open until the credit appears or a write-off is approved.

### AC5.4 Tax computation memo book

- **s.56:** interest on NPAs taxed on receipt for notified NBFC classes (TL, UL and ML were notified under the 1961 Act by Notification 79/2023, 22 Sep 2023) [VERIFY: re-notification under the 2025 Act]; the `TAX` book applies receipt basis only where the tenant's class is notified.
- **s.31:** provision for bad and doubtful debts and bad-debt write-offs, with the NBFC limit [VERIFY]; reconciled with `PRUD` and `STAT`.
- **s.37** payment-basis items (formerly s.43B); deferred tax computation per framework.
- **Form 26 (s.63) tax audit data:** clause-wise schedules from the ledger (loans and deposits accepted and repaid in cash vs ss.185–188 limits, TDS compliance, payment-basis items, related-party payments) [VERIFY: Form 26 clause list]; delivered to the tax auditor through the Part 7D workspace.

### AC5.5 Borrower certificates

Issued by the RE, digitally signed, provisional (on request during the year) and final (after year end), per borrower and co-borrower with PAN and share:

- **Home loan:** account, sanction date and amount, purpose, property and possession date; financial-year **principal (s.123, Schedule XV)** and **interest (s.22)**; pre-construction interest and the instalment year; legacy windows under s.130 and s.131 (s.131 only where stamp-duty value ≤ ₹45 lakh) flagged by sanction date; a note that ss.129–132 deductions are unavailable under the default regime (s.202) unless the taxpayer opts out.
- **Education loan:** interest only (s.129), initial year plus 7 years; generated only if the lender meets the s.129 lender condition [VERIFY: whether an NBFC must be notified or approved].
- **Electric-vehicle loan:** s.132 for legacy sanctions only.
- `InterestCertificateIssued` is emitted per certificate. **Udofin displays RE-signed certificates and never issues tax certificates in its own name.**

### Acceptance tests

- A vendor payment dated 25 Mar 2026 uses the 1961 Act code and Form 26Q; one dated 2 Apr 2026 uses s.393 and Form 140.
- The Q1 instance of Form 140 for tax year 2026-27 is due 31 Jul 2026; the Q4 instance is due 31 May 2027.
- A borrower's ₹1,00,000 TDS deduction not visible in Form 168 keeps ₹1,00,000 of interest receivable open and creates a chase task.
- A home-loan certificate for joint borrowers in a 60:40 share splits principal and interest accordingly and carries both PANs.
- An education-loan certificate cannot be generated while the lender eligibility flag is unset.
- The `TAX` book shows NPA interest on receipt basis only for a tenant whose class is notified.

## AC6. Tally Prime and ERP connectors

**Purpose.** Push Finbyx's books to Tally Prime and ERPs that tenants keep for group consolidation or familiarity, safely and idempotently, while **Finbyx remains the book of record** (M10).

### AC6.1 Tally local agent

- **Why an agent:** the TallyPrime HTTP listener (default port 9000) accepts XML or JSON requests and Tally's documentation describes **no authentication** (help.tallysolutions.com, TallyPrime 7.0 integration). It must never be exposed to a network beyond the local host.
- **Architecture:** a signed Finbyx Connector Agent (Windows service) installed on the Tally machine. It makes **outbound-only** mutually authenticated TLS connections to Finbyx, pulls signed export batches, verifies the batch signature, and posts to Tally on `127.0.0.1:9000`. No inbound port is opened; the agent's device certificate is the only credential it holds and the tenant can revoke it.
- **Protocol:**
  - **TallyPrime 7.0 and later** (released 19 Dec 2025): native JSON ("JSONEx" recommended) with headers `content-type: application/json`, `version: 1`, `tallyrequest: Import`, `type: Data`, `id: Vouchers` or `All Masters`, optional `detailed-response`; `svCurrentCompany` is always set so data cannot land in the wrong company.
  - **Earlier releases:** XML ENVELOPE (TALLYREQUEST Import, Data, Vouchers or All Masters).
  - Exports use the `Ledger` and voucher collections for reconciliation.
- **Posting order:** groups → ledgers → cost categories and centres → voucher types → vouchers.
- **Idempotency:** each voucher carries a GUID or REMOTEID derived from the Finbyx journal ID, so a re-sent batch alters, never duplicates; the agent parses CREATED, ALTERED and ERRORS counts and line errors, retries only failed items and parks repeat failures in a dead-letter queue with the Tally error.
- **Batching:** moderate batch sizes (default 500 vouchers [REC]); Tally must be running with the company loaded, otherwise the batch waits with an alert.
- **Modes:** detailed (one voucher per Finbyx journal) or summarised (daily summary vouchers per ledger and cost centre) per tenant.
- **Reconciliation:** a daily trial-balance pull from Tally compared ledger by ledger with Finbyx `STAT`; any difference, including manual entries made directly in Tally, opens a break task. Breaks never flow back into Finbyx automatically.
- **Agent hygiene:** code-signed binary, signature-verified auto-update, heartbeat, local log shipping to the tenant audit trail, version inventory for IS audit (Part 7D AU4).

### AC6.2 Mapping

Versioned `tally_map` from Finbyx chart of accounts and dimensions to Tally groups, ledgers, cost centres and voucher types, with GST details where the tenant still uses Tally for GST filing (Finbyx's GST engine remains the recommended source [REC]). An unmapped account blocks the batch.

### AC6.3 Other ERPs

SAP S/4HANA (OData journal-entry APIs), SAP Business One (Service Layer) and Zoho Books follow the same contract (signed, numbered, idempotent batches; error parsing; daily TB reconciliation) as specified in M10 item 10 and R12.3. Generic CSV, XLSX, JSON and XML exports remain available.

### Acceptance tests

- Port 9000 is not reachable from any host other than the Tally machine in the reference deployment; the agent refuses to start if its configured Tally endpoint is not a loopback address.
- Sending the same batch twice results in one set of vouchers (ALTERED count equals the batch size on the second send).
- A batch for company A is rejected by the agent if `svCurrentCompany` does not match the company mapped to the tenant entity.
- A manual voucher entered in Tally appears as a break in the next daily reconciliation.
- A tampered batch (signature mismatch) is refused and logged.
