## AC7. Statutory audit trail, books backup and record retention

**Purpose.** Make Finbyx's books meet the Companies Act audit-trail, India-backup and retention rules and the RBI forensic-trail expectations, with evidence that auditors can test. Extends the M19 audit trail and Part 10.4.

### AC7.1 Legal requirements

- **Edit log (CA13: Companies (Accounts) Rules 2014, r.3(1) proviso, from financial years beginning 1 Apr 2023):** accounting software must record an audit trail of each transaction, creating an edit log of each change with the date of the change, and the audit trail **cannot be disabled**. Books must be accessible in India at all times (r.3(1)).
- **Daily backup in India (r.3(5)):** backups of books and papers kept electronically are taken daily on servers physically located in India, even where a copy is kept abroad.
- **Registrar statement (r.3(6)):** an annual statement with the financial statements giving the service provider's name, its internet protocol address and location, the cloud address where books are kept on cloud and, where the provider is outside India, the name and address of the person in India controlling the books (amended 5 Aug 2022, in force 11 Aug 2022).
- **Retention:** books for 8 financial years (CA13 s.128(5)).
- **Auditor reporting (Companies (Audit and Auditors) Rules 2014, r.11(g)):** the auditor reports whether the audit trail feature operated throughout the year for all relevant transactions, was not tampered with, and was preserved.
- **ICAI Implementation Guide on Rule 11(g) (revised January 2024) [ICAI]:** covers all software holding books of account, including payroll and sales sub-systems, and **database-level changes**; voucher listings, error logs and last-change-only logs are insufficient; the trail must stay on all year (technical glitches are no excuse); backups do not substitute for the trail; auditors may rely on SOC 1, SOC 2 or SAE 3402 reports for service organisations (SA 402).
- **RBI:** critical applications keep forensic-grade, non-repudiable audit trails and logs are monitored (CYB 109–111); read-only audit mode for auditors and regulators (CYB 46, 57).

### AC7.2 Design

1. **Scope inventory:** every table that forms books of account or drives postings (journals, postings, sub-ledgers, GL masters, posting rules, charge definitions, product versions, users and roles, period locks) and every sub-system holding books (client payroll in Part 7F GV6; connector batches in AC6).
2. **Capture at database level:** row-level triggers or logical-replication CDC write to an append-only `audit_log` (tenant, table, primary key, operation, before and after values, transaction ID, database user, application user, session, channel, reason code, UTC and IST timestamps). Application context is attached through session variables so that both layers are recorded.
3. **Append-only and reversal-only:** no UPDATE or DELETE on posted journal rows; corrections only by reversal and re-posting (M10 item 2); masters versioned.
4. **Hash chain and daily seal:** each `audit_log` row carries the hash of the previous row in its tenant partition; a daily seal (Merkle root per tenant per day) is signed with a KMS key and written to WORM storage (object lock in compliance mode); optional external anchoring of the seal [REC].
5. **Cannot be disabled:** there is no configuration flag for the trail; triggers are owned by a dedicated database role that application and support roles cannot assume; DDL event triggers raise a P1 alert on any attempt to drop or alter capture objects; privileged database sessions are logged (pgaudit); a gap detector compares transaction sequences and WAL positions with captured rows. Any gap or capture failure raises a P1 incident and an entry in the Rule 11(g) exception register, which the auditor sees.
6. **Access:** time-boxed read-only audit-mode role and the auditor workspace (Part 7D AU7); every read of the trail is itself logged.
7. **Daily backup in India:** database and document backups at least daily to storage in an Indian region, with location, timestamp, size and hash recorded per backup; any copy abroad is additional, never a substitute (r.3(5)); quarterly restore tests with evidence (Part 10.3; Part 7L EO3). Customer-controlled backups (Part 7J) are in addition to, not instead of, this backup.
8. **Rule 3(6) data:** per tenant per financial year, generated from the infrastructure inventory: service provider name, IP address and location, server and backup locations, cloud address and the India contact; published in Finbyx's vendor assurance pack (Part 10.6) so the tenant can file it with its financial statements.

### AC7.3 Rule 11(g) evidence pack

Software inventory of book-holding systems; configuration snapshots showing capture enabled throughout the year; daily seal verification report for the year; gap and exception register with root causes; privileged-access log review; user-access reviews; India backup log and restore-test results; Rule 3(6) data; Finbyx's SOC report or bridge letter register [VERIFY: availability; Part 7L EO5]; a draft management representation on the audit trail. The pack is produced per entity per year and on demand.

### AC7.4 Retention schedule (minimums; the longest applicable period wins)

| Record class | Minimum retention | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| Books of account and vouchers, audit trail | 8 financial years | CA13 s.128(5); ICAI guide counts from 1 Apr 2023 |
| KYC identification records | 5 years after the relationship ends | KYC 47 |
| Transaction records | 5 years from the transaction | KYC 47 |
| GST accounts and records | 72 months from the due date of the annual return | GST: CGST Act s.36 |
| Income-tax records | Per ITA25 and Rules 2026 [VERIFY] | ITA25 |
| Regulatory return evidence | 10 years from filing | [REC]; Part 7B RR5.2 |
| CIC submission files and disputes | 10 years [REC] | CICRA; CIR |
| Secretarial audit files | 8 years | ICSI CSAS-2 (Part 7D AU6) |

- **Legal hold** suspends deletion for any record linked to litigation, investigation or supervisory query.
- **DPDP:** an erasure request does not delete records whose retention is required by law; processing is restricted and the requester is told why (DPDP) [REC].
- Deletion at the end of retention is a logged, approved batch with a destruction certificate.

### Acceptance tests

- Updating a posted journal row through any database role fails; a reversal is the only path.
- Disabling or dropping a capture trigger in a test environment raises a P1 alert within 5 minutes and creates a Rule 11(g) exception entry.
- Altering one historical `audit_log` row breaks the hash chain, and the daily seal verification flags the exact row and date.
- The daily backup job writes to an Indian region every day of a 30-day test window; a missed day raises an incident.
- The Rule 3(6) statement for a tenant lists provider name, IP address, server and backup locations, cloud address and the India contact, matching the infrastructure inventory.
- A DPDP erasure request for a borrower with a loan closed 2 years ago restricts processing but retains KYC and ledger records, with a reason given.

## AC8. Settings, menus and screens (workspace I — Finance and Accounts)

**Purpose.** One finance workspace for close, statements, tax and connectors. Every setting is effective-dated, changed under maker-checker and audited; floors are enforced server-side (403 `floor_violation` with the citation).

### AC8.1 Settings and options

| Setting | Level | Default | Floor or choice | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Accounting framework | Legal entity and year | As resolved by AC1 | Floor: no manual override; a lawful voluntary choice (non-NBFC Ind AS adoption) is a recorded CFO election | AC1 |
| Close calendar | Legal entity | Soft close on working day 3, lock on working day 7 (monthly); working day 10 at quarter-end | Choice; quarter-end lock must leave time for the 21-day returns | [REC]; SR 22 |
| Reopen policy | Legal entity | CFO approval, CCO concurrence where a return used the period | Floor: no reopen after `FINAL` statements or filed GST/TDS figures | AC2.8 |
| Impairment Reserve job | Legal entity (Ind AS NBFC) | Quarterly, plus on demand | Floor: at least quarterly; release only with a DoS permission reference | IRACP 34–36 |
| ECL overlay and SICR rebuttal approvals | Legal entity | Audit Committee | Floor | FS 12(1) |
| Bank ECL parallel run | Legal entity (SCB) | 2 quarters before 1 Apr 2027 | Floor of 2 quarters [REC] | AC2.6 |
| GL line-map changes | Format version | Maker-checker | Floor: no orphan account | AC3.1 |
| FS finalisation warning | Legal entity | Day 60 after 31 March | Choice (earlier only) | FS 9 |
| Charge GST treatment | Charge definition | None (activation blocked) | Floor: every charge needs a treatment; `PENAL_NO_GST` only for RBC 30 penal charges | AC4.1 |
| Co-lending spread treatment | Co-lending arrangement | `TAXABLE_18` | Choice only with a recorded tax opinion | AC4.1 |
| ITC option | GSTIN and year | Proportionate (s.17(2)) until elected | Floor: locked for the year once the first GSTR-3B is prepared | AC4.3 |
| IMS cut-off reminder | GSTIN | 3 working days before the GSTR-2B cut-off | Choice | AC4.3 |
| TDS regime selection | Legal entity | By payment or credit date and tax year | Floor | AC5.1 |
| Borrower certificates | Product | Provisional on request; final within 15 days of year-end close [REC]; borrower's language preference; portal, email and Udofin display | Choice of channels and timing | AC5.5 |
| `share_close_status_with_hub` | Tenant | Off | Choice; when on, `PeriodClosed` metadata only | Integration Spec 6.20 |
| Tally or ERP mode | Connector | Detailed vouchers; batch 500; nightly 22:00 IST; daily TB reconciliation | Choice; reconciliation cannot be switched off | AC6 |
| Audit trail | Platform | Always on | Floor: no setting exists | CA13 r.3(1) |
| Books backup | Platform | Daily, Indian region; quarterly restore test | Floor | CA13 r.3(5) |
| Retention periods | Record class | AC7.4 minimums | Floor: may lengthen only | AC7.4 |

### AC8.2 Menu and screens

| Path | Screen | Key actions | Filters, bulk actions and exports | Visible to |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Finance › Framework` | Framework profile per entity and year; decision log; transition projects | Re-run engine; approve decision (CFO); open Ind AS transition project | Entity, year; export decision log PDF | CFO office; auditors read-only |
| `Finance › Close` | Close calendar and checklist per entity, period and book; lock and reopen requests; back-dated postings list | Tick checklist item with evidence; request lock; approve lock (CFO); request or approve reopen | Entity, period, book, state, owner; bulk assign checklist items; export checklist | Accounts team, CFO |
| `Finance › Books` | TB per book; book-difference report; adjustment layers; Impairment Reserve and bank ECL runs | Run job; propose journal; approve (CFO) | Book, cause, period; export XLSX | Accounts, CFO, CRO read-only |
| `Finance › Statements` | Statement runs with the AC3.1 state stepper; `gl_line_map` editor with an orphan-account list; disclosure tie-outs; CARO pack; consolidation and eliminations; MCA payload | Generate, validate, approve per state, record Board and audit-report dates, record SRN | Entity, year, format, state; export PDF/A, XLSX, payload | CFO office, Company Secretary; auditors read-only |
| `Finance › GST` | Charge treatment master; invoices and notes; IMS inbox; ITC election; return packages; reconciliations | Accept, reject or keep pending (maker-checker); elect ITC option; generate and approve packages; record ARN | GSTIN, period, status; bulk IMS actions with checker approval; export JSON and XLSX | Tax team, CFO |

- **Empty and error states** name the fix, for example "Statement run blocked: 3 GL accounts have no line mapping (open the map editor)", "Lock blocked: loan sub-ledger to GL break of ₹12,400 on 30 Sep 2026".
- **Smart defaults:** the close checklist pre-fills from the last period; the GST package pre-fills from the books with differences highlighted; certificate runs pre-select borrowers with interest or principal paid in the year.
- **Notifications and shortcuts** follow Part 7B RR9.2 (in-app and email, daily digest, `j`/`k`/`a`/`r` on queues); WCAG 2.2 AA throughout.

### Acceptance tests

- A reopen request for a period whose statements are `FINAL` is refused with the AC2.8 floor cited; a reopen of an unaudited month with CCO concurrence returns it to `SOFT_CLOSE`, and re-locking re-emits `PeriodClosed` with `lock_version` 2.
- With `share_close_status_with_hub` off, the Operations Hub receives no finance event; with it on, it receives `PeriodClosed` metadata without balances or hashes, and never `InterestCertificateIssued`.
- `FinancialStatementsApproved` is not emitted until both the Board date and the audit report date are recorded.
- A bulk IMS "accept" by a maker stays pending until a checker approves it.

# PART 7D — AUDIT AND ASSURANCE SUITE

**Purpose.** Part 7D gives every Finbyx tenant one assurance workspace for all audits that touch a regulated lender: internal audit and risk-based internal audit (RBIA), concurrent audit, information systems (IS) audit, IT general-controls audit, VAPT tracking, statutory and external audit support, secretarial audit and Secretarial Standards compliance. It also provides the time-bound, read-only workspaces through which auditors and supervisors (RBI, NHB, NABARD, IFSCA, Registrars of Co-operative Societies) see tenant data. Finbyx is the **tooling**; the tenant's auditors own every opinion, report and finding. Finbyx never performs internal audit for a tenant (OUT para 15; IAF para 39) and never files a return on an auditor's behalf.

**What this Part extends (do not re-specify).** Part 8A.32 (IAF: applicability, Board/ACB duties, policy, 10 parameters, HIA rules), 8A.33 (SA: auditor register, Form A/B, eligibility, tenure), 8A.15 (AUD: what the auditor reports), 8A.12 (CYB: IS audit, VA/PT, audit trails), 8A.29 and Part 10.6 (OUT: vendor access and audit rights), M14 (auditor register, compliance calendar, RMP/MAP), M12 (fraud audit timelines) and Part 7C AC7 (statutory audit trail and Rule 11(g) data). Part 7D adds the engagement engine, workpapers, sampling, evidence, findings, ATR tracking, the audit-type packs and the external-access workspace.

**Applicability.**

| Capability | Mandatory for (law or regulation) | Offered to (recommendation) |
|---|---|---|
| RBIA and HIA controls (AU1, AU3) | NBFC-D, HFC-D; NBFC-ND and HFC-ND with assets ≥ ₹5,000 crore (IAF para 3); commercial banks (Commercial Banks – Internal Audit Function Directions 2026, RBI/DoS/2026-27/413, para 3; excludes SFB, PB, LAB) | Every tenant, including BL NBFCs, MFIs, CICs, ARCs, credit co-operative societies and IFSC entities [REC] |
| Concurrent audit (AU3) | Commercial banks (Commercial Banks – Concurrent Audit Directions 2026) [VERIFY: coverage, scope and appointment — PDF not read]; UCBs, StCBs and DCCBs per RBI/NABARD instructions [VERIFY] | NBFCs and credit co-operative societies as a voluntary control [REC] |
| IS audit (AU4) | BL ≥ ₹500 crore (CYB paras 47–58); ML, UL, TL excluding CICs (CYB paras 149–154); banks per bank IT directions | BL < ₹500 crore and CICs (CYB Ch III has no IS audit mandate) [REC] |
| VAPT tracking (AU4) | ML and above: VA ≥ every 6 months, PT ≥ every 12 months for critical and DMZ systems (CYB paras 121–126); BL ≥ ₹500 crore: vulnerability management (CYB para 23) | All tenants |
| Statutory audit support (AU5) | All NBFCs including HFCs (SA para 3; non-deposit NBFCs < ₹1,000 crore may keep their extant procedure); AUD for NBFC auditors (HFC auditors excluded); CARO 2020 for companies in scope | Banks, co-operatives (state-panel or Central Registrar-panel auditors), ARCs, AIF companies |
| Secretarial audit (AU6) | Companies meeting CA13 s.204 / Rule 9 thresholds; listed entities and material unlisted Indian subsidiaries (LODR Reg 24A) | Every company tenant (SS-1 and SS-2 checks apply to all companies under CA13 s.118(10)) |
| External read-only workspaces (AU7) | BL ≥ ₹500 crore: read-only MIS for RBI supervisors and audit-mode access (CYB paras 46, 57); every NBFC tenant through the outsourcing clauses (OUT paras 34(vii)–(ix), 74(ii), 74(xii)) | All tenants, all regulators; built once for every layer (see AU7.1) |

**REQ-ID / Direction codes used.** IAF, SA, AUD, CYB, OUT, GOV, CMP, CRM, FRM, MSD, MISC, SR, FS, IRACP; from Part 8A.37: `CB-IA` (Commercial Banks – Internal Audit Function Directions 2026, RBI/DoS/2026-27/413), `CB-CA` (Commercial Banks – Concurrent Audit Directions 2026), `CA13`, `ICAI`, `ICSI`, `LODR`, `DPDP`, `MSCS`, `SCS`. Labels: [LAW] statute or rules; [REG] RBI/SEBI/IFSCA instrument; [ICAI] or [ICSI] professional standard or guidance; [REC] Finbyx recommendation; [interpretation: …] where the text is silent.

**Data owned.** Audit universe, risk assessments, plans, engagements, workpapers, samples, evidence links, findings, management responses, action items, ATRs, QAIP records, VAPT trackers, PBC lists, checklist runs, secretarial-audit files and external-access records. Source records (loans, ledger, configuration, logs) stay owned by their modules; Part 7D stores only references and hash-pinned snapshots. Events (Integration Specification v1.1, `audit` domain): `AuditEngagementOpened`, `AuditFindingRaised`, `AuditFindingClosed`, `ExternalAccessGranted`, `ExternalAccessRevoked`, `ExternalAccessUsed`; reuse `ControlTestResultPublished`, `EvidenceSubmitted` and `ComplianceIssueRaised` towards LawDocsComply.

**Design rules.** (1) Audit roles are segregated from business, risk and compliance roles in the SoD matrix (M19); auditors write only audit objects. (2) Finbyx pre-fills data, scores and samples; ratings, conclusions and opinions are decisions of named auditors (M20 may draft, a human signs). (3) Every sample and system evidence item is reproducible from a population hash, a seed and a source snapshot. (4) Methodology is versioned configuration; regulatory minimums (for example IAF para 31's ten parameters) are locked. (5) Only items derived from the Standards on Auditing, CARO 2020, Rule 11(g) or an RBI Direction are labelled "mandatory"; ICAI Technical Guides and Guidance Notes are "recommendatory"; Standards on Internal Audit follow their phased dates [VERIFY].

---

## AU1. Audit universe, risk assessment and planning

### AU1.1 Audit universe

- **Units.** Every auditable unit is an `audit_universe_unit` (existing entity) of a type: branch, fixed-point service delivery unit, hub, department, process, product, IT system, outsourced arrangement, legal entity, LSP/DLA, co-lending arrangement, securitisation SPV servicing book, group company. Risk Management and Compliance are mandatory units (IAF para 26); every critical process and IT system is a mandatory unit for system and process audit (IAF para 34).
- **Auto-population.** The universe is seeded and kept current from masters: branches and `fixed_point_unit` flags (M1; MSD para 5), products and product versions (Part 6), IT systems and critical applications (CYB para 21(1) asset inventory), outsourcing arrangements (OUT register, Part 8A.29), DLAs (CF para 18), co-lending and transfer arrangements (M11), recovery vendors (R11) and group entities (SBR). IA must be kept informed of new products and changes in reporting lines and accounting policies (IAF para 23): a new product, branch, critical system, material outsourcing, reporting-line change or accounting-policy change raises a "universe change" task to the HIA within 1 working day [REC]; the HIA adds, merges or archives units (archive needs a reason and reviewer approval).
- **Attributes.** Owner, line of defence, last audit date, last rating, policy maximum interval (IAF para 14), regulatory touchpoints (obligation references from M14), linked KRIs (Part 7E RK2), volume measures (AUM, accounts, transactions, cash handled), and open findings.
- **Coverage clock.** `next_audit_due = last_audit_end + min(policy_max_interval, frequency_for_risk_tier)`. A unit reaching the policy maximum raises a hard alert and is force-included in the next plan; exclusion requires an ACB minute reference (IAF paras 14, 32).

### AU1.2 Risk assessment engine (IAF paras 25–31)

- **Cycle.** At least annual, with ad hoc reassessment on a trigger (IAF para 25): new product, regulatory observation, fraud classification, KRI breach, change of key personnel, significant incident.
- **Matrix.** Inherent business risk × control risk (IAF para 28). Each dimension is scored on the tenant scale (default 1–5), mapped to a level H/M/L with a trend (increasing, stable, decreasing) and a documented basis (IAF para 29).
- **Ten locked parameters (IAF para 31)** with default data sources Finbyx pre-fills; the auditor confirms or overrides each with a reason:

| # | Parameter | Default pre-fill source | Default dimension |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Previous internal audit reports and compliance | Open and repeat findings, ATR ageing (AU3) | Control |
| 2 | Proposed changes in business lines or focus | Product approvals and pipeline (M14 product gate) | Inherent |
| 3 | Significant change in management or key personnel | KMP and role-change events (Part 7F GV1, M19) | Control |
| 4 | Results of regulatory examination | RBI inspection observations and RMP/MAP status (M14) | Control |
| 5 | Reports of external auditors | Statutory, IS and concurrent audit findings (AU4, AU5) | Control |
| 6 | Industry trends and macro factors | Tenant-maintained register; sector NPA trends from Part 7E RK6 | Inherent |
| 7 | Time elapsed since last audit | Universe coverage clock (AU1.1) | Control |
| 8 | Volume of business and complexity | AUM, accounts, transaction counts, products per unit | Inherent |
| 9 | Variances between actual and budgeted performance | GL vs budget (M10) | Inherent |
| 10 | Business strategy vis-à-vis risk appetite | RAS utilisation for the unit (Part 7E RK1) | Inherent |

- **Additional tenant parameters** (configurable, weighted): fraud cases and EWS alerts (FRM), complaints per 10,000 accounts (RBC), DPD migration and slippage (RK6 R17–R18), cash intensity, cyber incidents, outsourcing materiality, data-quality issues.
- **Output.** Per unit: inherent score, control score, level, trend, cell in the Risk Audit Matrix, recommended frequency and scope tier, with the basis text and parameter evidence pinned (AU2.4). The assessment is approved by the HIA and noted by the ACB.

### AU1.3 Risk Audit Matrix and plan (IAF paras 32–34)

- **Matrix.** Magnitude × frequency of risk. Planning priority follows the six cells in IAF para 32, in order: **H/H, H/M, H/L, M/H, M/M, L/H**. Units in the remaining cells (M/L, L/M, L/L) are covered only by the policy-maximum clock. The order is locked; the tenant can add tie-breakers (for example, regulatory touchpoints, open high findings).
- **Scope tiers.** Low, medium, high, very high and extremely high (IAF para 34), mapped by the tenant from the three-level assessment (IAF para 29) [interpretation: the Direction uses both scales; keep both and store the mapping].
- **Plan builder.** Inputs: ranked universe, auditor capacity (person-days by skill: credit, IT/IS, treasury, KYC/AML, forensic), mandatory inclusions (policy-maximum units, regulatory requests, ACB asks, IS audit before the statutory audit — CYB para 56), and calendar constraints. Output: a draft annual RBIA plan with unit, quarter, scope tier, days, team and skills; a capacity gap report; and a list of units deferred with reasons.
- **Approval.** HIA → (MD & CEO or WTD for information where the reporting line requires) → ACB/Board approval with minute reference (IAF para 5). Plan versions are immutable; changes in-year are plan amendments with reasons and ACB noting.
- **System and process audits.** All critical processes are flagged; system-audit findings route also to the IT Committee of the Board (ITSC; IAF para 34), and IS audit findings to the Board or ACB (CYB paras 51, 151).

### AU1.4 Policy and methodology registry

- IA and RBIA Policy (IAF 13–15), IS Audit Policy (CYB 150; ACB-approved framework for BL ≥ ₹500 crore, CYB 49) and Concurrent Audit Policy are `policy_document` records; `audit_methodology_version` holds scales, weights, scope-tier mapping, ratings, sample-size tables and templates, and every plan and engagement records the version used.
- **Methodology change control.** A new methodology version is drafted by the HIA, reviewed by a second IA reviewer, approved by the ACB (minute reference) and effective from a stated date; in-flight engagements keep their version unless the HIA migrates them with a reason. Locked regulatory items cannot be edited in any version.

### Settings and options

| Setting | Default | Level | Floor or choice |
|---|---|---|---|
| Policy maximum interval per unit type (IAF para 14) | 3 years low risk, 2 medium, 1 high [REC] | Tenant | Must exist for every unit type (floor); values are the tenant's |
| Risk scale and H/M/L cut-offs | 1–5; H ≥ 4, M 2.5–3.9, L < 2.5 | Methodology | Choice; level and trend with basis are mandatory (IAF para 29) |
| Ten IAF para 31 parameters | Locked on | Methodology | Floor; tenant parameters and weights are additions |
| Matrix priority order | IAF para 32 order | Methodology | Floor; tie-breakers are a choice |
| Scope-tier mapping (3 levels to 5 tiers) | H→high, M→medium, L→low; very high and extremely high from overrides | Methodology | Choice; mapping stored (IAF paras 29, 34) |
| Universe-change task SLA | 1 working day | Tenant | Choice [REC] |
| Minimum service period for IA staff (IAF para 8) | 3 years [REC]; off for career-auditor functions | Tenant | Board sets the value (floor: a value must exist unless career auditors) |
| Plan approval chain | HIA → MD & CEO (information) → ACB | Tenant | ACB/Board approval is a floor (IAF para 5) |

### Menu and screens

| Path (workspace L) | Screens | Key actions and rules | Visible to |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Audit › Universe` | Unit list (filters: type, owner, risk level, due date, overdue); unit detail with coverage clock; change-task queue | Add, merge, archive with reason; bulk re-assign owner; export CSV/XLSX; empty state "seed from masters" button | HIA, IA staff (edit); ACB members (read) |
| `Audit › Risk assessment` | Assessment wizard per unit (parameter by parameter with pre-fill and source link); heatmap; trend view | Confirm or override with reason; submit for HIA approval; inline "why blocked" when a parameter lacks a basis | IA staff, HIA |
| `Audit › Plan` | Plan builder (ranked list, capacity bar by skill, deferred list); plan versions; amendment queue | Generate draft; drag a unit between quarters (capacity re-checked); submit to ACB; publish only with minute reference | HIA (edit); ACB (approve, read) |
| `Audit › Methodology` | Version list; diff view; locked-item badges | Draft, review, approve, set effective date | HIA (edit); ACB (approve) |

### Acceptance tests

- Creating a product version, a branch with `fixed_point_unit = true` or a material outsourcing arrangement creates a universe unit and an HIA task within 1 working day.
- A risk assessment cannot be approved while any of the ten IAF para 31 parameters is blank or lacks a basis text; removing a locked parameter from the methodology is rejected.
- With 40 seeded units, the plan builder orders them H/H, H/M, H/L, M/H, M/M, L/H, then fills by capacity; a unit past its policy maximum appears in the plan regardless of cell.
- Risk Management and Compliance units, and a unit for every critical IT system, exist in every universe and cannot be archived.
- A methodology version approved by the ACB with a future effective date does not change in-flight engagements until the HIA migrates them with a reason.
- A plan amendment without an ACB noting reference cannot be published.

## AU2. Engagements, workpapers, sampling and evidence

### AU2.1 Engagement types and lifecycle

- **Types.** `RBIA_UNIT`, `RBIA_THEMATIC`, `CONCURRENT`, `IS_AUDIT`, `IT_GENERAL_CONTROLS`, `VAPT_REVIEW`, `STATUTORY_SUPPORT`, `TAX_AUDIT_SUPPORT`, `RULE_11G`, `IFC_ICFR`, `SECRETARIAL`, `SPECIAL_INVESTIGATION` (fraud examination per FRM), `REGULATORY_INSPECTION` (RBI/NHB/NABARD/IFSCA inspection support), `OUTSOURCED_PROVIDER_AUDIT` (tenant auditing Finbyx, Udofin or another service provider under OUT para 34(vii)), `QAIP_REVIEW`.
- **States.** `PLANNED → SCOPED → APPROVED → FIELDWORK → DRAFT_REPORT → MANAGEMENT_RESPONSE → FINAL_REPORT → ISSUED → FOLLOW_UP → CLOSED`, plus `ON_HOLD` and `CANCELLED`. `AuditEngagementOpened` is emitted on `APPROVED`; its `type` maps to Integration Specification 6.21: `RBIA_UNIT`, `RBIA_THEMATIC` → RBIA; `CONCURRENT`; `IS_AUDIT` → IS; `IT_GENERAL_CONTROLS` → IT; `VAPT_REVIEW` → VAPT; `STATUTORY_SUPPORT`, `RULE_11G`, `IFC_ICFR` → STATUTORY; `TAX_AUDIT_SUPPORT` → TAX; `SECRETARIAL`; all others → INTERNAL.

| State | Entry condition | Owner | Timer (default, configurable) | Exit and failure paths |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `PLANNED` | Plan line published or ad hoc request approved by HIA | HIA | Starts in planned quarter | → `SCOPED`; → `CANCELLED` (reason, HIA approval; ACB noting if the unit is past policy maximum) |
| `SCOPED` | Objectives, scope, criteria, team, budget days, methodology version (IAF para 33) | Engagement lead | 10 working days before fieldwork | → `APPROVED`; HIA rejection returns to `SCOPED` with comments |
| `APPROVED` | HIA approval; engagement letter for external audits | HIA | — | → `FIELDWORK` only when every member has an independence declaration |
| `FIELDWORK` | Opening meeting recorded | Engagement lead | Budget days; alert at 80% and 100% | → `DRAFT_REPORT`; re-scope returns to `SCOPED` with HIA approval and keeps all workpapers; → `ON_HOLD` |
| `ON_HOLD` | Scope limitation, auditee unavailability, data outage or a fraud signal handed to FRM | Engagement lead | 30 days, then HIA escalation | Back to the state held before; a scope limitation that persists is reported in the final report and to the ACB |
| `DRAFT_REPORT` | All workpapers reviewed; no open review notes | Lead, reviewer | 10 working days | → `MANAGEMENT_RESPONSE` after closing meeting |
| `MANAGEMENT_RESPONSE` | Draft shared with auditee | Auditee owner | 15 working days; reminders T−5, T−1; escalation to the next level at T+1 | → `FINAL_REPORT`; a missing response is recorded as "no response" and the report proceeds |
| `FINAL_REPORT` | Responses incorporated; rating confirmed | HIA | 5 working days | → `ISSUED` on eSign; HIA can return to `DRAFT_REPORT` |
| `ISSUED` | Report hash stored; distribution logged; ATR items created | HIA | — | → `FOLLOW_UP` |
| `FOLLOW_UP` | At least one finding open | Finding owners | Per finding due dates (AU3.2) | → `CLOSED` when every finding is `CLOSED`, `RISK_ACCEPTED` or `WITHDRAWN` |
| `CLOSED` | File locked (AU2.2) | HIA | — | Reopen only by HIA with reason (creates an addendum, never edits the file) |

- **Engagement record.** Type, entity, units, period under audit, objectives, scope, exclusions, criteria (obligation references from M14), timeline, team with roles (lead, member, reviewer, external expert), independence declarations per member, methodology version, budget days, engagement letter (external audits), related prior findings.
- **Independence declarations.** Every team member declares, per engagement: no operational responsibility for the unit in the last 12 months [REC], no relative in the unit, no incentive tied to the unit's results (IAF para 22). For external firms, SA paras 18–20 and LODR Reg 24A checks run in AU5 and AU6.

### AU2.2 Workpapers (ICAI SA 230; SIA 330)

- **Workpaper structure.** Reference number (index), engagement, area, procedure (from a programme template or ad hoc), objective, criteria, population and sample reference, steps performed, results, exceptions, conclusion, preparer, preparation date, reviewer, review date, review notes and their clearance, evidence links, version.
- **Review hierarchy.** Preparer → reviewer → engagement lead → HIA (for high-risk areas). A workpaper cannot be signed off with open review notes. Sign-off is an eSign event with user, time and content hash.
- **Locking and assembly.** On report issue the engagement file is assembled and locked. Default assembly deadline: **60 days from the report date** for statutory-audit-style files (SA 230, [ICAI] [VERIFY]) and **45 days from signing** for secretarial audits (CSAS-2, [ICSI]). After lock, changes are append-only addenda with reason, author and date; the original is never altered (SA 230 treatment of post-assembly changes).
- **Retention.** Default ≥ 8 years from lock for internal and secretarial files (CSAS-2; CA13 s.128(5)); statutory-auditor working papers belong to the firm (SA 230, ≥ 7 years [VERIFY]) — Finbyx keeps only what the firm uploads.
- **Programme templates.** Versioned per audit type; RBIA programmes seeded by area from the ICAI Technical Guide on Risk Based Internal Audit of NBFC (2024) [ICAI, recommendatory] — sourcing, KYC/AML, appraisal and sanction, disbursement, loan book and ECL, collections, ALM and treasury, securitisation and co-lending, outsourcing and DLAs, finance and tax, governance, fraud, information security. Steps map to obligation references so regulatory coverage is measurable.

### AU2.3 Sampling (ICAI SA 530)

- **Population freeze.** A population query (saved, versioned, parameterised) runs against a point-in-time snapshot; Finbyx stores the row count, control totals (sum of amounts), the query text and a SHA-256 of the ordered key list (`population_hash`).
- **Methods.** Simple random (seeded PRNG), systematic (random start), stratified (by amount, product, branch, DPD bucket), monetary-unit sampling, attribute sampling, top-N and key items, and judgemental (each item with a reason). The method, parameters and seed are stored; re-running with the same snapshot and seed must return the same items.
- **Size calculators.** Attribute sampling from confidence level, tolerable deviation rate and expected deviation rate; MUS from confidence, tolerable misstatement and expected misstatement. SA 530 prescribes no sizes; the tenant methodology version holds the tables [ICAI].
- **Evaluation.** Deviations and misstatements per item; projected misstatement for MUS; upper deviation limit for attribute tests; conclusion recorded by the auditor.
- **CAATs and full-population analytics.** Full-population tests are first-class procedures (CYB para 58; IAF para 7): duplicate disbursements, disbursement before sanction, KFS not issued before execution, interest accrual before disbursement value date (MSD para 7), penal charges vs policy, NPA flag timing vs IRACP day-end rule, related-party loans above materiality without Board approval (CRM 13G–13I), DLG above 5% (CF para 24), users with conflicting roles, changes to interest rates without delegated authority (CYB para 21(3)). Each test is a versioned `analytic_test` with exceptions written as sample items.

### AU2.4 Evidence linking with hashes

- **System evidence.** An evidence link points to a source record by `(source_type, source_id, source_version or event_seq)` and stores a canonical JSON snapshot of the fields used, its SHA-256, the snapshot time and the audit-trail chain position (Part 7C AC7). The auditor sees the live record and the pinned snapshot side by side.
- **Drift detection.** If the source record changes after linking, the link shows "source changed since evidence" with a diff; the evidence itself is never updated. A restatement in the ledger or loan book also flags dependent workpapers.
- **Document evidence.** Uploaded files are stored in the DMS (M16) evidence vault: WORM, SHA-256, uploader, time, classification, malware scan, PII tag. Duplicates are de-duplicated by hash but keep separate link records.
- **Integrity verification.** A "verify file" action recomputes all hashes in an engagement and checks them against the audit-trail chain; the result is itself an evidence item, exportable for the statutory auditor or supervisor.
- **PII minimisation.** Evidence snapshots store only fields the procedure needs; PAN, Aadhaar, account and phone numbers are masked unless the procedure is identity-related and the reason is logged (DPDP s.8(5) security safeguards; AU7 masking rules apply to external users).
- **LawDocsComply.** Evidence for a control test is published as `EvidenceSubmitted` and `ControlTestResultPublished` with masked sample identifiers and hashes, never raw PII (Integration Specification Part 9).

### AU2.5 Reports

- Templates per type cover objectives, scope, results, recommendations and action plans (IAF para 35), overall rating, management responses, prior-finding status and scope limitations. Draft and final versions are immutable `audit_report` records with hash; system-audit reports also route to the ITSC (IAF para 34); output PDF/A and DOCX (Part 7J).

### Settings and options

| Setting | Default | Level | Floor or choice |
|---|---|---|---|
| Independence declaration before fieldwork | On | Tenant | Floor (cannot be switched off) |
| Cooling period for a member who held operational responsibility | 12 months [REC] | Tenant | Choice (minimum 6 months) |
| Review hierarchy | Preparer → reviewer → lead; HIA for high-risk areas | Engagement type | Two-person review is a floor; HIA step is a choice |
| File assembly deadline | 60 days (statutory style), 45 days (secretarial) | Engagement type | Choice within the professional standard |
| Evidence PII masking | Masked; unmask per item with reason | Tenant | Floor |
| Sample-size tables and default confidence | 95% confidence; tolerable deviation 5% | Methodology | Choice |
| Engagement timers in the AU2.1 table | As shown | Tenant | Choice |

### Menu and screens

| Path (workspace L) | Screens | Key actions and rules | Visible to |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Audit › Engagements` | Board (kanban by state) and list (filters: type, unit, lead, state, overdue); engagement detail with tabs Scope, Team, Programme, Workpapers, Samples, Evidence, Findings, Report, Log | Create (wizard: type → unit → scope → team → declarations → submit); put on hold; re-scope; cancel with reason; bulk assign reviewer | IA team on the engagement; HIA all |
| `Audit › Engagements › Workpapers` | Index tree; workpaper editor with side-by-side live record and pinned snapshot | Add procedure from programme; raise review note; clear note; eSign sign-off (blocked while notes are open, with the reason shown) | Preparer, reviewer, lead |
| `Audit › Analytics` | CAAT library; run history; exception queue | Run with snapshot; convert exceptions to sample items; schedule continuous runs | IA staff, IS auditors |
| `Audit › Evidence` | Evidence vault search; "verify file" result | Upload (malware scan first); link; verify; export integrity report | IA team; external auditors through AU7 |

Keyboard shortcuts on workpaper and sample screens: next item, mark "no exception", raise finding, add review note.

### Acceptance tests

- Re-running a random sample with the stored snapshot and seed returns identical items; changing the seed changes them; the population hash mismatches if one row is added to the snapshot.
- A workpaper with an open review note cannot be signed off; after file lock, an edit attempt creates an addendum and leaves the original hash unchanged.
- Editing a loan after it was linked as evidence shows "source changed since evidence" and the original snapshot remains retrievable and verifiable.
- "Verify file" detects a tampered evidence file (one byte changed in storage) and raises a P1 integrity alert.
- A full-population CAAT for "interest accrual starts before disbursement value date" over a seeded book returns exactly the seeded exceptions.
- An engagement cannot move to `FIELDWORK` without independence declarations from every team member.
- An engagement `ON_HOLD` for 31 days escalates to the HIA; resuming returns it to the state it held before; `AuditEngagementOpened` for an `IS_AUDIT` engagement carries type IS.

## AU3. Internal audit, RBIA and concurrent audit

### AU3.1 HIA and function controls (extends 8A.32)

- **No outsourcing (IAF para 39).** The report-owner and engagement-lead fields accept only tenant employees with the internal-auditor role. External experts (including former employees) get a time-boxed `ia_contributor` role, can prepare workpapers but cannot sign reports or rate findings; the system requires a Board/ACB reference that expertise is unavailable in-house and a conflict-of-interest declaration. Finbyx and Infrabyx staff can never hold either role for a tenant (OUT para 15; Part 10.6 item 27).
- **HIA register.** Appointment date, reporting line (Board, ACB, MD & CEO or WTD — IAF para 42), tenure start, planned tenure, Board/ACB approval references. Tenure below 3 years at exit raises an informational flag (IAF para 41 "preferably"), suppressed where IA is run by career internal auditors (tenant flag).
- **Independence checks.** The HIA user cannot be assigned business targets or a business reporting line (IAF para 43); the role-assignment service blocks it. Internal-audit pay records (if the client HRMS module in Part 7F GV6 is used) cannot reference business-result incentive plans (IAF para 22).
- **In-camera meetings.** Where the MD & CEO or WTD is the reporting authority, the ACB/Board meets the HIA at least quarterly without senior management (IAF para 42). The calendar (Part 7F GV2) schedules them; a quarter-end without a minuted meeting raises an exception to the CS and ACB chair.
- **Full access.** The HIA and IA staff have tenant-wide read-only access to all records (IAF para 40), implemented as an internal audit-mode role with the same logging as AU7 but without time expiry; every access is logged and visible to the ACB chair on request.
- **QAIP (IAF para 6).** Annual self-assessment against a configurable checklist (Board/ACB oversight, independence, risk assessment quality, coverage, documentation, follow-up), optional external assessment, results and improvement actions to the ACB.

### AU3.2 Findings lifecycle

- **Rating.** Tenant scale (default High, Medium, Low; optional Critical) with definitions, plus root-cause category (people, process, system, policy, external), regulatory-breach flag with obligation reference, financial impact estimate, repeat flag (same root cause and unit within 24 months [REC]).
- **States.** `DRAFT → DISCUSSED → ISSUED → RESPONSE_RECEIVED → ACTION_AGREED → IN_REMEDIATION → CLOSURE_SUBMITTED → RETEST → CLOSED`, with branches `RISK_ACCEPTED`, `REOPENED` and `WITHDRAWN`.

| State | Entry condition | Owner | Timer (default) | Allowed actions and exits |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DRAFT` | Auditor records condition, criteria (obligation reference), cause, effect, rating, evidence links | Preparer | — | Edit; reviewer approval → `DISCUSSED` |
| `DISCUSSED` | Closing meeting held; auditee comments recorded | Engagement lead | — | Re-rate with reason; → `ISSUED` with the report; → `WITHDRAWN` (factual error, reviewer approval) |
| `ISSUED` | Report issued; `AuditFindingRaised` emitted | Auditee owner | Response due in 15 working days | → `RESPONSE_RECEIVED`; overdue escalates to the next level, then to the HIA and CS for the ACB pack |
| `RESPONSE_RECEIVED` | Agree, partly agree or disagree with reasons | Lead | 5 working days to accept | Disagreement unresolved → HIA decides; the ACB sees both views; → `ACTION_AGREED` |
| `ACTION_AGREED` | Action items each with owner, due date, evidence required | Owner | Due date by rating (AU4.3 defaults: Critical 15, High 30, Medium 90, Low 180 days) | → `IN_REMEDIATION` |
| `IN_REMEDIATION` | Work started | Action owners | Reminders T−7, T−1; overdue daily | Extension (next-level approver; second extension of a High finding needs ACB noting); → `CLOSURE_SUBMITTED`; → `RISK_ACCEPTED` |
| `CLOSURE_SUBMITTED` | Every action item has closure evidence (hashed evidence items or system evidence links) and an owner attestation | Owner | Auditor picks up within 10 working days | Auditor returns incomplete packs with reasons (stays in remediation clock) |
| `RETEST` | Retest assigned to an auditor who did not perform or advise on remediation | Retester | 10 working days | Pass → `CLOSED`; fail or partial → `REOPENED`; population findings need a fresh sample (AU2.3) |
| `CLOSED` | Retest pass recorded with validator role | HIA (for High and Critical) or lead | — | `AuditFindingClosed` with closure evidence hashes, validator role and closed_at; ATR item validated |
| `REOPENED` | Retest failed, or the same root cause recurs in the unit within 24 months [REC] | Owner | New due date ≤ the original rating SLA | Repeat counter increments; repeat flag shown in the ACB pack; → `IN_REMEDIATION` |
| `RISK_ACCEPTED` | Delegated authority in the risk-acceptance matrix, rationale, compensating controls, expiry (≤ 12 months) | Risk acceptor | Expiry; reminder 30 days before | RMC noting for High and Critical; at expiry it renews (same approvals) or returns to `IN_REMEDIATION`; never for a regulatory breach without CCO concurrence |
| `WITHDRAWN` | Factual error confirmed | Reviewer | — | Terminal; reason kept |

- **Corrections after issue.** A rating, criteria or due-date change after `ISSUED` creates a new finding version (reviewer approval and reason) and re-emits `AuditFindingRaised` with the new version; the earlier version stays visible. A back-dated closure is not allowed: closure date is the retest date.
- **Management responses.** Owner, agreement (agree / partly agree / disagree with reasons), action plan items each with owner, due date and evidence required.
- **Events and links.** `AuditFindingRaised` on `ISSUED` and on each new version (Integration Specification 6.21 payload: finding_id, engagement_id, rating, criteria citation, owner role, due date, masked sample references; idempotency key finding_id and version; no PII). A finding with a regulatory-breach flag also raises `ComplianceIssueRaised` to the compliance function (M14 / LawDocsComply) and, if it indicates suspected fraud, opens an FRM signal (M12) — the auditor cannot classify fraud in Part 7D.
- **Board and ACB reporting.** All pending High and Medium findings and persisting irregularities are reported to the Board/ACB (IAF para 37); closure status of findings within timelines is reported by senior management (IAF para 9); the annual consolidated major-risk view from all audits (IAF para 11) is generated from findings across AU3–AU6 and RBI inspection observations.

### AU3.3 Action Taken Reports (ATR)

- **ATR register.** One ATR per source: internal audit report, concurrent audit report, IS audit report, statutory auditor's management letter, secretarial audit observations, RBI inspection report (Risk Mitigation Plan / Monitorable Action Plan items from M14), NHB/NABARD inspection, IFSCA inspection, customer-service audit.
- **ATR pack.** For each item: observation, rating, response, action, owner, due date, status, evidence, auditor validation, ageing bucket (0–30, 31–90, 91–180, > 180 days). Generated for each ACB meeting with comparison to the previous pack; items closed without auditor validation are shown as "management-closed, unvalidated".
- **RBI inspection compliance.** Compliance submissions to RBI go through DAKSH as a guided filing (Part 7B RR4/RR5); Part 7D tracks the underlying evidence and validation only. No RBI portal credentials are stored or scripted.

### AU3.4 Related-party and other mandated periodic reviews

- **Quarterly related-party review (CRM para 13M):** a standing quarterly engagement pre-loaded with the related-party loan population (Part 7E RK5), materiality checks, approval body checks (Board or committee other than ACB — CRM 13I) and recusal evidence (13J); deviations go to the ACB (13N).
- **Other standing thematic engagements:** fraud examinations (timelines feed the FRM case clock, M12), customer-service and grievance, KYC periodic updation, outsourcing and DLA audits (OUT 34(vii)), recovery-agent audits (R11.6).

### AU3.5 Concurrent audit

- **Applicability.** Mandatory for commercial banks per `CB-CA` [VERIFY: coverage of business turnover, branch selection, appointment, rotation and reporting periodicity]; UCBs, StCBs and DCCBs per RBI/NABARD instructions [VERIFY]. Optional for NBFCs and co-operative societies [REC]. Parameters (coverage %, units, periodicity) are configuration until verified.
- **Model.** Concurrent-audit units (branches, treasury, central processing centres) with a monthly or fortnightly cycle; checklists by area (deposits, advances, treasury, KYC, revenue leakage, cash, clearing) seeded from the ICAI Manual on Concurrent Audit of Banks [ICAI, recommendatory] [VERIFY: edition].
- **Real-time feed.** A transaction queue per unit: high-value disbursements, rate overrides, waivers, reversals, user-limit breaches, manual journal entries, back-dated entries; each item is "reviewed — no exception" or raised as a finding. Daily cut-off and monthly report with a summary of irregularities and rectification status.
- **Conflict rule.** A concurrent auditor (or a firm in its network or with common partners) is not considered for appointment as statutory auditor (SA paras 18, 20); AU5 blocks the appointment, and AU3 blocks appointing the statutory auditor as concurrent auditor for one year before and after its tenure (internal assignments, SA para 19) and during it [interpretation: concurrent audit is not a para 19 "no conflict" service].
- **Revenue-leakage checks.** Interest and fee recomputation versus charge masters; GST on fees vs exempt interest (Part 7C AC4); penal-charge conformity.

### Settings and options

| Setting | Default | Level | Floor or choice |
|---|---|---|---|
| Finding rating scale | High, Medium, Low (+ optional Critical) | Methodology | Choice; High and Medium pending items always go to the ACB (IAF para 37) |
| Remediation due dates by rating | 15 / 30 / 90 / 180 days (AU4.3 defaults) | Tenant | Choice; a tighter regulatory or contractual date wins |
| Management response window | 15 working days | Tenant | Choice |
| Extensions before ACB noting (High) | 1 | Tenant | Floor: a second High extension always needs ACB noting |
| Retester independence | Different user from remediator and owner | Tenant | Floor |
| Risk-acceptance maximum term | 12 months | Tenant | Choice (≤ 12 months [REC]); regulatory-breach findings need CCO concurrence (floor) |
| Repeat-finding look-back | 24 months | Tenant | Choice |
| ATR ageing buckets | 0–30, 31–90, 91–180, > 180 days | Tenant | Choice |
| Concurrent-audit cycle and queue rules | Monthly; rules as AU3.5 | Unit | Choice until `CB-CA` parameters are verified |

### Menu and screens

| Path (workspace L) | Screens | Key actions and rules | Visible to |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Audit › Findings` | List (saved views: My open, Overdue, High and Critical, Repeat, Regulatory breach); finding detail with timeline, actions, evidence, retest | Raise; issue; record response; agree actions; request extension; submit closure pack; assign retest; accept risk; bulk reminders; export | IA; finding owners see their findings and actions only; ACB members read |
| `Audit › Findings › Retest queue` | Packs awaiting retest, with SLA | Pick up, request more evidence, pass, fail | Retesters (never the remediator) |
| `Audit › ATR` | ATR register by source; ACB pack builder; comparison with previous pack | Generate pack; freeze with hash; mark "management-closed, unvalidated" | HIA, CS; ACB read |
| `Audit › HIA and QAIP` | HIA register; in-camera meeting tracker; QAIP checklist | Record meeting with minute reference; run QAIP; actions to ACB | HIA, CS, ACB chair |
| `Audit › Concurrent` | Unit queue (daily), monthly report | Mark "reviewed — no exception" (keyboard shortcut) or raise finding; bulk clear low-value items with sampling note | Concurrent auditors |

Notifications: owners get in-app and e-mail reminders at T−7 and T−1 and daily when overdue; the HIA gets a weekly digest; empty states explain the next step ("No open findings — closed findings are under the Closed view").

### Acceptance tests

- Assigning a business target or a business reporting line to the HIA user is rejected with the IAF para 43 citation; an external expert cannot sign a report.
- A quarter passes without a minuted ACB–HIA in-camera meeting (where required): exception raised to CS and ACB chair on day 1 of the next quarter.
- A High finding with two extensions without ACB noting cannot be extended a third time; the ATR pack shows it as overdue.
- Closing a finding without retest evidence by a different user is rejected; `AuditFindingClosed` is not emitted.
- A closure pack missing evidence for one action item cannot be submitted; a failed retest moves the finding to `REOPENED`, increments the repeat counter and sets a new due date no later than the rating SLA.
- Changing the rating of an issued finding creates version 2 and re-emits `AuditFindingRaised` with version 2; a risk acceptance reaching expiry without renewal returns the finding to `IN_REMEDIATION`.
- The quarterly related-party engagement is created automatically each quarter with the loan population and flags a seeded loan above ₹5 crore (ML tenant) sanctioned by the ACB.
- A concurrent-audit firm proposed as statutory auditor is blocked with the SA para 18 citation.

## AU4. IS audit, IT audit and VAPT tracking

### AU4.1 IS audit (CYB paras 47–58 for BL ≥ ₹500 crore; 149–154 for ML and above)

- **Framework and policy.** BL ≥ ₹500 crore: IS audit forms an integral part of internal audit (CYB para 48) under an ACB-approved framework (para 49), with ACB members able to understand IS audit (para 50) and findings to the Board/ACB (para 51). ML+: ACB oversight (para 149), IS Audit Policy stating mandate, universe, periodicity and reporting (para 150, reviewed annually), ACB review of critical IT/IS issues (para 151), a separate IS audit function or resources with requisite skills (para 152), risk-based planning (para 153) and continuous auditing where possible (para 154).
- **Scope library.** Policy and oversight (para 52), BCP and DR (53), legal and regulatory compliance (54), plus CYB control families: SoD and parameter changes (21(2)–(3)), maker-checker (21(6)), audit trails (109–111), change and patch (41–42, 112), MFA (115–116), cryptography (118), STP (119–120), VA/PT (121–126), DR (127–138), incidents (139–147), data migration (99), vendor obligations (104–106).
- **Resourcing.** Internal team; external IS auditors only where internal skills are lacking (para 55) — the system records the reason and ACB approval. External IS auditors use the AU7 audit-mode workspace.
- **Timing.** Annual at least, and **preferably before the statutory audit** so reports are available to statutory auditors (para 56). The planner warns if the IS audit report date falls after the statutory audit fieldwork start in AU5.
- **Compliance.** Management responsibility, owners, timelines and authority for accepting compliance are recorded per finding (para 57); findings flow through AU3.2 and AU3.3.
- **CAATs.** Full-population IT tests (para 58): orphan and dormant accounts, privileged-access usage outside change windows, SoD conflicts, configuration drift versus approved baseline, failed-login spikes, audit-trail gaps.
- **Continuous auditing (para 154).** Scheduled analytics run daily or weekly and post exceptions to the IS audit queue; each run is a `ControlTestResultPublished` event.

### AU4.2 IT audit (IT general controls for financial reporting)

- **Purpose.** Supports the statutory auditor's understanding of the IT environment and controls (SA 315), reporting on internal financial controls over financial reporting where applicable (CA13 s.143(3)(i); ICAI Guidance Note on Audit of Internal Financial Controls [VERIFY: edition]), and the audit-trail reporting under Rule 11(g) (Part 7C AC7).
- **ITGC library.** Access to programs and data (user provisioning, periodic access review, privileged access), program change (approval, testing, segregation of developers from production, emergency changes), computer operations (job scheduling, backup and restore, incident handling), program development (SDLC). Each control has design description, owner, frequency, test steps, population query and evidence pattern.
- **Finbyx-side evidence.** Because Finbyx is the tenant's system of record, Finbyx provides evidence of its own controls: release and change records from Part 7L EO1–EO2, backup and restore tests (EO3), access reviews, SOC 1 Type 2 report for SA 402 service-organisation reliance and SOC 2 report or bridge letter, each only once issued (OUT para 79; Part 7L EO4.2, EO5), and audit-trail configuration snapshots (AC7). The tenant's auditors retrieve these through the AU7 workspace; Finbyx never asserts compliance on the tenant's behalf.
- **Key reports:** user roles with SoD conflicts; access-review completion; change log; configuration changes to rates, charges, BRE rules and GL mappings; audit-trail capture-gap report; backup and restore log with India location.

### AU4.3 VAPT tracking

- **Cadence (ML and above, critical and DMZ systems).** VA at least once every 6 months and PT at least once every 12 months, plus before and after implementation of new systems or major changes (CYB paras 121–122, 124); risk-based for non-critical systems (para 123); performed by trained, independent professionals (para 122).
- **Tracker.** `vapt_engagement` (scope assets from the CYB asset inventory, tester, independence declaration, dates, methodology, report hash) and `vulnerability_finding` (CVE/CWE, CVSS base and environmental score including cloud context — para 126, asset, severity, first seen, due date by severity SLA, fix evidence, retest result, recurrence flag).
- **SLAs (tenant policy; defaults [REC]).** Tenant-side vulnerabilities and audit findings: Critical 15 days, High 30 days, Medium 90 days, Low 180 days. Platform vulnerabilities in Finbyx product code and infrastructure (`provider_vapt` items) follow Part 7L EO1.6 (critical or actively exploited 72 hours, High 7 days, Medium 30 days, Low 90 days). Where both apply, the stricter date wins. Severity bands from CVSS (environmental where scored): Critical ≥ 9.0 or CISA KEV-listed, High 7.0–8.9, Medium 4.0–6.9, Low < 4.0. A recurring CVE on the same asset after closure is a High-rated audit finding (para 125 "time-bound fixes ... to avoid recurrence").
- **Due-date engine.** Next VA = last VA end + 6 months; next PT = last PT end + 12 months; a major change (Part 7L EO2 change record with `requires_vapt = true`) creates a pre-production VAPT task that blocks the production release until the test or a documented risk acceptance exists.
- **Finbyx's own VAPT.** Reports and remediation status for the hosted platform are shared with tenants under Part 10.6 item 5 and appear read-only in each tenant's tracker as `provider_vapt` items. Tenant-commissioned tests of the Finbyx platform follow the Finbyx testing-notice process (Part 7L EO4).
- **Dashboards:** open vulnerabilities by severity and age, SLA breaches, overdue VA/PT → ITSC dashboard (Part 7E RK8) and R56.

### Settings and options

| Setting | Default | Level | Floor or choice |
|---|---|---|---|
| VA and PT cadence for critical and DMZ systems | 6 and 12 months | Tenant (ML and above) | Floor (CYB para 121); BL and CIC tenants may set their own (choice) |
| Non-critical systems cadence | Risk-based, 12 months VA [REC] | Tenant | Choice (CYB para 123) |
| Vulnerability SLAs | AU4.3 defaults; EO1.6 for platform items | Tenant | Choice; stricter wins |
| `requires_vapt` release gate | On for major changes | Tenant | Floor for critical systems (CYB paras 121, 124) |
| IS audit timing warning | Report before statutory fieldwork | Tenant | Warning only (CYB para 56 "preferably") |
| Continuous-audit job schedule | Daily for access and configuration tests | Tenant | Choice |

### Menu and screens

| Path (workspace L) | Screens | Key actions and rules | Visible to |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Audit › IS audit` | Scope library by CYB family; IS audit plan; continuous-audit exceptions | Plan from scope library; run CAATs; raise findings | IS auditors, HIA, CISO (read) |
| `Audit › ITGC` | Control library; test calendar; provider-evidence shelf | Test control; request provider evidence; record result | IA, statutory auditors through AU7 |
| `Audit › VAPT` | VAPT engagements; vulnerability list (filters: severity, asset, SLA status, recurring, provider); due-date calendar | Import scanner or tester report (CSV, SARIF or XML); bulk assign owner; request retest; accept risk with expiry | CISO office, IA, ITSC members (read) |

### Acceptance tests

- For an ML tenant, a critical system whose last VA ended 6 months and 1 day ago shows "VA overdue" and raises an exception to the CISO and ITSC dashboard.
- A production release flagged `requires_vapt` cannot be deployed without a linked post-implementation test or a signed risk acceptance.
- A vulnerability closed and later re-detected on the same asset is flagged as recurring and creates a High finding.
- A critical `provider_vapt` item shows a 72-hour due time (EO1.6), not 15 days; a tenant policy of 10 days for tenant-side Critical items overrides the 15-day default.
- The planner warns when the IS audit report due date is after the statutory audit fieldwork start date.
- An external IS auditor can download the user-role listing with SoD conflicts but cannot see unmasked PAN or Aadhaar values.

## AU5. Statutory and external audit support

### AU5.1 Auditor appointment and eligibility (extends 8A.33)

- **Applicability resolver.** From the entity regulatory profile: SA applies to all NBFCs and HFCs; non-deposit NBFCs with assets < ₹1,000 crore may continue extant procedure (SA para 3) — the resolver shows "SA Directions optional" and still runs eligibility checks as a recommendation.
- **Number of auditors.** Joint audit by at least two firms when assets at the end of the previous year are **≥ ₹15,000 crore** (SA para 11), with no common partners and no shared network (Companies (Audit and Auditors) Rules 2014 Rule 6(3) as referenced in SA para 11); maximum firms by asset band (SA para 12). Work allocation between joint auditors is recorded before audit start.
- **Eligibility engine.** Form B (Annex II) data captured from the firm and checked against SA para 14 bands (FTPs, FCAs, CISA/ISA, experience, professional staff) and para 15 conditions (s.141 qualification, not debarred, no partner who is a director of an RBI-regulated group entity, with a disclosure to the ACB and Board where the directorship is in a non-RBI-regulated group entity; CAAT/GAS capability preferred above ₹1,000 crore). Partner exclusivity and the 10-year association of two partners above ₹1,000 crore (para 14, Note 1) are captured per partner. Continued eligibility is re-attested before each annual audit; a firm that loses eligibility must report it and regain it before the annual audit starts (para 16). The ACB (or Board) records its independence assessment, including any audit of an entity with Large Exposure to the NBFC (paras 7, 18).
- **Independence and tenure.** Concurrent auditor ineligible (para 18); non-audit work 1-year gap either side (para 19) against the non-audit-service log; network and common-partner extension (para 20); continuous 3-year term (para 23); 6-year cooling-off (para 24); firm-wide cap of 8 NBFCs (para 25) recorded from the firm's declaration; removal before 3 years → SSM/RO intimation within 1 month (para 23). Group-wide checks (a partner's directorship in any group RE; non-audit work across group REs) run against the Operations Hub group entity register when the tenant is an Infrabyx-group or multi-entity customer.
- **Procedure.** At least two firms shortlisted per vacancy (para 30(2)); Form A (Annex I) generated for DoS CO (Mumbai Region) or the RO within one month of appointment (para 30(1)) and tracked as a supervisory return in Part 7B (SR para 21 item 20); annual performance review, with serious lapses reported to DoS within two months of audit completion (para 8); appointment policy published on the website (para 10) — the CMS link is recorded.

### AU5.2 PBC (prepared-by-client) lists

- **Templates by profile.** NBFC (Ind AS Div III or AS Div I), HFC, bank (Forms A/B), co-operative, CIC, ARC, IFSC entity. Each PBC item has: description, owner, source (auto-generated report or upload), due date, status (`REQUESTED → IN_PREPARATION → PROVIDED → AUDITOR_QUERY → ACCEPTED`), auditor comments and hash of the provided file.
- **Auto-generated items.** Trial balance and GL mapping to Schedule III / FS Annex I (Part 7C AC3); loan-book listing with classification, stage, ECL and IRACP provision; IRACP vs Ind AS table (FS para 21(15)); NPA movement; restructured and > 90 DPD-not-impaired lists with ACB references (FS Annex 1); Impairment Reserve computation; CRAR computation with RWA walk (Part 7E RK3); ALM statements; related-party register and transactions; borrowings and covenant compliance; investment register and valuation; fixed-asset register; GST and TDS reconciliations (AC4–AC5); bank and suspense reconciliations; fraud register; litigation and contingent liabilities (R9.6); CERSAI and CKYC filing status; audit-trail configuration and capture-gap report (AC7); user-access and change reports (AU4.2); board and committee minutes index (Part 7F GV2).
- **Query log.** Auditor queries against PBC items or workpaper areas, with response owner, due date and resolution; ageing shown to the CFO.

### AU5.3 Auditor's Report Directions checklists (extends 8A.15)

- **Checklist runs by profile.** Para 6 (all NBFCs: CoR and Principal Business Criteria with bank FDs excluded from financial assets, continued entitlement at 31 March, NOF), para 7 items (1)–(12) for deposit-taking NBFCs, para 8 items for non-deposit NBFCs (Board resolution on non-acceptance of deposits, no deposits accepted, IRACP/investment/AS compliance, CRAR correct and DNBS03 filed on time for ML and above — para 8(4), correct MFI classification — para 8(5)), para 9 for exempted companies holding RBI advice.
- **Evidence per item.** Each checklist line links the computation that answers it: PBC test (Principal Business Criteria) from the SBR module, NOF from Part 7E RK3, deposit register, DNBS03 filing evidence from Part 7B, MFI qualifying-asset test (R47), IRACP reconciliation. The auditor marks each line favourable, unfavourable or qualified with reasons (AUD para 10).
- **DNBS10 timer.** Due within **5 working days of the date of signing of the audit report**, and not later than **31 December** (AUD para 6; SR para 21 item 7, para 23). The working-day calendar uses the tenant holiday calendar; reminders at T−3, T−1 and on the due date to the auditor contact and CFO. The auditor compiles and files DNBS10 on CIMS with credentials the NBFC creates; **Finbyx neither stores nor scripts CIMS credentials or OTPs**; the acknowledgement is uploaded as evidence (Part 7B RR5).
- **Exception reports (AUD paras 11–12).** Register of exception reports sent by the auditor to the SSM/RO for adverse para 6 items or any non-compliance with RBI Act Chapter IIIB or Directions; Finbyx records receipt of the copy, links the underlying finding and opens a compliance issue. The register reports contraventions only; no editorialising fields.

### AU5.4 CARO 2020 data

- **Clause data packs** are assembled in Part 7C AC3.4 (applicability, clauses 3(ii)(b) to 3(xxi), lineage); Part 7D adds clauses 3(i) PPE and title deeds and 3(vii) statutory dues from the fixed-asset register and tax module, runs the auditor's clause checklist, links each clause to its pack and records the auditor's remark (`caro_clause_response`).
- **Principal Business Criteria evidence.** Financial assets more than 50% of total assets (net of intangible assets) and income from financial assets more than 50% of gross income (RBI press release 1998-99/1269 of 8 Apr 1999, as referenced in AUD para 6(1)); fixed deposits with banks are not reckoned as financial assets (MISC para 21, referenced in AUD para 6(1)). Computed per quarter and at 31 March with lineage; the same computation feeds AU5.3 (para 6(1)–(2)).

### AU5.5 Bank, co-operative and other statutory audits

- **Banks:** LFAR question banks from the ICAI Guidance Note on Audit of Banks (2026 Edition) [ICAI] [VERIFY: chapters]; branch coverage per RBI SCA/SBA instructions [VERIFY]. **Co-operatives:** panel audits under the State Act or MSCS Act, audit class where used [VERIFY: per state], rectification reports tracked as ATRs (`MSCS`, `SCS`). **ARCs, IFSC entities, AIF companies:** placeholders until Part 7G and 7H rules are verified.

### AU5.6 Branch-coverage rule

- **Rule (SA para 13; not CICs).** Statutory auditors visit at least the **top 20 branches**, or the **top 20% where the NBFC has fewer than 100 branches**, ranked by outstanding advances, covering **≥ 15% of total gross advances**; s.143(8) also applies to all branches.
- **Calculator.** Ranks branches by gross advances as on the balance-sheet date; selects the minimum set; if 15% coverage is not reached by the count rule, extends the list until it is; outputs the list with cumulative coverage % and a signed selection record. Branches visited are recorded per auditor; the final report shows achieved coverage.

### Settings and options

| Setting | Default | Level | Floor or choice |
|---|---|---|---|
| SA Directions mode for non-deposit NBFCs below ₹1,000 crore | "Optional" with eligibility checks as recommendation | Tenant | Choice (SA para 3) |
| Joint-audit threshold, firm maxima, tenure, cooling-off, firm-wide cap | SA paras 11, 12, 23–25 | Rule pack | Floor (locked) |
| Shortlist per vacancy | 2 firms | Tenant | Floor: at least 2 (SA para 30(2)) |
| PBC template by profile | Auto-selected from the entity profile | Engagement | Choice; items can be added, mandatory items cannot be removed |
| DNBS10 reminders | T−3, T−1, T | Tenant | Choice; due-date rule locked |
| Branch-coverage rule | Top 20 or top 20%; ≥ 15% of gross advances | Rule pack | Floor; a tenant may set a higher coverage |

### Menu and screens

| Path (workspace L) | Screens | Key actions and rules | Visible to |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Audit › Statutory › Auditors` | Firm register; eligibility check (Form B data); tenure tracker; non-audit service log | Shortlist; run eligibility; generate Form A; record ACB independence assessment | CFO office, CS, ACB (approve) |
| `Audit › Statutory › PBC` | PBC list per engagement (filters: owner, status, overdue); query log | Auto-generate items; upload; respond to query; bulk assign owners; export PBC tracker | CFO office; auditors through AU7 |
| `Audit › Statutory › Checklists` | AUD para 6–9 runs; DNBS10 timer; exception-report register; CARO clause checklist | Link computation; record auditor result; upload DNBS10 acknowledgement | Auditors (record results), CFO, CCO |
| `Audit › Statutory › Branch coverage` | Calculator and selection record | Run; sign selection; record visits | CFO office, auditors |

### Acceptance tests

- A tenant with ₹15,200 crore of assets at the previous year-end cannot finalise the auditor plan with one firm; two firms sharing a partner are rejected.
- A firm whose partner is a director of a group RE fails eligibility with the SA para 15 citation; a firm that did non-audit work 8 months before the proposed start is flagged under para 19.
- DNBS10 due date is computed as 5 working days after the signing date using the tenant calendar, and capped at 31 December; reminders fire at T−3, T−1 and T.
- For a branch book of 60 branches where the top 12 (20%) cover 11% of advances, the calculator extends selection until coverage ≥ 15% and records the reason.
- The para 8 checklist for an ML non-deposit NBFC includes the CRAR/DNBS03 line and links the RK3 computation and the DNBS03 filing acknowledgement.
- Searching the code base finds no stored CIMS credentials or OTP-handling code.

## AU6. Secretarial audit and secretarial standards compliance

### AU6.1 Applicability

- **Section 204 secretarial audit (CA13 s.204; Rule 9, Companies (Appointment and Remuneration of Managerial Personnel) Rules 2014).** Listed companies; public companies with paid-up share capital ≥ ₹50 crore, turnover ≥ ₹250 crore, or outstanding loans or borrowings from banks or public financial institutions ≥ ₹100 crore [VERIFY: thresholds and any 2025–26 amendment]. Report in **Form MR-3** annexed to the Board's report [VERIFY: format changes].
- **Listed entities (LODR Reg 24A, as substituted 12 Dec 2024).** Secretarial audit of the listed entity and its material unlisted Indian subsidiaries by a **peer-reviewed** Practising Company Secretary; appointment at the AGM on Board recommendation; individual: one term of 5 years; firm: up to two terms of 5 years; 5-year cooling-off (extends to firms with common partners); casual vacancy filled by the Board within 3 months; tenure before 31 Mar 2025 ignored. **Secretarial Compliance Report within 60 days of the end of the financial year**, signed only by the secretarial auditor or a qualifying peer-reviewed CS from 1 Apr 2025.
- **Non-listed, below-threshold companies.** Optional internal secretarial review using the same templates [REC].

### AU6.2 Secretarial auditor eligibility, tenure and prohibited services

- **CSAS-1 (Engagement).** Eligibility check, engagement letter, written communication to the previous auditor and a 7-day wait before acceptance, and the cap of 10 secretarial audits a year (+5 if peer-reviewed) [ICSI] [VERIFY: in the Revised Edition 2026, approved 28 Aug 2026, effective date not stated].
- **Reg 24A prohibited services.** The secretarial auditor (and network) may not provide internal audit, design of compliance/IS/policy systems, investment advice, investment banking, outsourced compliance or record-keeping, or management services to the listed entity, its holding company or subsidiaries. Finbyx runs a conflict check against the tenant's service-provider register. **Group rule [REC]:** where LawDocsComply or any Infrabyx entity implements compliance systems for a listed tenant, an Infrabyx-linked PCS may not be its secretarial auditor; the check reads the Operations Hub group register.
- **Tenure tracker.** Term number, start, end, cooling-off end; alerts 6 months before term end and for casual-vacancy timelines.

### AU6.3 Secretarial audit engagement

- **Plan and checklists (CSAS-2).** Checklists by law: CA13 and rules; SEBI regulations (LODR, PIT, SAST, ICDR, debt listing) where applicable; FEMA where applicable; RBI Act Chapter IIIB and NBFC Directions as laws specifically applicable (from the M14 register); SS-1 and SS-2. Data comes from Part 7F (GV1 directors and KMPs, GV2 meetings, GV3 registers and MCA filings, GV4 listed compliance) through workpapers and evidence links; nothing is re-keyed.
- **SS-1 and SS-2 compliance checks (automated, per meeting).** Notice period and mode; notes on agenda; quorum including interested-director exclusions; attendance and electronic-mode declarations (revised SS-1 effective 1 Apr 2024: annual declaration for electronic attendance); minutes circulation within 15 days, signing within 30 days and entry in the minute book; general-meeting notice period, place (revised SS-2), e-voting and scrutiniser timelines [ICSI] [VERIFY: each clock against SS-1/SS-2 text]. Each check is a `ss_compliance_check` with result and evidence link.
- **Opinion (CSAS-3).** Modified or unmodified; observations with qualification text; MR-3 or Secretarial Compliance Report rendered from the engagement; file collated within 45 days of signing and retained 8 years (CSAS-2).
- **Annual Secretarial Compliance Report (listed).** Reg 24A(2) timeline; observations and action-taken table carried from the prior year.

### Settings and options

| Setting | Default | Level | Floor or choice |
|---|---|---|---|
| s.204 applicability | Resolved from paid-up capital, turnover, borrowings and listing | Entity | Floor (locked thresholds once verified) |
| Internal secretarial review for out-of-scope companies | Off | Tenant | Choice |
| SS-1 and SS-2 clock pack | Revised SS-1 and SS-2 (1 Apr 2024) | Rule pack | Floor |
| Tenure alerts | 6 months before term end | Tenant | Choice |
| Prohibited-services check source | Tenant service-provider register plus Operations Hub group register | Tenant | Floor for listed tenants |

### Menu and screens

| Path (workspace L, shared with workspace S) | Screens | Key actions and rules | Visible to |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Audit › Secretarial › Engagements` | Engagement list by FY and type (MR-3, Reg 24A report, internal); checklist runs | Create; run SS checks; link evidence; record opinion | Secretarial auditor (through AU7 when external), CS |
| `Audit › Secretarial › Auditors` | Auditor register; peer-review certificate; tenure and cooling-off; prohibited-services check | Propose appointment (blocked with the citation if ineligible); record casual vacancy | CS, Board (read) |
| `Audit › Secretarial › SS checks` | Per-meeting results (filters: meeting type, failed checks) | Re-run after a correction; export exceptions | CS, secretarial auditor |

### Acceptance tests

- A public unlisted company with paid-up capital of ₹55 crore is flagged for s.204 audit; MR-3 cannot be finalised without a signed opinion.
- A PCS who is not peer-reviewed cannot be appointed for a listed tenant; a firm entering a third 5-year term is rejected.
- A listed tenant whose compliance system is implemented by LawDocsComply cannot appoint an Infrabyx-linked PCS as secretarial auditor; the block cites LODR Reg 24A.
- A Board meeting whose minutes were signed on day 34 is flagged in the SS-1 check with the evidence link.
- The Secretarial Compliance Report due date for FY 2026-27 is computed as 60 days after 31 Mar 2027.
