## RK8. KMP, committee and Board dashboards

### RK8.1 Role dashboards (12 standard roles; MD and CEO can be split into two personas)

| Role | KPIs and KRIs | Drill-downs | Alerts | Sign-off |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| MD and CEO | AUM and disbursement vs plan; NIM; ROA/ROE; CRAR headroom; GNPA/NNPA; LCR; PCA proximity; RAS scorecard; complaints | Branch, officer, product, vintage | Any red RAS metric; PCA forecast; LE breach; cyber incident | Board-pack cover; quarterly fit-and-proper statement certificate (GOV 14) |
| CFO | CRAR, Tier 1, CET1 and RWA walk; SLS and IRS; LCR; cost of funds; maturity wall; covenants; ECL vs IRACP and Impairment Reserve; profitability | RWA by class; lineage to GL | Covenant headroom; LCR below 110%; SLS above 80% of limit | DNBS03 and ALM returns; ICAAP capital plan |
| CRO | RAS utilisation; credit heatmap; concentration and SSE; EWS alert ageing; stress results; model inventory; operational losses; RCSA coverage; KRIs; impact tolerances; third-party risk | Group links; scenario detail | Limit breach; EWS ageing; model validation overdue; tolerance breach | Product vetting; ICAAP; stress results; RMC pack |
| CCO | Obligation register; returns calendar; compliance tests; RMP/MAP; product approvals; inspection observations; penalties | Obligation to evidence | Return due within 3 days and not ready; overdue inspection compliance; pending DAKSH items | Annual compliance risk assessment (CMP 7) |
| Chief Credit Officer | TAT; deviation rate; early delinquency by cohort; sector caps; related-party sanctions | Deviation to approver | Deviation-rate spike; related-party loan above materiality without Board approval | Deviation log; committee minutes |
| Head of Internal Audit | Plan progress; High/Medium findings and ageing; repeat findings; RBIA heatmap; quarterly related-party review; CAAT exceptions | Finding to response | High finding open more than 90 days | Reports; quarterly ACB in-camera note |
| Company Secretary | Board and committee calendar and composition (GOV 15–18; CYB 71); in-camera compliance; 31 March fit-and-proper declarations; KMP and independent-director limits (GOV 26–27); CRO and CCO change intimations; listed disclosures | Meeting to action | Missing declarations; quarterly statement due within 15 days of quarter-end (GOV 14) | Minutes, ATRs, DoS/NHB intimations |
| Board | One-page RAS RAG; capital; liquidity; asset quality; concentration; top 10 risks; compliance; frauds; cyber; ICAAP; PCA | Committee packs | — | RAS, ICAAP, policies, critical operations and tolerances (ORM 31–32), ECL model changes |
| Audit Committee | ECL overlays and model changes; accounts above 90 DPD not impaired; SICR rebuttals; divergence; IS audit; internal-audit findings; related-party deviations | Finding and overlay detail | — | Overlays; IS audit policy (CYB 150) |
| Risk Management Committee | All CRO items plus liquidity; EWS effectiveness (FRM 14); CISO review (CYB 82(7)); outsourcing review | Risk to KRI to loss | — | Recommends RAS and ICAAP |
| ALCO | SLS, IRS, LCR, stock ratios, FTP, funding plan, CFP triggers | Bucket and counterparty | Tolerance breach | Behavioural assumptions (ALM 54); gap limits (ALM 11) |
| IT Strategy Committee | IT strategy; incidents (6-hour reporting); VA/PT status; DR drills; vendor risk; CISO report; CFSS progress (MSD 6) | Incident and vulnerability | Critical-vulnerability ageing; DR failure | Minutes to Board |

### RK8.2 Semantic layer and customisation

- Tiles are built only from governed metrics (RK6) through the semantic layer; each tile shows metric version, as-of date, certification state and certifier.
- **Per-KMP customisation.** Users can add, remove and arrange tiles, set personal alert thresholds **tighter** than the RAS (never looser), save filters (entity, branch, product) and subscribe to alerts (in-app, email, Teams or Google Chat through Part 7F GV7). Customisations are stored per user and versioned.
- **Uncertified sandbox.** Ad hoc analysis (M17 copilot, SQL) is confined to a sandbox; sandbox outputs carry an "uncertified" watermark and cannot be added to a Board pack.
- **Access.** Row-level security by role and entity; directors see packs of the Board and of committees they sit on; supervisors and auditors use AU7.
- **Group view.** Consolidated metrics are separate metric versions with consolidation rules and entity drill-down.

### RK8.3 Sign-off and Board-pack workflow

- **Per metric value.** `COMPUTED → VALIDATED (data steward) → REVIEWED (checker) → CERTIFIED (owner eSign) → PUBLISHED`. A source restatement automatically revokes certification and notifies the owner and the CS; the value returns to `COMPUTED`.
- **Board-pack builder.** Pack template per committee; sections bound to certified metrics, narratives from owners, ATRs (Part 7D), compliance status (M14), ICAAP and stress summaries; pack freeze computes a hash over all values, versions and narratives; distribution through the board portal or workplace integration (Part 7F GV2, GV7); every tile in a frozen pack shows certifier, as-of date and metric version.
- **Never auto-certify.** No metric is certified by the system; certification requires a named user in the owner role; a pack cannot be frozen with uncertified regulatory metrics unless each is labelled "indicative" with a reason.
- **Events.** Pack freeze and certification are `EvidenceSubmitted` to LawDocsComply; daily `RiskSnapshotPublished` carries certification states.
- **Pack states.** `DRAFT → IN_REVIEW` (section owners submit narratives; CS checks completeness) `→ FROZEN` (hash) `→ DISTRIBUTED` (board portal, with read receipts) `→ SUPERSEDED` (restatement or re-issue; the original stays readable with its hash). A late change after freeze is an addendum pack, never an edit. Default timers: freeze 7 days before the meeting, distribution at least 7 days before for Board meetings (SS-1 notice clock in Part 7F GV2) [REC].
- **Dashboard template change control.** Standard role templates are versioned by the platform; tenant changes to a standard template (adding or removing tiles for a role) go through maker-checker by the role owner and the CRO or CFO; a metric definition change follows RK6.1 change control and never happens on a dashboard.

### Settings and options

| Setting | Default | Level | Floor or choice |
|---|---|---|---|
| Role templates | 12 standard templates (RK8.1) | Tenant | Choice to extend; certified tiles cannot be removed from Board and committee packs without the committee chair's approval |
| Personal alert thresholds | Off | User | Only tighter than the RAS (floor) |
| Alert channels | In-app and e-mail; Teams or Google Chat optional | User | Choice; regulatory breaches always in-app and e-mail (floor) |
| Quiet hours for non-breach alerts | 21:00–08:00 | User | Choice; breaches ignore quiet hours |
| Certification required for pack inclusion | On for regulatory metrics | Tenant | Floor; "indicative with reason" is the only exception |
| Export of dashboards | PDF and XLSX with watermark (user, time, certification state) | Tenant | Choice to disable |
| Default entity and period | User's home entity; last closed month | User | Choice |

### Menu and screens

| Path (workspace M; also in J) | Screens | Key actions and rules | Visible to |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Dashboards › My dashboard` | Role template landing page (MD and CEO, CFO, CRO, CCO, Chief Credit Officer, HIA, CS) with tiles showing value, RAG, metric version, as-of date and certification badge | Customise (add, remove, arrange tiles); save views (entity, branch, product, period); set personal thresholds; subscribe; drill down (tile → segment → record in at most three clicks, row-level security applied); open lineage; export | The role holder; delegates with "view as" granted by the role holder (logged) |
| `Dashboards › Committees` | RMC, Audit Committee, ALCO, ITSC, Board packs and live views | Open pack; comment by section; acknowledge read; download watermarked PDF | Committee members only (directors see only their committees) |
| `Dashboards › Sign-off` | Certification queue (values awaiting validation, review, certification); pack builder; freeze and distribution log | Validate; review; certify by eSign; mark "indicative" with reason; freeze; distribute; supersede | Data stewards, checkers, metric owners, CS |
| `Dashboards › Alerts` | Alert inbox (filters: severity, metric, status); subscriptions | Acknowledge; snooze non-breach alerts (maximum 24 hours); open the KRI or limit episode | All dashboard users |
| `Dashboards › Sandbox` | Ad hoc analysis with "uncertified" watermark | Query; save; share within the tenant (never into a pack) | Analysts, CRO and CFO offices |

Accessibility and usability: WCAG 2.2 AA (colour is never the only RAG signal; each tile has a text status), keyboard navigation across tiles, a "why this colour" explainer showing threshold version and value, and empty states that say which feed is missing.

### Acceptance tests

- Each of the 12 role templates renders on the seeded tenant with only governed metrics; adding a sandbox query to a Board pack is rejected.
- A CRO personal alert threshold looser than the RAS tolerance is rejected; a tighter one fires first.
- Restating a GL entry for a closed month revokes the certification of dependent metrics, notifies the owner and the CS, and the frozen Board pack shows "superseded by restatement" while keeping its original hash.
- An independent director who is not on the ALCO cannot open the ALCO pack.
- A frozen pack verifies (hash recomputed equals stored) and every tile shows certifier, as-of date and metric version.
- A drill-down from the CRAR tile reaches the exposure line in three clicks and hides records outside the user's row-level scope; a delegate "view as" session is logged with both user identities.
- Removing a certified tile from the Board pack template without the chair's approval is rejected; a change after freeze creates an addendum pack and leaves the frozen hash unchanged.

# PART 7F — CORPORATE GOVERNANCE, LISTED-COMPANY COMPLIANCE, CLIENT HRMS AND WORKPLACE INTEGRATION

**Purpose.** One governed place for each lender tenant to run its board governance (directors, KMPs, committees, meetings, registers, MCA filings), its listed-company obligations, its departments, delegation of authority and tasks, an optional HRMS and payroll for its own staff, and its link to Microsoft 365, Google Workspace or its own data centre. Software prepares, validates, timestamps and evidences; the Board, committees, Company Secretary (CS) and authorised officers decide, sign and file. Finbyx never stores MCA, exchange, EPFO, ESIC, TRACES or labour-portal credentials, DSC tokens or OTPs (same rule as Part 7B).

**Applicability.**

| Section | Entity types and layers | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| GV1–GV3 | Every company tenant: NBFCs of all layers (incl. CIC, MFI, HFC), ARCs, IFSC companies (company-law parts). Banks use the same engine with Banking Regulation Act overlays [VERIFY: bank governance Directions not supplied]. Co-operative tenants switch to the co-operative profile in Part 7G (general body, managing committee, MSCS or State Act registers; MCA forms off) | CA13; ICSI SS-1, SS-2; GOV (8A.28) by layer (GOV para 3); MSCS; SCS |
| GV4 | Equity-listed (main board or SME), debt-listed, HVDLE, or preparing an issue | LODR; PIT; ICDR; SAST |
| GV5 | Every tenant | CA13 ss.179–180; CYB paras 8(3), 21(2)–(6) |
| GV6 | Optional SKU `Workforce`; tenant as employer, Infrabyx as processor | LC; ITA25; POSH Act; DPDP |
| GV7 | Tenants connecting a workplace suite or own data centre | CF para 14(4); OUT paras 74(vi), 97; CYB para 116 |

**Requirement codes.** RBI: GOV, CYB, OUT, CF, IAF, FRM, CRM, WD, RBC, KYC. Non-RBI (Part 8A.37): `CA13`, `ICSI`, `LODR`, `PIT`, `ICDR`, `LC`, `ITA25`, `DPDP`, `MSCS`, `SCS`. REQ-ID examples: `REQ-CA13-173(1)`, `REQ-ICSI-SS1-7`, `REQ-LODR-23(2)`, `REQ-PIT-3(5)`, `REQ-LC-CoW-17(2)`, `REQ-GOV-14`.

**Data owned.** The tenant is data fiduciary for every governance record, register, minute, UPSI log, employee and payroll record; Infrabyx is processor (Part 7A.0.9 pattern). None of this data flows to the Operations Hub, Equator or another group company. Only the canonical governance events named below leave the tenant, and only to its own compliance destination (embedded M14 or LawDocsComply, Integration Spec Part 9).

**Extends, does not rebuild.** GV1 implements the GOV build list of Part 8A.28 (director master, Annex I–III e-forms, NRC log, 31 March campaign, deed tracker, quarterly statement, CRO controls). Reused: M19 (users, ABAC, maker-checker, delegation, break-glass), M16 (documents), M18 (notices), M21 (connectors). Elsewhere: secretarial audit AU6 and auditor workspace AU7 (Part 7D); KMP and Board dashboards RK8; PRAVAAH filing RR4; books backup and Rule 3(6) statement AC7. Infrabyx's own staff HRMS and workplace tenant: Operations Hub OH10, OH12.

## GV1. Entity, directors, KMPs and committees

### GV1.1 Governance profile

Extend `entity_regulatory_profile` (M1; 8A.25) with `governance_profile`: company class (private, public, OPC, small, Section 8, government, banking, co-operative), listing status (unlisted, equity main board, equity SME, debt-listed, HVDLE), last-audited paid-up capital, turnover, borrowings, members and security-holder counts (each with source and as-of date), market-cap rank (exchange list at 31 March), outstanding listed debt (from M10), RBI layer and asset size (from 8A.25).

Company-law thresholds sit in a versioned `ca13_threshold_pack` [LAW; VERIFY each against current Rules before coding as hard rules]:

- independent directors: one-third for listed (s.149(4)); at least 2 for public companies with paid-up ≥ ₹10 crore, turnover ≥ ₹100 crore or loans, debentures and deposits above ₹50 crore (Appointment Rules r.4); woman director for listed and public companies with paid-up ≥ ₹100 crore or turnover ≥ ₹300 crore (r.3);
- Audit Committee and NRC for listed and r.4-class companies (ss.177, 178; Meetings of Board Rules r.6); SRC above 1,000 security holders (s.178(5)); CSR Committee at net worth ≥ ₹500 crore, turnover ≥ ₹1,000 crore or net profit ≥ ₹5 crore, unless the obligation is ≤ ₹50 lakh (s.135(1), (9));
- whole-time KMP for listed and public companies with paid-up ≥ ₹10 crore (s.203; Managerial Personnel Rules r.8, 8A); secretarial audit per s.204 and r.9 (engagement in AU6);
- vigil mechanism for listed companies, companies accepting public deposits and companies with bank or PFI borrowings above ₹50 crore (s.177(9); Meetings of Board Rules r.7). GOV para 38 separately requires a whistle-blower mechanism for directors and employees of every NBFC-ML and NBFC-UL; BL tenants get it as a default-on policy [REC].

**GOV applicability** is resolved from the institution profile (GOV para 3): BL → Chapter III (paras 8–11); ML → Chapters II–IV; UL → Chapters II–V; CICs → paras 7–15, 18–39 and 41–43 (no para 17 Audit Committee rule); NBFC-AA and NBFC-P2P → paras 12–13 even at BL; compensation paras 29–37 never apply to government-owned NBFCs. A GOV rule outside the tenant's chapters is shown as best practice and never blocks.

### GV1.2 Director master and lifecycle

- **Fields added to the GOV director master:** DIN (ss.153–154), category (executive, non-executive, independent, nominee and nominating institution), residency for the s.149(3) resident-director test, term dates, retirement by rotation (s.152(6)), ID databank registration (s.149(7)), `din_status` (active, deactivated, disqualified, surrendered) with evidence and as-of date.
- **DIR-3 KYC** by 30 September for every DIN held on 31 March (Appointment Rules r.12A) [VERIFY: whether a 2025 amendment moved KYC to a three-yearly cycle; keep the cycle in the rule pack]. Finbyx cannot query MCA: the CS uploads the MCA master-data extract. A deactivated DIN is excluded from quorum (GV2) and opens a P1 task.
- **Appointment states:** `PROPOSED → NRC_SCRUTINY → RBI_GATE → BOARD_APPROVED → CONSENT_AND_DECLARATIONS → MEMBERS_APPROVAL (if required) → EFFECTIVE → FILED`.
  - NRC_SCRUTINY: Annex II and recorded NRC decision (GOV para 13(1)–(2); ML and UL, and AA and P2P at any layer; BL by policy [REC]); bureau and wilful-defaulter checks.
  - RBI_GATE: the change-of-management calculator (GOV para 10); above 30% of non-independent directors, EFFECTIVE is blocked until the PRAVAAH approval is attached (filing in RR4). Change-in-control approvals under the Acquisition of Shareholding or Control Directions are tracked here [VERIFY: Directions not supplied].
  - CONSENT_AND_DECLARATIONS: DIR-2 (s.152(5)), DIR-8 (s.164), MBP-1 (s.184(1)), Deed of Covenants (GOV para 13(4)), independence declaration.
  - Limits before EFFECTIVE: ≤ 20 directorships and ≤ 10 public (s.165); an independent director sits on at most 3 NBFC-ML or NBFC-UL boards at a time, BL boards not counted (GOV para 27), with a conflict check for simultaneous NBFC boards (para 28); LODR Reg 17A when GV4 is active.
  - FILED: DIR-12 within 30 days (s.170(2)) with SRN.
  - **Exits and failures:** `NRC_REJECTED`, `RBI_REFUSED` and `WITHDRAWN` are terminal with reason and evidence; a consent or declaration still missing 15 days after BOARD_APPROVED [REC] opens a CS task; a failed members' resolution moves the appointment to `WITHDRAWN` and ends any additional-director office per the Articles; a DIR-12 returned by MCA loops through GV3.2 `RESUBMISSION_REQUIRED` without reopening the appointment.
- **Continuing duties:** MBP-1 at the first Board meeting of each FY and on change; 31 March fit-and-proper declaration (GOV para 13(3)); annual independence declaration; s.164(2) disqualification monitoring from uploaded MCA lists; Annex II items feed the CRM 13K related-party register and the GV4 RPT register.
- **Cessation** (resignation s.168, removal s.169, vacation s.167, death, term end) re-runs committee composition and the independent-director vacancy timer (3 months where required; LODR Reg 25(6) for listed [VERIFY]).

### GV1.3 KMP and senior management

- **KMP master:** MD, CEO, WTD, CS, CFO, CRO, CCO, CTO/CIO, CISO, HIA, PMLA Principal Officer and Designated Director, GRO, Internal Ombudsman, Nodal Officer; appointing resolution, dates, reporting line, qualifications evidence; other-office check (no office in another ML/UL NBFC except a subsidiary directorship; GOV para 26).
- **Reporting-line guards (rejected, not warned):** CRO reports to MD&CEO or RMCB, holds no business role or targets, no dual hatting (GOV para 21); CISO has no direct reporting line to the head of IT and no business targets (CYB para 81); HIA is an employee for IAF in-scope NBFCs (IAF para 39); the Principal Officer is never the Designated Director (KYC para 14(3)).
- **Vacancy timers:** whole-time KMP within 6 months (s.203(4)); CRO quarterly closed-session tracker (GOV para 21(2)).
- **`KmpChanged`** (canonical) on any director or KMP appointment, cessation or redesignation: role, DIN, effective date, evidence hash, obligations started (GV1.5). Consumers: the tenant's compliance destination and RK8. No PAN or date of birth in the payload.

### GV1.4 Committees

Committee master (type, basis, charter version in M16, members with role chair, member, invitee or non-voting adviser) plus composition rule packs validated after every change; a breach opens a task with the cure window.

| Committee | Composition (defaults; stricter listed values override) | Meetings | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|
| Audit Committee (ACB) | ≥ 3 Board members; company law: independent majority; listed: two-thirds independent, independent chair [VERIFY] | Listed ≥ 4 a year, gap ≤ 120 days; quarterly ACB–HIA meeting | GOV para 17; s.177; LODR Reg 18; IAF |
| NRC (Nomination Committee if government-owned) | ≥ 3 non-executive, at least half independent; listed two-thirds [VERIFY] | Listed ≥ 1 a year | GOV para 18; s.178; LODR Reg 19 |
| Risk Management Committee | Board or executive level; listed top 1,000: ≥ 3, majority directors, ≥ 1 independent [VERIFY] | Listed ≥ 2 a year, gap ≤ 210 days [VERIFY] | GOV para 9; LODR Reg 21 |
| IT Strategy Committee | Ch IV: independent chair, CIO/CTO; Ch V: ≥ 3 directors, independent chair with ≥ 7 years' IT experience | Ch IV gap ≤ 6 months; Ch V quarterly | CYB paras 15, 71–72 |
| IT Steering Committee | Executive | Quarterly (Ch V) | CYB para 75 |
| Stakeholders Relationship | Non-executive chair; listed ≥ 3 with ≥ 1 independent [VERIFY] | Listed ≥ 1 a year | s.178(5); LODR Reg 20 |
| CSR | ≥ 3 directors incl. ≥ 1 independent where IDs are required | Per charter | s.135 |
| Fraud monitoring; WD identification and review | Per FRM and WD Directions | Per Directions | FRM; WD |
| ALCO, credit and sanction committees | Executive; CRO adviser (no vote) or voter (vote recorded, joint liability flag) | Per policy | ALM; GOV para 24 |

Mandatory agenda items are seeded per committee (for example ACB annual IS-audit review, CYB paras 51, 56 and GOV para 17(2); RPT prior approval, s.177(4)(iv) and LODR Reg 23(2); RMC risk appetite and ICAAP; NRC annual fit-and-proper review). A missed item at the last meeting in its window raises an M14 exception. Listed directors are limited to 10 Audit or Stakeholders committee memberships and 5 chairs (LODR Reg 26(1)) [VERIFY].

### GV1.5 Change reporting matrix

| Trigger | Obligation | Timer | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|
| Director or KMP appointment or cessation | DIR-12 | 30 days | CA13 ss.168, 170, 203 |
| Any change in directors or management | Intimation to DoS RO (NHB for HFCs) | None in text; default 7 days [REC] | GOV para 10 Explanation |
| Change above 30% of non-independent directors | Prior approval via PRAVAAH | Before effect | GOV paras 10–11 |
| Quarter end (ML and UL) | Change-of-directors statement with MD/CEO fit-and-proper certificate to the DoS RO (NHB for HFCs); March statement auditor-certified | 15 days after quarter end | GOV para 14 |
| CRO premature removal or transfer | Report to DoS RO; exchanges if listed | Default 7 days [REC] | GOV para 22 |
| UL independent director premature exit | Report to supervisors | Default 7 days [REC] | GOV para 42 |
| Listed: director, KMP, senior-management, CS or auditor change | Exchange disclosure | 30 minutes after the Board decision; otherwise 12 hours if internal, 24 hours if external (for example a resignation received); resignation letter with reasons within 7 days [VERIFY] | LODR Reg 30(6); Sch III Part A paras 7, 7B, 7C |
| Principal Officer or Designated Director change | Name, designation, address and contact details to FIU-IND and RBI | None in text; default 7 days [REC] | KYC paras 14(2), 15(2) |

### GV1.6 Controls

CS maker and CS-checker or Compliance Officer checker for governance masters; directors self-serve declarations in a director portal (MFA; no loan data); every declaration eSigned or DSC-signed and hashed into M16 (PDF/A with hash in XMP). Interested-director recusal computed from MBP-1 and Annex II is enforced in GV2 voting, sanction committees (CRM 13J) and settlement approval (R1.7).

### Acceptance tests

- An appointment that changes 4 of 10 non-independent directors stays in RBI_GATE until a PRAVAAH approval is attached; EFFECTIVE then starts the DIR-12 timer.
- A director with `din_status` deactivated is excluded from quorum; recording his vote fails with `din_inactive`.
- An independent director already on three NBFC-ML or NBFC-UL boards cannot be appointed to a fourth; a seat on an NBFC-BL board is allowed.
- For an NBFC-BL tenant the GOV para 13 Annex II check shows as best practice and does not block; for an NBFC-P2P tenant at BL it blocks.
- A CRO user also holding a business-target role is rejected (`sod_cro_business`).
- An independent director's resignation that leaves the ACB with 2 members raises a composition breach and an M14 exception.
- The GOV para 14 statement is generated on the first day after quarter end; the March statement cannot be marked ready without the auditor certificate.
- A schema test fails if PAN or date of birth is added to `KmpChanged`.

## GV2. Board, committee and general meetings (SS-1, SS-2)

### GV2.1 Meeting model and rule packs

- **Types:** Board, committee, independent directors' meeting (Schedule IV para VII, at least once a year), CRO closed session (GOV para 21(2)), AGM, EGM, postal ballot, class meetings.
- **States:** `DRAFT → SCHEDULED → NOTICE_SENT → AGENDA_CIRCULATED → IN_SESSION → (ADJOURNED) → CONCLUDED → DRAFT_MINUTES_CIRCULATED → COMMENTS_CLOSED → MINUTES_SIGNED → ENTERED → ARCHIVED`. Circular resolutions: `DRAFT → CIRCULATED → APPROVED or FAILED or CONVERTED_TO_MEETING → NOTED_AT_NEXT_MEETING`.
- **Exceptions:** postponement or cancellation is allowed only before IN_SESSION, with reason, and a postponed meeting recomputes notice from the new date; quorum lost in session moves the unfinished items to ADJOURNED with the s.174(4) date pre-filled, and the adjourned meeting carries only those items; draft minutes on which directors disagree after COMMENTS_CLOSED go to the chair, whose decision is final (SS-1) and recorded; a signed-minutes error is corrected only by a noted item at a later meeting.
- **Rule packs** (ICSI SS-1 and SS-2 revised, effective 1 Apr 2024, approved by MCA under s.118(10)) [ICSI]:

| Rule | Default | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| Board frequency | ≥ 4 a year, gap ≤ 120 days; small company and OPC one per half-year, gap ≥ 90 days | s.173(1), (5) |
| Board notice | ≥ 7 days, plus 2 days when sent by speed or registered post; shorter for urgent business only with ≥ 1 independent director present, otherwise final only on ratification by one | s.173(3); SS-1 |
| Agenda and notes | ≥ 7 days before; notes containing UPSI may go at shorter notice only with the consent of a majority of directors including ≥ 1 independent director | SS-1 [VERIFY para] |
| Quorum | One-third or 2, whichever is higher; VC attendees count; interested directors excluded per item; if interested directors are two-thirds or more, ≥ 2 disinterested directors present suffice | s.174(1), (3); s.184(2) |
| Adjournment for want of quorum | Board: same day, time and place next week (next day that is not a national holiday) unless the Articles say otherwise; general meeting: no quorum within 30 minutes → same day next week or a date the Board fixes, with ≥ 3 days' notice of any change | s.174(4); s.103(2)–(3) |
| Video conference | All matters; roll call with name, location and no-one-else confirmation; recording preserved where made [VERIFY current r.3 text]; annual electronic-attendance declaration valid for the calendar year | Meetings of Board Rules r.3; SS-1 (2024) |
| Circular resolution | Majority of directors entitled to vote; one-third may demand a meeting; noted at next meeting | s.175 |
| Minutes | Draft within 15 days; comments within 7 days; signed and entered within 30 days; kept permanently; attendance register 8 FY | s.118; SS-1 |
| AGM | Within 6 months of FY end (first within 9), gap ≤ 15 months | s.96 |
| GM notice and quorum | 21 clear days (plus 2 days for posted notices, SS-2 [VERIFY]); shorter notice: AGM with consent of ≥ 95% of members entitled to vote, other GMs of a majority in number holding ≥ 95% of the paid-up voting capital; public quorum 5, 15 or 30 by membership; private 2 | ss.101–103 |
| E-voting | Listed and ≥ 1,000 members; window ≥ 3 days closing 17:00 the day before; cut-off ≤ 7 days before; through an authorised agency | Management and Administration Rules r.20 [VERIFY] |
| Results | Scrutiniser report and listed results within 2 working days | r.20; LODR Reg 44(3) |
| VC or OAVM general meetings | Under MCA General Circulars | [VERIFY: position after 30 Sep 2025] |

### GV2.2 Agenda and board pack

- Items from mandatory items (GV1.4), DoA rules that require a resolution (GV5), regulatory triggers (RBI approvals, policy reviews due, ICAAP approval RK7, audit findings) and manual entries.
- Each item declares counterparties; the engine pre-marks interested directors (s.184(2)) and routes RPT items to GV4.3 (listed) or s.188 (unlisted).
- UPSI-flagged items (listed tenants) create SDD entries for every recipient at circulation (GV4.4).
- Board pack: the meeting engine assembles agenda papers with the frozen RK8 metric pack for that committee (RK8 owns metric content and certification; GV2 owns notice, circulation and minutes) into a bookmarked PDF/A, watermarked per recipient, served in the director portal (no email attachments by default); the pack hash is stored with the meeting.

### GV2.3 In session, minutes and resolutions

- **Live quorum monitor** per item from attendance, recusals and DIN status; no item is resolved without quorum. Votes per director per item (for, against, abstain, recused); dissent recorded. VC links come from GV7 calendars; Finbyx records roll call and join/leave times but is not a VC provider.
- **Minutes:** SS-1/SS-2 templates; AI may draft from agenda, notes and votes under M20 rules (human review, disclosure); 15-day and 7-day timers; chair signs with DSC or Aadhaar eSign; locked at ENTERED (corrections only as a noted item at a later meeting). Certified true copies signed by the CS with an issue register.
- **`BoardMeetingScheduled`** (canonical) on SCHEDULED: type, date, mode, mandatory items covered. **`ResolutionPassed`** (canonical) per resolution: meeting and resolution type, subject code, effective date, filings started, evidence hash. Consumers: compliance destination; GV5 activates DoA rules referencing the resolution; GV3 starts MGT-14 where applicable.
- Action items become GV5 tasks; an action-taken report is generated for the next meeting.

### GV2.4 General meetings

Members' snapshot at cut-off (GV3 register or RTA/depository import); proxies (48 hours, s.105); attendance; poll; e-voting data file to the authorised agency and results import (Finbyx does not run statutory e-voting itself [REC]); scrutiniser workflow; postal ballot with dispatch evidence and a reply window of 30 days from dispatch (s.110; r.22) [VERIFY].

### Acceptance tests

- A Board meeting with 6 days' notice is blocked unless marked urgent; an urgent meeting without an independent director shows every resolution "pending ratification".
- With 9 directors, 2 on VC and 1 recused on item 3, quorum holds for items 1–2 and is recomputed for item 3.
- Draft minutes circulated on day 16 record a breach; signed minutes cannot be edited.
- A circular resolution where one-third of directors demand a meeting cannot become APPROVED.
- An AGM notice of 20 clear days is rejected unless the 95% short-notice consent is complete.
- A Board meeting that loses quorum after item 4 shows items 5–8 as ADJOURNED to the same weekday next week; the adjourned meeting's agenda contains only items 5–8.
- `ResolutionPassed` for a s.180 special resolution activates the borrowing limit in GV5 and the MGT-14 timer in GV3.

## GV3. Statutory registers, MCA filings and compliance calendar

### GV3.1 Registers (generated, never typed)

Each entry carries its source event and hash; exports in the prescribed layout (PDF/A, XLSX); electronic maintenance per Management and Administration Rules [VERIFY r.27–28].

| Register | Form and basis | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Members; debenture and other security holders | MGT-1, MGT-2 (s.88) | Share-capital ledger, benpos import; NCD master (`ncd_issue`, `ncd_subscriber`) |
| Directors and KMP with shareholding | s.170 | GV1 |
| Contracts with interested directors | MBP-4 (s.189) | GV1, GV4.3 |
| Loans, guarantees, security, investments | MBP-2 (s.186(9)); NBFC ordinary-course lending and guarantees, and investments by NBFCs whose principal business is acquiring securities, are exempt (s.186(11); Meetings of Board Rules r.11(2)) [VERIFY wording] | Non-exempt items only |
| Investments not in company's name | MBP-3 (s.187) | Part 7H |
| Charges created by the company | CHG-7 (s.85) | M10 borrowings, M5 charge evidence |
| Significant beneficial owners | BEN-3 (s.90) | BEN-1 declarations |
| Share certificates, ESOP, sweat equity, buy-back | SH-2, SH-6, SH-3, SH-10 | Share-capital ledger |
| Minutes books | s.118 | GV2 |
| Deposits | Not for RBI-registered NBFCs or NHB-registered HFCs (Acceptance of Deposits Rules r.1(3)) | — |

### GV3.2 MCA form engine

Catalogue `mca_form` (trigger, due rule, attachments, certifier, fee reference, applicability). Starting set [LAW; VERIFY on MCA V3]: AOC-4, AOC-4 CFS or AOC-4 NBFC (Ind AS) within 30 days of AGM (s.137; payload from AC3; no XBRL for NBFCs); MGT-7/7A within 60 days of AGM (s.92); ADT-1 within 15 days (s.139); ADT-3 within 30 days (s.140(2)); MGT-14 within 30 days (s.117) [VERIFY: scope of the s.117(3)(g) proviso for NBFC ordinary-course lending resolutions]; DIR-12 30 days; DIR-3 KYC; CHG-1, CHG-4, CHG-9 within 30 days (s.77 additional-fee extension [VERIFY]); PAS-3 within 30 days of allotment (s.39(4)) or 15 days for a private placement (s.42(8)) [VERIFY]; SH-7 30 days (s.64); INC-22 [VERIFY]; MSME-1 by 30 April and 31 October; BEN-2 30 days; CSR-2; MR-3 annexed to the Board's report (AU6); PAS-6 half-yearly for unlisted public companies [VERIFY].

- **Guided filing:** data validated (DIN active, linked SRNs), attachments from M16, certifier assigned, checklist, evidence slot for SRN, challan and approval. The authorised person files on MCA V3 with his own DSC.
- **States:** `DUE → DATA_READY → CERTIFIED → FILED (SRN) → APPROVED or RESUBMISSION_REQUIRED → CLOSED`; late filing computes the additional-fee band and records the reason. RESUBMISSION_REQUIRED carries the MCA remark and the resubmission deadline from the rule pack, returns to DATA_READY and keeps the original SRN chain; a form marked "rejected" opens a fresh instance linked to the first. A filed form is never edited; corrections are new filings.

### GV3.3 Integrated compliance calendar

One calendar per legal entity: MCA forms, GV1.5 items, RR1 returns (by reference), GV4 clocks, GV6 labour and payroll clocks, policy reviews, committee windows and Part 7D milestones. Each instance: owner, checker, due date, basis, consequence note, evidence requirement, escalation at T-15, T-7, T-1 and overdue to the CS and CCO. A quarterly **Board compliance certificate** lists every statutory compliance with exceptions, signed by the CS [REC]. Due dates shift only by the regulator's own rule, not the branch holiday calendar [REC].

### Acceptance tests

- A charge on the tenant's receivables for a bank loan creates a CHG-1 instance due in 30 days; the CHG-7 entry appears only after the SRN is recorded.
- An NBFC's ordinary-course disbursement creates no MBP-2 entry; an inter-corporate deposit outside its lending business does.
- Changing the AGM date recomputes the MGT-7 and AOC-4 dates; an Ind AS NBFC gets AOC-4 NBFC (Ind AS) and no XBRL instance.
- Evidence without an SRN cannot move an instance to FILED.
- The members' register at a cut-off reconciles to the benpos import or lists the breaks.

### Settings and options (GV1–GV3)

| Setting | Level | Default | Nature |
|---|---|---|---|
| Governance profile and GOV chapter set | Legal entity | Derived from 8A.25 and the institution profile; CS confirms | Regulatory floor |
| Company-law threshold, SS-1/SS-2 and MCA form packs | Platform | Latest verified version, effective-dated | Regulatory floor |
| Minute timers (draft 15, comments 7, entry 30 days) | Tenant | Statutory values | Floor: may be shortened, never lengthened |
| Board-pack delivery | Tenant | Director portal, view-only, watermarked | Commercial choice: allow download per pack; email attachment off by default |
| AI drafting of minutes | Tenant | Off | Commercial choice; needs M20 approval and human review |
| Reminder offsets for calendar items | Tenant, per obligation | T-15, T-7, T-1, overdue | Tenant may add earlier reminders, not remove the overdue escalation |
| GOV para 10 and para 22 intimation default | Tenant | 7 days [REC] | Tenant may shorten |
| Signing methods | Tenant | DSC for filings; DSC or Aadhaar eSign for minutes and declarations | Commercial choice within law |
| Mandatory agenda items | Platform seeded; tenant adds | GV1.4 set | Floor for seeded items |
| Board compliance certificate | Tenant | Quarterly | Tenant may add monthly |
| Minutes language | Tenant | English; Hindi optional | Commercial choice |

## GV4. Listed-company compliance (LODR, PIT, ICDR)

The `Listed Entity` pack activates from `listing_status`. Every clock runs from the event timestamp, not from user entry. Values are rule-pack defaults [VERIFY each on sebi.gov.in before go-live].

### GV4.1 Applicability

| Status | Packs |
|---|---|
| Equity, main board | LODR Reg 15–48 incl. Reg 17–27; PIT; SAST disclosures received; BRSR and RMC for top 1,000 |
| Equity, SME | Governance exemptions per Reg 15(2) [VERIFY], but Reg 23 RPT rules apply after the 2025 SME reforms |
| Debt-listed | LODR Chapter V (Reg 50–62); PIT for debt UPSI; SEBI NCS Regulations 2021 [VERIFY] |
| HVDLE | Outstanding listed non-convertible debt ≥ **₹5,000 crore** from **22 Jan 2026** (raised from ₹1,000 crore): Chapter V-A governance (Reg 62A onward; 62D board, 62K RPT, 62L subsidiaries, 62M secretarial audit, 62P committees, 62Q governance report) [VERIFY]; entities exiting because of the new threshold are not held to the 3-year sunset |
| Preparing an issue | ICDR data room (GV4.6) |

The HVDLE detector reads outstanding listed debt from M10 daily and opens an onboarding task set on crossing.

### GV4.2 Governance (Reg 17–21, 24, 24A, 27)

- **Reg 17** [VERIFY]: ≥ 6 directors (top 2,000); woman independent director (top 1,000); half independent if the chair is executive or promoter-related, else one-third; ≥ 4 meetings, gap ≤ 120 days; quorum one-third or 3 incl. 1 independent; CEO/CFO certificate (Reg 17(8)).
- **Reg 18–21** committees: values in the GV1.4 pack; stricter listed values override.
- **Reg 24** material subsidiaries (income or net worth above 10% of consolidated, from AC3) and their governance [VERIFY thresholds].
- **Reg 24A** secretarial audit: in AU6. **Conflict guard-rail:** if any Infrabyx or LawDocs group professional is proposed as the tenant's secretarial auditor, flag the Reg 24A prohibited-services conflict, because the group supplies the tenant's compliance system.
- **Reg 27(2)** integrated governance filing within 30 days of quarter end [VERIFY], assembled from GV1–GV3.

### GV4.3 Related-party transactions (Reg 23; CA13 s.188)

- Related-party master extends `related_party` and the CRM 13K register with LODR (Reg 2(1)(zb), (zc)), CA13 s.2(76) and Ind AS 24 flags, each stored separately.
- **States:** `PROPOSED → AC_PRIOR_APPROVAL → BOARD (s.188 if not ordinary-course and arm's length) → SHAREHOLDERS (if material) → APPROVED → EXECUTING → CLOSED`. Omnibus approvals tracked by limit and validity (to the next AGM if approved at an AGM; one year otherwise).
- **Materiality from 18 Nov 2025** (Schedule XII slabs on last audited annual consolidated turnover):

```
if turnover <= 20000 cr:   threshold = 10% × turnover
elif turnover <= 40000 cr: threshold = 2000 cr + 5% × (turnover − 20000 cr)
else:                      threshold = min(3000 cr + 2.5% × (turnover − 40000 cr), 5000 cr)
material = FY aggregate with the party, incl. this transaction, > threshold
```

- **Subsidiary RPTs** above ₹1 crore (listed entity not a party) need prior audit-committee approval above the lower of 10% of the subsidiary's standalone turnover (or paid-up plus premium if no audited year) and the listed entity's threshold.
- **Lending RPTs:** a loan to a related party is also a CRM para 13 credit decision and an FS para 21(9A) disclosure; the RPT record links to the M4 application and never bypasses the credit DoA.
- Disclosures: half-yearly with results (Reg 23(9)); AOC-2 in the Board's report.

### GV4.4 PIT: structured digital database and trading controls

- **SDD (PIT Reg 3(5)–(6)):** append-only, hash-chained entries: UPSI id, nature, internal or external origin, `occurred_or_received_at`, `entered_at`, discloser, recipient, PAN or other identifier, legitimate purpose (Reg 3(2A)), confidentiality notice sent (Reg 3(4)), closure when public. Maintained in-house, time-stamped, retained at least 8 years [VERIFY].
- **External UPSI** (PIT Amendment 2025, effective 9 Jun 2025): entry may be made within 2 days of receipt; lateness computed from the two timestamps; no trading-window closure is needed for such UPSI. The UPSI taxonomy includes the 2025 additions (rating changes other than ESG, fund-raising plans, out-of-ordinary-course orders or contracts, auditor resignations).
- **Automatic entries:** board-pack circulation, access to draft results in AC3 during the closed period, data-room access (GV4.6), sharing with debenture trustees or rating agencies.
- **Lender-side UPSI [REC]:** when a borrower's PAN or CIN maps to a listed issuer, covenant packs, restructuring and stressed-asset documents are marked `upsi_counterparty`, viewers join that issuer's insider list and the issuer goes on the Part 7H restricted list until closure, whether or not the tenant is listed.
- **Designated persons:** DP master with immediate relatives and material financial relationships [VERIFY Schedule B fields]; trading window closed from quarter end to 48 hours after results [VERIFY]; pre-clearance above the code threshold; 6-month contra-trade check; Reg 7(2) continual disclosure above ₹10 lakh a quarter and onward disclosure within 2 trading days [VERIFY]. Holdings come from declarations or RTA/depository uploads; no demat credentials.

### GV4.5 Disclosure clocks

| Obligation | Default clock | Data source |
|---|---|---|
| Prior intimation of Board meeting (results, fund-raising, dividend) | ≥ 2 working days excl. intimation and meeting dates (Reg 29) [VERIFY] | GV2 |
| Board meeting outcome | 30 minutes after close (Reg 30(6)) | GV2 resolutions |
| Material event | 12 hours if internal, 24 hours if external | Event register |
| Shareholding pattern | 21 days after quarter (Reg 31) | RTA import |
| Results, equity and debt | 45 days quarterly, 60 days annual (Reg 33, 52); Reg 52(4) ratios incl. CRAR, GNPA, NNPA, PCR, liquidity | AC3; RK6 |
| Security cover certificate | Quarterly (Reg 54) [VERIFY timeline] | M10, M5 |
| Listed-debt payment intimation | 1 working day (Reg 57) | M10 schedule |
| Annual report; BRSR | On dispatch (Reg 34(1)); BRSR top 1,000 (Reg 34(2)(f)); BRSR Core assurance or assessment phase-in top 150 to 1,000 by FY | AC3; ESG inputs |
| Secretarial compliance report | 60 days after FY end (Reg 24A(2)) | AU6 |
| Loan or debt default disclosure | Per SEBI circular [VERIFY] | M10 |

The **event register** records `event_time`, the Reg 30(4) quantitative test, the authorised KMP's judgement (Reg 30(5)), decision, disclosure time and exchange acknowledgement; a late disclosure records and states the delay reason. Finbyx prepares the XBRL or PDF and checklist for NSE NEAPS or BSE Listing Centre; the authorised official uploads. Exchange data is used only within licence terms.

### GV4.6 ICDR and issue readiness

Read-only, watermarked, SDD-linked issuer data room (constitution, approvals, financials and TB mapping, RBI registration and return acknowledgements, related parties, material contracts, R9 litigation, regulatory actions, KMP details) for merchant bankers, auditors and counsel through the AU7 external-access pattern (`ExternalAccessGranted`; default the engagement window, hard maximum 90 days per grant, renewal a fresh approval). Issue checklists for preferential issues, QIPs, rights and public NCD issues with pricing and lock-in parameters [VERIFY all ICDR values]. QIB status is an attested flag with legal sign-off, never derived from the RBI layer. SAST Reg 29 and 31 disclosures received are logged with receipt time.

### Acceptance tests

- Outstanding listed debt crossing ₹5,000 crore on 3 Feb 2026 flags HVDLE and opens Chapter V-A tasks; ₹2,000 crore does not.
- Consolidated turnover ₹30,000 crore gives an RPT threshold of ₹2,500 crore; ₹1,00,000 crore caps at ₹5,000 crore.
- A related-party loan cannot reach sanction without the audit-committee approval and the CRM para 13 recusal check.
- External UPSI entered 3 days after receipt is flagged late; neither late nor timely entry closes the trading window.
- A pre-clearance request in a closed window is rejected; a DP trade 5 months after an opposite trade fails the contra-trade check.
- A dividend decision at a meeting closing 16:10 creates a disclosure task due 16:40; disclosure at 16:55 records a delay reason.
- Opening a listed borrower's restructuring proposal adds the viewer to the insider list and puts the issuer on the 7H restricted list.

## GV5. Departments, delegation of authority and task management

### GV5.1 Departments and positions

- **Department master (customisable, maker-checker):** code, name, parent, legal entity, cost centre (M1), head, function type (business, control, support), control-function flag (risk, compliance, internal audit; drives GOV para 35(4) pay mix and SoD). Templates seeded per entity type; retired departments keep history and cannot hold active users or tasks.
- **Positions** belong to departments and carry the M19 roles; people hold positions, so a transfer moves permissions in one transaction and opens an access review (`AccessReviewCompleted` with `review_scope = TENANT` on attestation, routed only to the tenant's compliance destination). Org chart generated with KMP and committee overlays.

### GV5.2 Delegation of authority service

One DoA service, called by M4 sanction, R1.7 recovery, R8 settlement, M10 payment release and GV6 payroll release.

- `doa_rule(legal_entity, domain, action, product, amount_from, amount_to, approver_positions[], approvals_required, sequence, exclusions (interested, sanctioner, self), enabling_resolution_id, valid_from, valid_to)`.
- Rules above management level point to the enabling resolution (s.179(3) powers to borrow, invest and lend can be delegated by Board resolution); an expired, revoked or exhausted resolution stops routing and escalates.
- Statutory caps checked before routing: s.180(1)(c) borrowing limit (special resolution) in M10; s.186 for non-exempt items; CON and CRM limits in their modules.
- Within his band a user decides; above it the request routes upward; every decision stores reason code, rule version and inputs (Part 10.2 principle 25). Substitutes (M19) inherit only the delegator's band; self-approval is impossible.
- Maker-checker by at least two individuals for every sensitive action (CYB paras 8(3), 21(6)); delegated authority for key-parameter changes such as rates (CYB para 21(3)).
- **Rule changes:** a DoA rule is drafted, simulated ("who approves a ₹2.4 crore LAP in branch X?" against the last 90 days of real requests, showing every request that would route differently), approved by maker-checker with the enabling resolution attached, and activated from a future `valid_from`; requests already in flight keep the rule version they started under.

### GV5.3 Tasks

- **Sources:** GV2 action items, GV3 calendar, M14 obligations and control tests, Part 7D findings, RK2 KRI breaches, policy reviews, GV6 checklists, manual.
- **Model:** source link, entity, department, assignee (position or person), checker, priority, due date and calendar rule, SLA, evidence requirement, dependencies, confidentiality (normal, restricted HR, restricted legal, UPSI); `OPEN → IN_PROGRESS → SUBMITTED → CHECKED (accepted or returned) → CLOSED` or `CANCELLED (reason, approver)`; `BLOCKED` (open dependency; SLA paused only for non-statutory tasks, a statutory due date never pauses); `REOPENED` from CLOSED within 90 days when a checker, auditor or later evidence shows the closure was wrong. Reassignment records reason and approver; leave substitutes come from M19.
- Regulatory, audit, Board and control tasks close only when a checker other than the assignee accepts the evidence. Escalation at SLA breach to the department head, then the CS or CCO; overdue regulatory tasks appear in the Board compliance certificate.
- Assignment only within the tenant; cross-group work belongs to the Operations Hub grant model.
- **`TaskAssigned`** (canonical) for tasks sourced from regulatory obligations, audit findings or resolutions, to the compliance destination: source reference, due date, owner position, evidence requirement.
- Notices to Teams or Google Chat via GV7 carry a deep link only.

### Acceptance tests

- A ₹2.4 crore loan routes past the ₹2 crore branch band to the credit committee; revoking the committee's enabling resolution escalates to the Board.
- A substitute cannot approve above the delegator's band or an application he sourced.
- A drawdown breaching the s.180(1)(c) limit without a special resolution is blocked.
- Retiring a department with active users is rejected; a position transfer removes old permissions atomically and opens an access review.
- An inspection-observation task cannot be closed by its assignee alone.
- A DoA rule change with a future `valid_from` leaves in-flight requests on the old version; the simulation lists every historical request whose approver would change.
- A `BLOCKED` statutory task keeps its due date and escalates on time.

### Settings and options (GV5)

| Setting | Level | Default | Nature |
|---|---|---|---|
| Department templates | Tenant | Seeded per entity type | Commercial choice |
| DoA matrix | Legal entity, domain, product | Seeded bands per Board resolution; empty for amounts above management level | Regulated configuration (maker-checker; enabling resolution required above management level) |
| Self-approval, sanctioner exclusion, interested-director exclusion | Platform | On | Regulatory floor, no override |
| Task SLA and escalation ladder | Tenant, per source | Department head, then CS or CCO | Commercial choice; statutory dates cannot be extended |
| Checker required to close | Platform for regulatory, audit, Board and control tasks; tenant for others | On | Floor for the listed sources |
| Notifications | User | In-app plus email digest; Teams or Google Chat via GV7 with deep link only | User choice |

## GV6. Client HRMS and payroll (optional module)

Optional SKU `Workforce` (module registry, CM1). The tenant is employer and fiduciary; Infrabyx is processor. Employment processing is a legitimate use (DPDP s.7(i)) [VERIFY wording], still bound by purpose limitation, safeguards and erasure. HR data is RESTRICTED: invisible to loan-side roles, excluded from AI training, Operations Hub dashboards and general exports (DP1). All rates and thresholds live in versioned, effective-dated rule packs.

The Labour Code rule packs (wage definition, leave, overtime, gratuity, State PT and LWF tables, form layouts, prohibited-monitoring list) are one signed, versioned artefact shared with the Operations Hub (OH10): `infrabyx-labour-rulepack`, published under `infrabyx-contracts/rulepacks/labour-codes/[semver]/`, pinned in `contracts.lock` and signature-checked at load; a rule still marked `[VERIFY]` cannot drive a statutory output; salary TDS uses the companion pack `ita25-salary-tds` (Integration Spec Part 12.3). Both repositories run the pack's golden fixtures in CI and must produce identical results.

### GV6.1 Legal status and applicability

- The four Labour Codes are in force from **21 Nov 2025**; final **Central Rules notified 8 May 2026** (G.S.R. 342(E)–345(E); Wages (Central) Rules G.S.R. 343(E), corrigendum G.S.R. 629(E) of 15 Jul 2026) [LAW].
- Most States had not notified final rules by May 2026; old State rules continue so far as consistent (MoLE FAQ 1). A `state_rule_status` table per State and Code holds status, notification and effective date [VERIFY: Delhi, UP, Rajasthan, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Gujarat at go-live].
- **Appropriate Government** per establishment (Central for banking companies and central-sphere establishments; State for most NBFCs [VERIFY]) selects Rules and wage floors.
- **Establishment profile:** headcount by worker type (employee, worker, fixed-term, contract, gig); "worker" excludes supervisors above ₹18,000 a month (MoLE FAQ 14); S&E Act registration and State thresholds (UP 20+; Maharashtra and Gujarat 20+; Rajasthan up to 10 exempt; Karnataka OSHWC exclusion); EPF 20+, ESI 10+ in notified areas, gratuity 10+, POSH IC 10+ per office, Model Standing Orders 300+.

### GV6.2 Lifecycle

`REQUISITION (DoA) → OFFER → OFFER_ACCEPTED → PREBOARDING → IDENTITY_PROVISIONED → JOINED → PROBATION → CONFIRMED → (TRANSFER or ROLE_CHANGE)* → EXIT_INITIATED → LAST_WORKING_DAY → FNF_WAGES_PAID → FNF_OTHER_PAID → ARCHIVED`.

- **Appointment letter** mandatory, existing staff within 3 months of the OSHWC Rules: identity, dates, designation, UAN or ESI number, wage components tagged by CoW class, social security, probation, notice, place of work, WFH clause.
- **Checks:** background verification for sensitive and privileged positions (CYB para 21(4)); fit-and-proper for KMP (GV1); conflicts; code of conduct. Mandatory leave for sensitive positions (ORM `sensitive_position_leave`).
- **Provisioning** (HR maker, IT checker): Finbyx user and position (GV5), mailbox and licence via GV7 if connected; `EmployeeOnboarded` and `MailboxProvisioned` stay inside the tenant boundary. MFA before first access.
- **Exit:** access off at last working day 18:00 (immediately on dismissal), sessions revoked, mailbox retained per policy, documents to the manager; `EmployeeOffboarded` (tenant-internal). Timers from EXIT_INITIATED: **final wages incl. leave encashment within 2 working days** of the last working day (CoW s.17(2)) on the State calendar; gratuity within 30 days; service certificate within 10 days where MSO apply.
- **Hard rule:** final wages never wait for clearance; notice-pay, joining-bonus and training-bond recoveries are not s.18 permitted deductions; any excess becomes a separate receivable.
- **Exceptions:** an offer withdrawn after OFFER_ACCEPTED or a no-show on the joining date ends at `ARCHIVED` with reason and de-provisions any pre-created identity; a resignation withdrawn before LAST_WORKING_DAY returns to the prior state with manager and HR approval; a back-dated exit (absconding) sets the final-wage timer from the recorded last working day and flags the breach for HR head review, never a silent recalculation.

### GV6.3 Time, attendance and lawful WFH

- **Allowed:** SSO sign-in and sign-out, self-entered timesheets, device-compliance status, security logs (180 days in India, CERT-In).
- **Prohibited (no tenant override):** keystroke or mouse scores, screenshots, webcam capture, off-duty location tracking, covert monitoring, AI productivity scores used for discipline or pay.
- **Transparency:** monitoring notice (purposes, data, retention); employees see and correct their records with audit trail; outcomes, not activity, are assessed [REC; DPDP; *Puttaswamy* proportionality].
- **WFH** per appointment terms; for 300+ worker establishments the services MSO lets the employer permit WFH for periods it decides (IRC s.29 MSO, 8 May 2026).
- **Hours:** 8 a day, 48 a week, ≤ 6 days (Wages (Central) Rules r.5); ≤ 10 consecutive days without rest (r.6); **overtime only with recorded consent, at 2×, capped at 144 hours a quarter** (OSHWC Central Rules), stricter State limits applied (for example UP 11 hours a day incl. overtime). Women's work before 06:00 or after 19:00 only with consent and safeguards. Attendance registers kept 5 years (r.51).
- **Regularisation:** a missed sign-in is corrected by an employee request (reason, evidence) approved by the manager; corrections after the payroll cut-off flow to the next run as arrears; every correction keeps the original record and the approver.

### GV6.4 Leave

Statutory default (OSHWC s.32): eligibility after 180 days' work in a calendar year; 1 day per 20 days worked; carry forward up to 30 days (employer-refused leave without cap); year-end encashment on request and of any excess above 30; on exit paid with final wages (2 months on superannuation or death). Tenant policies add casual, sick, maternity (CoSS) [VERIFY entitlements], paternity and special leave, never below the floor; approvals through GV5; refusals recorded with reason. Requests run `DRAFT → SUBMITTED → APPROVED or REJECTED → TAKEN → (CANCELLED or CURTAILED)`; a cancellation after the period re-credits the balance only with manager approval; a balance can never go negative unless the policy allows advance leave, and leave without pay flows to payroll automatically.

### GV6.5 Payroll engine

```
total_rem = Σ remuneration excl. employer PF/pension, gratuity, retrenchment compensation
excl_50   = Σ components tagged as CoW s.2(y) exclusions
cow_wages = basic + DA + retaining + max(0, excl_50 − 0.5 × total_rem)            // CoW s.2(y); MoLE FAQ 2–7
pf_wage   = min(cow_wages, 15000) unless higher voluntary wage                    // re-notified 29 May 2026
pf_ee = 12% × pf_wage; eps = 8.33% × min(pf_wage, 15000); epf_er = 12% × pf_wage − eps   // [VERIFY under CoSS]
esi_ee = 0.75%, esi_er = 3.25% if covered; ee share 0 if avg daily wage ≤ ₹176     // [VERIFY ceiling]
ot_pay  = ot_hours × (monthly_rate / 26 / 8) × 2; block if quarter OT > 144 h or no consent
pt, lwf = state_table(state, period, gross)                                         // versioned; none hard-coded
tds     = ITA25 s.392 projection by regime
deductions ≤ 50% × cow_wages; excess → carry-forward schedule                       // CoW s.18(3); r.13
```

- **Run states:** `DRAFT → INPUTS_LOCKED (cut-off) → COMPUTED → VARIANCE_REVIEWED → APPROVED → BANK_FILE_RELEASED → PAID → STATUTORY_FILES_READY → CLOSED`. A bank credit that bounces opens a re-issue line (never a new run); a back-dated salary revision is paid as arrears in the next run with the tax recomputed; an error after PAID is corrected only by an off-cycle run or recovery schedule within s.18, never by editing a closed run; an exit inside a cycle triggers an off-cycle final-wage run so the 2-working-day timer is met.
- **Validations:** block pay below the applicable minimum (or floor) wage; automatic 50% add-back with warning; flag per-head change above ±10% and new or changed bank accounts.
- **KMP and control-function variable pay (ML/UL, not government-owned):** deferral, malus and clawback ledger, no guaranteed bonus except joining, higher fixed share for control functions (GOV paras 29–37), NRC-approved policy version stored per award.
- **Outputs:** Form V wage slip on or before pay day (r.52); Forms I, IV and IX registers, electronic, 5 years (r.51); EPF ECR and ESI files (ESI within 15 days of month end) and State PT and LWF returns for upload by the authorised person.
- **Income tax:** TDS on salary under ITA25 s.392, on the default regime (s.202 [VERIFY]) unless the employee opts out; quarterly statement in Form 138; **Form 130** (Parts A–C) by 15 June after the tax year, after TRACES processing; Form 16 for FY 2025-26; declarations with proofs [VERIFY: 12BB successor]; tax tables shared with AC5.
- **Gratuity:** `round(15/26 × last monthly cow_wages × completed years)`, part year above 6 months counts, ceiling ₹20 lakh; after 5 years, on death or disablement, fixed-term after 1 year pro rata; actuarial accrual (AS 15 or Ind AS 19) to M10.
- **Bonus** under the Code on Wages [VERIFY percentages and eligibility ceiling].
- **Maker-checker:** payroll prepares; finance releases the bank file through M7 payout rails; no one approves a run containing his own pay line. Payroll journals post via M10; payroll is a books-of-account sub-system, so the audit trail is always on (Rule 3(1) proviso; AC7). Staff loans use Product 19 (`STAFF`), deducted only within the s.18 limits.

### GV6.6 POSH, conduct and payroll-fraud analytics

- **POSH:** Internal Committee per office with 10+ employees (s.4) with composition validation [VERIFY]; restricted case register; annual report (s.21); Board's report statement (Accounts Rules r.8(5)(x)). Whistle-blower cases stay in the GOV register (`whistleblower_case`) routed to the ACB chair.
- **Training records** (CYB paras 35–36; RBC paras 98–99; KYC/AML) feed control evidence.
- **Monthly ghost-employee tests** (HR head and internal audit only): shared bank accounts; pay with no sign-in for 30 days; duplicate PAN; no appointment letter or manager; pay after exit; missing UAN; salary account matching a vendor or borrower account (hashed match). Findings go to a human; no automatic action.

### GV6.7 Appraisal and rewards

- **Cycle:** `GOALS_SET → MID_YEAR_CHECK_IN → SELF_REVIEW → MANAGER_REVIEW → CALIBRATION → HR_APPROVED → COMMUNICATED → (APPEAL → DECIDED)`; dates and rating scale per tenant policy; goals and ratings are outcome-based (GV6.3), never derived from activity monitoring.
- **Controls:** a manager cannot rate a direct relative or himself; calibration changes carry reasons; AI may summarise evidence but never proposes or sets a rating (M20); control-function staff are rated on control objectives, not business targets (GOV paras 21(3), 35(4); CYB para 81).
- **Rewards:** increments and variable pay flow to GV6.5 as effective-dated salary-structure changes after approval through GV5; KMP and senior-management awards follow the NRC-approved policy, deferral and malus or clawback (GOV paras 29–37 where applicable).

### Acceptance tests

- Total remuneration ₹76,000 with ₹40,000 allowances and ₹20,000 basic plus DA gives wages of ₹22,000.
- For a Monday–Friday establishment, last working day Friday 4 Dec 2026 sets the final-wage deadline to Tuesday 8 Dec 2026; seeding a State holiday on Monday 7 Dec 2026 moves it to Wednesday 9 Dec 2026; the run is not held for clearance.
- Deducting unserved notice pay from final wages fails with `not_permitted_deduction_s18`.
- A roster reaching 145 overtime hours in a quarter is blocked; 140 hours without recorded consent is blocked.
- No API or setting exists to enable screenshots; a crafted request returns `prohibited_monitoring`.
- 200 days worked accrue 10 days; 34 carried days at year end encash 4 automatically.
- A preparer cannot approve a run containing his own pay line; a loan-officer role cannot open HR records and an HR role cannot open loan records.
- A bounced salary credit creates a re-issue line on the same run; a closed run cannot be edited and a correction appears only as an off-cycle run.
- An appraisal rating cannot be saved by an AI action, and a manager cannot rate his own appraisal.
- Finbyx and the Operations Hub produce identical outputs for every golden fixture of the pinned `infrabyx-labour-rulepack` version.

## GV7. Workplace suite integration (Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, client data centre)

**Owner decision recorded.** "Business Starter" is a Google Workspace edition; Microsoft's SMB plans are Business Basic, Standard and Premium. Finbyx supports Microsoft 365 (Business and Enterprise plans) and Google Workspace (all editions) through one `WorkplaceProvider` interface, plus a client data-centre agent. Infrabyx's own tenant is configured in the Operations Hub (OH12).

### GV7.1 Residency guard-rails

| Target | Residency | Borrower and loan data | HR and legal restricted data | Other data |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Microsoft 365, Default Geography India (or ADR) | Exchange, SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams chats at rest in India; ADR (India a Local Region) on Business Basic, Standard and Premium, covering all eligible seats [VEND] | Allowed after attestation with evidence | Allowed with DPO approval | Allowed |
| Microsoft 365, other geography | Outside India | Blocked | Blocked, no override | Non-regulated data only |
| Google Workspace | Data regions only US or Europe [VEND] | **Blocked, no override** (CF para 14(4); OUT para 74(vi)) | **Blocked, no override** | **Non-regulated data only** |
| Client data centre (agent) | Tenant-controlled | Allowed if attested in India | Allowed if attested in India | Allowed |

"Non-regulated data" means `PUBLIC` or `INTERNAL` material and `CONFIDENTIAL` documents with no personal data, books of account, returns, loan or HR data (for example approved policies and product brochures; Integration Spec Part 12.2). Enforced per data class (Integration Spec Part 13.2) on every write, with no tenant or DPO override for regulated classes outside India; books of account are never held only outside India (Accounts Rules r.3(1), 3(5); AC7). [VERIFY: a Graph property proving Default Geography; until confirmed, an admin-centre export signed by the tenant's IT head, re-attested annually.]

### GV7.2 Identity into Finbyx

- **SSO** through the M19 OIDC abstraction: Entra ID (multi-tenant app, admin consent, OIDC or SAML), Google (OIDC or SAML), on-premises AD through AD FS or LDAP federation. MFA stays mandatory (CYB para 115; OUT para 97(viii)); the IdP's MFA claim is accepted only with a conditional-access attestation, else Finbyx adds its own factor.
- **SCIM 2.0 endpoint** for Entra ID or Google provisioning; SCIM groups map to positions (GV5), never directly to privileged roles, which still need maker-checker. IdP deactivation disables the Finbyx user and revokes sessions and tokens within 15 minutes [REC].

### GV7.3 Mailboxes and licences (optional outbound)

- **Microsoft Graph:** `POST /users` (disabled until the day before joining, `usageLocation = IN`), then `POST /users/{id}/assignLicense` with `addLicenses[{skuId, disabledPlans}]` [VERIFY usageLocation prerequisite]; groups and Teams; least-privilege application permissions (`User.ReadWrite.All` scoped by administrative unit where available, `LicenseAssignment.ReadWrite.All`, `Group.ReadWrite.All`); exit: `revokeSignInSessions`, block sign-in, shared mailbox or forward, licence removed after the retention hold.
- **Google Admin SDK:** `users.insert` into the configured OU, groups; exit: suspend, Data Transfer API for Drive ownership, delete per policy. Domain-wide delegation only with the minimal scopes approved by the Super Admin (changes take up to 24 hours). For a tenant whose own mail system is Google Workspace, Finbyx sends only the directory attributes an email account needs (name, work email, department, position title); no HR record field (PAN, salary, leave, bank, health, address) is ever written to any Google service.
- **Address rules:** `first.last@[domain]`, then middle initial, then a digit; reserved names blocked; 90-day quarantine after exit; never reissued to another person. Steps idempotent on `(employee_id, provider, action)`; `MailboxProvisioned` stays tenant-internal.

### GV7.4 Documents, calendars and notifications

- **SharePoint and OneDrive:** `Sites.Selected` per site granted by the tenant admin; dedicated libraries (board packs, signed minutes, policies, exports); upload sessions for large files; delta queries with stored `deltaLink` plus change notifications for two-way sync of the policy library only. **Google Drive:** tenant-owned shared drive, narrowest scope, non-regulated libraries only (approved policies and brochures); board packs, minutes, registers, HR and loan documents and exports are never offered for Google Drive sync. M16 stays the system of record; copies carry the M16 hash; an edited copy re-enters only as a new version through maker-checker. Exports and backups: Part 7J.
- **Calendars:** GV2 schedules create Graph or Google Calendar events with Teams or Meet links; the event carries meeting type, time and a Finbyx deep link only (no agenda, papers or UPSI); Finbyx attendance remains the legal record.
- **Notifications:** Teams app bot proactive messages and Google Chat app messages; Office 365 connectors (incoming webhooks) are not used because Microsoft is retiring them in favour of Workflows [VERIFY timeline]. Payloads carry category, count and a sign-in deep link only: never borrower names, PAN, account numbers, amounts or UPSI.
- **Subscriptions:** renewed at 80% of lifetime (users about 23 days, drive about 24 days, mail about 5.5 days, Teams about 2.4 days); `reauthorizationRequired` or `missed` triggers delta resync; `clientState` checked; validation token echoed within Microsoft's limit [VERIFY].

### GV7.5 Client data-centre agent and migration

- **Agent:** the Finbyx Connector Agent of Part 7C AC6.1 (one agent, one `connector_agent` record), extended with storage and directory-sync capabilities; signed container or Windows service in the tenant's data centre; outbound-only mTLS (no inbound ports); pulls tenant-scoped jobs (exports, backups, renditions, directory sync) and writes to the tenant's file share, NAS, S3-compatible store or SFTP; heartbeats; certificate rotated every 90 days [REC]; updates only to signed versions after tenant approval; every job hashed and logged on both sides. Read-only AD or LDAP sync where there is no cloud IdP. Finbyx does not attach arbitrary disks in its cloud; the agent is the supported route.
- **Migration:** bulk import of policies, board records and historical minutes from SharePoint, OneDrive, Drive or file shares (dry run, hash, classification, reject file). Mailbox and drive moves between suites use the vendors' tools (Microsoft Migration Manager, Exchange migration batches, Google Workspace Migrate or Data Migration Service) as an Operations Hub professional-services engagement (OH4) [VERIFY edition limits]; Finbyx re-points its connector and re-validates residency.

### Settings and options (GV7)

| Setting | Level | Default | Nature |
|---|---|---|---|
| Provider per legal entity | Tenant | None (no outbound connection) | Commercial choice; the office-suite decision is recorded first |
| Residency attestation | Connection | Required before any regulated class; re-attested yearly | Regulatory floor |
| Data classes allowed per target | Connection | Derived from GV7.1; tenant may narrow | Floor: cannot widen beyond GV7.1 |
| SSO and MFA claim trust | Tenant | Finbyx adds its own factor unless a conditional-access attestation is on file | Floor: MFA always required |
| SCIM group-to-position map | Tenant | Empty; privileged roles never mapped directly | Regulated configuration (maker-checker) |
| Deprovisioning latency | Platform | ≤ 15 minutes after IdP deactivation | Floor |
| Mailbox provisioning, address pattern, quarantine | Tenant | Off; `first.last`; 90-day quarantine, never reissued | Commercial choice except the no-reissue rule |
| Notification channel | Tenant | In-app and email; Teams or Google Chat optional | Payload rule (category, count, deep link) cannot be changed |
| Agent update policy | Tenant | Signed versions after tenant approval; certificate rotation 90 days | Floor for signing |

### Menu and screens (workspace N, menu `Settings › Workplace`)

### Acceptance tests

- A Google Drive target receiving the "Loans" dataset fails with `residency_blocked_borrower_data`; "Policies" succeeds; signed Board minutes and HR documents are not offered for Google Drive sync.
- A Microsoft 365 target in another geography refuses HR documents with no override path.
- A Microsoft 365 target without residency attestation accepts only non-regulated classes (no personal data, books of account, returns, loan or HR data); after attestation, loan document renditions sync with the M16 hash.
- An exit blocks the Entra account, revokes sessions and converts the mailbox, keeping the licence until the hold is confirmed; steps retry idempotently after a simulated 429.
- A SCIM group change mapped to a privileged role creates a pending maker-checker request.
- CI scans notification payloads for PAN, account-number and amount patterns; any match fails the build.
- A simulated `missed` lifecycle event triggers a delta resync with no duplicate document versions.
- An agent with an expired certificate cannot fetch jobs; an unsigned build is refused at registration.

# PART 7G — INSTITUTION PROFILES: CO-OPERATIVES, MICROFINANCE, ARCs AND IFSC ENTITIES

**Purpose.** v1.4 was built around the NBFC. v1.5 sells the same engine to institutions whose law, vocabulary, capital rules, returns and permitted products differ: credit co-operative societies (not RBI regulated entities), urban and rural co-operative banks, group-model microfinance lenders, asset reconstruction companies (ARCs) and IFSCA finance companies. The **institution profile** is the single switch that loads the right law: rule packs, returns, accounting framework, capital engine, products, guard-rails and interface vocabulary. Nothing downstream may hard-code NBFC assumptions.

**Applicability.** NBFCs of every layer (Part 8A.25); State and multi-State credit co-operative societies; UCBs, StCBs and DCCBs; microfinance overlays; ARCs; IFSCA FCs and FUs. Core Investment Companies (written NBFC-CIC; bare "CIC" in this Part means a credit information company), AIFs and PMS are profiled here and specified in Part 7H.

**Requirement codes.** Existing: CF, CIR, CON, INV, CAP, SBR, MFI, TDCR, SEC, IRACP, RBC, KYC, RSA, FS, MSD, SR. New (Part 8A.37): `MSCS` (MSCS Act 2002 as amended 2023, MSCS Rules 2023, CRCS orders, model bye-laws), `SCS` (State co-operative Acts and Rules; Maharashtra as `SCS-MH`), `ARC` (RBI (Asset Reconstruction Companies) Directions 2025 and SARFAESI provisions for ARCs), `IFSCA-FC`, `CICRA`, `DPDP`, `IND-AS`. Also in Part 8A.37: `SARFAESI`, `BUDS`, `UCB` (RBI UCB Directions 2025 set), `NABARD`, `SRO-MFIN`, `KA15` (Karnataka Act 15 of 2025), `TN40` (Tamil Nadu Act 40 of 2025), `FEMA`.

**Data owned.** Profile and rule-pack bindings; member register, share ledger, deposit-ledger snapshots, surety register, appropriation runs, AGM and election records, Registrar audit paras (co-operatives); group, centre, meeting, cash-in-transit and SHG records (microfinance); trust ledgers, SR register, NAV history, settlement approvals (ARCs); USD ledgers and activity whitelist (IFSC). Returns are produced by Part 7B, books by Part 7C, ratios and capital by Part 7E.

**Extends, does not repeat:** Part 3.1, Product 11 and Part 8A.31 (microfinance), Part 8A.25 (entity profile), M11 and R13 (transfers, co-lending), R1.4 (mechanism selection). Labels: `[LAW]`, `[REG]`, `[SRO]`, `[PRAC]`, `[REC]`, `[VERIFY: …]`.

### IP1.2 Profile record

Extends `entity_regulatory_profile` with: type and sub-type; governing Act and State; registrar or regulator; registration number and date; area of operation; deposits and assets (monthly, last audited); MSCS size class, UCB tier, NBFC layer, ARC NOF band, IFSC activity class; flags (RBI regulated entity, deposit-taking, public funds, customer interface, listed, Ind AS, SRO member, CIC member under CICRA, QB attestation, Maharashtra Regulatory Board coverage, audit class by year, PCA status, FEMA resident-dealing basis). Computed bindings: rule-pack versions, return packs, accounting framework, capital engine, entitlements, guard-rails, calendar seeds, vocabulary and language packs.

### IP1.3 Rule-pack resolution

Rule packs are versioned, effective-dated documents (`effective_from`, `effective_to`, `source_url`, `status` in force / enacted-not-notified / draft / stub, `counsel_signoff`).

| Layer | Source | Tenant change |
|---|---|---|
| L0 | Statute and rules | No |
| L1 | Regulator directions and orders (RBI, NABARD, CRCS, IFSCA) | No |
| L2 | SRO code (held or adopted) | Tighten only |
| L3 | Bye-laws (co-operatives) or Board policy | Versioned upload with approval |
| L4 | Tenant configuration | Tighten only |

- The strictest applicable limit wins; a lower layer that loosens a higher one is rejected with `RULE_LOOSENING_BLOCKED`.
- A `stub` pack cannot drive a live decision; a profile whose products touch a stub cannot be activated until it is completed and counsel-signed.
- Every decision stores the pack versions used.
- **Pack lifecycle:** `DRAFT → COUNSEL_REVIEW → SIGNED → SCHEDULED → IN_FORCE → SUPERSEDED`; maker (Infrabyx regulatory content team for L0–L2, tenant CCO for L3–L4) ≠ checker; `SIGNED` needs `counsel_signoff` for L0–L2; cut-over runs at 00:00 IST on `effective_from` as a dated release with regression fixtures.
- **Back-dated correction:** a corrected pack with an earlier `effective_from` never rewrites past decisions. It produces an impact report (decisions taken in the window that would now fail), opens a remediation task per affected case for the CCO, and blocks only new decisions on the old version.

### IP1.7 Profile changes

Triggers: MSCS size class (₹10, ₹100, ₹500 crore deposits), UCB tier, NBFC layer, NBFC-ICC to NBFC-MFI (only on a recorded RBI registration change), Type I deregistration (7H IV5.6), ARC NOF band, IFSC activity class. Workflow `DETECTED → IMPACT_ASSESSED → APPROVED (CCO and Board or Managing Committee) → SCHEDULED → ACTIVE`, with `REJECTED` (reason recorded; re-detected at the next monthly run) and `ROLLED_BACK` (only before the first return or decision on the new version, by the same approvers). Detection runs on each monthly snapshot and on audited figures; the impact assessment lists changed packs, returns, limits, products and guard-rails and is due within 15 days of detection [REC], escalating to the CCO after that. Glide paths honoured (UCB 3 years on moving up; CRCS CRAR to 2028-29). Historic returns stay bound to the profile version of their period.

| Rule-pack versions bound | Profile | latest `IN_FORCE` | Regulatory floor; L2–L4 may only tighten |
| Vocabulary pack and languages | Tenant | from type; English plus Hindi | Commercial |
| Bye-law or Board-policy upload (L3) | Profile | none | Versioned; maker-checker; loosening rejected |
| Tenant tightening values (L4), for example a 45% household cap | Product | pack value | Commercial within the floor |
| Capability toggles in IP1.4 | Profile | off unless `Y` | `Y` cells commercial; **N** cells fixed |

### Menu and screens

- **Settings › Rule packs:** list with layer, version, status and effective dates (filters: layer, status, expiring in 90 days); detail with clause map and source link; **Compare versions**; **Upload bye-law (L3)**; approval queue for L3–L4 changes; error state shows `RULE_LOOSENING_BLOCKED` with the governing layer and value.
- **Compliance › Guard-rails:** registry (read-only for every role), evaluation log (filters: guard-rail, outcome, date, user), export CSV; profile-change queue with impact report and glide-path chart.

### Acceptance tests

- `CREDIT_COOP_MSCS` tenant creating a co-lending partner, DA pool or SR investment → each blocked with its guard-rail code.
- Board policy sets the microfinance household cap at 55% → `RULE_LOOSENING_BLOCKED`; 45% → accepted.
- Activating a Rajasthan `CREDIT_COOP_STATE` profile on a stub pack → refused until counsel-signed.
- `COOP` vocabulary relabels "Customer" as "Member" in the UI; CIC export field names unchanged.
- MSCS deposits cross ₹100 crore → Small to Medium; CRAR target 9% to 12% from the approved effective date, glide path shown.
- A society named "Sahakari Bank Credit Society" → activation fails (GR-7G-02).
- A corrected pack back-dated by 2 months → past decisions unchanged; impact report lists the failing ones and a remediation task opens for each.
