## IP2. Credit co-operative societies

### IP2.1 Legal position

- A State or multi-State credit co-operative society is **not** an RBI regulated entity; RBI Directions on digital lending, co-lending, IRACP, capital and returns do not bind it [REC, from TDCR para 97 and RBI press release of 22 Nov 2021].
- It is still bound by its Act, Rules and bye-laws; the DPDP Act 2023 (data fiduciary); consumer protection law; TRAI rules; BUDS (MSCS deposits from voting members are a regulated scheme, First Schedule item 8; State society schemes item 4(i)); State coercion laws (TN40).
- Non-bank co-operatives may not use "bank", "banker" or "banking" (since 29 Sep 2020); deposits from non-members, nominal or associate members are unlicensed banking without DICGC cover (RBI press release 22 Nov 2021).
- Money-lending Acts exclude co-operative loans (Maharashtra Money-Lending (Regulation) Act 2014 s.2(13)(e); KA15 s.1(3)) [VERIFY other States].
- **Default conduct [REC]:** RE-equivalent disclosure, collection, grievance and data practices.

### IP2.2 Rule packs

- **Shipped complete:** MSCS (Act, Rules 2023, CRCS orders of 22 Jan 2024 and July 2025, model thrift and credit bye-laws) and Maharashtra (MCS Act 1960 incl. Ch XI-1A, MCS Rules 1961, Regulatory Board regulations [VERIFY texts]).
- **Stubs, completed at onboarding with counsel:** Gujarat, Rajasthan, Karnataka (KCS Act 1959, Souharda Act 1997), Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh. Each covers member classes, deposit eligibility, share linkage, loan caps, NPA and provisioning, liquidity, appropriation, dividend cap, audit and return calendar, audit classes, dispute forum, recovery route and coercion overlay.

### IP2.3 Membership register

| Class | Vote | Deposit | Borrow | Surety | General Body | Dividend |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ORDINARY_VOTING` | Y | **Y** | Y | Y | Y | Y |
| `NOMINAL` | N | **N (hard)** | bye-law | N | N | N (SCS-MH s.24(2)) |
| `ASSOCIATE` | N | **N (hard)** | bye-law | N | N | per Act |
| `NON_VOTING_SHAREHOLDER` (MSCS s.26 proviso) | N | **N (hard)** | bye-law | N | N | bye-law |
| `INSTITUTIONAL` | bye-law | [VERIFY] | bye-law | N | bye-law | Y |

- Maharashtra "associate member" means a joint holder not first-named; the State pack maps it.
- **States:** `APPLIED → SCRUTINY → APPROVED | REJECTED | DEEMED_REFUSED → ACTIVE ⇄ DEFAULTER → RESIGNED | EXPELLED | DECEASED → LIABILITY_TAIL → CLOSED`.
- **Timers:** MSCS decision within 4 months, communicated within 15 days, else `DEEMED_REFUSED` (MSCS s.25(4)); ex-member liability 2 years (bye-law); expulsion bar 3 years (2023 amendment).
- **Capture:** KYC (Aadhaar offline only, never stored; Voter ID; PAN), residence or employment in the area of operation, nominee, admission fee, share money, board resolution, Maharashtra Form I and J-1 lists (MCS Rules 32–33), one-credit-society borrowing declaration (MCS Rule 45).
- **Holding cap:** one-fifth of share capital (model bye-laws). **Death:** freeze, nominee claim, lien and set-off against shares, dividend and deposits (bye-law cl.22), surety substitution task.
- **Channels:** branch entry, or an application from Udofin through `POST /v1/societies/{id}/membership-applications` (Integration Spec 6.24), which Finbyx serves for a society tenant and records as `APPLIED` with `source = UDOFIN` (idempotency key; acknowledgement within 5 minutes; the statutory timer starts on receipt). `SCRUTINY` exits only by a committee or board decision with resolution reference; the applicant is told the outcome in writing with reasons for a refusal.
- **Membership verification:** Finbyx serves `GET /v1/societies/{id}/members/{ref}` (class, status, borrowing eligibility, share-holding sufficiency; consent reference required; never deposit data).
- **Events (producer rule, Integration Spec 6.24):** the society's system of record produces `MemberAdmitted` (on `ACTIVE`) and `ShareCapitalPosted`; when that system is Finbyx, Finbyx produces them, otherwise the society's certified LOS does and Finbyx produces nothing. Udofin consumes them for member-only journeys (Udofin UP4, MG1); status changes after admission reach Udofin only through the verification API. Applications from Udofin carry `lender_type = NON_RE_SOCIETY` on `ApplicationSubmitted` and route to the `COOP` overlay (IP2.6).

### IP2.4 Share ledger

- Events: allotment, instalment, transfer (after 1 year, board approval), redemption at face value, forfeiture, non-voting issue, lien.
- Validations: holding ≤ 20% of capital; no loan on the security of own shares (MSCS s.66(1)); no finance to buy shares; no redemption while borrower or surety in default.
- Linkage top-up: `shares_required = ceil(loan × link_pct ÷ face_value)`; `top_up = max(0, shares_required − shares_held)`; collected before disbursal or deducted only with displayed consent [REC].
- Dividend on year-end holdings (bye-law cl.48(a)); unclaimed dividend forfeited to reserve after 3 years.
- Event: `ShareCapitalPosted`.

### IP2.5 Deposits: Deposit Ledger Adapter (v1.5); deposit module deferred to v1.6

- **v1.5 Deposit Ledger Adapter (mandatory where the society holds deposits):**
  - daily SFTP CSV or API import from the society's core: depositor and member IDs, product (savings, current, FD, RD, cumulative; bye-law cl.43), balance, rate, maturity, lien, as-of date, file hash;
  - every deposit matched to the register; a non-member or non-voting depositor raises a GR-7G-01 exception, Board alert and remediation task. Finbyx cannot stop the core accepting it, so it blocks every Finbyx use of that deposit (lien, FD loan, set-off) until the exception is closed with evidence;
  - leverage: `(deposits + borrowings) ≤ multiple × (paid-up capital + reserves − accumulated losses)`; multiple 10 for MSCS (CRCS order) and per State pack otherwise (MSCS s.67);
  - loan against FD ≤ 90% (MCS Rule 45A);
  - "Deposits with this society are not insured by DICGC" on every member statement Finbyx produces [REC];
  - import states `RECEIVED → VALIDATED → MATCHED → PUBLISHED`, or `REJECTED` (hash, schema or control-total failure; the previous snapshot stays, marked stale). No file by the cut-off (default 07:00 IST [REC]) → `STALE` alert to the society's operations owner; after 2 business days, lien, FD-loan and set-off use is blocked until a fresh snapshot arrives. A corrected file for a past date replaces that snapshot as a new version and re-runs the leverage and GR-7G-01 checks for it.
- **v1.6 deposit module (optional licensed add-on):** savings, FD, RD and cumulative accounts for societies and UCBs with GR-7G-01 enforced at source; gated on State legal review, an Income-tax Act 2025 TDS engine for deposit interest (7C AC5) [VERIFY sections], dormancy and unclaimed rules, and auditor sign-off on accruals.
- **Udofin never lists, solicits, markets or collects deposits**; read-only balances only if the society opts in (off by default).

### IP2.6 Loan origination (`COOP` overlay on Part 6 templates)

1. **Member gate:** `ACTIVE`, class can borrow, not `DEFAULTER`, KYC complete, MCS Rule 45 declaration (Maharashtra).
2. **Ceiling** `= min(bye-law product cap, share multiple × shares_held, 90% of pledged FD, single 15% / group 25% of Tier I + II capital)`; unsecured book ≤ 15% of loans after the loan (SHG, employee and microfinance co-operatives exempt); housing only by Medium (≤ ₹1 crore) and Large (≤ ₹1.2 crore) MSCS; no land or builder loans (CRCS order 22 Jan 2024).
3. **Sureties:** active non-defaulting members only (a non-member's security is barred, MSCS s.66(1)); live-guarantee cap per surety (default 2 [PRAC]); consent artefact; surety liability ledger.
4. **Directors and relatives:** recusal; aggregate ≤ 10% of member loans (bye-law cl.58(b)); reported to the AGM (MSCS s.39(3)).
5. **Affordability:** FOIR per policy; the 50% household cap for collateral-free loans to households ≤ ₹3 lakh [REC].
6. **Sanction** by committee or board with minutes reference and related-party check.
7. **Disclosure sheet:** APR, charges, schedule, recovery forum, grievance route [REC].
8. **Documents:** agreement (eSign or wet ink), surety bonds, land charge (MCS s.48) and salary-deduction authority (MCS s.49) where applicable [VERIFY].
9. **Disbursal** to the member's own bank account; no cash disbursal by default. **Recall** on 1 week's notice where permitted (MCS Rule 46).

### IP2.7 Prudential monitoring

**MSCS — CRCS order L-11012/01/2023-Reg of 22 Jan 2024 [REG] [VERIFY: order text; secondary sources]:**

| Parameter | Micro (≤ ₹10 cr deposits) | Small (≤ ₹100 cr) | Medium (≤ ₹500 cr) | Large (> ₹500 cr) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CRAR (glide to 2028-29) | 9% | 9% | 12% | 12% |
| Cash | ≥ 2% of deposits | same | same | same |
| Liquid investments | rising to 18% of deposits | same | same | same |
| Leverage | deposits + loans ≤ 10 × (capital + reserves − losses) | same | same | same |
| Exposure | single 15%, group 25% of Tier I + II | same | same | same |
| Unsecured loans | ≤ 15% of loans | same | same | same |
| Housing | none | none | ≤ ₹1 crore | ≤ ₹1.2 crore |
| Return | quarterly, CRCS portal | same | same | same |

**MSCS branch expansion (CRCS order, July 2025) [VERIFY text]:** prior approval; ≤ 10% of branches a year (maximum 10); State Registrar certificate of no deposits from non-voting members; CRAR met, **GNPA < 7%, NNPA < 3%**, profit in each of 3 years, liquidity buffers, KYC and grievance mechanism. Finbyx builds the eligibility pack with lineage; any failed test blocks it.

**Maharashtra Ch XI-1A [LAW]:** no deposits from non-members (s.144-5A); administrative-expense cap (s.144-8A) and cash reserve (s.144-9A) [VERIFY %]; **SLR ≥ 25% of deposits**, up to 5% in MSC Bank bonds (s.144-10A; circular of 22 May 2025) [VERIFY hook]; loan restrictions (s.144-11A); Regulatory Board regulations as an L1 pack (ss.144-13A–24A); Stabilisation and Liquidity Support Fund (ss.144-25A–30A) [VERIFY rate].

These are legal limits under the society's own Act, not RBI ratios; Part 7E RK6 shows them with source `MSCS` or `SCS`.

### IP2.8 NPA and write-off

NPA threshold (default 90 days [VERIFY State circulars]), buckets, provisions and BDDR from the pack. Maharashtra write-off: board → **prior General Body approval** → Registrar or financing central bank where indebted → BDDR or, for A and B class societies, the Bad Debt Fund (MCS Rule 49); technical write-off keeps recovery live (R12). Net profit is after provisions (Rule 49A); appropriation (IP2.9) runs only after provisioning is locked.

### IP2.9 Year-end: appropriation, dividend, AGM, elections

| Item | MSCS (s.63, s.63A) | Maharashtra (MCS ss.66–68; Rule 52) |
|---|---|---|
| Reserve fund | ≥ 25% of net profit | ≥ 25%; Registrar may permit ≥ 10% (s.66(2)) |
| Education fund | 1% to the Co-operative Education Fund | to the State federation (s.68) [VERIFY rate] |
| Unforeseen-loss reserve | ≥ 10% | bye-law |
| CRRD Fund | lesser of ₹1 crore and 1% of net profit, if profitable in each of the preceding 3 years (s.63A) | — |
| Dividend | ≤ prescribed limit [VERIFY rate] | ≤ 15% without Registrar sanction (s.67) |
| Dividend equalisation | bye-law | Rule 52 |
| Donations | ≤ 5% | [VERIFY] |

- Validations: minimums met; Σ = distributable profit; dividend ≤ cap; nominal members excluded (SCS-MH s.24(2)); [VERIFY] CRRD order. Dividend run: register, TDS (7C AC5) [VERIFY], credit to bank or savings account, 3-year forfeiture.
- **AGM (MSCS within 6 months of 31 March, s.39):** 14 days' notice (7 for special); quorum one-fifth; accounts, audit and rectification reports; annual report with non-unanimous decisions and director loans; budget; auditor from panel; bye-law amendments (two-thirds, 15 days' notice); write-offs (Maharashtra); minutes within 30 days. If the board defaults, the Central Registrar may convene within 90 days; Finbyx escalates at month 5.
- **Elections:** term tracker; notice to the Co-operative Election Authority 6 months before term end (MSCS s.45J(8)).
- **Governance (7F GV1–GV2 reused):** Audit and Ethics Committee, recusal, non-unanimous register, Information Officer log [VERIFY SLA], Co-operative Ombudsman tracker (decision 3 months, appeal to the Central Registrar 1 month, MSCS s.85A [VERIFY]).

### IP2.10 Audit and Registrar returns

| Item | MSCS | Maharashtra |
|---|---|---|
| Auditor | Central Registrar panel; special panel where deposits or turnover > ₹500 crore (s.70(2)) | State panel; appointed by AGM, filed within 30 days; ≤ 3 consecutive years; consent within 1 month of AGM (s.79(1B)) |
| Timing | report within 6 months (s.70(3A)) | within 4 months of year-end (s.75(1), s.81, Rule 69) |
| Concurrent audit | turnover or deposits > ₹500 crore (s.70A) | [VERIFY] |
| Rectification | para tracker | **Form O within 3 months**; Registrar review 6 months (s.82; Circular 254/2015) |
| Audit class | — | Form N-2, 7 parameters (Rule 69(3)); bands [VERIFY: A ≥ 70, B 50–69, C 35–49, D < 35] |
| Annual return | within 6 months (s.120; bye-law cl.51) [VERIFY] | within 6 months (s.79(1A)) |
| Lateness | directors disqualified 5 years (s.43(2)(e)–(f)) | Registrar action |

Returns sit in 7B RR1 (regulator `RCS-[State]` or `CRCS`), validated in RR3, filed by an authorised human via RR4. Audit uses 7D AU2, AU5, AU7; audit-class history drives class-dependent rules; a dashboard shows days to the s.43(2) trigger per director.

### IP2.11 Disputes and statutory recovery

**R1.4 for co-operative profiles:** SARFAESI and DRT hidden; civil suit hidden where the statutory forum is exclusive (SCS-MH s.91(3)); s.138 NI Act available; IBC s.7 only for corporate debtors after counsel confirms standing [VERIFY].

- **Maharashtra s.91 Co-operative Court:** disputes on constitution, management or business; limitation 6 years (s.92); appeal within 2 months (s.96); execution as decree or land revenue within 12 years (s.98).
- **Maharashtra s.101 certificate** (notified classes) [VERIFY notification for credit societies]: `NOTICES_SERVED → BOARD_RESOLUTION → PACK_BUILT (statement, sanction, agreement, surety bonds) → APPLIED (ARCS/DDR) → HEARING → CERTIFICATE_ISSUED → EXECUTION (s.156; Rule 107) [VERIFY Rules 86, 107] → CLOSED`. Recoverable as arrears of land revenue; post-certificate transfers void (s.99), so an encumbrance flag is set on attached property.
- **MSCS:** arbitration by an arbitrator appointed by the Central Registrar (s.84; bye-law cl.53) → award → recovery [VERIFY ss.84, 94].
- **Equator (GR-7G-05):** private arbitration under the 1996 Act blocked for s.91 or s.84 disputes; voluntary conciliation or mediation allowed; settlements filed before the statutory forum where proceedings are pending.

### IP2.12 Conduct overlays

- **TN40** (assent 9 Jun 2025): co-operative societies exempt from registration but bound by s.20 coercion provisions (s.2 proviso); up to 3 or 5 years and/or ₹5 lakh (s.21); deemed abetment under BNS s.108 (s.22) [VERIFY commencement].
- **KA15** (in force 12 Feb 2025): KCS and Souharda societies and co-operative banks exempt (s.1(3)); MSCS in Karnataka [VERIFY].
- **Contact windows (tenant may narrow):** 09:00–18:00 for collateral-free loans to households ≤ ₹3 lakh; 08:00–19:00 otherwise [REC]; enforced by R15.1. Each field event carries the coercion checklist and geo-time stamp; a coercion complaint suspends the agent.
- **Grievance:** society officer → Registrar or Co-operative Ombudsman (MSCS s.85A) → consumer commission; the RBI Ombudsman is never shown.
- **Bureau:** CIC submission only if the society is a CIC member under CICRA [VERIFY]; otherwise checks rely on declarations. Never borrow another lender's bureau access.

### IP2.13 No co-lending or loan sale; lawful alternatives

A credit society is not a "lender" (TDCR para 12(4)) or co-lending partner (para 97); NBFCs acquire only from listed lenders (para 7); co-operative banks are lenders only as stressed-loan transferors. Blocked (GR-7G-03, -04, -13): co-lending, blended pricing or shared escrow with a society or co-operative bank; DA or participation either way (except a co-operative bank's stressed-loan sale to a permitted transferee or ARC); split-loan routing; society DLG to an NBFC.

| Alternative [REC; counsel to confirm] | Conditions | Finbyx support |
|---|---|---|
| Wholesale term loan from an NBFC or bank to the society for on-lending | Within the society's borrowing limit (MSCS s.67; State pack) and bye-laws; lender's own CRM and CON limits | NBFC: Product 18 `CORP`; society: borrowings sub-ledger (M10 item 8) |
| Society as sourcing agent of an NBFC (NBFC sole lender, under its outsourcing controls) | Bye-laws permit; lender disclosed; no deposit cross-sell; conflict policy | NBFC: M2 partner; society: referral log |
| Business correspondent of a bank | Bank BC rules [VERIFY eligibility] | Record only |
| Independent parallel loans | Separate appraisal with aggregated affordability; no joint pricing, escrow or documents | Bureau and household views |
| Udofin member-only track for the society's own loans | Udofin UP4; no deposit marketing; no borrower fees | `MemberAdmitted`, `ShareCapitalPosted` |

### IP2.14 Fraud and scam controls

Patterns: agent-raised non-member deposits, fictitious and related-party loans, evergreening [VERIFY reported cases]. Controls: related-party graph (members, directors, relatives, sureties, agents) with block or escalation at sanction; daily leverage and exposure checks; branch new-borrower velocity and loans to members admitted within 30 days [REC]; agent-commission anomalies; deposit exceptions (IP2.5); concurrent-audit read-only access; CRCS returns reconciled to the ledger.

### Settings and options

| Setting | Level | Default | Nature |
|---|---|---|---|
| Member classes and rights | Profile | State or MSCS pack | Regulatory floor (deposit right only for `ORDINARY_VOTING`) |
| Admission fee, share face value, holding cap | Society | bye-law values | Bye-law (L3); cap ≤ one-fifth |
| Share linkage mode (`MULTIPLE` or `LINKAGE`) and value | Product | bye-law value | Bye-law |
| Top-up collection | Product | before disbursal | Deduction from disbursal only with displayed consent |
| Live guarantees per surety | Society | 2 [PRAC] | Commercial (tighten only) |
| Deposit Ledger Adapter feed, cut-off, stale block | Society | SFTP daily, 07:00, 2 business days | Adapter mandatory where deposits are held |
| Read-only deposit balances to Udofin | Society | off | Commercial; member consent |
| Dividend rate proposal and TDS | Year | none | Within the cap; General Body approval |
| AGM escalation lead time | Society | month 5 after year-end | Regulatory (MSCS s.39) |
| Contact window for member loans | Product | IP2.12 windows | Tighten only |

### Menu and screens

All under **Members** (workspace A for branch staff, S for the society secretary and board, K for compliance; read-only for auditors in V):

- **Members › Register:** list (filters: class, status, branch, area, defaulter, admitted in last 30 days), member 360 (shares, loans, sureties given, nominee, timers), **Admit member** wizard (KYC → area evidence → class → nominee → fees and shares → declarations → committee queue), applications queue with deemed-refusal countdown, bulk export of Form I and J-1 lists; actions **Mark defaulter**, **Resign**, **Expel** (bar date shown), **Record death**.
- **Members › Shares:** share accounts, transaction entry (allotment, transfer, redemption, forfeiture) with board-approval reference, top-up calculator, lien view; redemption button disabled with an explain-why message while the member or a surety is in default.
- **Members › Deposits adapter:** import runs (status, hash, row counts), exceptions queue (GR-7G-01) with owner and evidence upload, leverage test history, stale-feed banner; no create or edit of deposit accounts in v1.5.
- **Members › Dividends:** appropriation run (net profit → statutory funds → dividend) with minimum checks inline, dividend run, unclaimed and forfeiture tracker.
- **Members › AGM:** AGM and election calendar, notice and agenda pack builder, quorum tracker, minutes due, non-unanimous register, director loan report, Election Authority notice countdown.
- **Members › Audit and returns:** auditor appointment, audit paras with Form O due dates, audit-class history, Registrar returns (links to 7B RR1), director disqualification countdown (s.43(2)).
- Keyboard shortcuts on list screens (`/` search, `n` new, `a` approve where permitted); every screen meets WCAG 2.2 AA; vernacular labels from the vocabulary pack.

### Acceptance tests

- Adapter import shows an FD held by a `NOMINAL` member → GR-7G-01 exception and Board alert; the FD cannot back a lien or loan until closed with evidence.
- 50 shares of ₹100, bye-law multiple 10× → ceiling ₹50,000; ₹70,000 blocked. Under 10% linkage a ₹70,000 loan needs 70 shares: top-up 20.
- Non-member surety on an MSCS loan → rejected (s.66(1)).
- Director and relative loans at 9.8%; a ₹5 lakh director loan taking it to 10.3% → blocked.
- Large MSCS housing loan of ₹1.3 crore → blocked; ₹1.1 crore → allowed; Small MSCS any housing loan → blocked.
- MSCS net profit ₹2 crore, profitable 3 years → reserve ≥ ₹50 lakh, education ₹2 lakh, unforeseen ≥ ₹20 lakh, CRRD ₹2 lakh; 20% to reserve fails.
- Maharashtra 16% dividend without sanction → blocked. Audit report 15 Jul 2026 → Form O due 15 Oct 2026, overdue on 16 Oct.
- Branch pack with GNPA 7.4% → fails on GNPA with lineage.
- Member dispute referred to Equator arbitration → blocked; conciliation → allowed.
- NBFC co-lending with a credit society → blocked; lawful-alternatives panel shown.
- The same membership application posted twice from Udofin with one idempotency key → one `APPLIED` record; `MemberAdmitted` is emitted once on `ACTIVE` and never by Finbyx for a society whose system of record is another LOS.
- No adapter file for 3 business days → FD-backed loan sanction blocked with the stale-feed message; a fresh file clears it.

## IP3. Co-operative banks (UCBs, StCBs and DCCBs)

### IP3.1 Legal position and scope

- RBI regulated entities under the BR Act as applicable to co-operative societies (AACS, s.56); registration matters under the State or MSCS Act; NABARD supervises StCBs and DCCBs (BR Act s.35(6)) [REG].
- RBI consolidated UCB rules on 28 Nov 2025 into "RBI (Urban Co-operative Banks – …) Directions, 2025" (Credit Facilities, RBC, KYC, Resolution of Stressed Assets RBI/DOR/2025-26/287, IRACP, Capital Adequacy, Financial Statements, Credit Information Reporting, Concentration, Investment Portfolio, CRR and SLR, Outsourcing, Governance, ALM, Branch Authorisation); rural co-operative banks have a parallel set [VERIFY list, numbers and paragraphs before loading packs].
- **Scope:** LOS, LMS, collections and recovery, loan-side accounting, loan-book returns, risk dashboards. The core banking system remains the system of record for deposits, CRR/SLR and the GL unless the bank licenses Finbyx accounting; integration via the Deposit Ledger Adapter (IP2.5) and a GL interface. Bank ECL directions (SCBs only, from 1 Apr 2027) and Basel III bank calculations are not applied.

### IP3.2 UCB tiers and capital

| Tier | Deposits | Net worth | CRAR |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tier 1 | unit and salary-earner UCBs; others ≤ ₹100 crore | ₹2 crore (single district) or ₹5 crore | 9% |
| Tier 2 | ₹100–1,000 crore | ₹5 crore | 12% (in force from 31 Mar 2026) |
| Tier 3 | ₹1,000–10,000 crore | ₹5 crore | 12% |
| Tier 4 | > ₹10,000 crore | ₹5 crore | 12% |

3-year glide on moving up; scheduling eligibility for Tiers 3–4 with CRAR ≥ minimum + 3 points (RBI press release 19 Jul 2022) [VERIFY: 1 Dec 2022 circular and Nov 2025 Capital Adequacy Direction].

### IP3.3 Lending rules (UCB pack)

- **PSL** 60% of ANBC or CEOBSE from 1 Apr 2025 (was 75%); women-beneficiary cap removed [VERIFY sub-targets].
- **Small-value loans:** per-loan ceiling raised from ₹1 crore to ₹3 crore [VERIFY definition and target].
- **Housing:** member housing up to 25% of loans; individual up to ₹3 crore [VERIFY tier caps]. RCBs: ₹75 lakh; real estate ≤ 5% [VERIFY].
- **Gold:** the ₹2 lakh bullet ceiling (₹4 lakh for PSL-compliant UCBs, RBI/2023-24/66) removed; 2025 gold and silver directions apply (bullet ≤ 12 months; LTV 85/80/75% at ≤ ₹2.5 lakh / ≤ ₹5 lakh / above; adoption by 1 Apr 2026). Product 8 engine reused.
- **Director loans:** UCB pack [VERIFY]; RCBs permitted with conditions from 7 Jan 2026 [VERIFY].
- **Pack data:** automatic branches; OTS and technical write-off; SR investment glide to FY 2027-28; CGTMSE MLI where GNPA ≤ 7%; director tenure ≤ 10 years; ECBA classification replacing FSWM (4 Dec 2025) [VERIFY].

### IP3.4 Transfers, co-lending and investments

Stressed-loan sales only, as transferor (GR-7G-04); no co-lending with NBFCs (GR-7G-03); AIF investments under the RBI (Investment in AIF) Directions 2025 (7H IV4); investment and CRR/SLR positions monitored against UCB Directions [VERIFY]; no dealing-room functions.

### IP3.5 Returns and supervision

- **UCB CIMS returns:** the UCB seed rows of 7B RR1.5 (Form I, Form B, RAL, ROE, RCL, RCP, RBP, Form IX, Form II, PSA, Form VIII, Dir-I, Dir-IV, Planning-3) under the UCB Supervisory Returns Directions 2026 [VERIFY]; each row stays `ACTIVE_UNVERIFIED` until confirmed.
- **CRILC:** UCBs with assets ≥ ₹500 crore, exposures ≥ ₹5 crore (RBI/DOR/2025-26/287 para 12) [VERIFY]. **Credit information companies:** all four, all formats, 1 Jul 2026 cadence (7B RR6).
- **StCBs and DCCBs:** NABARD ENSURE (OSC-10 quarterly; CS-01 and CS-02 within 15 days; CSIR-01 cyber incident within 6 hours); CAMELSC rating (A, B+, B, C, D) tracked; statutory forms on CIMS. No RBI Supervisory Returns Direction for them in the 31 Jul 2026 set.
- **Ombudsman:** Reserve Bank – Integrated Ombudsman Scheme 2026 (`RBIOS26`, from 1 Jul 2026) coverage per its thresholds [VERIFY]; RCBs covered since 7 Oct 2025 [VERIFY].
- **KYC:** StCB as AUA/KUA and DCCB as sub-AUA (UIDAI, 1 Aug 2025) enable Aadhaar e-KYC modes for those profiles only [VERIFY].
- **Accounting and audit:** AS plus Third Schedule via s.56 and NABARD formats (7C AC1); RBI statutory audit plus State or MSCS audit; concurrent audit [VERIFY] (7D AU5).

### Settings and options

Tier and glide-path end (computed; override only through IP1.7); CBS adapter feeds (deposits, GL; daily); Finbyx accounting licensed (default off: CBS stays the GL); PSL sub-target tracking (on); gold pack version (2025 directions); member register (on only where the bank maintains members in Finbyx; then IP2 Members screens apply without the deposit-adapter exception rules, which the CBS owns). Bank ECL and Basel III bank engines are not selectable (IP3.1).

### Menu and screens

Standard workspaces (A–M) with the `COOPBANK` vocabulary; **Risk › Co-operative bank** (workspace J): tier and CRAR with glide path, PSL dashboard, CRILC population, CAMELSC history; **Compliance › Returns** shows UCB CIMS or NABARD ENSURE rows only; **Finance › Connectors › CBS interface** (workspace I): batch list, reconciliation breaks, re-run with reason.

### Acceptance tests

- Tier 2 UCB at 11.6% CRAR on 31 Mar 2026 → breach; on 31 Mar 2025 → within glide path.
- UCB buys a standard pool from an NBFC → blocked; sells an NPA to an ARC → allowed via R13.4.
- UCB assets ₹480 crore → no CRILC; ₹520 crore → CRILC instances for exposures ≥ ₹5 crore.
- DCCB cyber incident at 10:00 → CSIR-01 due 16:00, escalation at 14:00.
- UCB gold bullet of ₹3 lakh for 14 months → blocked; LTV at the ₹5 lakh slab.
- Bank ECL floors applied to a UCB → refused.

## IP4. Microfinance: JLG and SHG lifecycle

### IP4.1 Scope

Product 11, Part 8A.1 (CF Ch V) and Part 8A.31 already define the microfinance loan, household cap, pricing, loan card, 60% qualifying-asset test, provision floor and 25% non-MFI cap. This section adds the group operating model. It applies to NBFC-MFIs, other NBFCs with a microfinance book (≤ 25% of assets, MFI para 49), co-operative banks under their own Directions [VERIFY] and co-operatives adopting the model [REC].

### IP4.2 Household affordability engine

- Household = spouses and unmarried children (CF para 51); roster with relationships, earners and identifiers. Income ≤ ₹3,00,000 a year; above that the loan is routed to a non-microfinance product.
- Income assessment per Board policy over ≥ 1 year with corroboration (para 52); income reported to CICs with divergence reasons (para 54).
- `monthly_obligations = Σ monthly_equivalent(all household loans, secured and unsecured) + new_EMI`; bullet loans `(principal + interest) ÷ months to maturity` [REC]; missing-EMI tradelines estimated by stored Board method.
- Pass if `monthly_obligations ÷ (annual_income ÷ 12) ≤ min(50%, Board cap)`, excluding income from the financed activity (para 55); households above the cap get no new loan (para 57). Inputs, bureau report IDs and rule version are stored.

### IP4.3 MFIN Guardrails 2.0 pack

MFIN Directive #14 of 25 Nov 2024, current in Aug 2026 [SRO]; mandatory for MFIN members (NBFC-MFIs must belong to an SRO, MFI para 46), adoptable by others.

| Guardrail | Rule | Gate |
|---|---|---|
| Lenders | ≤ 3 microfinance lenders incl. this one (from 1 Apr 2025) | Sanction |
| Indebtedness | ≤ ₹2 lakh incl. unsecured retail, excl. secured retail, incl. proposed loan (from 1 Jan 2025) | Sanction |
| Delinquency | no new loan if any loan with > ₹3,000 outstanding is > 60 DPD | Sanction |
| Fees | processing fee ≤ 1.5% plus GST; only it and credit-life premium deducted at disbursal | Product; disbursal |
| Third-party products | consent and ≥ 1 month after disbursal | Cross-sell |
| Identity | Voter ID e-validation, reject "no hit"; PAN seeding where held | KYC |
| Bureau | report ≤ 15 days old; daily submission; disputes within 7 days | Sanction; 7B RR6–RR7 |
| Death | stop collection; refund excess (Directive #6) | IP4.8 |
| Staff | employee bureau updated by the 10th; employee originals returned in 7 days | 7F GV6 |
| Loan card | MFIN grievance details shown | Template |

### IP4.4 JLG lifecycle

Group rules: 4–10 members [VERIFY NABARD; 5 typical PRAC]; one member per household; no close relatives; self-selected [REC].

**Member:** `PROSPECT → KYC_DONE → HOUSEHOLD_ASSESSED → BUREAU_PASS | BUREAU_FAIL → CGT_ATTENDED → GRT_PASS | GRT_FAIL → SANCTIONED → DISBURSED → ACTIVE ⇄ OVERDUE → CLOSED | WRITTEN_OFF`; any active state `→ DECEASED_CLAIM`.
**Group:** `FORMING → CGT_IN_PROGRESS → CGT_DONE → GRT_PASSED | GRT_FAILED → ACTIVE → DORMANT → DISSOLVED`.

| Step | Rule | Captured |
|---|---|---|
| Village survey | lender density, risk, State overlays | survey, approval |
| KYC | Aadhaar offline (never stored); Voter ID e-validation | evidence |
| Household and bureau | IP4.2, IP4.3 | roster, income, report IDs |
| CGT | 3–5 days [PRAC]; free (RBC para 88); every member every day | attendance, geo-photo, trainer |
| GRT | supervisor other than the CGT trainer; knowledge, house visit, coercion screen | score, visit evidence |
| Centre | 2–6 groups [PRAC]; fixed day, time and place = **designated place** (RBC para 90) | centre master |
| Sanction | per member; vernacular KFS and loan card (RBC paras 78–80) | sanction, card |
| Disbursal | cashless to each member's own account; CIC updated | UTR |
| Utilisation check | 30–45 days [PRAC] | visit |
| Meetings | weekly, fortnightly or monthly by member choice (CF para 59) | attendance, receipts, card entries |
| Closure | discharge on card; repeat cycle needs fresh assessment and bureau | closure |

**Events (producer rule, Integration Spec 6.24):** the lender's system of record (Finbyx here, or the RE's other LMS) produces `GroupFormed` (group `ACTIVE` after GRT) and `GroupCollectionPosted` (meeting postings, with shortfall and cash-variance flags); Udofin consumes them. `CentreMeetingHeld` is produced by whichever system closes the meeting: Finbyx when it is closed in the M22 field app, Udofin when it is closed in Udofin's assisted tools (Finbyx then consumes it, reconciles and posts). A meeting is never closed in both; the second close attempt is rejected with the closing system's reference.

**Joint liability is voluntary (GR-7G-06).** Each loan is an individual contract; Finbyx never applies one member's payment, savings or disbursal to another's loan. A member may help a co-member only by a separate, explicit, revocable instruction posted as a third-party payment [REC]. No public defaulter lists, centre announcements or pressure on co-members or relatives (RBC para 91). Group "liability" fields are analytics only.

### IP4.5 Centre meeting, cash and cash-in-transit reconciliation

**Meeting states** (one record per centre per scheduled date; owner: centre officer, then branch manager):

| State | Entry | Allowed actions | Exit and timer |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SCHEDULED` | Created from the centre calendar 7 days ahead; collection sheet frozen at 00:00 on the meeting day (expected instalment and arrears per member) | Reassign officer; reschedule with members' recorded agreement | `OPENED` on check-in; `NOT_HELD` if no check-in by the scheduled time + 2 hours |
| `OPENED` | Officer checks in on a bound device within the designated-place geo-fence (default 200 m [REC]); outside it needs a reason and photo | Attendance, receipts, loan-card entries, issues; works offline | `CLOSED_IN_FIELD` when the officer closes the sheet |
| `CLOSED_IN_FIELD` | Sheet totals locked; leader-signed sheet photographed | None in the field; receipt cancellation only by a supervisor before handover, with reason | `SYNCED` when every device batch is accepted; unsynced at 20:00 IST → escalation to the branch manager; at 24 hours → incident |
| `SYNCED` | Batches verified (device signature, hash chain, serial continuity, clock drift ≤ 5 minutes), or a `CentreMeetingHeld` received from Udofin (`closing_system = UDOFIN`) | Conflict review: field wins for attendance and receipts, server wins for loan master data, every conflict logged | `RECONCILED` when shortfall and variance are computed and assigned |
| `RECONCILED` | `collection_shortfall` and `cash_variance` computed | Handover, bank deposit, variance review | `POSTED` after postings; `VARIANCE_OPEN` if cash variance ≠ 0 |
| `VARIANCE_OPEN` | Non-zero cash variance | Independent reviewer investigates; recovery from the officer only through HR process, never from members | `POSTED` with closure evidence |
| `POSTED` | Loan postings done (same day [REC, mirroring CF para 10(5)]); `GroupCollectionPosted` and, if closed in Finbyx, `CentreMeetingHeld` emitted | Reversal only by journal with reason and checker | `CLOSED` |
| `NOT_HELD` | No meeting | Reason (weather, holiday, members absent, officer absent); reschedule; a `NOT_HELD` date never counts as a member's non-appearance | `SCHEDULED` (new date) |

**Postings and controls:**

1. Field receipts (M22): device-signed, hash-chained serial, payer, amount, mode (UPI, cash), time, geo-tag, photo of the leader-signed sheet; instant DLT receipt to the member; offline store encrypted, scoped to the day's centres and purged after sync.
2. On sync: Dr Cash-in-transit (officer) / Cr Loan; duplicates rejected by `(device_id, serial)`.
3. Handover with dual sign-off: Dr Branch cash / Cr Cash-in-transit. `collection_shortfall = expected − receipted` (overdue on named members) is kept apart from `cash_variance = receipted − handed_over`; any non-zero cash variance is an exception closable only by an independent reviewer.
4. Bank deposit: Dr Bank / Cr Branch cash, matched to the statement (M7); undeposited branch cash beyond the next business day raises an alert.
5. **UPI by default:** dynamic QR per member per instalment on the lender's merchant account; reference = loan ID + instalment; webhook auto-post; unmatched to suspense, cleared in 2 working days [REC]. Money never passes through Udofin.
6. **Loans sourced through Udofin or another LSP's DLA (GR-7G-14):** UPI QR is the only collection mode for regular instalments unless the RE has recorded a legal opinion allowing its own staff to collect cash at centre meetings for that product (CF paras 10(2), 10(5)); the cash option is hidden on the collection sheet until then. Udofin staff appear as collectors only as the RE's appointed recovery agent on overdue loans (Udofin UR4).
7. Controls: officer cash limits, route rotation, surprise counts, centre-officer rotation at least yearly [REC], no cash disbursal by default, Income-tax Act 2025 cash limits [VERIFY].

### IP4.6 SHG lifecycle

- SHG master: 10–20 members [VERIFY DAY-NRLM]; bank account; office bearers; meeting, savings and internal-lending registers; promoting institution.
- States: `FORMED → SAVING → GRADED → LINKAGE_APPROVED → LINKED → ACTIVE → CLOSED`; minimum saving period per pack [VERIFY].
- Grading on Panchasutra parameters (meetings, savings, internal lending, repayment, books) [VERIFY format]; minimum grade for linkage; loan sized by corpus multiple or micro-credit plan [VERIFY]; member-wise attribution at sanction and disbursal.
- Attributed amounts are tested under the household cap [REC; VERIFY RBI treatment of SHG loans under CF para 51]. Optional SHG book-keeping service with exportable registers.

### IP4.7 Bureau rules

Microfinance accounts go only to the MFI file (UCRF MFI v3.3.1), never also to consumer (7B RR6); group → consumer → account; separate SHG and JLG-plus-individual files; account types JLG-Individual, JLG-Group, Individual, SHG-Individual, SHG-Group (CIR Annex I Form 3); SHG member data per CIR para 13: Table 1 where the amount attributed to a member exceeds ₹30,000, Table 2 up to ₹30,000, both reported as Table 3 inside Form 3, collected for members of SHGs whose loans exceed ₹1,00,000 (para 13(3)(ii)). The 1 Jul 2026 regulatory cadence (9th, 16th, 23rd, month-end) is the floor; MFIN daily submission is the overlay.

### IP4.8 Conduct, State overlays, death claims

- **Conduct (Product 11; RBC paras 76–94 until 31 Dec 2026):** designated place; home or workplace only after 2 successive non-appearances (para 90), counted from meeting records (`NOT_HELD` dates excluded); calls 09:00–18:00 (para 91(2)); no prepayment charge, delay charge only on the overdue amount (para 81); police-verified agents (para 94). **From 1 Jan 2027** the contact engine (R15.1) switches to the RBC Third Amendment pack (RBI/2026-27/230: paras 89–100 deleted; para 100Y(5) and (7) for visits and centre collection; para 100Y(4) window) [VERIFY: whether a separate microfinance window survives]; a tenant may keep 09:00–18:00 as an L4 tightening (default on [REC]).
- **State overlays:** KA15 (NBFCs exempt from registration), TN40 s.20 (binds NBFCs and co-operatives), Andhra Pradesh 2011 and Assam 2020 Acts [VERIFY]; State checklist on every field event; coercion complaint suspends the agent.
- **Death:** `DEATH_INTIMATED → DEMAND_STOPPED (same business day) → DOCUMENTS_COLLECTED → CLAIM_LODGED → SETTLED | REPUDIATED → APPLIED_TO_LOAN → EXCESS_REFUNDED → CLOSED`. Claim lodged within 15 days [REC]; excess to the nominee within 7 working days of receipt [REC]; repudiation goes to management review (waiver or write-off); no demand on co-members; credit-life, PMJJBY or PMSBY terms per policy [VERIFY].

### IP4.9 Portfolio monitors

Reuses ratios R47 (qualifying assets ≥ 60%, 4-quarter counter, channelising book excluded) and R48 (non-MFI ≤ 25%, pre-sanction gate) from Part 7E RK6. Adds State and district limits (MFI para 10), centre PAR and attendance heat-maps, officer cash variance, pricing-ceiling compliance (CF paras 60–61; RBC para 82) and guardrail breach counts.

### Settings and options

| Setting | Level | Default | Nature |
|---|---|---|---|
| Household cap | Product | 50% | Regulatory ceiling (CF para 55); Board may only lower |
| MFIN Guardrails 2.0 pack | Tenant | on for MFIN members | SRO code (L2); others may adopt |
| Group size, centre size | Product | 4–10 members; 2–6 groups | Commercial within pack limits |
| CGT days, GRT supervisor rule | Product | 3 days; GRT by a different supervisor | GRT rule fixed |
| Meeting frequency | Centre | members' choice (weekly, fortnightly, monthly) | CF para 59 |
| Designated-place geo-fence | Centre | 200 m | Commercial |
| Collection modes | Product | UPI QR per member first; cash allowed on loans the lender sourced itself | Cash off and locked for LSP-sourced loans without the RE's opinion (GR-7G-14) |
| Officer cash limit, sync deadline | Branch | ₹50,000; 20:00 IST | Commercial [REC] |
| Contact window | Product | 09:00–18:00 | Regulatory until 31 Dec 2026; then the Third Amendment pack, tighten only |
| Death-claim lodging and refund SLAs | Tenant | 15 days; 7 working days | Commercial [REC]; MFIN Directive #6 floor |
| Vernacular languages for KFS and loan card | Tenant | State languages of operation | Regulatory (RBC paras 77, 79) |

### Menu and screens

All under **Microfinance** (workspace A for branch staff, G for collections, P for the field app, J for monitors):

- **Microfinance › Centres:** centre list (filters: branch, officer, day, PAR bucket, attendance below 75%), centre detail (designated place on a map, calendar, groups), **New centre** wizard (village survey → place and time agreed with members → officer), bulk reassign officer.
- **Microfinance › Groups:** group pipeline board (`FORMING` to `ACTIVE`), member roster with household test and MFIN results, CGT and GRT scheduler (GRT supervisor picker excludes the CGT trainer), **Recognise group** action (emits `GroupFormed`), SHG register tab.
- **Microfinance › Meetings:** today's meetings by officer with state chips, meeting detail (collection sheet, attendance, receipts, issues, photos), not-held log, non-appearance counter per member; field app screen works offline with a sync status badge.
- **Microfinance › Collections:** posted collections, UPI suspense queue, third-party payment consents, shortfall by member, death-claim tracker.
- **Microfinance › Cash-in-transit:** officer balances, handover queue (dual sign-off), variance exceptions with independent-reviewer assignment, undeposited cash ageing; export to the branch cash book.
- Empty states explain the next step ("No centre yet: run a village survey"); errors name the rule (for example "Household cap 50% exceeded: 52.5%"); read-aloud and large-type modes in the field app; WCAG 2.2 AA.

### Acceptance tests

- Income ₹2,40,000 a year, EMIs ₹7,000, new EMI ₹3,500 → 52.5% → blocked; new EMI ₹2,900 → 49.5% → allowed.
- Three existing microfinance lenders → blocked. A ₹3,500 loan at 61 DPD → blocked; ₹2,800 outstanding → allowed.
- GRT by the CGT trainer → rejected.
- Member A pays ₹1,000 toward B's instalment without consent → refused; with consent → third-party payment on B's loan.
- Expected ₹40,000, receipted ₹39,500, handed over ₹39,000 → ₹500 cash exception; ₹500 shortfall tracked as overdue on named members.
- Home visit after one missed meeting → blocked; after two → allowed within the window.
- Death at 11:00 → demands suppressed that day; excess ₹4,200 → refund due in 7 working days.
- Microfinance account in a consumer bureau file → validation failure.
- Meeting captured offline and synced at 19:10 → `SYNCED`, receipts posted the same day; a second device batch replaying serial 0042 → rejected as duplicate; a device clock 9 minutes off → batch held for review.
- Meeting not synced by 20:00 IST → branch-manager escalation; at 24 hours → incident.
- Regular instalment on a Udofin-sourced loan with no RE legal opinion recorded → cash option absent; UPI QR shown; an API attempt to post a cash receipt → `GR-7G-14`.
- A meeting closed in Udofin's tools → Finbyx consumes `CentreMeetingHeld`, posts and emits only `GroupCollectionPosted`; a later close attempt in M22 → rejected.
- Microfinance recovery call at 18:15 on 15 Dec 2026 → refused.

## IP5. Asset reconstruction companies and stressed-asset acquisition

### IP5.1 Two sides

1. **ARC tenant** under SARFAESI and the RBI (Asset Reconstruction Companies) Directions 2025 (DoR.FIN.REC.No.293/26.03.001/2025-26, 28 Nov 2025, updated 10 Mar 2026). Paragraph numbers below are taken from the RBI web text (Master Direction index id 12930), not the signed PDF [VERIFY every ARC paragraph number before coding].
2. **NBFC in the stressed-asset domain** without being an ARC (IP5.8). The NBFC selling side is in R13.4.

SARFAESI [LAW]: asset reconstruction s.2(1)(b); ARC s.2(1)(ba); qualified buyer s.2(1)(u); securitisation s.2(1)(z); security receipt s.2(1)(zg) [VERIFY lettering]; registration s.3; acquisition s.5; SRs through trusts s.7; measures s.9; other functions s.10.

### IP5.2 Capital and business limits

| Rule | Value | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| NOF | ≥ ₹300 crore; existing ARCs by 31 Mar 2026, else no new business | ARC paras 14–16 |
| IBC resolution applicant | NOF ≥ ₹1,000 crore | para 18 |
| CRAR | ≥ 15% | para 93 |
| Business | securitisation, asset reconstruction, s.10 functions | para 17 |
| Deposits | prohibited | para 23 |
| Surplus funds | ≤ 10% of NOF, short-term instruments | para 21 |
| Own-use property | ≤ 10% of owned funds; acquired property sold within 5 years | para 22 |
| FATF jurisdictions | new investors < 20% of voting power | para 126 |

### IP5.3 Acquisition, trusts and SR register

`PIPELINE → DUE_DILIGENCE (≥ 2 weeks) → BID_APPROVED → AUCTION | BILATERAL → ACQUIRED → TRUST_FORMED → SR_ISSUED → PLANNING → RESOLUTION_PLAN_APPROVED → REALISATION → REDEEMED | WRITTEN_OFF → TRUST_CLOSED`

- Side exits: `DROPPED` from `PIPELINE` or `DUE_DILIGENCE` (reason recorded); `LOST` from `AUCTION`; `ACQUIRED` only on the settlement UTR and executed assignment deed; a failed settlement returns to `BID_APPROVED` with the counterparty notified. Owners: acquisition team to `BID_APPROVED` (approval per Board policy), finance for settlement, resolution team from `PLANNING`.
- Board acquisition policy within 90 days of CoR (para 24); DD ≥ 2 weeks (para 27); SMA and non-fund exposures allowed (para 30); ARC-to-ARC sales in cash within 8 years of first acquisition (para 33).
- **Auction only** where the seller is the sponsor, its lenders or subscribers, or its group (para 34): counterparty links make `BILATERAL` unavailable.
- `ACQUIRED` emits `AssetAcquired`; assets move to the trust at acquisition price (para 78).
- **One trust per scheme**, ARC as trustee (para 76), own bank account and ledger (assets, recoveries, recoverable expenses, fees, distributions by SR class per the offer-document waterfall); never mixed with the ARC's funds.
- **SR register:** ISIN, scheme, class, face value, units, QB holder (para 79), transfers among QBs only, NAV, rating and redemption history; `SecurityReceiptIssued` on issue; read-only SR holders' portal.
- **Self-investment (para 81):** per class and scheme, ARC holding ≥ `max(15% × transferors' SR holding, 2.5% × total SRs)` until redemption; breach raises `LimitBreached`.

### IP5.4 Clocks, NAV and fees

| Item | Rule | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| Planning period | ≤ 6 months from acquisition | para 12 |
| Realisation | 5 years; Board may extend to 8 | paras 35–36 |
| Rating | within 6 months of acquisition | paras 82–84 |
| NAV | as on 30 June and 31 December, within the CRA recovery range | para 90 |
| Management fee | on NAV at the lower end of the range, capped at acquisition value | para 142 |
| Fee reversal | unrealised fees reversed 180 days after the planning period; ageing disclosed | paras 143–144 |
| Restructuring support finance | only if acquired assets > ₹500 crore; ≤ 25% of scheme funds | para 91 |

NAV publication emits `SrNavPublished` (consumed by 7H IV4 investors and R13 transferors); a nightly job reverses qualifying fee accruals.

### IP5.5 Resolution measures and settlements

- Management change: debt ≥ 25% of the borrower's assets, 60% of SR holders and IAC review (paras 45, 47). Enforcement: 60% of secured creditors (para 58; R13.5 engine). Debt-to-equity ≤ 26% (paras 70–71). s.9(1)(b) sale or lease of business unavailable until notified (para 51) [VERIFY].
- Settlement (paras 60–67): Board policy, last resort, `NPV of offer ≥ realisable value` stored, instalments need a business plan.

| Settlement | Route | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| ≤ ₹1 crore, no fraud or wilful default | authority other than acquisition officials; quarterly Board report | para 65 |
| > ₹1 crore | IAC review → Board with ≥ 2 independent directors, or committee; rationale minuted | paras 64, 66 |
| Fraud or wilful defaulter, any amount | IAC review → Board or committee | paras 64, 66 |
| Litigation pending | consent terms filed | para 67(2) |

Negotiation or conciliation may run through Equator (R8.6); approval stays with the ARC.

### IP5.6 Disclosures, returns and accounting

- Returns (7B): DNBS07 Important Financial Parameters (quarterly), DNBS10 auditor certificate (annual), DNBS13 overseas investment (quarterly, NIL), and the ARC Supervisory Returns Directions 2026 set [VERIFY]; audited balance sheet to the regional office within 1 month of the AGM (para 152).
- Public: monthly possession list (para 154); seller, realisation, redemption and > 20%-discount schedules (para 150); Ind AS versus IRACP (para 137). CERSAI and IU filings (paras 158–162); CIC reporting [VERIFY ARC CIR text].
- Accounting (7C AC1): Ind AS where Rule 4 applies, else AS plus RBI ARC norms (RBI guidance of 13 Mar 2020) [VERIFY limb]; trust books separate. ARC tenants receive R13.6 data rooms from transferors; R1.4 runs with the ARC's own SARFAESI eligibility and the 60% consent rule.

### IP5.7 What an NBFC may and may not do

| Activity | Permitted | Conditions | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sell stressed loans to permitted transferees or ARCs | Yes | R13.4 | TDCR para 58 |
| Buy stressed loans as permitted transferee | Yes | hold ≥ 6 months; none transferred as stressed in prior 6 months; recoveries first reduce cost; 100% RW while standard | TDCR paras 74, 76–77 |
| Invest in SRs as QB | Yes, since the SARFAESI gazette notification of 28 Feb 2025 (all RBI-regulated NBFCs and HFCs) | defaulting promoters and related parties must not regain assets through SRs; valuation per TDCR paras 82–86 (7H IV4) | SARFAESI s.2(1)(u) |
| Take over standard accounts from ARCs | Yes | after satisfactory monitoring period; Board policy; never its own earlier transfers | TDCR para 87 |
| ARC as fee-based recovery agent | Yes | loan stays on books; provisioning continues | TDCR para 88 |
| s.7 trust, SR issue, s.9 measures, "ARC" description | **No** | needs s.3 registration | SARFAESI ss.3, 7, 9 |

GR-7G-08 to GR-7G-10 enforce these. Purchases reuse `loan_transfer` (v1.3) with `role = transferee` and a 6-month lock. Each NBFC records its QB basis and, per SR purchase, a declaration that it is not related to the defaulting promoter.

### Settings and options

| Setting | Level | Default | Nature |
|---|---|---|---|
| NOF, CRAR, surplus-fund and own-use property limits | ARC tenant | Directions values | Regulatory floor |
| Due-diligence minimum | ARC tenant | 2 weeks | Regulatory floor; Board may lengthen |
| Settlement routing threshold | ARC tenant | ₹1 crore | Regulatory; Board may lower |
| Realisation extension | Scheme | none | Board resolution required (8 years maximum) |
| Waterfall template per SR class | Scheme | from the offer document | Versioned with the trust deed |
| SR holders' portal | ARC tenant | on, read-only | Commercial |
| NBFC side: stressed-loan purchase lock | NBFC tenant | 6 months | Regulatory floor (TDCR para 74) |

### Menu and screens

All under **ARC** (workspace H for the resolution team, I for trust accounting, M for the Board; NBFC tenants see only **Recovery › Stressed-loan sales and purchases**):

- **ARC › Acquisitions:** pipeline board by state, deal detail (seller, sponsor-link check, DD checklist and clock, bid approvals), **Record auction result**, **Record settlement** (UTR), counterparty-link warning that hides the bilateral route.
- **ARC › Trusts:** trust list, trust ledger (assets, recoveries, expenses, fees, distributions), bank reconciliation, waterfall run with preview and approval, fee accrual and 180-day reversal ageing.
- **ARC › SRs:** SR register by ISIN and class, QB holder check on transfer, self-investment monitor, rating and NAV calendar (30 June, 31 December), **Publish NAV** (emits `SrNavPublished` after checker approval).
- **ARC › Resolution:** plan workspace (management change, enforcement, restructuring support, settlement) with consent tallies (SR holders 60%, secured creditors 60%), IAC review queue, settlement approval route by amount and fraud flag, realisation clock with extension request.
- **ARC › Disclosures:** monthly possession list, para 150 schedules, returns links (7B RR1.5).

### Acceptance tests

- ARC NOF ₹280 crore on 1 Apr 2026 → acquisitions blocked; CRAR 14.2% → breach.
- Bilateral purchase from a bank that subscribed to the ARC's equity → blocked; by auction → allowed.
- Transferors hold 70% of ₹100 crore SRs → ARC must hold max(10.5, 2.5) = ₹10.5 crore; ₹9 crore → breach.
- Acquired 1 Jan 2026 → planning ends 30 Jun 2026; realisation 31 Dec 2030; extension to 31 Dec 2033 only with a Board resolution.
- For the same acquisition, a fee accrued during planning and still unrealised on 28 Dec 2026 (180 days after 30 Jun 2026 is 27 Dec 2026) → reversed and shown in ageing.
- Auction lost → `LOST`; no trust or SR records can be created for it.
- ₹1.4 crore settlement by one executive → blocked; routed IAC → Board with two independent directors.
- NBFC creating a trust or issuing SRs → blocked. NBFC resale of a purchased stressed loan after 4 months to an NBFC → blocked; to an ARC → allowed (para 74 proviso). NBFC take-over of its own 2024 transfer → blocked.

## IP6. IFSCA Finance Companies and Finance Units

### IP6.1 Legal basis

- IFSCA (Finance Company) Regulations 2021 as amended; Amendment Regulations notified 5 May 2026 (F.No. IFSCA/GN/2026/009); consolidated **IFSCA (Finance Company) Regulations, 2026** text (amended to 7 May 2026) issued 9 Jul 2026 [REG]. Regulation numbers below follow the 2021 text as amended to 1 Jul 2022 [VERIFY against the 2026 consolidated text].
- GRCTC framework of 4 Apr 2025; IFSCA (Fund Management) Regulations 2025 (7H IV6); IFSCA AML/CFT/KYC Guidelines 2022 as amended [VERIFY current version].
- A Finance Company is incorporated in the IFSC; a Finance Unit is a branch of a home-regulated entity (home NOC may be needed). Neither may take public deposits or act as a Banking Unit (reg 2(1)(e)–(f)).

### IP6.2 Separate USD tenant

- Always a **separate tenant**, never a legal entity inside an onshore tenant (GR-7G-12); group MIS consolidates read-only projections only.
- USD functional and reporting currency; freely convertible currencies; INR account only for administrative and statutory expenses, allow-listed chart (reg 6). An FU keeps books separate from its parent. Daily revaluation at the configured reference rate.
- Hosting: India-region cloud, optional GIFT City data centre, pending IFSCA data-localisation confirmation [VERIFY].

### IP6.3 Activity whitelist

| Class | Activities | Finbyx support |
|---|---|---|
| Core (reg 5(1)(ii)) | lending (loans, commitments, guarantees, CE, securitisation, financial lease, loan-portfolio trading); factoring and forfaiting; permitted investments; derivatives; GRCTC | USD lending; securitisation (7H IV7); investments (7H) |
| Non-core (reg 5(1)(iii)) | merchant banking, arranger, RTA, trusteeship, advisory, PMS, operating lease, ITFS, distribution, exchange membership; separate departments with firewalls (reg 5(3)) | department segregation and access walls; operating lease deferred to v1.6 [REC] |
| SPV structures | leasing and financing through SPVs (since 5 May 2026) | SPVs as legal entities of the IFSC tenant with intra-group exposure tracking |
| GRCTC | treasury services to group entities | treasury and intra-group ledger |

Hard blocks: public deposits; speculative transactions (reg 5(6)); derivatives without a `hedge_link` where non-core activities are undertaken (reg 5(5)). **Residents** only as FEMA permits (reg 5(4), (7)): each resident counterparty carries a FEMA basis (ECB, LRS, ODI or other) and legal sign-off before sanction [VERIFY]. Udofin blocks resident retail onboarding for an IFSC lender unless the RE confirms the FEMA basis.

### IP6.4 Capital, liquidity and exposure

| Rule | Value | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| Owned fund — core | higher of USD 3 million and IFSCA-specified capital | IFSCA-FC |
| Owned fund — non-core only | USD 0.2 million | IFSCA-FC |
| Owned fund — GRCTC | USD 0.2 million (FU may meet at parent level) | GRCTC framework, Apr 2025 |
| Capital ratio | ≥ 8% | reg 4 |
| Liquidity | standalone LCR; FU may rely on parent with approval | reg 4 |
| Exposure | single counterparty or group ≤ 25% of eligible capital without IFSCA approval | reg 4 |
| Non-core-only units | exempt from prudential norms | reg 4 |

The 7E RK3 engine runs an `IFSCA` pack in USD; `CapitalRatioComputed` carries currency.

An FU follows its parent's framework for consolidation.
- Asset classification per IFSCA norms [VERIFY]; IRACP not applied by default.
- Returns to IFSCA in USD as IFSCA specifies (reg 9) [VERIFY: return list, frequency, portal]; 7B RR1 regulator `IFSCA`, filed by an authorised human. FIU-IND as a PMLA reporting entity [VERIFY]; FEMA/ECB reporting to RBI where lending into India [VERIFY].
- IFSCA AML/CFT/KYC rule set as the KYC pack [VERIFY]; sanctions screening per Part 8A.21.

# PART 7H — INVESTMENTS, TREASURY AND CAPITAL-MARKETS MODULE

**Purpose.** v1.4 gives the lender an investment register (M10 item 7A; Part 8A.5). v1.5 turns it into a book of record for investment companies, Core Investment Companies (NBFC-CIC), treasuries of lenders, AIFs and IFSC entities: instrument and issuer masters, licensed market data, order capture with human approval, settlement and demat reconciliation, corporate actions, IPO participation, AIF, REIT, InvIT and SR holdings, Ind AS 109 and AS 13 accounting, regulatory limits, and securitisation servicing for lenders that sell pools to SPVs. **Finbyx records, checks, values, accounts and reports. It never executes trades and never gives investment advice.**

**Applicability.**

| Entity | Rule set | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| NBFC-D, ICC, Factor, MFI, IFC, IDF, HFC, NBFC-CIC | INV (Ch II for BL; Ch II and III for ML/UL) | INV para 3 |
| MGC, P2P, AA, SPD, NOFHC, Type I, BL with customer interface but no public funds | INV not applicable; for the two no-public-funds categories paras 11–13 and 28–29 still apply | INV para 3 |
| NBFC-CIC | INV plus CICD (IV5.6) | always ML or UL (SBR para 15(2)); outside TDCR and SEC |
| Banks, UCBs, StCBs, DCCBs | own investment norms [VERIFY]; RBI AIF Directions 2025 apply | monitoring pack only (Part 7G IP3) |
| ARC | surplus funds ≤ 10% of NOF (ARC para 21) | Part 7G IP5 |
| AIF, PMS, IFSC fund (as customers) | SEBI AIF Regulations 2012, SEBI PM Regulations 2020, IFSCA FM Regulations 2025 | IV6 |
| IFSC FC/FU | IFSCA-FC; USD | Part 7G IP6 |

**Requirement codes.** Existing: INV, CON, CF, FS, SBR, CAP, TDCR, SEC, MSD, IRACP. New (Part 8A.37): `AIF` (SEBI AIF Regulations and circulars), `ICDR`, `LODR`, `PIT`, `IND-AS`, `ICAI`, `IFSCA-FC`, `ARC`. Also in Part 8A.37: `RBI-AIF` (RBI (Investment in AIF) Directions 2025, consolidated into the Undertaking of Financial Services Directions 2025), `CICD` (RBI (Core Investment Companies) Directions 2025). In this Part a Core Investment Company is written NBFC-CIC; bare "CIC" means a credit information company, `SEBI-MF` (market-cap categorisation), `SEBI-PM`, `SEBI-IA`, `IFSCA-FM`, `SARFAESI`.

**Data owned.** Instrument, issuer and corporate-action masters; market-data licence register; price snapshots; order tickets, pre-trade and restricted-list check results, broker-release records, contract notes, broker-error exceptions, settlements, positions and tax lots; demat reconciliations; IPO applications and lock-ins; AIF commitments, drawdowns, capital accounts and look-through files; REIT/InvIT distributions; SR holdings and valuations; valuation runs; limit results; securitisation servicing ledgers, waterfalls and investor reports. Accounting postings go through the M10 ledger engine; capital and limit results feed Part 7E.

**Extends:** M10 item 7A, Part 8A.5 (INV), Part 6.4 (LAS security master and price snapshots are shared, never duplicated), M11, R13, Part 8A.22 (TDCR) and 8A.23 (SEC).

## IV1. Instrument master, market data and classification

### IV1.1 Instrument master

One `security_master` shared with Part 6.4, extended with:

- **Identity:** ISIN (mandatory for demat; internal ID for unlisted), issuer, instrument type, listing status and exchanges, segment (mainboard, SME, debt), face value, currency.
- **Debt terms:** coupon schedule, day count, call and put, maturity, seniority, secured flag, rating and agency history, tranche (PTC or securitisation note), guarantee (Central or State Government).
- **Fund terms:** AIF category (I, II, III) and unit class (senior, subordinated, sponsor), scheme corpus, LVF flag; MF scheme code and category; REIT or InvIT trust, sponsor.
- **Classification:** market-cap bucket (IV1.4, effective-dated), INV category (para 14), CME line (FS para 21(8)(ii) items i–x), group-company and related-party flags (from the issuer), debtor-company flag (computed).

| Instrument type | INV AS category (para 14) | CME line (FS 21(8)(ii)) | Default Ind AS route |
|---|---|---|---|
| Equity share (listed, unlisted) | Equity shares | (i) direct investment | FVTPL; FVOCI by irrevocable election |
| CCPS, CCD, convertible debenture | Preference shares or Debentures | (i) convertibles | FVTPL (fails SPPI) |
| Preference share (non-convertible) | Preference shares | not CME [VERIFY] | per SPPI result |
| NCD, bond, CP, CD | Debentures and bonds; CP at carrying cost | — | AC, FVOCI or FVTPL by business model and SPPI |
| G-sec, SDL, T-bill | Government Securities | — | AC or FVOCI |
| MF unit (equity-oriented) | Units of mutual fund | (i) equity-oriented MF units | FVTPL |
| MF unit (debt) | Units of mutual fund | — | FVTPL |
| ETF | Units of mutual fund | (i) where equity-oriented | FVTPL |
| AIF unit | Others | (x) AIF by category | FVTPL |
| REIT or InvIT unit | Others | non-CME by default; Board flag to treat as CME (IV4.6) [VERIFY] | FVTPL |
| Security receipt | Others (TDCR paras 82–86 override) | — | FVTPL (NAV-based) |
| PTC or securitisation note | Debentures and bonds | — | per SPPI look-through (contractually linked) |

### IV1.2 Issuer and counterparty master

CIN, LEI, PAN, listing, group membership (SBR group definitions), subsidiary or associate or joint venture of the tenant, related party (Part 7F GV1), sponsor link (for ARC rules), promoter group of any borrower, rating. **Debtor-company flag** = the tenant had a loan or non-equity investment exposure to the company at any time in the preceding 12 months (RBI-AIF para 4), recomputed daily from the loan book and holdings.

### IV1.3 Market data and licence register

| Source | Data | Frequency | Licence rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| NSE and BSE end-of-day files (bhavcopy), corporate announcements | prices, corporate actions | daily | free download is for viewing; commercial use inside a SaaS and any redistribution need an exchange data licence [VERIFY current terms]; licence ID per tenant |
| AMFI | MF NAV; market-cap categorisation list | daily; half-yearly | per AMFI terms [VERIFY] |
| Credit rating agencies | ratings, outlooks | event | CRA licence per tenant for bulk feeds |
| Bond and G-sec valuation provider | valuation prices | daily | provider licence [VERIFY provider] |
| Depositories (NSDL, CDSL), RTAs | holding statements | daily or monthly | tenant's own data |
| AIF managers, ARCs | capital-account statements, NAV, portfolio files, SR NAV | quarterly; half-yearly | tenant's own data |

- `market_data_licence` (tenant, source, scope view/internal-use/redistribution, start, expiry, evidence). An import from a source without a valid licence is refused; expiry 30 days ahead raises a task.
- **Price waterfall:** exchange close → secondary exchange → valuation provider → last traded with `stale` flag → manual price (maker-checker, evidence attached). Listed equity is stale after 1 business day; stale prices cannot be used for month-end valuation without CFO override.
- Exports to auditors and RBI include prices the tenant is licensed to share; GR-7H-03 strips other vendor data from client-facing exports.

### IV1.4 Market-cap categorisation

- Large cap = 1st–100th, mid cap = 101st–250th, small cap = 251st onward by full market capitalisation (SEBI circular SEBI/HO/IMD/DF3/CIR/P/2017/114, 6 Oct 2017). SEBI's revised categorisation circular of 26 Feb 2026 supersedes Master Circular clause 2.6 [VERIFY: whether the 100/250 cut-offs are unchanged].
- AMFI publishes the list **half-yearly** using six-month average full market capitalisation across BSE, NSE and MSEI; the latest covers the period ended 30 Jun 2026.
- Each list is stored as an effective-dated version from the date AMFI states; history retained; holdings and limits can be reported "as of" any date. Unlisted and SME-platform securities carry their own buckets (`UNLISTED`, `SME`).
- Board limits by bucket (for example small-cap ≤ x% of the equity book) run in IV5.4.

### IV1.5 Classification at acquisition

- **Ind AS:** business model per portfolio (hold to collect, hold to collect and sell, other) with documented evidence, plus an SPPI checklist per instrument (leverage, non-recourse, contractually linked tranches, prepayment and extension features, interest-rate mismatch); result AC, FVOCI-debt or FVTPL; equity FVOCI election per instrument, irrevocable, not for trading. Subsidiaries, associates and joint ventures: cost or Ind AS 109 in separate statements (Ind AS 27). Reclassification only on a change in business model [VERIFY Ind AS 109 paragraph numbers].
- **AS:** current or long-term per Board policy, decided at acquisition (INV para 9); later transfers only under IV5.2.
- Captured on every acquisition: accounting regime, classification, purpose tag (strategic, liquidity, trading, hedge), approver, Board policy version. Classification fields lock after the first posting.

### Acceptance tests

- Importing bhavcopy for a tenant with no exchange data licence → refused; with a licence expiring in 20 days → imported and a renewal task raised.
- AMFI list effective 1 Aug 2026 moves a stock from mid to small cap → holdings report as of 31 Jul shows mid, as of 1 Aug shows small.
- A CCD acquired by an Ind AS NBFC → SPPI fails → FVTPL; an attempt to elect FVOCI → refused (not equity).
- A listed equity price older than 1 business day at month-end → valuation run halts for that ISIN until a CFO override or a fresh price.
- A company with a term loan repaid 11 months ago → debtor-company flag true; 13 months ago → false.

## IV2. Trade capture, settlement, demat reconciliation and corporate actions

### IV2.1 Order capture (GR-7H-01)

**Flow:** order capture → limit and restricted-list checks → approval → execution by the broker outside Finbyx → contract-note import → matching, settlement and reconciliation.

| State | Entry condition | Owner and allowed actions | Exit, timer and failure path |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DRAFT` | Dealer creates a ticket (instrument, side, quantity, price limit or market, validity, purpose tag, broker, portfolio) | Dealer: edit, delete, submit | `PRE_TRADE_CHECKED` on submit; drafts older than 5 business days auto-archive |
| `PRE_TRADE_CHECKED` | All IV2.2 checks run on the current snapshot; results stored | Dealer: withdraw; next level: reasoned override of a soft fail | `PENDING_APPROVAL` if no hard fail; `REJECTED_BY_CHECK` (hard fail, reason codes) |
| `PENDING_APPROVAL` | Routed by DoA band | Approver (never the dealer): approve, reject, send back | `APPROVED`; `REJECTED`; `DRAFT` on send-back; checks re-run if the approval comes after the snapshot is 30 minutes old or the next business day |
| `APPROVED` | Approval with DoA reference | Dealer: record release; approver: revoke | `RELEASED_TO_BROKER`; `EXPIRED` at validity end; `CANCELLED` on revoke |
| `RELEASED_TO_BROKER` | Dealer records channel (broker terminal, recorded phone line with recording reference, broker portal), time and broker order number; Finbyx never transmits orders | Dealer: record cancel or modify request sent to the broker (a modify that increases quantity or price beyond the approval needs a new order) | `EXECUTED`, `PARTIALLY_EXECUTED` or `CANCELLED` from the contract note or broker confirmation; `EXPIRED` at validity end with no fill |
| `EXECUTED` or `PARTIALLY_EXECUTED` | Contract note matched (IV2.3) | Back office: confirm match, raise exception | `SETTLED` on depository and bank confirmation; a partial fill leaves the unfilled balance `EXPIRED` at validity end |
| `SETTLED` | Securities and funds legs confirmed | Back office | `RECONCILED` after the next demat and bank reconciliation agree; a failed or short delivery opens `SETTLEMENT_EXCEPTION` with ageing and auction or close-out recording |
| `RECONCILED` | Position, ledger and statement agree | Read-only | Terminal; corrections only by `TRADE_REVERSED` |

- **Out-of-policy fills:** the quantity above the approved quantity, a whole fill priced outside the approved limit, or a whole note with no approved order is booked to a `BROKER_ERROR` exception and an error account; it creates no position until the CFO accepts it (with a retrospective approval and a fresh pre-trade check) or the broker reverses it.
- **Reversal and back-dated correction:** `TRADE_REVERSED` posts reversing journals dated today with a link to the original; a correction to a closed period follows the R12-style reopening approval. `TradeBooked` is re-emitted with a higher `update_seq`.
- **Segregation [REC]:** dealer (front office) ≠ approver (DoA) ≠ settlement and accounting (back office) ≠ limits monitoring (mid office). Approval limits by instrument type, amount and bucket.
- **Personal dealing:** if the tenant or its group is listed, dealers and approvers are designated persons and the PIT pre-clearance and trading-window checks of Part 7F GV4.4 apply to their own trades; the restricted-list check below applies to the tenant's own-account orders whether or not the tenant is listed.

### IV2.2 Pre-trade checks

| Check | Rule | Type | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|
| Restricted list | Issuer (or the issuer of the underlying, for convertibles, derivatives and IPO bids) is on the Part 7F GV4.4 restricted list → reject with `RESTRICTED_LIST`; the dealer sees only "restricted", never the reason or the UPSI | Hard (GR-7H-12) | PIT Reg 4 [REC]; GV4.4 |
| Lock-in and pledge | Sell quantity ≤ free holding (excludes locked-in, pledged and frozen) | Hard | IV2.5, IV3.3 |
| Instrument whitelist | Board investment policy | Hard | INV paras 7–8 |
| CME and SSE | Board limits by FS 21(8)(ii) line | Hard at the Board limit; soft at the early-warning level | CON paras 12, 24 |
| Single and group exposure (credit plus investment) | ML: 25% / 40% of Tier 1 (+5 / +10 for infrastructure); IFC 30% / 50%; UL: LEF; not applied where CON para 16 exempts the NBFC (no public funds, no guarantees) | Hard | CON paras 13–14, 16, 33–39 |
| NOF deduction | Group, subsidiary and other-NBFC exposure above 10% of paid-up equity plus free reserves | Soft (capital impact shown) | SBR para 45 |
| AIF caps | IV4 | Hard at 10% | RBI-AIF para 6 |
| NBFC-CIC tests | IV5.6 pro forma | Hard where the order breaks a 90%, 60% or 10% test | CICD |
| Derivatives | INV permissions; hedge link | Hard | INV paras 28–34 |
| IFSC | FEMA and USD rules | Hard | IFSCA-FC |
| Liquidity | ALM bucket impact (Part 7E RK4) | Soft | ALM |
| Board buckets | IV5.4 | Per policy | Board policy |

Each check stores inputs, rule version and result. A failed hard check blocks approval and cannot be overridden; a soft check needs a reasoned override by the next level. The restricted list is read inside the tenant at check time and again at approval; an issuer added between check and release moves an `APPROVED` order back to `REJECTED_BY_CHECK` and alerts the CCO. The wall exception (Settings) is off by default.

### IV2.3 Execution capture and settlement

- Contract notes imported (PDF parsed, CSV or XML; bulk upload or broker e-mail drop folder): trade date and time, exchange, ISIN, side, quantity, price, brokerage, STT, stamp duty, exchange and SEBI fees, GST, settlement number. The file hash is the idempotency key; a re-imported note is ignored, and a revised note from the broker supersedes the earlier one with both kept.
- **Matching:** by broker order number, else by (ISIN, side, trade date, quantity) to a `RELEASED_TO_BROKER` order; price within the approved limit and charges within the tolerance; unmatched notes go to the contract-note inbox; a note not received by T+1 for a released order raises a back-office task.
- Trade-date accounting; `TradeBooked` emitted with order ID, contract-note hash and posting ID.
- Funds and securities obligations tracked to the settlement date (equity T+1 [VERIFY current cycle per segment]); failed or short deliveries open an exception.
- Cost basis per Board policy (weighted average or FIFO) [REC: FIFO tax-lot tracking held in parallel for tax].

### IV2.4 Government securities and corporate bonds

- G-sec transactions only through a gilt account or demat account (INV paras 11–12).
- **OTC corporate-bond trades reported within 15 minutes** on the exchange reporting platform (INV para 13): the timer starts at the execution timestamp; the reporting reference is captured; a late report is logged with reason and counted in the compliance KRI.

### IV2.5 Demat and holding reconciliation

- Daily (minimum monthly) import of NSDL and CDSL holding statements and RTA or MF Central statements; reconcile by account, ISIN and status (free, pledged, locked-in, frozen).
- Break types: quantity, status, missing ISIN, unexpected credit; each break has an owner and ageing.
- Own holdings are segregated from LAS collateral (Part 6.4); a borrower's pledged securities never appear in the tenant's positions.

### IV2.6 Corporate actions

- Event master: dividend, interest, redemption, split, bonus, rights, merger, demerger, buyback, conversion, delisting; announcement, ex-date, record date, payment date; source (licensed exchange feed, depository or RTA notice).
- Entitlement computed on record-date holdings; quantity and cost adjusted (split and bonus re-base unit cost; merger at the scheme ratio; rights captured as a new order ticket); income per INV paras 22–24; TDS receivable recorded.
- Reconciled against the demat credit and the bank receipt; unreceived entitlements age as exceptions.

### Acceptance tests

- An order for a non-whitelisted instrument → blocked at `PRE_TRADE_CHECKED`.
- The dealer who drafted an order tries to approve it → refused.
- OTC bond executed 11:02, reported 11:21 → late report logged and KRI incremented.
- A 1:1 bonus on 1,000 shares at ₹200 cost → 2,000 shares at ₹100; total cost unchanged.
- A pledged LAS security of a borrower in the same demat file → excluded from the tenant's positions and reconciled to Part 6.4.
- A contract note without a matching approved order → `BROKER_ERROR` exception; no position created.
- An order in a listed borrower's NCD while that issuer is on the GV4.4 restricted list → `REJECTED_BY_CHECK` with `RESTRICTED_LIST`; the dealer's screen shows no UPSI detail.
- Issuer added to the restricted list after approval but before release → order returns to `REJECTED_BY_CHECK` and the CCO is alerted.
- Contract note shows 1,200 shares against an approved 1,000 → 200 shares to `BROKER_ERROR`; 1,000 booked.
- The same contract-note file imported twice → one trade; `TradeBooked` emitted once.
- A released order with no contract note by T+1 → back-office task opened.

## IV3. IPO participation (mainboard and SME)

### IV3.1 Scope

Own-account subscription by the tenant. **IPO funding to borrowers** is lending: ceiling ₹1 crore per borrower (CON paras 11, 24(2); CF para 104), enforced in the loan products and reported as CME.

### IV3.2 Issue master and eligibility

- Issue: issuer, mainboard or SME, exchange, price band, lot size, category quotas, anchor portion, bid dates, allotment and listing dates.
- **Book-building quotas** (ICDR Reg 32): QIB ≤ 50%, NII ≥ 15%, retail ≥ 35%; QIB ≥ 75% for Reg 6(2) issuers; anchor ≤ 60% of the QIB portion [VERIFY all on sebi.gov.in].
- **QIB category** only with a current attestation (GR-7H-11): ICDR Reg 2(1)(ss) lists "systemically important non-banking financial companies", tied to net worth above ₹500 crore per the last audited accounts [VERIFY wording]; SEBI has not aligned it with SBR layers. The attestation records the test, the audited net worth and a legal sign-off, refreshed on each audited balance sheet.
- **NII sub-categories:** one-third for applications up to ₹10 lakh and two-thirds above ₹10 lakh; **SME minimum application** two lots (≥ ₹2 lakh) (ICDR amendment of 4 Mar 2025).
- **SME issue diligence checklist** (facts from the offer document for the investment committee; not advice): EBITDA ≥ ₹1 crore in 2 of 3 years; OFS ≤ 20% of issue; selling shareholders ≤ 50% of holding; general corporate purposes ≤ 15% or ₹10 crore; no proceeds to repay promoter or related-party loans; excess promoter holding locked in 50% for 2 years and 50% for 1 year (ICDR amendment 4 Mar 2025; LODR amendment 28 Mar 2025).

### IV3.3 Workflow

`ISSUE_CREATED → DILIGENCE_NOTE → COMMITTEE_APPROVED → BID_PLACED (ASBA block evidence) → ALLOTTED | NOT_ALLOTTED (unblock confirmed) → LISTED (T+3) → LOCK_IN → FREE`

- Anchor allotments locked in for 30 days on 50% and 90 days on the rest; pre-IPO shares 6 months [VERIFY]. The lock-in tracker blocks any sell order before expiry and reconciles the depository lock-in status.
- ASBA amount held as a memo entry; allotment books the trade; unblocked funds reconciled to the bank statement.
- Pre-trade checks of IV2.2 apply at `COMMITTEE_APPROVED` and again before `BID_PLACED`, including the restricted list, CME and issuer group exposure (the issuer may be a borrower).
- Side exits: `WITHDRAWN` (only where the investor category may withdraw or lower a bid [VERIFY: ICDR rules for QIB and NII bids]; unblock confirmed); `ISSUE_WITHDRAWN` or `ISSUE_FAILED` (unblock confirmed; memo reversed).

### Acceptance tests

- An NBFC without a current QIB attestation selects the QIB category → blocked; NII available.
- SME bid of one lot worth ₹1.2 lakh → blocked (minimum two lots, ≥ ₹2 lakh).
- A sell order on anchor shares on day 25 after allotment → blocked.
- A loan to fund IPO subscription of ₹1.2 crore for one borrower → blocked in the loan product.
- Unallotted application with ASBA block not released within the issue timeline → exception opened.
