## IV4. AIF, REIT, InvIT and security-receipt investments

### IV4.1 AIF rules from 1 January 2026

RBI (Investment in AIF) Directions 2025 (RBI/DOR/2025-26/138, 29 Jul 2025), consolidated for NBFCs into the Undertaking of Financial Services Directions 2025 [VERIFY final paragraph numbers; the draft showed paras 7–15]. Paragraph numbers below are those of the July 2025 Direction. Scope: commercial banks (incl. SFB, LAB, RRB), UCB, StCB, DCCB, AIFIs and NBFCs incl. HFCs (para 3); NBFC-CICs and ARCs [VERIFY].

| Rule | Implementation | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| Individual RE ≤ 10% of a scheme's corpus | Hard block on commitment (GR-7H-04) | para 6(a) |
| All REs together ≤ 20% of corpus | Manager attestation with date; re-attested each drawdown | para 6(b) |
| > 5% of corpus and a downstream non-equity investment in the RE's debtor company | 100% provision on the proportionate look-through exposure, capped at the direct exposure to that debtor | para 6(c) |
| Subordinated units | Deducted fully from capital, proportionately from Tier 1 and Tier 2 | para 6(d); CAP para 15(1) |
| Definitions | Debtor company = loan or non-equity investment exposure in the preceding 12 months; equity instruments = equity shares, CCPS, CCDs | para 4 |
| Exemptions | Investments with prior RBI approval under the 2016 directions; Government-notified AIFs (Annex: SWAMIH Investment Fund-I) | para 7 |

### IV4.2 Regime tagging

- Effective 1 Jan 2026 (or earlier by internal policy); the 19 Dec 2023 and 27 Mar 2024 circulars repealed from that date; fully honoured commitments stay under them; commitments existing on 29 Jul 2025 or made before the effective date follow the old or the new regime **in full** (paras 2, 8).
- Each commitment carries `regime = LEGACY_2023 | AIF_DIR_2025`, irrevocable once elected. Legacy rules (INV paras 25–27): debtor look-through with exit within 30 days or 100% provision; subordinated units deducted 50:50 from Tier 1 and Tier 2; investments through fund of funds or mutual funds excluded (para 27).
- [VERIFY] why consolidated INV (updated 1 Jul 2026) still prints paras 25–27 (most likely for legacy commitments) and whether the fund-of-funds carve-out survives under the new regime.

### IV4.3 Commitment lifecycle and look-through

`PROPOSED → CHECKED → APPROVED → COMMITTED → DRAWDOWN (n) → DISTRIBUTION (n) → EXITED | WOUND_UP`

- Corpus from the PPM or the manager's latest capital-account statement; commitment; drawdown schedule; unit class; fees.
- **Check:** `commitment ÷ corpus ≤ 10%` (block); RE-aggregate attestation present; CME line (x) by category within the Board limit; NOF test.
- **Quarterly look-through:** import the AIF portfolio file (investee PAN or CIN, instrument type, amount); match investees to the borrower and investee master over a rolling 12 months.
  - `AIF_DIR_2025`: if `own_units ÷ total_units > 5%` and the scheme holds a non-equity instrument of debtor D, then `provision_D = min(own_share × aif_investment_in_D, direct_exposure_to_D)` at 100% [VERIFY: whether the look-through base is the non-equity holding only].
  - `LEGACY_2023`: start a 30-day exit clock; at expiry, 100% provision on the look-through amount (INV para 25).
  - Manager refuses or delays the file → `KriBreached`, CRO escalation, file marked unverified [REC].
- **NOF:** group investments through an AIF are treated as group investments where ≥ 50% of the AIF's funds came from the NBFC (company form), or where the NBFC is beneficial owner and ≥ 50% contributor (trust form) (SBR para 46).
- Postings: commitment (memo), drawdown (investment), distributions split into income and return of capital; NAV-based fair value (Ind AS) or category valuation (AS).

### IV4.4 REIT and InvIT units

- No RBI cap specific to NBFC holdings of REIT or InvIT units was found [VERIFY]. Default: non-CME investment exposure (units are not equity shares), counted in single and group limits against the trust and the sponsor group, with a Board flag to treat them as CME.
- Bank-specific limits (10% of unit capital; bank lending framework from 1 Oct 2026) are not applied to NBFCs.
- Distributions are captured by component (interest, dividend, repayment of capital, other) for accounting and tax [VERIFY Income-tax Act 2025 treatment].
- NBFC-CIC tenants: sponsor holdings in InvIT units count toward the 60% test (CICD para 3).

### IV4.5 Security receipts

- Eligibility: QB basis (SARFAESI gazette of 28 Feb 2025) and a per-purchase declaration that the tenant is not a defaulting promoter's related party (Part 7G IP5.7).
- **Valuation (TDCR paras 82–86):**
  - periodic valuation at the NAV declared by the ARC from the recovery rating (para 82);
  - SRs held by the transferor against its own transferred loans: lower of NAV-based redemption value and the NBV of the loan at transfer (para 82 proviso);
  - transferor holding > 10% of the SRs of that transfer: lower of the above and face value less the notional provision that would have applied had the loan stayed on the books (para 83);
  - Government-guaranteed SRs at NAV; unrealised fair-value gains deducted from CET1 or NOF and not distributable; valued at ₹1 after guarantee settlement or expiry (para 84);
  - unredeemed at the end of the resolution period (5 or 8 years) → loss asset, fully provided (para 85);
  - non-SLR investment norms otherwise, with NAV for instruments limited to actual realisations (para 86).
- NAV arrives through `SrNavPublished` (ARC tenants) or an imported ARC NAV letter; valuations run as on 30 June and 31 December and at each reporting date.

### Acceptance tests

- Commitment of ₹55 crore to a ₹500 crore scheme → 11% → blocked; ₹45 crore → allowed if the manager's RE-aggregate attestation is on file.
- Tenant holds 8% of a scheme whose ₹40 crore NCD holding is in debtor D; tenant's direct exposure to D is ₹2 crore → provision min(3.2, 2.0) = ₹2 crore.
- Same scheme with a 4% holding → no provision.
- A legacy-tagged commitment detects a debtor investee → 30-day exit clock; on day 31 a 100% provision is posted.
- Attempt to change a commitment's regime tag after election → refused.
- Transferor holds 15% of SRs from its own transfer: NAV value ₹62 crore, NBV at transfer ₹70 crore, face less notional provision ₹58 crore → carrying value ₹58 crore.
- SR unredeemed 5 years after acquisition with no extension recorded → loss asset and 100% provision.

## IV5. Classification, valuation, accounting and limits

### IV5.1 Ind AS 109 engine

- Classification per IV1.5; ECL for AC and FVOCI debt using the M10 ECL plug-in with rating-based PD and LGD for investments; staging on rating migration and days past due.
- Fair value hierarchy (Ind AS 113): level 1, 2 or 3 with inputs, model, valuer and timestamp; level 3 valuations need maker-checker and quarterly valuation-committee review.
- FVOCI debt recycles to profit or loss on derecognition; FVOCI equity never recycles. Disclosures for Ind AS 107 and 113 generated with Part 7C AC3.

### IV5.2 AS 13 with INV overlay

- **Current investments, quoted:** grouped into six categories — equity shares; preference shares; debentures and bonds; Government securities incl. T-bills; MF units; others (INV para 14). Per category: `depreciation = max(0, Σ cost − Σ market)`, scrip-wise aggregation, appreciation ignored, no set-off across categories (para 15).
- **Unquoted:** equity at lower of cost and break-up value (fair value may be substituted), ₹1 if the investee's balance sheet is unavailable for 2 years (para 16); preference at lower of cost and face value (para 17); G-secs and Government-guaranteed bonds at carrying cost (para 18); MF units at NAV (para 19); CP at carrying cost (para 20).
- **Long-term:** per AS 13 — cost less other-than-temporary diminution (para 21).
- **Unquoted debentures:** income recognition and asset classification as loans (para 21 Note; IRACP).
- **Inter-class transfers:** only on 1 April or 1 October with a Board resolution ID; scrip-wise at the lower of book and market value; depreciation provided, appreciation ignored (para 10).
- **Income:** dividends on cash basis, or accrual once declared and the right is established (para 22); interest on accrual only where the rate is pre-determined and interest is serviced and not in arrears (para 23); Government-guaranteed PSU securities on accrual (para 24).

### IV5.3 Valuation run

Daily indicative run for monitoring; official month-end run. Steps: price waterfall (IV1.3) → classification lookup → valuation rule → ECL or category depreciation → journals through M10 → `PositionValued` per position (value, method, price source, hash) → exceptions (stale, manual, level 3). Re-runs after period lock need the R12-style reopening approval.

### IV5.4 Limits engine

| Limit | Formula or rule | Basis | On breach |
|---|---|---|---|
| CME and SSE | Σ exposure by FS 21(8)(ii) lines i–x ≤ Board limit; restructuring conversions exempt but disclosed | CON paras 12, 24; FS para 21(8)(ii) | block new CME; `InvestmentLimitBreached` |
| Single and group (credit plus investment), ML | ≤ 25% / 40% of Tier 1 (+5 / +10 infrastructure); Tier 1 from latest audited or limited-review statements | CON paras 13, 14(3) | block; Board note |
| IFC | ≤ 30% / 50% of Tier 1 | CON para 14 | block |
| UL large exposures | 20% (+5% with Board approval) single; 25% group of eligible capital base | CON paras 33–39 | block; LEF return |
| NOF deduction | group, subsidiary and other-NBFC exposure above 10% of paid-up equity plus free reserves deducted | SBR paras 45–46 | capital recompute (7E RK3) |
| AIF | IV4.1 | RBI-AIF para 6 | block or provide |
| Board buckets | issuer, sector, rating, market-cap bucket, unlisted, SME, single scheme | Board policy | per policy |
| IFSC | 25% of eligible capital | IFSCA-FC | block |

Every breach emits `InvestmentLimitBreached` and the Part 7E `LimitBreached` (`limit_type = INVESTMENT`, `status = OPEN`) with the computation and data lineage. A passive breach (price movement, capital fall) opens an episode and blocks only new exposure; the cure is an update with a higher `update_seq` and `status = CURED` (Integration Spec 6.22, 6.25). Single and group limits are not applied where CON para 16 exempts the NBFC (no public funds and no guarantees issued); the exemption is a recorded profile fact, re-tested monthly.

### IV5.5 Derivatives and arbitrage

| Instrument | Who | Purpose | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|
| Exchange currency futures (as client) | INV-covered NBFCs | hedging only | INV para 28 |
| Interest rate futures (as client) | INV-covered NBFCs | hedging; half-yearly return to the DoS regional office within 1 month | INV para 29 |
| Repo in corporate debt | non-deposit ML and UL | per repo directions | INV paras 31–32 |
| Exchange currency options | non-deposit ML and UL | hedging only | INV para 33 |
| IRF as trading member | non-deposit ML and UL | per exchange rules | INV para 34 |
| Credit derivatives | users per the 2022 Directions; market-maker only with NOF ≥ ₹500 crore and RBI approval | per RBI (Credit Derivatives) Directions 2022 | CDS protection recognition per CON [VERIFY para] |
| Equity F&O, cash-futures arbitrage | no RBI NBFC direction found permitting or prohibiting it [VERIFY: FMRD and DoR position] | — | **OFF by default** |

- Every derivative carries a `hedge_link` to the hedged exposure except where a permission covers non-hedge use; effectiveness evidence stored.
- **Arbitrage switch:** enabling requires a Board-approved policy, a legal opinion on file, CCO approval and a recorded RBI position; both legs linked; treated as CME; daily mark-to-market and exchange margin ledger; no naked positions.
- The IRF half-yearly return is registered in Part 7B RR1.

### IV5.6 Core Investment Company tests (CICD)

RBI (Core Investment Companies) Directions 2025 (RBI/DOR/2025-26/367, 28 Nov 2025, updated 10 Mar 2026).

| Test | Formula | Frequency | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|
| Group investment | (equity, preference, debt and loans in group companies) ÷ net assets ≥ 90% | monthly | CICD para 3 |
| Group equity | (group equity + sponsor InvIT units) ÷ net assets ≥ 60% | monthly | para 3 |
| Non-group non-financial assets | ≤ 10% of net assets | monthly | para 3 |
| Capital | ANW ÷ RWA ≥ 30% | quarterly | para 20 |
| Leverage | outside liabilities ÷ ANW ≤ 2.5 | quarterly | para 23 |
| Layering | ≤ 2 NBFC-CIC layers in the group | on change | para 19 |
| Registration | total assets (with group NBFC-CICs) ≥ ₹100 crore **and** public funds held or raised → apply through PRAVAAH within 3 months; otherwise Unregistered Core Investment Company | monthly | paras 11(7), 15–17 |
| PCA | ANW ÷ RWA below 30% and leverage 2.5× and above trigger risk thresholds | quarterly | MSD paras 16–17 |

- Governance: Group Risk Management Committee (≥ 5 members, ≥ 2 independent directors, independent chair, quarterly) (paras 69–71); quarterly deviation statement on use of funds (paras 67–68, 72); RMC and CRO.
- GR-7H-06: no trading in group investments except block sales; other financial activity limited to bank deposits, money-market instruments, G-secs, group bonds and loans, and guarantees; no commodity derivatives.

### IV5.7 Type I NBFC helper

SBR Amendment Directions 2026 (RBI/2026-27/43, 29 Apr 2026, effective 1 Jul 2026): an NBFC with no public funds (including funds received indirectly through associates and group entities), no customer interface and group-aggregated assets below ₹1,000 crore may operate as an Unregistered Type I NBFC, exempt from ss.45-IA and 45-IC. Finbyx computes the tests monthly and builds the deregistration pack — 3 years' audited statements, auditor certificate, Board resolution — for a PRAVAAH application **by 31 Dec 2026**, with a task to surrender the original CoR. After exemption: annual Board resolution, disclosure in the accounts, auditor exception reporting, no overseas non-financial investment (para 65A).

### IV5.8 Financial statements

Investment schedules for Schedule III Division III and Division I; FS Directions notes including CME (para 21(8)(ii)), AIF exposures by category and restructuring conversions; produced with Part 7C AC3.

### Acceptance tests

- AS NBFC, current quoted equity cost ₹10 crore and market ₹9.2 crore; debentures cost ₹5 crore and market ₹5.3 crore → depreciation ₹0.8 crore; no set-off of the ₹0.3 crore gain.
- Unquoted equity whose investee has filed no balance sheet for 2 years → ₹1.
- Inter-class transfer dated 15 Nov → refused; dated 1 Oct with a Board resolution → executed at the lower of book and market.
- ML NBFC with Tier 1 ₹400 crore holds ₹70 crore loans and ₹35 crore bonds in one party → 26.25% → `InvestmentLimitBreached`.
- NBFC-CIC with group equity at 58% of net assets → test fails and a compliance issue opens.
- Enabling arbitrage without a legal opinion on file → refused.
- IRF position without `hedge_link` → blocked.
- Type I helper on 1 Dec 2026 with indirect public funds via an associate → test fails; no deregistration pack.

Files go to RE tenants through the Integration Specification file contract.

## IV7. Securitisation servicing, SPV remittance, replenishment and co-lending extensions

### IV7.1 What is new

M11 (pools, MRR, MHP, sale accounting), Part 8A.23 and R13.3 (servicer duties) stand. IV7 adds the servicing lifecycle, trust sub-ledger and sweep, waterfall engine, servicer and investor reports, replenishment with early-amortisation triggers, the clean-up call gate, the recycling rule, servicer replacement, dual derecognition flags, the transfer validator and the co-lending partner validator.

### IV7.2 Transaction states

`POOL_SELECTED → ELIGIBILITY_PASSED → RATED → SOLD → NOTES_ISSUED → SERVICING ⇄ REPLENISHING → EARLY_AMORTISATION → CLEAN_UP_CALLED | MATURED → CLOSED`; `SERVICER_REPLACED` from any servicing state.

- `SOLD` only on cash consideration received no later than transfer; `NOTES_ISSUED` within 30 days of transfer (SEC para 31).
- MRR recomputed monthly on unamortised principal; retained tranches locked against sale, hedge or pledge (SEC para 14).
- Side exits and failures: `ELIGIBILITY_FAILED` (loans removed and pool re-selected), `ABANDONED` before `SOLD` (pool tags released, no accounting); a sale reversed for a legal defect before notes are issued needs CFO and CRO approval and reverses every posting with a link to the original. Each transition records actor, approval and document hash.

### IV7.3 Collections held in trust (GR-7H-07)

- Receipts on a securitised or assigned loan post to a **"Held in trust — [transaction]" liability sub-ledger**, never to the originator's income; principal and interest components kept.
- Postings: receipt Dr Bank (collection account) / Cr Trust collections payable; remittance Dr Trust collections payable / Cr Bank; servicing fee only as the waterfall allows.
- Sweep to the SPE collection account at the agreed frequency (daily or T+1 per the servicing agreement). The servicer remits only funds collected (SEC para 95(2)), unless it is also an eligible liquidity facility provider; it holds collections in trust without commingling (95(3)) and remits all collections irrespective of any retained interest (95(4)).
- **Commingling monitor:** trust money in an operating account beyond the agreed window raises an alert; beyond twice the window, an incident. A breach is shown with its consequence: the servicer is treated as providing a liquidity facility for capital purposes (SEC para 96), and Part 7E RK3 recomputes capital.
- No loss support beyond the servicer's own default, negligence or fraud (SEC para 95).

### IV7.4 Remittance waterfall

- Configurable priority list per transaction, versioned with the transaction documents. Example: taxes and statutory dues → trustee and servicer fees → senior interest → senior principal (sequential or pro-rata, switching on triggers) → credit-enhancement replenishment → junior interest and principal → residual or excess interest spread to the originator.
- Principal- and interest-deficiency ledgers maintained.
- Output is a payout instruction to the trustee (the trustee pays); `ServicerRemittanceMade` carries collected, remitted, retained-fee and deficiency amounts.

### IV7.5 Servicer and investor reports

- Monthly servicer report: scheduled, prepaid and overdue principal and interest; fees; delinquent, defaulted and restructured amounts; deficiency ledgers; trigger status and breaches (SEC paras 18–21; para 71 for STC).
- Annex I MHP and MRR disclosure at origination, half-yearly (September and March) and on breach (SEC paras 112–113); 14-day material-change notice to investors, CRAs and service providers (para 22); quarterly RBI report, format to be advised (para 115); STC loan-level or stratified data at least quarterly (paras 51–52); third-party servicer data certified by auditors, preferably annually (para 109).
- Investor and trustee read-only portal; `InvestorReportPublished` on each release.

### IV7.6 Replenishment and the recycling rule (GR-7H-08)

- The originator may freely use the **upfront sale consideration** for new lending.
- **Post-sale collections belong to the SPE** and never fund the originator's lending.
- New loans enter the pool only during a documented **replenishment period**, funded from SPE cash per the documents, meeting the original eligibility criteria, never to improve pool quality after deterioration (CAP para 27(9)); MRR maintained at the end of the replenishment period (SEC para 14(2)).
- **Early-amortisation triggers (SEC para 21):** deterioration in credit quality of the underlying exposures; failure to acquire sufficient new exposures of similar quality; an insolvency-related event of the originator. Thresholds are configured per transaction and disclosed; on trigger, replenishment stops, the waterfall switches to sequential amortisation and investors are notified.
- Replacement for breach of representations is not replenishment: only within 120 days on original terms, notified to RBI DoS (SEC para 30).

### IV7.7 Clean-up call and derecognition

- **Clean-up call gate (GR-7H-09):** exercisable only when outstanding is ≤ 10% of the original value of the underlying exposures or notes (CAP para 27(8)); at the originator's discretion (27(6)); at arm's length on market terms with normal credit approval (27(2)); never structured to avoid allocating losses or to provide credit enhancement — exercise that does so is implicit support (27(7)). Valuation evidence stored.
- **Capital derecognition (CAP para 27):** no effective control (retained servicing rights are not control); repurchase only by clean-up call; legal isolation including under IBC; notes not obligations of the originator; investors free to pledge or trade; no increase in credit enhancement after inception; no yield step-up on deterioration; only eligible termination triggers (27(1)–(12)); legal opinion on file that the conditions are met (CAP para 28). Failing any condition, the exposures stay in RWA and the consideration is treated as an advance.
- **Accounting derecognition** runs separately under Ind AS 109 (retaining first loss usually retains substantially all risks, so the loans stay on balance sheet [VERIFY ICAI position]); AS NBFCs use the "Unrealised Gain on Loan Transfer Transactions" account (SEC para 34). Both flags are shown; they may differ.

### IV7.8 Servicer replacement

Triggers: servicer default, insolvency event, investor or trustee decision under the replacement provisions (SEC para 70). The hand-over pack contains the loan tape, collection mandates (NACH and UPI re-pointing), collection-account change, borrower notices and the data room. Servicers must be regulated by a financial-sector regulator (SEC para 80); an unregulated Infrabyx entity may act only as a technology sub-contractor (R13.3).

### IV7.9 Loan-transfer validator additions

- Counterparty lender type checked against TDCR para 12(4): RRBs, LABs, UCBs, StCBs and DCCBs only as transferors of stressed loans; credit societies never (Part 7G GR-7G-04). NBFCs acquire only from listed lenders (para 7).
- MHP 3 months (tenor ≤ 2 years) or 6 months (> 2 years) from CERSAI registration, else from first repayment; project loans from commercial operations; **purchased loans not resold within 6 months of booking** (para 43).
- 10% transferor retention where the transferee uses portfolio-level due diligence (para 40); servicing is the only permitted fiduciary role (para 36(4)); certified servicer data and auditor verification rights (paras 41–42).
- Stressed loans bought: Part 7G IP5.7.

### IV7.10 Co-lending partner validator (GR-7H-10)

| Partner type | Allowed | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| SCB other than SFB, LAB, RRB | Yes | TDCR para 97(1) |
| AIFI (NABARD, NHB, EXIM Bank, SIDBI, NaBFID) | Yes | para 97(2) |
| NBFC incl. HFC (within TDCR applicability) | Yes | para 97(3); para 3 |
| SFB, LAB, RRB | No | para 97(1) |
| UCB, StCB, DCCB, credit co-operative society | No | para 97 |
| NBFC-CIC, P2P, MGC, AA, SPD, NOFHC, NBFCs without public funds (no customer interface, or Base Layer with customer interface) (outside TDCR) | No | para 3 |
| ARC, AIF, IFSC FC or FU | No (IFSC entities are not listed in para 97; any change awaits the owner's decision and counsel, Appendix B) | para 97 |

The partner master stores the regulatory type with evidence (licence or CoR number) and re-validates annually; Udofin displays only co-lent offers whose partner passed (Udofin Part 7B). Existing v1.4 co-lending rules (10% retention, blended rate, escrow, 15-day booking, 5% DLG, next-working-day classification sync) are unchanged.

### Acceptance tests

- A borrower EMI on a securitised loan posts to operating income → refused; posted to the trust payable → accepted.
- Trust money held in the operating account 3 days against a T+1 window → incident and capital recompute flagged.
- Servicer instructed to remit ₹10 crore when ₹9.4 crore was collected → blocked unless an approved liquidity facility exists.
- Using post-sale collections to fund a new disbursal → blocked; using the upfront consideration → allowed.
- Replenishment after a credit-deterioration trigger → blocked; sequential amortisation applied.
- Clean-up call at 12% of original pool → blocked; at 9% to buy only delinquent loans → blocked as implicit support.
- Resale of a purchased standard loan 5 months after booking → blocked.
- Adding an SFB or a UCB as co-lending partner → blocked; an SCB with valid licence evidence → allowed.

---

# PART 7J — DATA PORTABILITY, ARCHIVES AND CUSTOMER-CONTROLLED STORAGE

**Purpose.** A tenant must be able to take all of its data out of Finbyx, at any time and on exit, in a form its staff, auditors, a successor vendor or a court can read without Finbyx; keep its own copies and backups in storage it controls; and prove that those copies are complete and restorable. Access to historical records never depends on a continuing subscription for regulated tenants (CM4 dunning rules). This Part sets the archive standard, the export jobs, the storage connectors, customer-held backups with restore tests, and the exit process, and states what Infrabyx can and cannot promise.

**Applicability.** All tenants get every feature; the legal basis differs. NBFC-ML and above (incl. HFCs, MFIs and CICs in those layers) are bound by the OUT IT-outsourcing chapter (OUT para 3(2): Chapter IV, including paras 74(vi), 74(xv)–(xvi), 87, 88, 97(ii), 97(vii)(b) and 97(xvi)). NBFC-BL tenants, banks, ARCs and other entities receive the same exit and data clauses by contract, with the para 34(xii) preservation duty [REC]. CYB backup clauses apply by chapter (Ch III para 8(9); Ch IV and V paras 129–133). Digital-lending data is subject to CF para 14(4). Every company tenant's books of account are subject to Companies (Accounts) Rules r.3 (daily backup in India; AC7). Credit co-operative societies (not REs) get the same features under their State or MSCS Act record rules and their contract [REC]. Udofin has its own subset (Udofin Part 7H, RA3).

**Requirement codes.** OUT, CYB, CF, DPS, KYC (retention), RBC (call-recording retention), CA13 (books, s.128), DPDP, ISO, SOC2. REQ-ID examples: `REQ-OUT-87`, `REQ-OUT-97(xvi)`, `REQ-CF-14(4)`, `REQ-CYB-133`, `REQ-CA13-AccountsRules-3(5)`.

**Data owned.** The tenant owns every byte of tenant data and configuration; Infrabyx is processor and custodian. Archive metadata (manifests, job logs, connector configurations, restore-test results) is tenant data too and is exported with the archive. Infrabyx keeps only its own contract, billing and security-incident records after exit.

**Extends, does not rebuild.** The Recovery Suite detach export (Part 7A.0.5), R14 `export_job` and `export_manifest`, M16 document storage and hashes, M17 report exports, the Integration Spec Part 12 layouts and manifests, Part 10.3 platform backup and DR targets, Part 10.6 items 17 and 24 (data and exit obligations), and AC7 (books-of-account backup and audit trail). Auditor and supervisor packs are in AU7; Udofin borrower downloads in Udofin UB1.

**Canonical events.** `ExportRequested`, `ExportCompleted`, `StorageTargetConnected`, `BackupCompleted`, `RestoreTested` (Integration Spec v1.1 Part 6.26); consumers are the tenant's compliance destination (evidence), the Operations Hub engineering console (OH13) for export counts and backup status, and the control library (OH14) for restore-test evidence; payloads never carry content. A storage-target health failure is published as `ControlTestResultPublished` (control `STORAGE_TARGET_HEALTH`) to the tenant's compliance destination.

## DP1. Archive standard (folders, Word, Excel, PDF, manifest)

### DP1.1 Design rules

1. **Readable without Finbyx.** A person with Microsoft Office or LibreOffice, a PDF reader and a checksum tool can find, open, verify and understand every record.
2. **Machine-readable as well.** Every dataset is also in CSV and JSON Schema-described form so a successor system can load it.
3. **Nothing implied.** IDs, codes, units, time zones and relationships are explicit in a data dictionary and a relationship map.
4. **Verifiable.** Every file is hashed; the manifest is signed; control totals reconcile to the source at the as-of point.
5. **Least exposure.** Restricted HR and legal folders are separately encrypted and excluded unless expressly authorised; Aadhaar numbers are never exported (only vault reference tokens; UIDAI rules), and card data is never held (DPS; CM4).
6. **Stable.** The standard is versioned (`archive_standard_version`, starting `1.0`); a breaking change needs a new major version and a converter.

### DP1.2 Folder tree (folder profile `finbyx_tenant_v1`; Integration Spec Part 12.1)

```
[Tenant legal name] - Finbyx Archive - [scope] - as of [YYYY-MM-DD]/
  00 Start Here/
      README.pdf, README.docx, README.txt   (README.md optional)
      export-manifest.csv, manifest.json, manifest.json.jws
      data-dictionary.xlsx, data-dictionary.csv
      relationships.csv, relationship-map.pdf
      code-tables/            (one CSV per code table)
      schemas/                (JSON Schema 2020-12 per dataset)
      verify/                 (open-source verifier and instructions)
  01 Entity and Regulatory Profile/      legal entities, registration certificates, regulatory profile, branches, policy registry
  02 Governance and Board/[FY]/          directors, KMP, committees, meetings, minutes, resolutions, registers, MCA filings, listed-company records (Part 7F)
  03 Accounting and Tax/[FY]/            chart of accounts, journals, trial balances, financial statements, GST, TDS, Tally exports, audit-trail extracts
  04 Lending/
      Products/  Customers/  Applications/  Loans/[loan id]/  Collateral/  Collections/  Co-lending and Transfers/
  05 Regulatory Returns/[regulator]/[portal]/[return code]/[period]/   generated files, validation reports, sign-offs, acknowledgements
  06 Credit Bureau Reporting/[CIC]/[file type]/[period]/               submitted files, rejections, corrections, disputes
  07 Risk and Compliance/                 risk register, KRIs, capital, ALM, ICAAP, compliance register, controls, evidence index
  08 Audit/[engagement]/                  plan, workpapers, findings, reports, management responses
  09 Customer Service and Grievances/     service requests, complaints, Internal Ombudsman, RB-IOS, ODR referrals
  10 HR and Payroll/Restricted/           (encrypted inner archive; excluded by default)
  11 Investments, Treasury and Borrowings/
  12 Legal and Recovery/                  case registers, notices, service proofs, matters, settlements
  12 Legal and Recovery/Restricted/       privileged documents (encrypted inner archive; excluded by default)
  13 Configuration, Integrations and Data Lineage/   products, rule packs, templates, workflows, roles and permissions, DoA, feature flags, integration logs, lineage
  14 System Audit Trail/[YYYY-MM]/       audit-events.jsonl, hash-chain anchors
```

- **Folder policy is configurable** (rename, reorder, split by legal entity or FY) through a versioned `folder_policy`; the canonical path of every dataset is kept in the manifest, so renaming never breaks the relationship map.
- **Folder 00** is identical in every profile across products (Integration Spec Part 12.1); the root folder name carries the tenant's legal name, never a person's name.
- **Folder 13** carries the configuration data that OUT para 97(xvi)(d) requires a successor to take over, with each rule pack's version, effective dates and approvals.
- **Folder 14** holds the audit trail in the M19 format, partitioned by month, with the daily hash-chain anchors so integrity can be verified offline (Rule 11(g) evidence; AC7).

### DP1.3 Naming rules

- Names in plain English, Windows-safe (no `\ / : * ? " < > |`, no trailing dots or spaces), Unicode NFC, total path ≤ 240 characters (long names are shortened with an ID suffix).
- **No personal data in folder or file names by default** (`label_policy = ids_only`): loan folders are `Loans/LN-000123/`; the README explains how to look up names in `customers.xlsx`. A tenant may choose `id_and_masked_name` for internal-only archives; full names in paths are not offered.
- Dates ISO 8601 (`2026-10-23`); periods `2026-27-Q2`, `2026-09`; FY folders `FY 2026-27`.

### DP1.4 File formats per dataset

| Content | Formats | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| Structured data (each dataset) | `[dataset].csv`, `[dataset].xlsx`, `[dataset].schema.json`; optional `[dataset].jsonl` | CSV: RFC 4180, UTF-8 with BOM (so Excel opens it correctly), ISO 8601 dates with time zone, amounts as fixed 2-decimal strings in INR with a `currency` column, no thousands separators, codes plus a label column. XLSX: a "Read me" sheet, frozen header row, column comments with the dictionary text, data typed (dates as dates, amounts as numbers with 2 decimals); sheets split at 1,000,000 rows with part numbers |
| Documents (originals) | As stored in M16 (PDF, images, DOCX, signed PDFs, XML) | Original bytes unchanged; SHA-256 equals the M16 hash; signing evidence alongside |
| Renditions and reports | PDF/A-2b plus DOCX for narrative documents (minutes, policies, notices, CAMs, loan file summaries); XLSX for tabular reports | PDF/A carries `document_id` and source hash in XMP (Integration Spec Part 12) |
| Per-loan summary | `Loan summary - LN-[id].pdf` and `.docx` | One readable file: parties (masked by role), sanction and KFS terms, schedule, receipts, DPD and classification history, charges, collateral, documents index, events timeline, links to the dataset rows |
| Per-meeting record | Notice, agenda, board pack, minutes (signed PDF/A and DOCX), resolutions, attendance | From Part 7F GV2 |
| Regulatory and bureau files | Exactly as generated and submitted, plus validation report, sign-off and acknowledgement | Byte-identical to the submitted file (hash match with RR3 and RR6 records) |
| Audit trail | `audit-events.jsonl` plus monthly XLSX digest | Hash-chain verifiable offline |

CI renders every Office and PDF output headless (LibreOffice) and validates PDF/A (veraPDF); a rendering failure blocks the release (Part 11.6).

### DP1.5 Manifest, data dictionary, relationship map and README

- **`export-manifest.csv`** (one row per file): `path`, `sha256`, `bytes`, `media_type`, `record_count`, `legal_entity`, `dataset`, `schema_version`, `as_of`, `created_at`, `source_ids` (canonical IDs covered, or a range), `restricted` (Y or N), `retention_class`, `legal_hold` (Y or N), `upsi` (Y or N) (`archive_manifest_v1`).
- **`manifest.json`** repeats the rows and adds: `archive_id` (ULID), `archive_standard_version`, `folder_profile`, producer product and Finbyx release, tenant, `reid` and legal entities, scope definition, requester and approvers, the `as_of` instant, `control_totals` (below), `predecessor_archive_id` for incremental chains, a pack-level SHA-256 over the sorted file list and the signing key id; `manifest.json.jws` is a detached JWS (RFC 7515, 7797) with the tenant's export-signing key (Part 10.4 KMS); the public key and its fingerprint are in the README.
- **Control totals** per legal entity at the as-of point: number of customers, applications, loans by status; principal outstanding and interest receivable; GL trial-balance totals by account; number of documents and total bytes; number of audit events and the last hash-chain anchor. The export job reconciles these to the live system before signing; any difference fails the job.
- **Data dictionary** (`data-dictionary.xlsx` and `.csv`): dataset, field, label, plain-English description, type, length, unit, format, code table, nullable, example, data class (PUBLIC, INTERNAL, CONFIDENTIAL, RESTRICTED), PII flag, source module, REQ-ID references where a field exists because of a regulation.
- **Relationship map:** `relationships.csv` (from dataset and field, to dataset and field, cardinality, description) and `relationship-map.pdf` (entity-relationship diagram). Canonical IDs follow Integration Spec Part 5.1, so a loan in `04 Lending` joins to its bureau rows in `06`, its return lines in `05` and its audit events in `14`.
- **README** (PDF, DOCX and TXT, in English; Hindi optional): what the archive is and its scope; as-of time and time zone; who requested and approved it; folder guide; how to open CSV files in Excel without corrupting leading zeros (use the XLSX or the import wizard); how to verify checksums (`sha256sum -c`, `Get-FileHash`, `CertUtil -hashfile`) and the signature (verifier in `verify/`); how to join tables; glossary of lending and regulatory terms used; restricted-folder handling; retention and legal-hold notes; contact details. A test reads the README and checks every folder it names exists.
- **Verifier:** an open-source command-line tool (licence Apache-2.0) and its source in `verify/`, which checks hashes, the JWS signature, control totals and CSV schema conformance offline.

### DP1.6 Restricted folders

- `10 HR and Payroll/Restricted` (Part 7F GV6) and `12 Legal and Recovery/Restricted` (privileged documents, Part 7A.0.10) are packaged as separate AES-256 encrypted ZIP archives (openable with common tools such as 7-Zip), each with its own manifest inside.
- Included only if the requester holds `export.restricted.hr` or `export.restricted.legal` and a second approver (HR head or General Counsel, plus the DPO) approves; the password is generated per archive and delivered out of band to the named recipient; neither password nor key is stored with the archive.
- UPSI-flagged records (GV4) carry a `upsi` marker in the manifest; exporting them creates SDD entries for the recipient.
- Processor exports (to vendors) never include privileged documents (Part 7A.0.10) or HR data.

### Acceptance tests

- A full archive for a synthetic tenant opens in LibreOffice and Microsoft Office (CI), validates as PDF/A, and the verifier reports zero hash, signature or schema errors.
- Changing one byte in any file makes the verifier fail on that file; deleting a file fails the manifest count.
- Control totals in `manifest.json` equal the live system's loan count, principal outstanding and TB totals at the as-of point; a seeded discrepancy fails the job before signing.
- No folder or file name contains a customer name under the default label policy; a path longer than 240 characters is shortened with an ID suffix and still resolves through the manifest.
- An archive requested without `export.restricted.hr` contains no `10 HR and Payroll/Restricted` content and the manifest marks the folder as excluded.
- The README names every top-level folder present; a folder rename via `folder_policy` updates the README and keeps every relationship resolvable.
- A CSV with an account number starting with `0` keeps the leading zero in the XLSX rendition.

## DP2. Scoped, scheduled and full exports

### DP2.1 Scopes

| Scope | Example | Approval | Event `scope type` |
|---|---|---|---|
| Dataset | Loans of branch X; collections of September | Tenant user with `export.dataset` for that dataset and branch scope | DATASET |
| Legal entity or FY | Everything for entity B, FY 2025-26 | Tenant admin | LEGAL_ENTITY |
| Module | Recovery Suite on detach (7A.0.5); HRMS on detach (GV6) | Module owner plus tenant admin | MODULE |
| Regulatory or audit pack | Inspection, statutory audit, CIC dispute | Owned by AU7 and RR5; uses this engine | AUDIT_PACK |
| Data principal request | Copy of one borrower's data for a DPDP or RBC request handled by the tenant | Tenant GRO or DPO; delivered by the tenant, not by Infrabyx | DATASET (data classes listed; no identifier in the event) |
| Full tenant | Every dataset, document, configuration and audit trail | Tenant admin plus a second approver (CCO or CFO); MFA (CYB para 115) | FULL_TENANT |
| Exit | Final export in DP5 | Authorised signatory plus tenant admin; MFA | EXIT |

### DP2.2 Job lifecycle

`REQUESTED → APPROVED → SNAPSHOT → RENDER → PACKAGE → SIGN → DELIVER → CONFIRMED`, with `REJECTED`, `CANCELLED` (by the requester before SNAPSHOT), `FAILED (retryable)` and `EXPIRED` (an approval not used within 7 days, or an unconfirmed delivery after its link expires).

- **Retries and partial failure:** every worker step is idempotent on `(job_id, dataset, part)` and checkpointed; a retry resumes from the last completed part against the same snapshot; three failed attempts on a part move the job to `FAILED` with the failing dataset named; a job never signs or delivers a partial archive, and a failed delivery is retried only to the same target.

- **REQUESTED** emits `ExportRequested` (scope, requester, data classes, destination type; no data).
- **SNAPSHOT:** a consistent point-in-time view at the as-of business date and time (repeatable-read transaction on a read replica, or a logical snapshot) so every dataset and the control totals describe the same instant; documents referenced by the snapshot are frozen by version.
- **RENDER and PACKAGE:** parallel workers per dataset; ZIP64 for archives over 4 GB; optional split volumes at a configurable size (default 2 GB).
- **SIGN:** control-total reconciliation, manifest, JWS.
- **DELIVER:** to a storage target (DP3) or as a signed download link valid for 7 days, single-use per recipient, IP and user logged; downloads from outside India are allowed only for scopes without regulated classes (DP3.1 "non-regulated" test) and are logged with a warning [REC].
- **CONFIRMED:** the recipient or target acknowledges (checksum re-computed by the target where the connector supports it); emits `ExportCompleted` (archive id, file count, bytes, manifest hash, destination type).
- Every export is audit-logged and appears in the bulk-export anomaly alerts (Part 10.4 monitoring).

### DP2.3 Scheduled and incremental exports

- **Schedules:** daily incremental, weekly incremental, monthly full, FY-end full (default after period close), and on-demand.
- **Incremental design:** a change watermark per dataset (CDC position or `updated_at` plus event sequence); the archive contains a `changes/` folder with inserted and changed rows and a `reversals/` file for reversed or cancelled records (Finbyx never hard-deletes financial or regulatory records; Part 10.2 principle 19); each incremental manifest names its predecessor's `archive_id` so a chain can be verified.
- **Missed runs** are caught up in order; a gap in the chain raises an alert to the tenant admin.

### DP2.4 Performance and limits

- Reference target [REC]: a full export of 1 million loans with 10 million schedule rows and 5 million documents (by reference, not re-read) completes within 8 hours without degrading staff SLOs (Part 10.3); rate-limited per tenant; scheduled outside COB windows.
- Restricted folders, privileged documents and UPSI follow DP1.6 in every scope.

### DP2.5 Export wizard

1. **Scope:** pick scope type, legal entities, FY or period, datasets and the as-of instant (default: last completed COB); the wizard shows record counts and estimated size before submission.
2. **Data classes:** each class with its handling note; restricted classes appear only to holders of `export.restricted.[class]` and add the DP1.6 approvers; Aadhaar and card data are never offered.
3. **Folder preview:** the tree under the active `folder_policy`, the label policy and the first rows of each dataset in a sample view; path-length and naming checks run inline.
4. **Format and encryption:** CSV, XLSX and schema always; optional JSONL and split-volume size; encryption: TLS in transit and the target's server-side encryption (default), AES-256 inner archives for restricted folders, and optional client-side encryption of the whole archive to the tenant's public key (DP3.3).
5. **Delivery target:** a connected DP3 target whose data-class policy allows every selected class (others are greyed out with the reason) or a signed download link; residency is re-verified at submission.
6. **Approvals and schedule:** required approvers computed from DP2.1 and shown by name; one-off or saved as a schedule (DP2.3).
7. **Review and submit:** a plain-language summary ("12 datasets, about 3.2 GB, to S3 bucket X in ap-south-1, approved by CFO") and MFA; drafts are kept for 7 days.

### Acceptance tests

- An export taken during live posting reconciles exactly to the snapshot's control totals, and a posting committed one second after the as-of instant is absent.
- A full export without a second approver stays in REQUESTED; an approver who is also the requester is rejected.
- Three daily incrementals followed by a reversal produce a chain whose `reversals/` file lists the reversed receipt, and the verifier confirms the chain links.
- A download link used twice or after 7 days returns `link_expired`; each attempt is logged.
- `ExportRequested` and `ExportCompleted` payloads contain no customer data (schema test).
- A worker crash during RENDER resumes from the last completed part on retry and the final control totals still equal the snapshot; three failures on one part end in `FAILED` with no signed archive.
- The wizard greys out a Google Drive target when any regulated class is selected and states why.

## DP3. Customer-controlled storage connectors

### DP3.1 Storage modes and responsibilities

| Mode | Finbyx role | Tenant role | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. SaaS default | Primary store in AWS ap-south-1, DR ap-south-2 (Part 10.1); platform backups (EO3) | Exports on demand | Default for all tenants |
| 2. Customer cloud bucket | Writes exports and backups to the tenant's bucket | Owns bucket, region, retention, object lock, keys | S3, Azure Blob, GCS |
| 3. SharePoint or OneDrive | Writes to a granted site or library | Owns the Microsoft 365 tenant and residency | Via Graph `Sites.Selected` (Part 7F GV7) |
| 4. Google Drive | Writes non-regulated data only | Owns the shared drive | No India data region: never personal data, books of account, returns, loan or HR data |
| 5. On-premises | Pushes to SFTP or is pulled by the outbound-only Finbyx Connector Agent (AC6.1, extended in GV7.5) | Owns servers, disks, network and physical security | No arbitrary disk attachment in Finbyx's cloud |

A RACI per mode (keys, backup, restore, retention, legal hold, deletion, incident response, RTO/RPO, residency evidence) is generated into the tenant's contract annex and the evidence pack (OUT para 74; Part 10.6).

### DP3.2 Connector contract

All storage connectors implement the Integration Spec connector SPI (Part 10.1) as `StorageTarget` with: `describe()` (provider, region, encryption, immutability), `verifyResidency()`, `testWrite()` (write, read back, compare hash, delete the canary where permitted), `put(stream, path, sha256)` with resumable upload, `head(path)` (size and checksum), `list(prefix)`, `retentionInfo()`, `healthCheck()`. Certification (Integration Spec Part 14.3) is required before production use.

| Provider | Authentication (no long-lived secrets where federation exists) | Residency check | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Amazon S3 | Cross-account IAM role assumed with an `ExternalId`; bucket policy limited to Finbyx's role | `GetBucketLocation` must return ap-south-1 or ap-south-2 for RE data | SSE-KMS with the tenant's key; S3 Object Lock recommended; checksum SHA-256 on upload |
| Azure Blob | Entra workload identity federation (federated credential) or a user-delegation SAS valid ≤ 7 days | Storage account location Central India, South India or West India | Immutability policies recommended |
| Google Cloud Storage | Workload identity federation | Bucket location asia-south1 or asia-south2 | Retention policy and bucket lock recommended |
| SharePoint, OneDrive | Entra app with `Sites.Selected` for the granted site | Tenant Default Geography India attestation (GV7.1) | Upload sessions for large files; library versioning on |
| Google Drive | Service account with minimal Drive scope on a shared drive | No India region: non-regulated classes only (DP3.1) | Shared drive only, never a personal "My Drive"; write-once not offered |
| Other S3-compatible stores | Access key in the tenant vault rotated at least every 90 days, or the on-premises agent | Signed tenant attestation of site in India | Object lock where the store supports it |
| SFTP | Key-based, host-key pinned, ed25519 keys rotated yearly | Tenant attests server location | Server-side checksum command used where available; write-once only if WORM is attested |
| On-premises agent | mTLS device certificate (AC6.1; GV7.5) | Tenant attests site in India | Agent writes to NAS, file share or S3-compatible store (for example MinIO) |

- **`StorageTargetConnected`** is emitted after `verifyResidency()` and `testWrite()` pass, with provider, region, data classes allowed, key mode, write-once flag and certification version.
- **Data-class policy** per target (Integration Spec Parts 12.2, 13.2): a write of a class the target does not allow is refused before upload. Borrower, applicant, loan, KYC, bureau, grievance, recovery and HR data, books of account and regulatory returns require an India-resident target (CF para 14(4); OUT para 74(vi); Accounts Rules r.3(5)); books of account additionally require a daily India copy (AC7).
- **Residency and health:** residency is verified at connection, re-verified weekly and before every full or exit export; `healthCheck()` and a canary write run daily; credential expiry is warned 30 days ahead. A failure (credential revoked, residency unverifiable, canary mismatch) pauses the target's jobs, alerts the tenant admin and publishes `ControlTestResultPublished`; nothing is silently retried with a different target.
- **Write-once:** when the tenant selects it, every `put` sets the provider lock with `retainUntil` equal to the archive's longest retention class; a target that cannot honour the lock is not offered the option.
- **Credentials** live in the per-tenant integration vault (M19) with rotation reminders.

### DP3.3 Keys: BYOK and HYOK

| Option | How | Trade-off |
|---|---|---|
| Platform-managed (default) | Per-tenant AWS KMS key; envelope encryption | Simplest; Infrabyx operates the key under tenant-scoped policy |
| BYOK, cross-account | Tenant-owned KMS key in the tenant's AWS account; Finbyx uses it through a key grant | Tenant can revoke; revocation stops Finbyx from decrypting new and existing data |
| BYOK, imported material | Tenant generates key material and imports it into a Finbyx-account KMS key (external origin) | Tenant keeps escrow of the material; rotation is manual |
| HYOK (external key store) | AWS KMS External Key Store backed by the tenant's HSM through an XKS proxy | If the HSM or proxy is unavailable, Finbyx cannot decrypt; if keys are lost, data is lost; symmetric only; no automatic rotation; offered only with a written risk acceptance signed by the tenant's CISO and CTO |
| Client-side archive encryption | Archives encrypted to the tenant's public key (age X25519 or OpenPGP) before delivery | Infrabyx cannot read delivered archives; tenant must protect its private key |

ML and UL tenants must be offered tenant-controlled keys (OUT para 97(vii)(b); Part 10.4). Key events (create, grant, revoke, rotate) are logged and visible to the tenant.

### Acceptance tests

- An S3 bucket in us-east-1 is refused for the "Loans" class with `residency_not_india`; the same bucket is accepted for "Policies" only if the tenant enabled that class for non-India targets.
- A Google Drive target can never be configured to accept personal data, books of account, returns, loan or HR classes (no UI path; the API returns `residency_blocked_borrower_data`, mapped to `residency-blocked` on the ecosystem error model).
- A weekly residency re-check that cannot read the bucket region pauses the target and publishes `ControlTestResultPublished` with result FAIL.
- `testWrite()` detects a checksum mismatch introduced by a faulty proxy and the target is not connected.
- Revoking the BYOK grant in the tenant account causes the next export and the next document read to fail closed with `key_unavailable`, with an alert to the tenant and to Infrabyx operations; restoring the grant resumes work without data loss.
- An HYOK configuration cannot be saved without an uploaded, signed risk acceptance.
- A connector that has not passed certification cannot be selected for a production tenant.

## DP4. Backups to customer storage and restore testing

### DP4.1 Two layers of backup

| Layer | What | Owner | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|
| Platform backups | Database PITR and snapshots, object-store versioning and cross-region replication, immutable vault, DR site | Infrabyx (EO3) | Part 10.3; CYB paras 102, 129–137 |
| Customer-held copies | Daily encrypted incremental archive (DP2.3) and monthly full archive in the DP1 standard, delivered to the tenant's DP3 target | Tenant, with Finbyx delivering | CYB para 8(9) (Ch III "backup of data with periodic testing"), para 133 (Ch V); OUT paras 34(xii), 97(xvi); tenant BCP |

Books of account and their audit trail are backed up daily on servers in India by Finbyx regardless of customer copies (Companies (Accounts) Rules r.3(5); AC7); if the tenant has a DP3 India target, the AC7 daily books backup is also delivered there.

### DP4.2 Customer-held backup policy

- **Default schedule [REC]:** daily incremental at 02:00 IST after COB, weekly incremental consolidation, monthly full on the 1st after month-end close, FY full after audit sign-off.
- **Dedicated deployments** (Part 3.1 item 3) may also receive an encrypted logical database dump of the tenant's schemas, with a restore script; multi-tenant deployments receive the archive standard only (a shared database cannot be dumped per tenant safely).
- **Retention on the tenant side** is the tenant's decision; Finbyx recommends object lock or WORM and a retention at least equal to the longest applicable class (books 8 FY, s.128(5); KYC 5 years after relationship end; litigation records per Part 7A.0.5) [REC].
- **`BackupCompleted`** per run, once delivered and verified, with archive id, type (DAILY_INCREMENTAL, WEEKLY, MONTHLY_FULL, FY_FULL; a dedicated deployment's logical dump travels with the monthly full), bytes, manifest hash and target id; the daily run is due by 06:00 IST.
- **Failures:** a run not verified by 06:00 IST counts as missed; one missed run raises a P2 alert to the tenant admin and Infrabyx support; two consecutive misses raise P1 and a tenant notice; repeated failure is reported in the tenant's monthly service report (OUT para 74(v)).

### DP4.3 Restore testing

| Test | Frequency | Method | Pass criteria |
|---|---|---|---|
| Integrity | Every backup | Verifier on the delivered archive (hash, signature, chain link) | Zero errors |
| Readability | Monthly | Open a random sample of 50 files across formats in headless LibreOffice and a PDF validator | All open; PDF/A valid |
| Rehydration | Quarterly [REC]; at least the tenant's BCP cadence (CYB para 133 for Ch V; para 8(9) for Ch III) | Load the latest full plus incrementals into an isolated sandbox tenant through the Finbyx archive importer; run reconciliation | Control totals equal; trial balance equal; sample of 100 loans re-computes the same outstanding, DPD and classification as at the as-of date; audit-trail hash chain verifies |
| DR drill | Half-yearly (platform) | EO3 and Part 10.3 drill | As Part 10.3 |

- **Archive importer:** Finbyx can import its own archive format (all versions it has issued) into a sandbox or a new tenant. This is also the re-onboarding path after an exit.
- **`RestoreTested`** with test type (INTEGRITY, READABILITY, REHYDRATION, DR_DRILL), archive id, result, discrepancy count and approver role; results go to the tenant's evidence pack and the control library (OH14; EO5). A failed test opens a P2 problem record, and the next customer-held backup is not marked healthy until a re-test passes.
- Tenants may run rehydration on their own infrastructure using the documented schemas; Finbyx publishes a reference loader script for PostgreSQL [REC].

### Acceptance tests

- A daily backup to a tenant S3 bucket completes, the verifier passes, and `BackupCompleted` is emitted once even when the job is retried after a network failure.
- A quarterly rehydration of a synthetic tenant into a sandbox reproduces the trial balance and the DPD of 100 sampled loans exactly; a seeded missing incremental makes the chain check fail and the test is marked failed.
- Two consecutive missed backups raise a P1 alert and a tenant notice.
- The archive importer accepts an archive of the previous standard version and rejects one whose signature does not verify.

## DP5. Tenant exit and off-boarding

### DP5.1 Legal basis

- No erasing, purging, revoking, altering or changing data during the transition unless the regulator or the NBFC advises otherwise; safe removal or destruction clauses (OUT para 87).
- Full cooperation with the NBFC and its new provider (OUT para 88); orderly transfer (74(xv)).
- Exit strategy with agreed processes and turnaround times for returning data, data completeness and portability, secure purge, smooth transition and contractual exit plans (OUT para 97(xvi)(a)–(c)), and prompt take-over of transaction, customer, operational and configuration data with purging at the provider's end and independent assurance before sign-off (97(xvi)(d)); data lifecycle to permanent erasure (97(ii)); preservation per the NBFC's legal obligations, including after termination (the para 34(xii) duty, applied by contract).
- Digital-lending data stays in India (CF para 14(4)); books backed up in India daily until the tenant's own system takes over (Accounts Rules r.3(5)).

### DP5.2 Exit states

`EXIT_NOTICE → EXIT_PLAN_AGREED → CONFIG_FREEZE → PARALLEL_RUN (optional) → CUT_OVER → FINAL_EXPORT → TENANT_VERIFICATION → SUCCESSOR_SUPPORT → READ_ONLY_RETENTION → PURGE_APPROVED → PURGED → PURGE_CERTIFIED → CLOSED`

| State | What happens | Default turnaround [REC] |
|---|---|---|
| EXIT_PLAN_AGREED | Plan lists datasets, formats, successor contacts, cut-over date, open statutory clocks (as Part 7A.0.5), returns and CIC submissions due in the window, TATs, liabilities | 10 working days from notice |
| CONFIG_FREEZE | No configuration changes except regulatory; transactions continue; purge and retention-deletion jobs suspended for the tenant (OUT para 87) | From plan approval |
| CUT_OVER | Writes stop at the agreed time; COB final run; period closed | Agreed date |
| FINAL_EXPORT | Full archive (DP1) including folder 13 configuration and folder 14 audit trail, plus the Integration Spec Part 12 layouts the successor asks for | 5 working days after cut-over for ≤ 1 million loans |
| TENANT_VERIFICATION | Tenant reconciles control totals and signs off, or lists defects that Finbyx fixes and re-exports | Tenant-driven |
| SUCCESSOR_SUPPORT | Field-mapping sessions, data-dictionary clarifications, re-exports in agreed layouts, a cooperation log of every request and response (OUT para 88) | Up to 60 days [REC] |
| READ_ONLY_RETENTION | Tenant users keep read-only access and export rights | 90 days after cut-over [REC], extendable by contract |
| PURGE_APPROVED | Tenant's authorised signatory approves purge in writing after confirming it holds the archive and its retention duties are met from its own systems | Tenant-driven |
| PURGED | Live data deleted; tenant KMS key scheduled for deletion so every backup copy becomes unreadable (crypto-shredding); object stores and search indexes cleared; logs beyond legal minimums deleted | Within 30 days of approval; KMS deletion window 7–30 days |
| PURGE_CERTIFIED | Purge certificate listing systems, methods, dates and the key-deletion record; independent assurance by the auditor that covers Infrabyx's ISMS or SOC 2 scope (OUT para 97(xvi)(d)) | Certificate within 10 working days of purge |

During the transition, dunning (CM4) never suspends read or export for an RE tenant.

- **Exceptions:** an exit notice withdrawn in writing before CUT_OVER returns the tenant to normal operation and lifts CONFIG_FREEZE (the purge hold stays until the withdrawal is countersigned); a successor that rejects the final archive keeps the case in TENANT_VERIFICATION while defects are fixed and re-exported under a new `archive_id` linked to the first; records under legal hold or an open statutory clock at PURGE_APPROVED are listed and cannot be purged until the tenant takes custody or contracts the paid read-only archival tier; a READ_ONLY_RETENTION extension is a contract change recorded with its new end date.

### DP5.3 What Infrabyx can and cannot promise

**Can promise (put in the MSA):**

- a complete export in documented, non-proprietary formats with manifest, checksums, control totals and a signature;
- configuration export (products, rule packs, templates, workflows, roles, DoA, flags);
- no deletion or alteration of tenant data during the transition;
- cooperation with the successor within the agreed TATs, with a cooperation log;
- read-only access for the agreed retention window;
- secure purge with a certificate and independent assurance;
- escrow release of source code under the escrow agreement if Infrabyx fails (CYB para 105; Part 10.6 item 25).

**Cannot promise (say so in the MSA and sales material):**

- zero-downtime or "lossless" migration into any successor system (that depends on the successor);
- recovery of data after the tenant has purged or lost its own customer-held copies or keys;
- attachment of arbitrary disks, USB drives or tenant hardware to Finbyx's cloud;
- HYOK availability if the tenant's HSM or XKS proxy fails;
- retention of the tenant's regulated records after purge (the tenant must hold them; an optional paid read-only archival tier can be contracted instead of purge).

### DP5.4 Partial exits

- **Legal-entity exit** (one entity in a group tenant leaves): same states, scoped to that entity; shared configuration is copied, not moved.
- **Module detach** follows Part 7A.0.5 for the Recovery Suite and the same pattern for other modules (CM1): read-only, export pack, never delete.
- **Insolvency or resolution of the tenant:** Finbyx cooperates with the resolution professional or administrator under the contract (OUT para 74(xvi)); access is granted to the person the tenant's authorised signatory or the competent authority designates, recorded through the external-access workflow (AU7, `ExternalAccessGranted`; at most 90 days per grant, renewable by fresh approval).

### Acceptance tests

- After EXIT_NOTICE, a scheduled retention-deletion job for the tenant is suspended and an attempt to purge a document returns `exit_transition_hold`.
- The final archive's control totals equal the post-COB totals at CUT_OVER and include folder 13 with every active rule pack and its approvals.
- Read-only users can open and export during READ_ONLY_RETENTION but cannot post; access ends automatically at the end of the window unless extended by contract.
- PURGED cannot be reached without a signed PURGE_APPROVED; after purge, a restore attempt of any backup snapshot for the tenant fails because the tenant key is deleted, and the purge certificate lists that key-deletion event.
- A payment default by an RE tenant during the exit window does not reduce read or export access.
- PURGE_APPROVED with one loan under legal hold purges everything else, keeps that loan's records, and lists them on the purge certificate as retained with the reason.
- An exit notice withdrawn before CUT_OVER lifts the configuration freeze; the same withdrawal after CUT_OVER is refused with `exit_past_cut_over`.

# PART 7K — PLANS, ENTITLEMENTS, BILLING AND PAYMENTS (TENANT SIDE)

**Purpose.** Let tenants see and manage what they buy from Infrabyx in plain language, and let Finbyx enforce exactly what they bought, without ever letting a commercial event interrupt a regulated function. The **Operations Hub owns the revenue catalogue, prices, invoices, Razorpay account and revenue accounting** (OH8); Finbyx owns the tenant-facing pages, server-side entitlement enforcement, usage metering at source, and the regulatory-continuity rules. Vendor billing is completely separate from lender-to-borrower loan accounting and collections (M7, M10).

**Applicability.** Every tenant. Dedicated and on-premises deployments use an offline signed licence file instead of live entitlement sync (CM1.5). Udofin has its own plans and borrower-side rules (Udofin Part 7G); nothing here permits charging borrowers.

**Requirement codes.** OUT (paras 15, 74, 87, 97(xvi)), CF (paras 10(1)–(5) for the separation of loan money), CYB (para 115 MFA), DPS (card data), `PCI`, `GST`, `ITA25`, `DPDP`, `CCPA`, `ASCI`, `EMD` (RBI E-mandate Directions 2026, RBI/DPSS/2026-27/396, 21 Apr 2026), `PA` (RBI Payment Aggregator Directions 2025), CoFT circular 2021 (codes in Part 8A.37). REQ-ID examples: `REQ-EMD-8(a)`, `REQ-EMD-6(a)`, `REQ-OUT-87`, `REQ-PCI-SAQA`.

**Data owned.** Catalogue, prices, invoices, payments and contracts: Operations Hub (Infrabyx is the seller and data owner of its commercial records). Entitlement state as applied, usage records at source, billing-page preferences and billing contacts: Finbyx, as part of the tenant's account with Infrabyx. Only aggregated usage quantities and statement hashes leave Finbyx for billing; no borrower or loan-level data is ever sent to the Operations Hub.

**Extends, does not rebuild.** Part 7A.0.1–7A.0.3 (module registry, `licence_sku`, entitlement plus feature flag, module lifecycle) generalised to every optional module; Part 10.2 principle 35; Part 11.6 commercial viability; M19 roles; Integration Spec billing domain events.

**Canonical events.** Consumed from the Operations Hub: `PlanChanged`, `EntitlementChanged`, `InvoiceIssued`, `SubscriptionPaymentReceived`, `SubscriptionPaymentFailed`, `SubscriptionCancelled`. Produced by Finbyx: `UsageRecorded`. `TenantProvisioned` (ops domain) is consumed when a sandbox or production tenant is created.

## CM1. Plan catalogue consumption and entitlement enforcement

### CM1.1 Catalogue consumption

- The Operations Hub publishes a **signed catalogue document** per version: products, plans, SKUs, modules per SKU, meters, price books (by market, currency and channel), add-ons, revenue-stream flags (CM5), plain-language explainer text (CM2.3), effective dates and grandfathering rules.
- Finbyx fetches it through the Hub API, verifies the JWS signature against the pinned Hub key, validates it against the catalogue schema, and stores it read-only (`catalogue_version`). An invalid or unsigned catalogue is rejected and the previous version stays live.
- **Every SKU must map to modules in the Finbyx module registry**: each `module.yaml` (Part 7A.0.1) carries `licence_sku`; a catalogue SKU that names an unknown module, or a module without a SKU, fails the catalogue import with a report to Hub operations.
- Prices are displayed from the catalogue only; Finbyx never computes a price or a tax.

### CM1.2 Module registry and SKUs [REC; final packaging is an owner decision]

| SKU family | Modules (registry ids) | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Core | M1–M8, M10–M19, M21 (M9 points to Part 7A), Part 7J DP1–DP2 on-demand export and DP5 exit | Export and exit export are never removed from any plan |
| AI layer | M20 | Usage-metered where model cost applies; every AI use stays under M20 governance |
| Accounting and tax | Part 7C | Required for statutory audit-trail evidence when Finbyx holds books |
| Regulatory returns and bureaus | Part 7B (RR1–RR8) | Priced per entity, not per return |
| Risk and capital | Part 7E | — |
| Audit and assurance | Part 7D | Auditor and supervisor seats never charged to the regulator |
| Governance | Part 7F GV1–GV3, GV5 | — |
| Listed entity | Part 7F GV4 | Activated by listing status |
| Workforce | Part 7F GV6 | Separate data-processing addendum |
| Workplace connectors | Part 7F GV7 | — |
| Recovery Suite (Core, Settlement and ADR, Secured Enforcement, Shared-Exposure, Playbooks) | Part 7A SKUs | Unchanged from v1.4 |
| Institution profiles | Part 7G packs (co-operative, microfinance, ARC, IFSC) | Profile-gated |
| Investments | Part 7H | — |
| Data portability plus | Part 7J DP3 scheduled deliveries, DP4 customer-held backups and rehydration tests, BYOK and HYOK | On-demand and exit exports stay in Core |
| Voice and AI contact centre | Part 7L EO6 | Usage-metered |
| Field app; borrower portal | M22; M23 | — |

### CM1.3 Entitlement model

- **Entitlement record** (set only by Infrabyx through the Hub; emitted as `EntitlementChanged`, signed): tenant, legal-entity scope, SKU, start, end, limits, and source contract reference.
- **Limit types:** `module` (on or off), `capacity` (named users, branches, legal entities, active loans, AUM band, devices), `rate` (API tier), `environment` (sandboxes), `support_tier`.
- **Quota behaviour per limit** (set in the catalogue): `hard` (blocks creation of new units beyond the limit, after the grace defined below), `soft` (allows and meters overage), `informational` (alerts only).
- **Server-side checks** on every API call, workflow step, worker and UI slot, as in Part 7A.0.2: a capability runs only if the entitlement is active, the tenant flag is on and every required module is ENABLED (or READ_ONLY for reads). Denials return `403` with `not_entitled`, `limit_reached`, `not_enabled`, `dependency_missing` or `read_only`, and are logged.
- **Tenant flags** (maker-checker, per entity, product and branch) can only narrow what is entitled, never widen it.
- **`PlanChanged`** updates the plan view and schedules the entitlement changes for their effective time; upgrades take effect immediately, downgrades at the end of the paid term unless the contract says otherwise (OH8.4). Entitlements change only on the signed `EntitlementChanged`, never on `PlanChanged` alone; an `EntitlementChanged` whose version is lower than the applied one is ignored and logged.

### CM1.4 Regulatory-continuity rule (platform guard-rail)

No commercial state (quota exhausted, payment overdue, downgrade, suspension, cancellation) may stop or degrade:

- COB, accruals, classification, provisioning and period close;
- disbursement of loans already sanctioned, servicing, receipts, mandate presentation already scheduled, refunds and document release (RBC paras 35–39);
- CIC submissions, regulatory returns, FIU-IND reports and incident notices;
- grievance handling, Internal Ombudsman and RB-IOS workflows;
- statements, certificates and disclosures owed to borrowers;
- collections conduct controls (contact-policy engine), call-recording retention;
- the audit trail, read access and export (OUT para 87);
- auditor and RBI supervisor access (CYB paras 46, 57).

Hard limits apply only to creating new non-regulated units (new users above the seat limit, new module attachments, new product configurations) and, after notice, to new lead and application intake above a contracted cap. A downgrade or cancellation moves modules to READ_ONLY through the Part 7A.0.5 detach workflow (open-deadline gate, export pack, no deletion).

### CM1.5 Offline and dedicated deployments

- Dedicated and on-premises installations use a signed licence file (tenant, SKUs, limits, validity, grace) verified at start-up and daily; renewal by uploading a new file.
- If the Hub is unreachable, SaaS tenants keep the last valid signed entitlement for 30 days [REC]; there is no remote "kill switch" and no remote deletion path.

### Acceptance tests

- A catalogue signed with an unknown key is rejected and the previous version remains live; a catalogue naming a module absent from the registry fails import with a report.
- A tenant without the `Investments` SKU receives `403 not_entitled` on every Part 7H API and sees no 7H menu; enabling the tenant flag alone changes nothing.
- An expired subscription with an overdue invoice still runs COB, files the CIC submission due on the 16th, and lets a borrower download a statement.
- Reaching the named-user limit blocks creating a new user with `limit_reached` but does not affect existing users' sessions.
- Downgrading away from Recovery Core with an open s.138 clock is held at the Part 7A.0.5 open-deadline gate.
- With the Hub unreachable for 10 days, entitlements continue; at day 31 the tenant sees a warning and no regulated function is affected.
