## CM2. Billing, membership and settings pages

### CM2.1 Roles

- `billing_admin` (tenant): manage payment methods and mandates, billing profile, contacts, purchase requests and cancellation requests; MFA for every billing change.
- `billing_viewer` (for example CFO office): read invoices, usage and statements.
- `tenant_admin`: membership (users and seats); cannot change payment methods unless also `billing_admin`.
- Nobody in the tenant can change entitlements; only Infrabyx can (through the Hub). Infrabyx staff see tenant billing pages only through break-glass support access (M19), logged and visible to the tenant.

### CM2.2 Menu and screens (workspace N, menus `Settings › Plan and billing` and `Settings › Users and roles › Seats`)

| Path | Content and key actions | Roles |
|---|---|---|
| `Settings › Plan and billing › Overview` | Current plan, SKUs and modules with status (ENABLED, READ_ONLY), contract term and renewal date, limits with current usage and 30-day forecast, open requests, notices (renewal, price change, quota, dunning stage); actions Change plan, Add seats, Raise ticket | `billing_admin`, `billing_viewer`, `tenant_admin` (read) |
| `… › Compare plans` | Generated from the catalogue: plain-language rows, entity-type fit, limits, included exports and support, price basis with GST; current plan highlighted; "contact sales" for enterprise plans creates a Hub CRM request | All three roles |
| `… › Add-ons` | Each module's explainer, dependencies (`requires`), regulatory notes, the legal or data addendum required (for example Workforce), status; actions Add (CM2.4) and Remove (downgrade path) | `billing_admin`; module owners read |
| `… › Usage` | Each meter: definition, period totals, daily trend, drill-down to the counted record IDs (inside Finbyx only), monthly statement with a dispute button open for 7 days | `billing_admin`, `billing_viewer` |
| `… › Invoices` | GST invoices, credit and debit notes, receipts, statement of account, payment status, TDS certificate (Form 131) upload, invoice dispute; PDF and XLSX downloads; filters by legal entity, period and status | `billing_admin`, `billing_viewer` |
| `… › Payment methods` | Methods and mandates (type, maximum amount, frequency, validity, status, last 4 digits and issuer only) held at Razorpay or the bank; add, replace or cancel through hosted pages only | `billing_admin` with fresh MFA |
| `… › Billing contacts` | Billing profile (legal name, CIN, PAN, GSTIN per registration and place of supply, addresses, PO numbers, e-invoice details, SEZ or IFSC status with LUT reference) and contacts per event (invoice, failure, renewal, quota) with channels (email; Teams or Google Chat via GV7) | `billing_admin` maker, second `billing_admin` or `tenant_admin` checker for GSTIN and legal-name changes |
| `… › Cancel or downgrade` | What changes, what stays available (read, export, exit, auditor access), open statutory clocks from the 7A.0.5 gate, export shortcut, cancellation or downgrade request; never more steps than purchase | `billing_admin` plus second approver |
| `Settings › Users and roles › Seats` | Seats by type (named, active, device), users per legal entity and role, invitations, deactivation, seat-pool reallocation, seat-limit warnings | `tenant_admin` |

Data, storage, backup and exit screens are under the `Data` menu (Part 7J DP6) and are linked from Overview. Every page has an empty state ("No invoices yet: your first invoice is issued on [date]") and an error state that never blocks a regulated function (for example "Billing service unavailable: your modules continue to work").

### CM2.3 Plain-language explainers

Each catalogue item carries explainer fields, approved in the Hub with marketing and legal review (OH7, OH8):

- **What it does** (≤ 40 words, no jargon); **who it is for** (entity types and layers);
- **What is included and the limits**; **what happens at the limit** (soft or hard, overage price);
- **What happens on downgrade or cancellation** (for example "Recovery Suite records become read-only. Nothing is deleted. You can export them at any time.");
- **Regulatory note** in honest terms (for example "Prepares and validates your CIMS returns and keeps the evidence. Your authorised officer files them on the RBI portal.");
- **Price basis**, with GST shown separately.

Rules: never claim that Finbyx "makes you compliant" or that a certification is held when it is not (EO5); no pre-ticked add-ons; cancellation as easy as purchase; renewal reminders at 90, 30 and 7 days (OH8.9); price-change notice of at least 30 days [REC]; no countdown timers, fake scarcity, inflated "value" figures or unverifiable testimonials (CCPA Dark Patterns Guidelines 2023 adopted as good practice for B2B; ASCI Code for any advertising claims). Explainer text passes the shared claims-gate linter (OH14.6) and a readability check (sentence length, glossary-term coverage) in CI.

### CM2.4 Plan, add-on, seat and cancellation workflows

- **Plan change (upgrade, downgrade or switch):** `DRAFT → PREVIEWED → SUBMITTED → APPROVED → ORDERED → (PAYMENT_PENDING → PAID) → SCHEDULED → EFFECTIVE`, with `REJECTED`, `CANCELLED` (before EFFECTIVE) and `EXPIRED` (quote validity, default 7 days [REC]).
  - **Preview:** Finbyx requests a priced quote from the Hub (OH8.4: catalogue prices; proration by IST calendar day) and shows the new price, prorated charge or credit, GST, effective date, the entitlement diff (modules gained or lost, limits), missing dependencies, and for a downgrade the Part 7A.0.5 open-deadline list and the records that become read-only. Finbyx computes no price or tax itself.
  - **Approval:** `billing_admin` submits with MFA; a second person (`tenant_admin` or a designated CFO-office approver) approves every increase above the tenant's threshold and every downgrade; self-approval is impossible.
  - **Order and effect:** the Hub creates the order; immediate payment uses the hosted-page redirect (CM4.1), otherwise the charge is invoiced. Entitlements change only when the signed `EntitlementChanged` arrives (CM1.3); a failed payment leaves the current plan untouched and the request in PAYMENT_PENDING until it expires; a Hub outage queues the request and changes nothing.
  - **Downgrades** wait in SCHEDULED until term end and can be cancelled until then; at effect the detach workflow runs (READ_ONLY, export pack, no deletion).
- **Add-on:** the plan-change flow plus acceptance of any required addendum before the order, then the Part 7A.0.4 attach workflow (prerequisites, configuration, certification) before the module is ENABLED.
- **Seats:** additions are prorated and effective on payment or order; reductions apply at term end and only when active users fit the new limit (the screen lists users to deactivate first).
- **Cancellation or non-renewal:** request with reason and second approval → Hub `CANCELLATION_REQUESTED` → effective at the end of the paid term → `SubscriptionCancelled` → Part 7J DP5 exit; withdrawable until effective; read, export and auditor access continue throughout.
- **Payment method change:** a new mandate is registered with AFA on the hosted page; the old one is cancelled only after the new one is active; a mandate above the plan's expected maximum is not offered.
- **Billing profile change:** GSTIN format and checksum validated; effective for invoices issued after approval; issued invoices change only through credit or debit notes (OH8.6).

### Settings and options (CM1–CM5)

| Setting | Level | Default | Nature |
|---|---|---|---|
| Regulatory-continuity rule (CM1.4), export and exit always included | Platform | Always on | Regulatory floor; no setting exists to change it |
| Second approver for plan changes | Tenant | Every downgrade and every increase above ₹0 | Tenant may raise the threshold, not remove the downgrade rule |
| MFA on billing changes | Platform | Always | Floor (CYB para 115 pattern) |
| Usage alerts | Tenant | 80% and 100% of each limit | Tenant may add earlier thresholds |
| Renewal and price-change notices | Platform | Renewal at 90, 30 and 7 days; price change ≥ 30 days ahead [REC] | Floor |
| Courtesy notice before a recurring debit | Tenant | T-48 hours, on | Commercial choice; the issuer's pre-debit notice is separate and mandatory |
| PO number on invoices | Tenant | Optional | Commercial choice |
| Invoice delivery | Tenant | Portal plus email PDF to billing contacts | Commercial choice |
| Vendor-announcements panel | Tenant | Off (opt-in) | Commercial choice; never shown inside lending workflows or borrower surfaces |
| Offline licence grace (dedicated deployments) | Contract | 30 days | Contractual |

### Acceptance tests

- The comparison table renders only from catalogue data; a test removing a limit from the catalogue removes it from the page with no code change.
- A `tenant_admin` without `billing_admin` cannot reach the payment-method page; a billing change without fresh MFA is refused.
- Every module page shows a downgrade explainer; a catalogue item missing one fails catalogue import.
- An explainer containing "guarantees compliance" or "certified" (without an EO5 certificate record) fails the CI content check.
- The cancellation page offers export and explains what remains available, and requires no more steps than purchase.
- A plan-change preview shows the Hub's prorated amount and GST unchanged; Finbyx code contains no price or tax computation (static check on the `billing` module).
- A downgrade submitted by a `billing_admin` cannot be approved by the same user; an approved upgrade whose payment fails leaves entitlements unchanged.
- Reducing seats below the number of active users is refused with the list of users to deactivate.
- A GSTIN change does not alter any issued invoice.

## CM3. Usage metering

### CM3.1 Meter definitions (from the catalogue; computed in Finbyx)

| Meter | Definition | Aggregation | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| `active_loans` | Distinct loan accounts in the tenant's own or serviced book with a non-zero balance on any ledger or any posted transaction in the period; excludes sandbox, closed-before-period and loans in a migration reconciliation window | Month-end snapshot and monthly peak (catalogue chooses which is billed) | M6, M10 |
| `aum_band` | Average of daily gross on-balance-sheet loan principal outstanding per legal entity (own share only for co-lent loans); derecognised but serviced pools reported as `serviced_aum` separately | Monthly average mapped to catalogue bands; band change applies from the next quarter after notice | M10 GL |
| `named_users`, `active_users` | Users with an active account; users who signed in at least once in the period | Peak and distinct count | M19 |
| `branches`, `legal_entities` | Active nodes | Month-end | M1 |
| `regulatory_runs` | Regulatory returns and CIC files approved for a period; validation re-runs and revisions in the same period are not billed | Count per period | RR3, RR6 |
| `reports` | Scheduled or on-demand report exports above the plan allowance | Count | M17 |
| `api_calls` | Calls by API product tier, excluding Udofin and certified ecosystem connectors where the contract says so | Sum | M21 |
| `storage_gb` | Documents and archives stored | Average | M16 |
| Pass-through meters | Bureau pulls, eSign, eStamp, KYC checks, SMS, WhatsApp, voice minutes | Count or minutes, priced at cost plus the disclosed margin | Provider call log (cost captured per call; M21) |

### CM3.2 Pipeline

- **Capture:** domain events produce `usage_record(tenant, legal_entity, meter, quantity, source_ref, occurred_at, idempotency_key)`; the key `(tenant, meter, source_ref, period)` prevents double counting on retries.
- **Aggregate:** nightly per meter and period (IST periods); reconciled against source counts (for example the month-end `active_loans` count equals the M6 status report); a break raises `ReconciliationBreakRaised`.
- **Statement:** `OPEN → (DISPUTED) → FINAL`. The monthly usage statement is issued in CM2 by the third working day after period end, with drill-down to record IDs inside Finbyx; the tenant has 7 days from issue to dispute a meter; the Hub holds invoicing for a disputed meter only; a dispute outcome or correction is a new statement version, never an edit; changes after invoicing appear as credit or debit lines next cycle.
- **Publish:** `UsageRecorded` (`usage_aggregate_v1`) to the Hub on statement issue and on each new version carries tenant, legal entity, meter, `meter_kind = USAGE`, period, quantity, meter code version, statement version and the statement hash, idempotent on `(tenantid, meter, period, statement_version)`; daily provisional totals may be sent for forecasting; **never record IDs or personal data**.
- **Alerts** at 80% and 100% of any limit to billing contacts; forecast warnings when the 30-day trend crosses a band.

### CM3.3 Metering integrity

- Meters are computed from the authoritative ledgers and registers, never from UI counters; the meter code version is stored with each statement.
- Back-dated postings that change a closed period's count do not re-bill a closed statement; they are reported as an adjustment line.
- No meter may create an incentive against borrowers or conduct rules: no pricing per recovered rupee, per legal notice sent or per collection call connected [REC; RBC para 100 conduct].

### Acceptance tests

- Replaying the same disbursement event three times yields one `usage_record`.
- The month-end `active_loans` equals the M6 count of qualifying accounts for a synthetic book of 10,000 loans, including NPAs and excluding loans closed before the month.
- A co-lent loan with a 20% tenant share contributes 20% of its principal to `aum_band`.
- `UsageRecorded` payloads pass a schema test that forbids any loan, customer or user identifier.
- A dispute raised on day 5 holds invoicing for that meter; on day 8 the dispute button is disabled and the statement is final.
- An upheld dispute publishes statement version 2 with a new hash; replaying version 1 changes nothing at the Hub.

## CM4. Payments via Razorpay and gateway security

### CM4.1 Architecture and separation

- **Merchant of record:** the Infrabyx legal entity that sells Finbyx (owner decision). The Razorpay account, API keys and webhook secrets live only in the Operations Hub; Finbyx never holds them.
- **Flow:** a Finbyx billing page calls the Hub billing API to create an order, payment link, subscription or mandate, then **redirects the browser (top-level navigation) to the Razorpay-hosted page**; Razorpay returns the user to a Finbyx return URL that shows status only after the Hub confirms the payment server-side.
- **No Razorpay script on Finbyx pages.** Embedding Standard Checkout JavaScript would put a third-party script on our page and bring the page into the SAQ A script-attack eligibility question (PCI DSS v4.0.1 SAQ A, revised 31 Jan 2025) [REC]; redirect or Payment Links keep Finbyx outside the cardholder-data environment.
- **Strict separation from loan money:** the `billing` module has no access to tenant payment credentials (M7) and M7 has no access to Hub billing; different secrets, service accounts and network paths. Razorpay Route, pooled or nodal-style tools are never used for loan money (CF paras 10(1)–(3)); tenant borrower collections run on the tenant's own gateway accounts (M7).
- **Card data:** never stored, processed or logged by Finbyx or the Hub; only Razorpay or network tokens and the last 4 digits with issuer name may be displayed (CoFT circular, 7 Sep 2021). CI log scanners fail the build on any PAN-like pattern in logs or fixtures.

### CM4.2 Payment methods and mandates

| Method | Use | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| Payment Link or hosted checkout (card, UPI, net banking) | One-off invoices, implementation milestones | Redirect only; amount in paise; receipt = invoice id (idempotent) |
| Razorpay Subscriptions with card or UPI AutoPay mandate | Recurring subscriptions | E-mandate Directions 2026 (RBI/DPSS/2026-27/396, 21 Apr 2026): AFA at registration; recurring debits without AFA up to **₹15,000 per transaction** (para 8(a)); higher amounts need AFA per debit; issuer pre-debit notice **at least 24 hours** before, with merchant, amount, date and time, reference and reason (6(a)–(b)); validity period mandatory (4(b)); opt-out with AFA (6(c)); no charge to the customer for the mandate (10(a)) |
| eNACH | Recurring invoices above ₹15,000 | NPCI eNACH rules (outside the 2026 card and UPI e-mandate Directions); maximum amount and validity set at registration |
| Bank transfer to a virtual account (Smart Collect) | Large B2B invoices | Auto-reconciliation by virtual-account number and amount |

- Finbyx shows a **courtesy notice at T-48 hours** before each recurring debit (CM2 and billing contacts) in addition to the issuer's notice [REC].
- Mandate maximum amount covers the plan's highest expected invoice including GST with stated headroom; any increase needs re-registration with AFA.
- Razorpay's RBI payment-aggregator authorisation and its PCI DSS Attestation of Compliance are obtained and filed annually in the vendor register; Razorpay's self-reported status is not relied on alone and is never presented as Infrabyx's own compliance [VERIFY: current PA authorisation reference].

### CM4.3 Verification and webhook security (implemented in the Hub; Finbyx consumes results)

```
on webhook:
  raw = request body bytes (before any parsing)
  expected = HMAC_SHA256(webhook_secret, raw)              // header X-Razorpay-Signature
  if not constant_time_equal(expected, header): reject 400, log, alert on repeats
  if seen(x-razorpay-event-id): return 200 (duplicate)
  upsert by entity id and status rank (events may arrive out of order)
on checkout return:
  verify payment signature over order_id and payment_id with key_secret (Razorpay documented scheme)
  fetch payment from Razorpay API; trust only the server-side status
daily: settlement reconciliation of payments, refunds and fees against the bank statement
secret rotation: new secret active; old secret accepted only for retries during the overlap window
```

Finbyx receives `SubscriptionPaymentReceived` and `SubscriptionPaymentFailed` from the Hub (signed per Integration Spec Part 3.6) and never treats a browser redirect as proof of payment.

### CM4.4 GST invoices and tax

- Invoices are issued by the Hub (CM2 shows them; OH8.6): both GSTINs, place of supply (B2B: recipient's location, IGST Act s.12(2)(a)), SAC as a tax-review field per SKU (candidates 998315 or 997331 for SaaS) [VERIFY code], 18% IGST or CGST plus SGST, e-invoice IRN and signed QR once the selling entity's aggregate turnover in any year from 2017-18 exceeds ₹5 crore (Notification 10/2023-Central Tax), credit notes for proration and refunds (CGST Act s.34).
- Supplies to IFSC or SEZ units are zero-rated under LUT (IGST Act s.16) [VERIFY for IFSC tenants]; the billing profile captures the unit's status and LUT reference.
- **TDS by tenants:** tenants deduct TDS on Infrabyx's fees under ITA25 s.393(1) (the successor of 1961 Act s.194J) [VERIFY: table serial, rate and threshold]; they upload the TDS certificate (Form 131) in CM2 and the Hub reconciles it to the receivable.

### CM4.5 Dunning with regulatory continuity

`ACTIVE → PAST_DUE (D0) → RETRY (D+1, D+3, D+7) → GRACE (to D+14) → RESTRICTED (D+30, after 7 days' written notice) → TERMINATION_NOTICE (D+45 or per contract) → EXIT (Part 7J DP5)`; any state returns to `ACTIVE` on full payment or an approved payment plan (OH8.7).

- **GRACE:** reminders to billing contacts and the CFO; no functional change.
- **RESTRICTED:** blocks only new non-regulated units (new users, module attachments, product configuration changes) and, if the contract says so, new lead and application intake; everything in CM1.4 continues. A banner names the stage, the amount and the hosted payment link; it never appears to borrowers.
- **TERMINATION_NOTICE** is signed by an Infrabyx authorised signatory under the contract and starts DP5; read and export remain available for RE tenants throughout and during the exit window (OUT para 87) [REC].
- At most 3 automatic retries per invoice, each respecting mandate rules (no retry without a fresh pre-debit notice where the issuer requires one); an invoice under dispute (OH6) pauses dunning for that invoice.

### Acceptance tests

- The billing page's HTML contains no third-party script; a CSP report test fails on any injected script source.
- A forged webhook with a wrong signature is rejected; a replayed valid webhook with the same event id is acknowledged once and changes nothing.
- A browser return with a "success" query string but no server-side confirmation leaves the invoice unpaid.
- A recurring card debit of ₹18,000 is not set up as a no-AFA mandate; the flow proposes eNACH or bank transfer.
- A tenant at RESTRICTED still disburses an already sanctioned loan, runs COB and files its CIC file; creating a new user is blocked; full payment returns it to ACTIVE and unblocks user creation without a deploy.
- A log line containing a 16-digit card-like number fails the CI log scanner.

## CM5. Revenue streams for Finbyx (switchable)

### CM5.1 Catalogue of streams

Each stream is switchable in the Hub catalogue by product, market, tenant, contract, channel and date (OH8), with version history and approval; Finbyx reads `revenue_stream_flags` to show or hide purchase options and to apply entitlement behaviour.

Stream codes follow OH8.2 (`PERPETUAL_LICENCE_AMC`, `SUBSCRIPTION`, `MONTHLY_RENTAL`, `PAYG`, `IMPLEMENTATION`, `PROFESSIONAL_SERVICES` with `MANAGED_SERVICES`, `DATA_MIGRATION`, `TRAINING` and `ONE_TIME_SERVICE`, `PASS_THROUGH`, `MARKETPLACE_REFERRAL`).

| Stream | Basis | Finbyx behaviour | Guard-rails |
|---|---|---|---|
| One-time licence | Perpetual licence for a dedicated or on-premises deployment, plus annual maintenance (AMC) | Offline licence file (CM1.5); updates while AMC is active | Source-code escrow for critical deployments (CYB para 105) |
| Subscription | Annual or monthly SaaS, tiered by entity size, AUM band, modules and seats | Live entitlements | Export and exit export always included |
| Monthly rental | Month-to-month term for a dedicated environment or licence pool without annual commitment | Entitlement end date rolls monthly | Notice period in contract; DP5 on end |
| Pay-as-you-go | Metered per active loan, per regulatory run, per API call, per report, prepaid wallet or postpaid | CM3 meters; wallet balance shown; low-balance alerts | Regulatory functions never stop on zero balance (CM1.4) |
| Implementation | Milestones: discovery, configuration, migration, integrations, training, go-live | Milestones tracked in the Hub (OH4); `ImplementationMilestoneReached` | Acceptance by the tenant before invoicing |
| Professional services | Data migration, custom integrations, regulatory-change packs, training, managed operations | Time and materials or fixed | No core management functions for tenants (OUT para 15); no outsourced internal audit for IAF in-scope NBFCs (IAF para 39); no Reg 24A prohibited services for listed tenants (GV4.2) |
| Pass-through with margin | eSign, eStamp, KYC, SMS, WhatsApp, voice (never credit-bureau charges: Infrabyx never buys or resells credit information; the tenant contracts each CIC directly, CICRA) | CM3 pass-through meters | Cost and margin disclosed on the invoice |
| Marketplace referral | Fees from third-party vendors whose certified connectors a tenant activates | Shown on the vendor's marketplace card | Disclosed to the tenant; never conditional on borrower outcomes; no ranking for payment |
| Vendor announcements (no fee) | Opt-in "What's new" panel for Infrabyx release news and newly certified connectors | Off by default; tenant switches it on or off | Not a paid placement (CM5.2); never inside lending workflows or borrower-facing surfaces (portal, notices, statements); no targeting on tenant data; labelled |

### CM5.2 Prohibited or avoided revenue

- Any fee charged to or collected from the tenant's borrowers by Infrabyx; any fee linked to loan pricing, interest income or borrower charges [REC; CF para 10(4) spirit for the ecosystem].
- Success fees per recovered rupee, per notice or per connected collection call (conduct incentive; RBC para 100) [REC].
- Selling, sharing or monetising tenant data, credit information or bureau data (CICRA; CIR) or using it for group marketing (confidentiality of customer data: OUT paras 34(v), 47(i); customer disclosure of the actual provider: para 46).
- Third-party advertising in the core lender UI or in any borrower-facing surface.
- Sponsored placement or paid ranking of connectors, lenders or professionals (the advocate directory follows BCI Rule 36: no paid placement; OH9).

### CM5.3 Legality gate per stream

Before a stream is switched on for a market or tenant class, the Hub takes it through the OH8.3 gate (`DRAFT → LEGAL_REVIEW → TAX_REVIEW → OWNER_DECISION → APPROVED → ACTIVE`) and records: legal review reference, tax treatment (GST and TDS), revenue-recognition treatment (AS 9 or Ind AS 115, per the selling entity's framework, an owner decision under OH8.8), entitlement behaviour in Finbyx, refund and cancellation rules, disclosure text, and the approver. Finbyx mirrors gate status and refuses to display a purchase option, or to apply an entitlement, whose stream is not `ACTIVE`; a mismatch raises `ComplianceIssueRaised`.

### CM5.4 Self-serve funnel (legitimate automation only)

- **Sandbox trial:** self-serve sign-up creates a sandbox tenant with synthetic data only (`TenantProvisioned`, environment sandbox); no real borrower data can be uploaded (upload validators reject PAN- or Aadhaar-like data in sandbox).
- **Activation:** guided checklist, in-product tours, factual usage nudges, recorded webinars with disclosures, automated nurture through the Hub CRM with consent.
- **Production gate:** a production tenant is provisioned only after the signed MSA and DPA with the OUT clause matrix (Part 10.6), customer due diligence (CIN, GSTIN, RBI certificate of registration or other licence verified), and the tenant's own outsourcing assessment where it applies; self-serve never ends in a production RE tenant without these.
- No fake urgency, scarcity timers, anchor prices or unverifiable testimonials (CCPA Dark Patterns Guidelines 2023; ASCI); the owner's reference page (ptstdm.co.in, reviewed 23 Oct 2026) is a coaching-workshop funnel, not a software model to copy (Part 8A.37.1 row 6). Trials never convert to paid automatically.

### Acceptance tests

- Switching off the "monthly rental" stream for a market hides that option on every Finbyx billing page for tenants in that market without a deploy.
- A purchase option whose stream is not `ACTIVE` in the legality gate is not displayed and the Hub import report lists it.
- The vendor-announcements panel never renders inside origination, servicing, collections or recovery screens, nor in the borrower portal, and disappears when the tenant switches it off.
- A sandbox upload containing a valid-format PAN is rejected.
- A production-tenant provisioning request without a signed MSA and DPA reference is refused by the provisioning API.

# PART 7L — ENGINEERING OPERATIONS, ASSURANCE READINESS AND CERTIFICATIONS

**Purpose.** Make the way Finbyx is built, changed, patched, backed up, tested and assured produce evidence automatically, so that tenants, their auditors, RBI and certification bodies can rely on it; and connect Finbyx to voice, AI contact-centre and Jio services through provider-neutral adapters that obey telecom, conduct and AI rules. EO1–EO5 apply to the Finbyx repository and its environments; the Operations Hub engineering console (OH13) and control library (OH14) aggregate the evidence across products. EO1 controls start in Phase 1, not at the end of the roadmap.

**Applicability.** All Finbyx code, environments and releases. The strictest tenant obligation sets the platform standard, because one multi-tenant release serves every tenant: CYB Chapter V (paras 102–147) for ML, UL and TL tenants; Chapter IV (paras 15–64) for BL ≥ ₹500 crore; Chapter III (para 8) for BL < ₹500 crore and CICs; OUT for in-scope NBFCs; DPS for card-issuing tenants; CERT-In Directions (28 Apr 2022) for Infrabyx as a body corporate. EO6 applies to every tenant that switches on voice, messaging or AI contact-centre features.

**Requirement codes.** CYB, OUT, DPS, CF, RBC, M20 FREE-AI guidance, `PCI`, `SOC2`, `ISO`, `TRAI`, `DPDP`, `CERTIN` (codes in Part 8A.37). REQ-ID examples: `REQ-CYB-121`, `REQ-CYB-105`, `REQ-OUT-61`, `REQ-TRAI-1600-2025`, `REQ-RBC-100`, `REQ-ISO27001-A.8.32`, `REQ-SOC2-CC8.1`, `REQ-PCI-SAQA`.

**Data owned.** Infrabyx owns engineering records (code, changes, releases, vulnerability and VAPT records, backup and drill logs, control evidence). Tenants own their configuration and data; evidence that names a tenant is shared only with that tenant. Voice and messaging records (contact attempts, recordings, transcripts) are tenant data (M18, R15).

**Extends, does not rebuild.** Part 10.3 (RPO, RTO, DR drills), 10.4 (security controls), 10.6 (vendor obligations: escrow, CYB 106 certificate, VAPT, incidents, certifications), 11.3 (Git rules: pull requests only, no direct push to `main`), 11.5–11.6 (definition of done, quality gates), R15.1–R15.3 (contact-policy engine, call recording, AI and voicebots), M18 (channels, DLT, consent), M20 (AI governance).

**Canonical events** (Integration Spec Parts 6.23, 6.26, 6.29). Produced by Finbyx: `ReleasePublished`, `ControlEvidenceCollected`, `BackupCompleted` (type PLATFORM for platform backups), `RestoreTested` and `AccessReviewCompleted`, consumed by OH13 and OH14 and, where the evidence names a tenant, by that tenant's compliance destination. `AccessReviewCompleted` is routed by `review_scope`: PLATFORM (Infrabyx staff access to Finbyx production) to OH13 and OH14; TENANT (the tenant's own reviews, GV5.1) only to the tenant's compliance destination. Consumed by Finbyx: `ChangeApproved` from the OH13 CAB record, which the deployment gate requires (EO2.2).

## EO1. Repository, branching and release controls (GitHub)

### EO1.1 Plan and repository model

- **GitHub Team plan, private repositories** (owner decision recorded; upgrade to Enterprise Cloud is a decision gate, see EO1.5). Repositories: `finbyx` (monorepo, Part 10.1), `finbyx-infra` (IaC), `finbyx-escrow` (mirror for the escrow agent, CYB para 105). Organisation-wide: SSO-linked accounts, 2FA required, base permission "none", teams per domain, no personal access tokens with organisation access except fine-grained ones with expiry.
- **Branching:** trunk-based; short-lived `feat/`, `fix/`, `chore/` branches; `hotfix/` from the release tag; `release/x.y` only for release lines still supported for dedicated deployments; no long-lived `develop`. Tags `vX.Y.Z` are signed.

### EO1.2 Rulesets

Rulesets (available for private repositories on Team) [VEND]:

| Target | Rules |
|---|---|
| `main` | Restrict deletions; block force pushes; require linear history; require signed commits; pull request required with ≥ 1 approval; dismiss stale approvals on new commits; approval of the most recent push by someone other than the pusher; code-owner review required; conversation resolution required; required status checks (below); `staging` deployment must succeed before merge; bypass list empty (emergency changes use EO2.4, not a bypass) |
| `release/*` | As `main`, plus only `hotfix/` merges; 2 approvals |
| Tags `v*` | Restrict creation to the release workflow identity; restrict update and deletion |

**Required status checks:** lint and typecheck; unit and property-based tests; integration (Testcontainers); contract tests (Pact) and Integration Spec schema compatibility; migration dry-run with expand-and-contract lint (Part 11.6); golden-case suite (Part 11.2); tenant-isolation and IDOR tests (Part 10.4); dependency and licence scan; CodeQL; secret scan; SBOM generation; PII-in-logs and card-pattern scanner; Office and PDF/A rendering check (Part 7J DP1.4); workflow lint for GitHub Actions (for example zizmor).

**Two approvals for sensitive paths.** Rulesets set one approval count per branch, so a required check (`sensitive-path-approvals`) counts distinct approving code owners when a pull request touches the paths below and fails below two [REC].

### EO1.3 CODEOWNERS

```
/packages/domain-kernel/      @infrabyx/ledger-owners
/modules/ledger/ /modules/accounting/ /modules/schedule/   @infrabyx/ledger-owners
/migrations/                  @infrabyx/db-owners @infrabyx/ledger-owners
/modules/iam/ /modules/auth/  @infrabyx/security-owners
/modules/billing/ /modules/payments/   @infrabyx/payments-owners @infrabyx/security-owners
/rule-packs/ /packages/recovery-rules/ /modules/returns/ /modules/bureau/   @infrabyx/regulatory-owners
/modules/audit-trail/         @infrabyx/security-owners @infrabyx/regulatory-owners
/infra/ /.github/             @infrabyx/platform-owners @infrabyx/security-owners
/docs/regulations/ /docs/compliance/   @infrabyx/regulatory-owners
```

A CI check fails if any file under `/modules/` or `/packages/` has no owner. Team names are placeholders for the Phase 1 setup.

### EO1.4 Commits, workflows and environments

- **Signed commits:** SSH or GPG signing keys registered per engineer; vigilant mode for maintainers; bot commits signed by GitHub.
- **Actions hardening:** third-party actions pinned to full commit SHA (Dependabot updates them); default `permissions: contents: read`; no `pull_request_target` that checks out pull-request code; no secrets to forked pull requests; GitHub OIDC to AWS with the trust policy pinned to repository, branch or tag and environment; no long-lived cloud keys in GitHub; self-hosted runners only ephemeral, in the Infrabyx AWS India account, never shared with untrusted repositories.
- **Environments:**

| Environment | Data | Deploys from | Protection |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dev` | Synthetic | Any branch | None beyond CI |
| `staging` | Synthetic | `main` | Automatic after merge |
| `uat-[tenant]` | Synthetic, or irreversibly anonymised with tenant and DPO approval | Signed tags | 1 reviewer |
| `prod-in` | Real (India regions only, Part 10.1) | Signed release tags only | 2 required reviewers (not the author), wait timer 15 minutes, environment-scoped secrets, deployment window |
| `dr-in` | Replica | Same tag as `prod-in` | As `prod-in`; drift check (CYB para 137) |

- Production data never flows to `dev`, `staging` or `uat` (Part 11.3); anonymisation, where approved, is irreversible and tested.

### EO1.5 Security features and supply chain

- **Dependabot** version and security updates (grouped weekly; security updates immediately); **CodeQL** code scanning; **secret scanning with push protection**. On the Team plan these need the GitHub Secret Protection and Code Security products for private repositories [VERIFY current packaging and price]; if not purchased, equivalent open-source tools run as required checks (Semgrep, gitleaks or trufflehog, osv-scanner).
- **SBOM:** SPDX from the GitHub dependency graph and CycloneDX from the build (application and container image), attached to every release and supplied to tenants (Part 10.6 item 9).
- **Signing and provenance:** GitHub artifact attestations for private repositories need Enterprise Cloud [VEND]. On Team, container images and release bundles are signed with cosign using a KMS-held key (not keyless signing to the public transparency log, which would publish private repository metadata) [REC]; the deploy pipeline verifies signatures and refuses unsigned images.
- **Decision gate:** move to Enterprise Cloud before the SOC 2 Type 2 window if attestations, audit-log streaming or enterprise rulesets are needed for evidence (Appendix B).

### EO1.6 Releases and patch SLAs

- **Release train [REC]:** weekly production release window outside business-critical windows, plus a hotfix lane; semantic versioning; release notes with a "regulatory impact" section (rule packs, formats, calculations changed) published to tenants 5 working days before a normal release; breaking API changes follow the Integration Spec deprecation rules (Part 14).
- **Freeze windows:** last 2 and first 3 working days of each month (close and returns); quarter-end and FY-end close periods; for the bureau module, the CIC submission days (9th, 16th, 23rd and month-end file by the 5th); Board-approved exceptions only through EO2.4.
- **Patch SLAs [REC]** from triage: CVSS ≥ 9.0, listed in CISA KEV or actively exploited: 72 hours; High: 7 days; Medium: 30 days; Low: 90 days. These are the platform SLAs for product code and infrastructure; Udofin and every group repository apply them through OH13, and where a tenant contract or audit-finding policy is stricter, the stricter value wins. Vulnerabilities in a tenant's own systems tracked in Part 7D use the AU4.3 tenant-policy defaults (15, 30, 90 and 180 days); a finding about the Finbyx platform, whoever raises it (including a tenant-commissioned VAPT or a `provider_vapt` item), follows the platform SLAs above. Time-bound fixes and no recurrence of known CVEs (CYB paras 125–126); exceptions only with a CISO risk acceptance that expires within 90 days.
- **`ReleasePublished`** after each production deployment: version, change ids, SBOM hash, signature digest, release-notes link.

### Acceptance tests

- A direct push to `main`, a force push or an unsigned commit is rejected by the ruleset (verified by a nightly ruleset-drift job that exports the ruleset JSON as evidence).
- A pull request touching `/migrations/` with one code-owner approval fails `sensitive-path-approvals`; a second distinct owner's approval passes it.
- A workflow file referencing an action by tag instead of SHA fails the workflow lint.
- A deployment to `prod-in` from an untagged commit is refused; an unsigned image is refused at deploy.
- A seeded critical CVE opens a ticket with a 72-hour due time; closing it without a regression test linked fails the check.

## EO2. Change, patch and vulnerability management

### EO2.1 Change classes

| Class | Examples | Approval |
|---|---|---|
| Standard (pre-approved catalogue) | Dependency patch with all checks green; copy changes; documentation; feature-flag toggles within tested configurations | Pull-request review only; logged |
| Normal | New features, refactors, infrastructure changes | Change Advisory Board (CAB) |
| Regulated | Rule packs, interest, fee, schedule and allocation logic, IRACP and ECL, return and CIC formats, KFS, contact policy, audit trail, security controls, data residency | CAB plus a compliance reviewer; golden-case suite pass; regulatory-register reference (Part 11.6) |
| Emergency | Production incident fix, actively exploited vulnerability | EO2.4 |

Tenant configuration changes made by tenant admins follow M19 maker-checker, not the CAB.

### EO2.2 Change record and CAB

- **Record:** id, title, class, risk score (impact × likelihood, tenants affected, data migration, reversibility), linked pull requests and commits, migration plan (expand, migrate, contract), rollback or forward-fix plan, test evidence, tenant communication plan, deployment window, approvers, post-implementation review result.
- **CAB:** weekly; engineering lead, CISO or delegate, product owner, QA lead, SRE, compliance reviewer for regulated changes, customer success for tenant impact; quorum 4 including security. The CAB sits in OH13 (states `DRAFT → SUBMITTED → ASSESSED → CAB_REVIEW → APPROVED | REJECTED | DEFERRED → SCHEDULED → IMPLEMENTED → PIR_DONE → CLOSED`; failed changes `ROLLED_BACK` or `FORWARD_FIXED`); OH13 emits `ChangeApproved` with change id, class, approvers and window, and the Finbyx `prod-in` deployment gate refuses a release whose change ids lack a matching `ChangeApproved` (standard changes carry a catalogue approval).
- **Basis:** change and patch policy (CYB para 112), change management (Ch IV paras 41–42), secure SDLC (para 39).

### EO2.3 Vulnerability management

- **Intake:** Dependabot, CodeQL, container and IaC scans, VAPT (EO4), CERT-In and vendor advisories, a vulnerability disclosure policy with `security.txt` (RFC 9116) and safe-harbour terms.
- **Triage within 24 hours for critical:** CVSS base score, EPSS and KEV status, reachability in Finbyx, exposure (internet-facing or internal), data at risk; SLA from EO1.6.
- **Closure:** fix, regression test, verification scan; recurrence check across release lines; exceptions with CISO acceptance and expiry.
- **End-of-support register** for languages, frameworks, databases and OS images with refresh plans (CYB paras 92–93).
- **CYB para 106 certificate:** per material change (materiality agreed in the tenant contract: authentication, cryptography, data flows, new external interfaces, major versions), a CISO-signed certificate that the release is free of known vulnerabilities, malware and covert channels, backed by SAST, SCA, malware scan and VAPT evidence; distributed to tenants with the release.
- **Escrow (CYB para 105):** every production release deposited with the escrow agent; verified build by the agent at least yearly [REC].

### EO2.4 Emergency change

- Trigger: Sev-1 incident or actively exploited vulnerability.
- Approval by two of CTO, CISO and on-call engineering lead, recorded in the GitHub environment approval and the change record; the deployment still uses a signed tag and the full required checks, except tests explicitly waived with reason.
- Retrospective CAB within 2 working days; incident link; tenant notice where tenant-impacting within the Part 10.6 item 6 target (≤ 2 hours from Finbyx detection, so tenants can meet their 6-hour RBI clock; OUT para 61; CYB para 141); CERT-In report within 6 hours where the incident is reportable.

### Acceptance tests

- A change touching `/rule-packs/` without a compliance reviewer cannot be marked approved; the golden-case suite failing blocks deployment.
- An emergency change approved by only one approver cannot deploy; an approved emergency change without a retrospective CAB record after 2 working days raises an exception in OH14.
- A material release cannot be published to `prod-in` without a CYB 106 certificate and an escrow-deposit receipt attached.
- A `security.txt` file is served at `/.well-known/security.txt` with a valid expiry.
- A `prod-in` deployment whose change id has no `ChangeApproved` from OH13 (and no standard-change catalogue entry) is refused.

## EO3. Backups, restore and resilience evidence

### EO3.1 Platform backup design

| Asset | Backup | Retention [REC] | Copy |
|---|---|---|---|
| PostgreSQL (ledger and all tenant data) | Continuous WAL archiving with point-in-time recovery; daily snapshots | PITR 35 days; daily 35 days; monthly 13 months; FY-end 8 years for books (s.128(5); AC7) | Cross-region to ap-south-2; immutable copy in a separate backup account |
| Object storage (documents, archives) | Versioning, Object Lock, cross-region replication | Per retention class | ap-south-2 |
| Workflow engine (Temporal) | Database backup (self-hosted) or provider backups in an India region | 35 days | ap-south-2 |
| Search indexes | Rebuildable from the database | — | — |
| Keys | KMS multi-Region keys limited to India regions; HSM backups for vault and signing keys | Life of data | ap-south-2 |
| Infrastructure state, images, configuration | IaC state with versioning; image registry replication | 13 months | ap-south-2 |
| Audit trail and logs | Append-only stores; logs ≥ 180 days in India (CERT-In) and ≥ 1 year (DPDP Rules r.8(3)); tenant-configurable longer | As stated | ap-south-2 |

- **Immutable vault:** a separate AWS account with organisation policies denying deletion, vault lock in compliance mode, and access only through break-glass; protects against compromise of the production account (ransomware scenario).
- **Books of account:** daily backup on servers in India verified daily (Companies (Accounts) Rules r.3(5); AC7).
- **Time:** NTP synchronised to NIC or NPL sources with drift alarms (CERT-In).

### EO3.2 Restore and drill programme

| Exercise | Frequency | Pass criteria | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|
| Automated backup verification | Daily | Backup completes; checksum and restore-to-scratch of a sample table succeed | CYB para 133 |
| Full restore test | Quarterly | Restore of a production snapshot into an isolated, production-classified recovery environment in India (destroyed after the test; access logged); trial balance, loan counts and audit hash chain equal the source; document hash sample matches | Part 10.3; CYB para 133 |
| DR drill | Half-yearly | Production runs on DR for one full working day, BOD to EOD including COB; RTO and RPO measured; failures re-tested | CYB paras 129–131, 138 |
| Ransomware recovery test | Yearly | Recovery from the immutable vault assuming the production account is lost | [REC] |
| Joint tests with tenants | On request and at least yearly for Chapter V tenants | Tenant RTO met | CYB para 138; OUT para 83 |
| Customer-held backup rehydration | Per Part 7J DP4.3 | As DP4.3 | DP4 |

- **Evidence:** `BackupCompleted` and `RestoreTested` events and a drill report (scope, timeline, RTO and RPO achieved, data reconciliation, issues, actions) per exercise, stored as control evidence (`ControlEvidenceCollected`) and issued to tenants in their evidence pack.

### Acceptance tests

- A quarterly restore reproduces the source trial balance and audit hash chain exactly; a seeded corrupted WAL segment fails the test and opens a Sev-2 problem record.
- An attempt to delete a vault recovery point from the production account is denied by policy (logged as evidence).
- The DR drill report records measured RTO and RPO and is attached to each Chapter V tenant's evidence pack.
- Clock drift above the configured threshold raises an alert.

## EO4. VAPT and audit readiness (IS, internal, external)

### EO4.1 VAPT programme

- **Testers:** independent, CERT-In-empanelled firm (the market norm tenants expect), not involved in building the system (CYB para 122); firm rotated at least every 3 years [REC]; rules of engagement and scope letter signed; tests on production or documented deviations (CYB para 124).
- **Cadence and scope by layer:**

| Layer | Vulnerability assessment | Penetration test | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Internet-facing web app, APIs, borrower portal, partner and Udofin endpoints, webhooks | Continuous automated plus independent every 6 months | Every 12 months, before go-live and after major change | CYB para 121 sets the floor for Chapter V tenants; the platform applies it to all |
| Field app (mobile) | Each major release | Every 12 months (OWASP MASVS) | — |
| Cloud configuration and network | Continuous posture scanning (CIS benchmarks) | Every 12 months | DC and DR both |
| Source code | SAST on every pull request | Manual secure code review every 12 months of high-risk modules (auth, ledger, payments, exports) | DPS paras 29–35 where in scope |
| On-premises agent and storage connectors | Each release | Every 12 months | Part 7C AC6.1; Part 7F GV7.5; Part 7J DP3 |
| People | Phishing simulation for Infrabyx staff | Yearly | [REC] |

- **Findings:** tracked with the EO1.6 SLAs; retest by the same firm; closure evidence; trend reporting to the Infrabyx board and to tenants. Tenants receive an executive summary each cycle and the full report under NDA on request; pooled audits are supported (OUT para 77).

### EO4.2 Audit readiness

- **Tenant IS audit** (CYB para 56; Part 7D AU4): a standing evidence pack (policies, architecture, data flows, access reviews, change and patch records, VAPT reports, DR drill reports, SOC or ISO reports, sub-processor list, SBOM, escrow receipt, CYB 106 certificates) delivered through the AU7 auditor workspace.
- **Tenant statutory audit:** because Finbyx holds tenants' books of account, tenants' statutory auditors may need a service-organisation report on controls relevant to financial reporting (SA 402). Offer a **SOC 1 Type 2 (SAE 3402 or ISAE 3402) report** in addition to SOC 2 [REC], plus the Rule 11(g) audit-trail evidence pack from AC7.
- **Infrabyx internal audit:** quarterly control testing of the common control framework by a function independent of engineering (an outsourced internal-audit firm is allowed for Infrabyx, which is not an RBI-regulated entity); findings tracked in OH14.
- **External assurance:** SOC 2 auditor and ISO certification body (EO5); RBI and tenant access to Infrabyx premises, data, logs and subcontractors on request (OUT paras 34(ii), 74(ii), 81).
- **Incidents:** CERT-In report within 6 hours; tenant notice target ≤ 2 hours from Finbyx detection (Part 10.6 item 6); forensics and RCA support (CYB para 140); every clock recorded as evidence.

### Acceptance tests

- A VAPT critical finding is tracked to closure within 72 hours with a retest record; an unretested closure fails the evidence check.
- Every Chapter V tenant's evidence pack contains the latest VA (≤ 6 months old) and PT (≤ 12 months old) summaries; a stale report raises an exception 30 days before expiry.
- The IS-audit evidence pack can be generated for a tenant in one action and contains only that tenant's tenant-specific evidence plus platform-level evidence.
- An incident drill records detection time, tenant notice time and CERT-In report time, and flags any clock missed.

## EO5. Certification readiness: PCI DSS, SOC 2 Type 1 and Type 2, ISO standards

### EO5.1 Programme rules

- Certification is a **programme**, not a claim. Until a report or certificate is issued, Infrabyx says "aligned to" or "in progress"; once issued, it states scheme, scope, report period or certificate number, issuing body and date. The claims gate in the Operations Hub (OH7, OH14.6) blocks any marketing, sales or product text that claims otherwise (CM2.3 check).
- Tenants may rely on recognised certifications instead of their own audit, subject to their risk assessment, if scope covers the OUT para 97(xvii) heads (OUT para 79; Part 10.6 items 12 and 30).
- Policies are drafted later as a separate workstream; this Part fixes the control framework and evidence they will reference.

### EO5.2 Schemes

| Scheme | Scope and approach | Status target [REC] |
|---|---|---|
| PCI DSS v4.0.1, SAQ A | Infrabyx as merchant for its own fees: hosted or redirect payment pages only (CM4); Finbyx outside the cardholder-data environment. SAQ A (revised 31 Jan 2025) removed requirements 6.4.3, 11.6.1 and 12.3.1 but requires confirming the site is not susceptible to script attacks; keep a script inventory, CSP and change detection on billing and borrower-portal pages anyway. Tenant borrower payments use the tenant's own gateway; if a tenant embeds a payment iframe in the borrower portal, the same script controls apply. Card-issuing tenants: PCI confirmations where in scope (DPS para 69) | SAQ A self-assessment yearly, from the first paid invoice |
| SOC 2 Type 1, then Type 2 | AICPA 2017 Trust Services Criteria with 2022 points of focus: Security (CC1–CC9) plus Availability, Confidentiality and Processing Integrity (lending calculations); Privacy optional. Licensed CPA firm. Type 1 tests design at a point in time; Type 2 tests operating effectiveness over a window of 3–12 months [VERIFY]. Subservice organisations (cloud, payment aggregator, messaging) by carve-out with complementary user-entity controls | Type 1 around month 9; first Type 2 window 6 months |
| SOC 1 Type 2 | Controls relevant to tenants' financial reporting (EO4.2) | After SOC 2 Type 1 |
| ISO/IEC 27001:2022 (with Amendment 1:2024) | ISMS; Statement of Applicability over the 93 Annex A controls; accredited certification body; Stage 1 and Stage 2, annual surveillance, 3-year cycle [VERIFY amendment details] | Certificate around months 9–12 |
| ISO/IEC 27701:2025 | Stand-alone privacy information management system (published 14 Oct 2025); maps to DPDP | After 27001 |
| ISO 22301:2019 | Business continuity management; CYB para 127 best practice | Year 2 |
| ISO/IEC 42001:2023 | AI management system; only if AI features (M20, EO6) become material to the service | Decision gate |
| ISO/IEC 27017 and 27018 | Cloud security controls and protection of PII in public clouds, as extensions assessed with 27001 [VERIFY current editions and how certification bodies issue them] | With 27001 surveillance |

### EO5.3 Common control framework (CCF) and evidence automation

- **Master library in OH14**; Finbyx implements technical controls and evidence collectors in its repository and publishes evidence to OH14.
- **Control record:** id, objective, owner, frequency, test procedure, automation hook, systems in scope, mappings (many-to-many) to: CYB (Ch III, IV, V), OUT (paras 34, 47, 61, 74, 76–82, 87–88, 97), CF (paras 14–16), DPS (where in scope), CERT-In Directions, DPDP, ISO/IEC 27001 Annex A, 27701, 22301, SOC 2 TSC, PCI SAQ A, Companies Act internal financial controls (s.134(5)(e), s.143(3)(i)) and the ICAI Rule 11(g) audit-trail guide.
- **Evidence record:** control, period, collector, artefact hash, reviewer, status; `ControlEvidenceCollected` per item.
- **Automated collectors (Finbyx side):** nightly ruleset and branch-protection export with drift detection; CODEOWNERS coverage; CI results per release; SBOM and signature digests; vulnerability SLA metrics; MFA coverage and sign-in reports from the IdP; quarterly reviews of Infrabyx staff access to production (`AccessReviewCompleted`, `review_scope = PLATFORM`; Part 10.4); privileged-session logs; change records and CAB minutes; backup, restore and DR reports (`BackupCompleted`, `RestoreTested`); VAPT reports and retests; incident timelines and clocks; KMS key policies and rotation; tenant-isolation test results; audit-trail hash-chain verification; log-retention checks; joiner, mover and leaver tickets; training records; sub-processor due diligence.
- **Readiness dashboard** (OH14, with a Finbyx view): control status, evidence freshness, exceptions, upcoming audits.
- **Policies to draft later:** information security, access control, cryptography and key management, secure SDLC, change and patch, vulnerability management, logging and monitoring, incident response, BCP and DR, backup, data retention and disposal, privacy, vendor management, acceptable use, AI use, remote work.

### EO5.4 Roadmap [REC; owner decides order, certification body and CPA firm]

| Months | Milestone |
|---|---|
| 0–2 | Scope (Finbyx production in India regions, supporting engineering, support and operations processes, people and offices), risk assessment, gap assessment, CCF baseline |
| 2–6 | Controls implemented, collectors live, policies approved, training |
| 6 | Internal audit and management review |
| 7–9 | ISO/IEC 27001 Stage 1 and Stage 2; SOC 2 Type 1 |
| 9–15 | SOC 2 Type 2 observation window (6 months); SOC 1 readiness |
| 16+ | SOC 2 Type 2 report; 27701; 22301; 42001 decision |

### Acceptance tests

- Product or website text containing "SOC 2 certified" or "ISO 27001 certified" without an issued-report or certificate record fails the claims gate.
- Every control in the CCF maps to at least one requirement and has an owner and a collector or a documented manual procedure.
- The billing and borrower-portal pages pass a CSP and script-inventory check; adding an unlisted script fails CI.
- Evidence older than its control frequency is flagged stale on the readiness dashboard.

## EO6. Voice, AI contact-centre and Jio adapters

**Scope.** Extends M18 (channels, DLT, consent), R15.1 (contact-policy engine), R15.2 (call recording) and R15.3 (AI and voicebots); M18 gains a pointer to this section. The tenant is the principal entity and decision-maker for every communication; Finbyx is the processor and orchestrator.

### EO6.1 Provider-neutral interfaces

| Interface | Capabilities |
|---|---|
| `MessagingProvider` | SMS with DLT header and template ids, RCS, WhatsApp Business (never for collection, recovery or legal notices; Part 7A.0.6), email; delivery receipts |
| `VoiceProvider` | Number pools by series and telecom circle; inbound IVR; outbound dialler and OBD; click-to-call with number masking; recording; call-detail-record webhooks |
| `SpeechProvider` | Indic ASR and TTS; language detection |
| `LLMProvider` | The M20 India-region inference endpoint only |

Each adapter implements the connector SPI and passes connector certification (Integration Spec Parts 10.1, 14.3) before production. Candidate implementations [VERIFY each provider's DLT, 1600-series and residency position]: **JioCX** (Jio Things Ltd: SMS, RCS, WhatsApp, voice incl. click-to-call, IVR, missed call, voice OTP and OBD, email, Verify branded caller ID), **Jio Business** SIP trunk and toll-free for tenant contact centres, Exotel, Ozonetel, Gupshup, Knowlarity and others; Indic speech (for example Sarvam AI, Bhashini) [VERIFY terms].

### EO6.2 Jio position and plan

- JioCX onboards through sales (no public API documentation, no published rates); it publishes **no data-residency statement and no AI voice-agent product**; the Jio Platforms DRHP (19 Jun 2026) discloses AI-assisted customer-service tools but **no public voice-agent API**; reports of a "JioBrain" LLM API with public pricing are uncorroborated and must not be relied on.
- **Plan:** build a stub `JioCxAdapter` against the interface with certification tests; request from JioCX the API documentation, DPA, India residency proof for recordings, transcripts and call records, DLT principal-entity support, 1600-series support, AI voice roadmap and rates; enable the adapter for production only after contract, residency proof and certification. Until then, other certified adapters serve tenants. The owner's Jio requirement is met by the adapter, not by a dependency on Jio.

### EO6.3 Number series, consent and calling rules

The contact-policy engine (R15.1) evaluates every outbound call or message and fails closed with a reason:

| Check | Rule | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| Purpose | Service, transactional, recovery or promotional, from the template or campaign | TCCCPR categories |
| Principal entity and numbers | The tenant is the DLT principal entity and holder of its numbers; Finbyx never registers headers, templates or numbers in Infrabyx's name for tenant traffic | TCCCPR; RBC para 101 |
| Series for RE voice | Service, transactional and recovery calls only from the tenant's **1600-series** numbers (1601 sub-series for RBI-regulated entities per providers [VERIFY]); mandatory from 1 Jan 2026 for banks, 1 Feb 2026 for NBFCs above ₹5,000 crore, payments banks and SFBs, 1 Mar 2026 for other NBFCs, co-operative banks and RRBs; no other number may be used even with consent; 1600 calls cannot be tagged or blocked | TRAI Direction 19 Nov 2025; TRAI clarification 10 Jul 2026 |
| Series for promotional voice | **140-series** through a registered telemarketer, DND scrub, explicit consent; ordinary 10-digit numbers barred for telemarketing | TCCCPR 2018 as amended 12 Feb 2025 |
| Non-RE tenants | Credit co-operative societies are not REs; their eligibility for 1600 numbers is unconfirmed; route through registered telemarketer series until confirmed [VERIFY] | TRAI |
| Consent | Explicit consent for promotions, default "No" from 1 Jan 2027 (RBC Second Amendment para 101I); promotional messages carry an opt-out; 90 days before re-seeking consent after opt-out; inferred service consent only while the contract lasts | RBC; TCCCPR |
| Time windows (effective-dated rule pack) | Until 31 Dec 2026: recovery calls 08:00–19:00 (RBC para 100; not microfinance), microfinance 09:00–18:00 (RBC para 91(2)). From 1 Jan 2027: the RBC Third Amendment pack (RBI/2026-27/230; para 100Y(4): 08:00–19:00 unless the borrower asks otherwise; avoid bereavement, weddings and festivals) [VERIFY: whether a separate microfinance window survives]. Marketing 09:00–19:00 from 1 Jan 2027 (M18). A stricter recorded borrower preference prevails | RBC |
| Frequency | No persistent calling; default ≤ 3 attempts and 1 connected recovery call a day unless the borrower asks [REC] | RBC para 100 (para 100Y from 1 Jan 2027) |
| Auto-diallers and robo-calls | Notified in advance to the originating access provider with purpose | TCCCPR reg 4 (2025 amendment) |
| Templates | DLT template id required for every SMS; header and template must match category | TCCCPR |

### EO6.4 AI contact centre

- **Inbound service assistant** (IVR, voice or chat): authenticate the caller (registered mobile plus OTP, or IVR PIN) before disclosing anything; answer balance, due date, receipt status and document-release status; create service requests (statement, foreclosure quote, NOC) and complaints in M15; hand over to a human at any time on request.
- **Outbound AI voice:** pre-due reminders and receipt confirmations; recovery calls by an AI voice only if the tenant's Board-approved policy allows it and the CCO approved the script and prompts.
- **AI must never:** negotiate or approve settlements or waivers, change loan terms, close or reject complaints, threaten, misstate dues, disclose to third parties, or collect card data (payments only through links to the tenant's gateway).
- **Disclosure and governance (RBI FREE-AI, 13 Aug 2025; M20):** the assistant states at the start that it is an automated assistant acting for the tenant; the customer can ask for a human; each interaction logs model, model version, prompt version, transcript reference and handover; scripts and prompts are versioned and approved; quality and bias reviews are sampled monthly; the tenant's AI inventory lists the use.
- **Recording consent:** recording and its purpose are announced at the start of every recorded call; a DPDP notice link is sent by DLT-registered SMS [REC]; recordings, transcripts and call records stay in India (CF para 14(4)) with access restricted by role; retention per tenant policy, and for recovery calls 6 months or until disposal while sub judice (RBC para 100P from 1 Jan 2027; Part 7A.0.5).
- **Residency gate:** an adapter whose provider has not proved India storage for recordings, transcripts and call records, and India inference for any AI, cannot be enabled for a production tenant.

### EO6.5 Metering and records

Voice minutes, SMS, WhatsApp and AI minutes are metered through CM3 pass-through meters with cost captured per call. Contact attempts, evaluations, recordings and AI interactions use the existing R15 entities (`contact_attempt`, `contact_evaluation`, `call_recording`, `ai_interaction_log`); no new ecosystem events are needed.

### EO6.6 Provider, number and script lifecycles

- **Provider account:** `PROPOSED → DUE_DILIGENCE (DPA, residency proof, DLT and 1600 support) → CONTRACTED → SANDBOX_CERTIFIED → PRODUCTION_ENABLED → (SUSPENDED → PRODUCTION_ENABLED) → RETIRED`; residency proof older than 12 months or a failed certification re-run suspends production traffic, and the contact-policy engine fails over only to another certified adapter of the tenant, never to an uncertified one.
- **Numbers and headers:** each number carries series, circle, purpose and the tenant's DLT entity id; a number whose series does not fit its purpose cannot be assigned to a campaign or queue.
- **Scripts and prompts:** `DRAFT → LEGAL_REVIEW → CCO_APPROVED → LIVE → RETIRED`, versioned; an AI recovery script cannot reach `LIVE` without a Board-approved policy reference; changing a live prompt creates a new version and needs fresh approval.

### Settings and options (EO6)

| Setting | Level | Default | Nature |
|---|---|---|---|
| Contact windows, frequency caps and consent rules | Platform rule pack, effective-dated | EO6.3 | Floor; tenant may only narrow |
| Series-to-purpose mapping | Platform | 1600 for service, transactional and recovery; 140 for promotional | Regulatory floor |
| Attempt and connected-call caps | Tenant | ≤ 3 attempts and 1 connected recovery call a day [REC] | Tenant may lower |
| AI inbound assistant | Tenant | Off | Commercial choice; disclosure and human handover cannot be switched off |
| AI outbound recovery voice | Tenant | Off | Needs Board policy and CCO-approved script |
| Recording retention | Tenant | 6 months for recovery calls, longer while sub judice | Floor from 1 Jan 2027 (para 100P) |
| Languages and voices | Tenant | English and Hindi; others per provider | Commercial choice |

### Menu and screens (workspace N, menu `Settings › Communications`)

| Path | Main screens and key actions | Roles |
|---|---|---|
| `… › Providers` | Provider accounts by state, due-diligence checklist (DPA, residency proof, DLT, 1600 support), certification results, enable or suspend | Tenant admin maker, CCO checker |
| `… › Numbers and DLT` | Numbers by series and purpose, DLT headers and templates, auto-dialler notifications | Tenant admin |
| `… › Contact policy` | Active rule-pack version and future versions with effective dates; simulator ("can I call this borrower now?") showing the deciding rule | CCO, collections head |
| `… › AI assistant` | Use cases, script and prompt versions with approvals, monthly QA and bias samples, handover statistics | CCO, AI owner (M20) |

Workspace G (Collections) and F (Servicing) agents see only the call controls and the reason when a call is refused.

### Acceptance tests

- A recovery call from a tenant NBFC to a borrower through a 10-digit number is refused with `series_not_permitted`; through the tenant's 1600-series number at 18:30 it proceeds; at 19:05 it is refused.
- A promotional call to a DND number without explicit consent is refused; with consent it goes only through the 140-series route.
- A microfinance recovery call at 18:15 in December 2026 is refused; on 4 Jan 2027 the same call is evaluated under the Third Amendment pack version, and the evaluation log records which pack version decided.
- The AI assistant does not disclose a balance before OTP verification, hands over to a human on "agent", and an attempted settlement negotiation is routed to a human with the transcript.
- A recorded call without the recording announcement in the transcript fails the QA check and raises a conduct exception.
- The JioCX adapter stub passes the certification suite in sandbox and cannot be enabled for production while the residency-proof record is missing.
- A provider whose residency proof is 13 months old stops carrying production traffic, and calls fail over only to another certified adapter of the same tenant.
- An AI recovery script without a Board-policy reference cannot be set `LIVE`.

# PART 8 — REGULATORY BASELINE (STARTING REGISTER — VERIFY BEFORE EACH MODULE)

## 8.1 Rules for handling regulation

Before implementing any regulated workflow:

1. Research the current authoritative source: rbi.org.in, the official gazette, MeitY, UIDAI, NPCI, CERSAI and NeSL.
2. Record in `docs/compliance/requirements-to-controls.md`:
   - instrument;
   - paragraph;
   - date;
   - applicability conditions;
   - responsible party (lender / LSP / Infrabyx / vendor);
   - system control;
   - evidence produced;
   - test case;
   - open questions.
3. Keep confirmed legal requirements separate from interpretations, recommendations and assumptions. Never claim regulatory compliance merely because a feature exists.
4. Never assume one obligation applies identically to every lender. Applicability depends on:
   - entity type (NBFC / HFC / UCB / SFB / commercial bank);
   - layer and asset size;
   - deposit-taking status;
   - customer interface;
   - product;
   - channel (digital or physical).
5. On **28 November 2025**, RBI repealed 9,445 circulars and issued 244 entity-wise Master Directions. On **31 July 2026** it issued **64 Department of Supervision Directions**, repealing a further 628 circulars. Older circular references are legacy. Cite the new Directions, and keep the legacy reference only for traceability.

## 8.2 Starting register

All items need confirmation against the primary text.

# PART 8A — REQUIREMENTS FROM THE RBI DIRECTIONS SUPPLIED BY THE PROJECT OWNER (verified against the official text)

## 8A.0 How to use this Part

The project owner supplied the official RBI PDFs for the 33 Directions and 1 guidance note listed in 8A.0.2 (15 in v1.2, 18 Directions and the ORM guidance note in v1.3). Each was read in full, and the paragraph citations in this Part come from that text. Sections 8A.1–8A.16 date from v1.2; 8A.17–8A.36 were added in v1.3.

### 8A.0.1 Rules for Claude Code

1. **Store the source texts.** Save the supplied PDFs in the repository under `docs/regulations/rbi/` (file name = RBI number, e.g. `RBI-DOR-2025-26-347.pdf`). Record a SHA-256 hash and the "updated as on" date of each in `docs/regulations/index.md`.
2. **Give every requirement an ID.** Load each requirement below into the regulatory register (M14) with the ID format `REQ-<code>-<para>`, for example `REQ-CF-10(1)`, `REQ-CIR-35(2)` or `REQ-CYB-121`.
   - Codes: CF, CIR, CRM, CON, INV, BR, ALM, FS, CLM, AA, CMP, CYB, DPS, FRM, AUD (v1.2); IRACP, RSA, RBC, WD, KYC, TDCR, SEC, CAP, SBR, DIV, MISC, GOV, OUT, ORM, MFI, IAF, SA, SR, MSD (v1.3); from v1.5, codes for non-RBI law and standards and for later or non-NBFC RBI instruments are listed in Part 8A.37 (for example `REQ-CA13-173(1)`, `REQ-ICSI-SS1-7`, `REQ-LC-CoW-17(2)`, `REQ-ITA25-393`, `REQ-CB-IA-3`, `REQ-RBIOS26-10`).
   - ORM is a guidance note, not a Direction. Its IDs (`REQ-ORM-<para>`) carry the register strength flag "guidance" and are never reported as statutory breaches.
   - MISC (DOR Miscellaneous Directions 373) and MSD (DoS Miscellaneous Supervisory Directions 467) are separate instruments; keep them apart.
   - Every rule pack, control test and golden test must reference these IDs.
3. **Status of [VERIFY] items.**
   - These paragraphs are **verified** for the copies supplied.
   - Remove any [VERIFY] elsewhere in this prompt that a citation here resolves.
   - **Do not** treat amendments issued after a copy's "updated as on" date as verified; check them separately.
4. **More Directions will follow.** Still to be supplied: the HFC Directions; the Internal Ombudsman Directions and RB-IOS 2026; the repeal circular DoS.CO.PPG.66/11.01.005/2026-27; the RBC Second and Third Amendment Directions, 2026; a later SBR copy (the supplied 339 copy does not contain the ₹1 lakh crore UL threshold or the "Type I NBFC" category). Add each one to this Part in the same format.
5. **Drafting slips.** Where the official text contains a drafting slip, implement the evident intent, document the slip in `docs/regulations/errata.md`, and never "fix" it silently in code. Appendix F lists every slip found so far; seed `errata.md` from it. Examples:
   - CF definition 4(1)(xix) refers to "Chapter IV" for LSPs; digital lending is Chapter III.
   - CF definitions (xxiii) and (xxiv) refer to "Chapter VII" for project finance; it is Chapter VI.
   - The FS Directions restart numbering after para 21.
   - The CIR Annex I state catalogue is misaligned.
