# PART 10 — TECHNOLOGY, ARCHITECTURE AND NON-FUNCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS

## 10.1 Recommended stack

Validate current versions in Phase 0. Propose changes through an ADR.

| Layer | Recommendation | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Monorepo | pnpm workspaces + Turborepo; TypeScript strict | Shared types, contracts and design system |
| Internal web app (all workspaces) | Next.js 16 (App Router) + React 19 + TypeScript; shadcn/ui + Tailwind with design tokens; TanStack Query; TanStack Table v9 or AG Grid Community (MIT) for data-dense grids. AG Grid Enterprise (paid: grouping, server-side row model, Excel export) only after a licence ADR | Complex workflows, large tables, theming |
| Backend | Node.js LTS + TypeScript; **NestJS 11 modular monolith** (or Fastify with explicit modules), with strict domain boundaries; OpenAPI 3.1 via Zod schemas | Business rules, integrations, controlled access |
| Database | PostgreSQL 16+ (Supabase now; Amazon RDS/Aurora PostgreSQL later); **Drizzle ORM or Kysely** for SQL control; versioned SQL migrations | Relational, transactional ledger; portable |
| Money and maths | `NUMERIC` columns; `decimal.js` (precision ≥ 40); property-based tests (fast-check) for schedule/allocation invariants | Paisa-exact accuracy |
| Workflow orchestration | **Temporal** (TypeScript SDK; Temporal Cloud has AWS Mumbai/Hyderabad regions, or self-host) for long-running sagas: origination, disbursement, mandate presentation and retries, legal timelines, COB orchestration. Encrypt workflow payloads with a client-side codec so no PII sits in Temporal history. pg-boss or Graphile Worker for simple jobs | Durable, retry-safe, auditable workflows |
| Rules / BRE | **GoRules ZEN engine** (JDM decision tables/graphs; MIT licence; Node bindings) with versioned rules stored in Postgres and the open-source JDM editor component for business users (the hosted GoRules BRMS is commercial) | Credit policy, pricing grids, deviations, eligibility |
| Events | Transactional outbox → queue/stream (start with Postgres-backed queue or Redis Streams; move to Amazon MSK/Redpanda + Debezium CDC on AWS) | Reliable integration events |
| Authentication | Supabase Auth now, **behind an OIDC abstraction**; Keycloak or Amazon Cognito later; SSO/SAML for bank tenants; MFA mandatory for staff | Portability |
| Authorisation | Server-side policy layer: RBAC + ABAC (Cedar or OpenFGA for hierarchy/amount limits) **plus Postgres Row-Level Security** as defence-in-depth for tenant/entity/branch isolation | Least privilege; Supabase must not be the only security boundary |
| Documents | S3-compatible private storage (Supabase Storage → Amazon S3) with SSE-KMS; docxtemplater/Handlebars templates → Gotenberg (HTML/DOCX → PDF) | Agreements, KFS, CAM, letters |
| Search | PostgreSQL FTS + pg_trgm first; OpenSearch later | Customer and loan search |
| Reporting/BI | Regulatory returns in code. Apache Superset (Apache-2.0; guest-token row-level security) for embedded MIS. Metabase only if its paid embedding/sandboxing tier is licensed. Cube semantic layer optional | Self-service MIS |
| Observability | OpenTelemetry → Grafana (Loki/Tempo/Mimir, self-hosted in India) or AWS-native; Sentry self-hosted, or SaaS with no PII (Sentry SaaS stores data in the US/EU); PII-scrubbing log processors; security audit events | Production support and traceability |
| Infrastructure | Docker. **Development and staging (synthetic data only):** Railway (no India region; nearest is Singapore) + Supabase. **Any environment holding real borrower data:** India-region hosting only — Supabase ap-south-1 with an India-region compute host, or directly AWS ap-south-1 (primary) and ap-south-2 (DR) on ECS/EKS — provisioned with OpenTofu/Terraform or AWS CDK. KMS/CloudHSM for signing and field-encryption keys. Aadhaar vault per UIDAI Circular 14 of 2025. Secrets Manager; WAF | Data localisation, scalable, portable |
| Testing | Vitest/Jest, Testcontainers (Postgres), Playwright (E2E), Pact (contract tests with Udofin/partners), k6 (load), OWASP ZAP and Semgrep/CodeQL (security), Fineract differential harness | Release gates |
| Field app | Expo React Native + TypeScript (offline-first, SQLite + sync) | Field ops |
| Rule and expression language (v1.5) | CEL (Common Expression Language) for return applicability, validation and guard-rail expressions inside versioned YAML rule packs (Part 7B RR1.3, RR3.3); GoRules ZEN remains the BRE for credit decisions | Side-effect-free, typed and portable evaluation [REC; owner decision, Appendix B] |
| Archives and exports (v1.5) | Part 7J DP1 archive standard: folder tree, XLSX and CSV registers, DOCX letters, PDF/A renditions, JSON manifest with SHA-256, data dictionary and README, built by workers with a rendering check in CI | Readable without Finbyx (OUT paras 87, 97(xvi)) |
| Customer-controlled storage (BYOS) (v1.5) | `StorageTarget` connectors to S3, Azure Blob, GCS, SharePoint and OneDrive, Google Drive (non-regulated data only), SFTP and on-premises stores; tenant KMS for BYOK and HYOK | Tenant control of copies and keys (OUT para 97(vii)(b)) |
| Connector agent (v1.5) | Signed, outbound-only Finbyx Connector Agent (`apps/agent`) with an mTLS device certificate and signature-verified auto-update, for Tally Prime and on-premises storage | No inbound port at the tenant site |

## 10.2 Architecture principles

These are mandatory. Principles 1–17 are carried over from the Udofin prompt, and 18–30 are added for a core-lending system.

1. Use a modular architecture with explicit domain boundaries. Start with a modular monolith, not microservices.
2. Define an owner for every important data entity.
3. Enforce tenant and legal-entity isolation in the API, the service layer and the database (RLS), and test it.
4. Apply least-privilege access control.
5. Validate all sensitive operations on trusted backend services. The browser and the mobile app never hold privileged keys.
6. Use database transactions for operations that must be atomic.
7. Make financial operations idempotent and safely retryable (idempotency keys stored and enforced).
8. Keep traceable state transitions for leads, applications, loans, payments, mandates, collateral, collections, legal cases and complaints. Use explicit state machines with allowed transitions, failure states, retries and human overrides. For example, an application must not move to "disbursed" just because it was sanctioned.
9. Record critical operations as immutable or tamper-evident (hash-chained) audit events.
10. Keep configuration separate from code.
11. Keep secrets outside source control.
12. Keep database migrations versioned and reviewed for locking, data loss, backward compatibility and rollback/forward recovery.
13. Use asynchronous processing for suitable long-running tasks.
14. Implement structured logging, monitoring, error handling and alerting, with **no Aadhaar, PAN, OTP, account numbers or sensitive personal data in logs.**
15. Document API contracts, data models and material architecture decisions (ADRs).
16. Avoid unnecessary duplication between web, field-app and backend.
17. Build reusable components only when their behaviour is clear.
18. **Single authoritative financial record.** The loan ledger and the GL are the only sources of financial truth. Balances are derived, never edited.
19. **No hard deletes of financial or regulatory data.** Use reversals, cancellations and legal-hold-aware retention.
20. **Business date ≠ system date.** Every financial posting carries a value date, a business date and a system timestamp.
21. **Back-dated transactions** replay deterministically from the affected date. Period locks block posting into closed periods, except through an authorised adjustment workflow.
22. **Duplicate prevention.** Prevent duplicate disbursements, duplicate receipt allocation and duplicate mandate presentation (unique constraints + idempotency + reconciliation).
23. **Reconcile provider records against internal records.** Never trust a successful API response alone.
24. **Regulation as configuration.** Regulatory parameters (classification days, provision rates, contact hours, cooling-off, KFS rules, prepayment rules) live in versioned, effective-dated rule packs with platform guard-rails and tests.
25. **Explainability.** Every credit decision, deviation approval, charge, waiver and classification stores the inputs, rule version and approver.
26. **Maker-checker** on every configurable sensitive action.
27. **Data localisation.** All production data, backups and logs stay in India. For digital lending, data processed abroad must be deleted there and repatriated within 24 hours (CF para 14(4)). The Cyber Directions themselves contain no localisation clause. Every SaaS sub-processor must be confirmed India-resident in an ADR; otherwise, self-host it or send it no personal data. This covers Supabase, the compute host, Temporal Cloud, Sentry/Grafana, LLM endpoints, and email/SMS/WhatsApp vendors.
28. **Privacy by design.** Consent lineage, purpose limitation, minimisation, masking in UI by role, and a retention engine.
29. **Scalability.** Design for at least 100 lender tenants, 10 million+ loan accounts and tens of millions of ledger entries a month, with partitioned tables (by tenant and date), read replicas for reporting, and horizontally scalable COB workers.
30. **Portability.** Containerised, environment-based config, storage and auth abstractions, IaC. Do not build an elaborate cloud-neutral platform before the product is validated.
31. **Straight-through processing.** No manual editing of data passed between Finbyx and other applications: CIC/CIMS files, GL/Tally, co-lender files, payment files. Generated files are hashed and signed, and the hash is verified on upload. Exceptions go through maker-checker with an audit trail (CYB paras 119–120).
32. **Regulator and auditor access.** Built-in, time-boxed, read-only roles over MIS, audit trails and evidence (CYB paras 46, 57).
33. **IPv6.** All public endpoints are dual-stack IPv4/IPv6 (CYB para 18(4)).
34. **System-driven regulatory outputs.** SMA/NPA identification, fraud reporting and returns are system-generated, never spreadsheet-compiled (CYB paras 44, 46).
35. **Attachable modules and entitlements.** Optional module packs (first, the Recovery Suite of Part 7A) carry a manifest, are registered in a module registry and are enabled per tenant, product and branch by licence entitlement plus a feature flag checked on the server for every call (OpenFeature-compatible provider; flag keys `mod.[module].[capability]`). Lifecycle: AVAILABLE → LICENSED → INSTALLED → CONFIGURED → CERTIFIED → ENABLED → READ_ONLY → DETACHED (Part 7A.0.3). Detaching turns off writes and UI and produces an export pack; regulated, legal and recovery records are never deleted. Plug-ins run out of process and reach data only through APIs and events with tenant-scoped tokens.
36. **Prepare, validate, human files (v1.5).** Finbyx prepares, validates, reconciles, packages and evidences every regulatory, bureau, MCA, GST, income-tax and exchange filing; an authorised human in the tenant approves and files. Portal credentials, OTPs, DSC tokens and PINs are never stored or scripted, and machine-to-machine channels are used only where the regulator documents them for that entity class (Part 7B 7B.0).
37. **Institution profile, not NBFC hard-coding (v1.5).** Law, vocabulary, capital rules, returns, accounting framework and permitted products load from the legal entity's institution profile (Part 7G IP1) and accounting-framework decision (Part 7C AC1).
38. **Archive standard (v1.5).** Every export follows Part 7J DP1 — a self-explanatory folder tree of Excel, Word, PDF/A and CSV files with a manifest (SHA-256), data dictionary, relationship map and README — and opens without Finbyx. Export and read access are never suspended for non-payment (Part 7K CM1.4, CM4.5).
39. **Bring your own storage (v1.5).** Tenants may hold exports and backups in storage they control (cloud bucket, SharePoint or OneDrive, Google Drive for non-regulated data only (no personal data, books of account, returns, loan or HR data), SFTP or on-premises) through certified `StorageTarget` connectors with residency checks and a data-class policy; borrower and loan data go only to India-resident targets (Part 7J DP3–DP4; CF para 14(4)).
40. **Rule language (v1.5).** Applicability, validation and guard-rail expressions are written in CEL inside versioned, effective-dated YAML rule packs with citations; rule packs contain no executable code (Part 7B RR1.3, RR3.3). Credit-decision rules stay in the GoRules BRE.
41. **Commercial events never interrupt regulated functions (v1.5).** Plan changes, dunning or termination never stop COB, regulatory outputs, grievance handling, read access or export (Part 7K CM1.4).
42. **Menus and settings from registries (v1.5).** Navigation is generated from the module registry, roles and entitlements, never hand-coded per tenant; every setting is defined once with scope, default, effective date, owner and class — a cited regulatory floor that no role can relax (`floor_violation`) or a commercial choice under maker-checker — and resolved server-side to the strictest applicable value; each module's `Menu and screens` and `Settings and options` subsections and Appendix G are the specification.

## 10.3 Non-functional targets (initial — confirm in Phase 0)

| Area | Target |
|---|---|
| Availability (production) | 99.9% monthly for staff app and APIs; COB must not block branch operations |
| Latency | p95 < 300 ms for reads, < 800 ms for standard writes, excluding third-party calls |
| COB | 1 million active loans processed in < 60 minutes on reference infrastructure, with linear scale-out |
| RPO / RTO | Near-zero RPO for the ledger (synchronous replica / PITR). The Cyber Directions set no numeric RTO: Ch V requires a minimal RTO approved by each NBFC's ITSC, a near-zero RPO for critical systems, and a reconciliation method where RPO ≠ 0 (CYB paras 134–136). Finbyx default RTO ≤ 4 hours, with a tighter per-tenant tier so each ML+ tenant's ITSC-approved RTO is met contractually (para 138) |
| DR drills | Half-yearly for critical systems for Chapter V entities (Cyber Directions para 129); annual BCP test for Chapter IV; restore tests at least quarterly |
| DR architecture | DC and DR geographically separated, e.g. ap-south-1 / ap-south-2 (CYB para 102); identical configuration and patches through IaC, with a drift check (para 137). A single-region deployment is not acceptable for Ch V tenants in production |
| DR switchover | Half-yearly platform drill running production on DR for one full business day, BOD to EOD including COB, with a tenant evidence pack; failures re-tested (CYB paras 129–131, 138) |
| Backup | Encrypted, immutable backups; quarterly restore test; half-yearly recovery test without loss of transactions or audit trails (DPS para 20 baseline) |
| Log retention | Configurable per tenant; the longest of the applicable legal and tenant-policy periods [VERIFY each]. The Cyber Directions prescribe none (CYB para 110) |
| Concurrency | 1 million+ borrower-portal users; 50,000 concurrent staff and field sessions across tenants (validate in Phase 0) |
| Security | OWASP ASVS Level 2 baseline. VA at least every 6 months and PT at least every 12 months on production by an independent CERT-In-empanelled firm, plus pre- and post-go-live and after major change (CYB paras 121–124; DPS para 32). Incident notice to the tenant fast enough for its DAKSH filing within 6 hours of detection by Finbyx (CYB paras 28, 141; OUT para 61) |
| Accessibility | WCAG 2.2 AA for portals |
| Localisation | English + Hindi at launch; framework for regional languages; INR formatting (lakh/crore), DD-MM-YYYY |

## 10.4 Security and cyber controls (map to the 2026 Cyber Directions)

- **Encryption:** TLS 1.2+ (prefer 1.3) in transit; AES-256 at rest; field-level encryption for PAN, Aadhaar reference, bank account and DOB; KMS envelope keys per tenant; HSM for vault and signing keys. **Tenant-controlled keys (BYOK/HYOK: tenant-owned KMS key or HSM partition, with revocation) available to every ML/UL tenant**, because OUT para 97(vii)(b) requires encryption keys and HSMs under the NBFC's control for cloud services.
- **Identity and access:**
  - MFA for all staff and privileged users;
  - privileged access management;
  - session timeouts;
  - IP and device restrictions;
  - quarterly access reviews (system-generated);
  - joiner-mover-leaver automation;
  - MFA mandatory for privileged users and critical actions — disbursement approval, rate/parameter change, user-rights change, bulk export (CYB para 115);
  - PAM with session recording;
  - monthly review of elevated-user activity (CYB para 114);
  - SoD between sysadmin, DBA and transaction roles (CYB para 21(2)).
- **Application security:**
  - input validation (Zod);
  - output encoding;
  - CSRF protection;
  - rate limiting;
  - signed short-lived document URLs;
  - IDOR/BOLA tests on every endpoint;
  - webhook signature verification and replay protection;
  - file-upload scanning (antivirus, type and size checks);
  - WAF and DDoS protection on every internet endpoint (DPS para 23);
  - no sensitive data in cookies, hidden fields or client storage (DPS para 22);
  - masked account and card numbers in SMS/email (DPS para 40);
  - threat model per module; SAST and source review per release; authenticated scanning (DPS paras 29–35);
  - CVSS-based remediation SLAs, with no recurrence of known CVEs (CYB paras 125–126).
- **Supply chain:**
  - SBOM;
  - dependency scanning;
  - signed builds;
  - pinned versions;
  - secret scanning in CI;
  - a source-code-escrow deposit of every production release (CYB para 105; DPS para 31);
  - a signed certificate per material change that the software is free of known vulnerabilities, malware and covert channels (CYB para 106);
  - an EOS register and technology refresh plan (CYB paras 92–93).
- **Monitoring:**
  - SIEM-ready security audit stream;
  - anomaly alerts (bulk export, off-hours privileged access, mass status changes);
  - an incident response runbook with severity matrix and regulatory/CERT-In reporting templates.
- **Independent security review:** in each phase, try to break your own implementation, not merely confirm that it works. Test:
  - cross-tenant and cross-entity access;
  - cross-branch access;
  - privilege escalation;
  - insecure document links;
  - IDOR;
  - replayed requests;
  - webhook forgery;
  - mass assignment;
  - unauthorised admin actions;
  - maker-checker bypass;
  - back-dated posting into closed periods.

## 10.5 UI/UX principles for internal teams

- Clean, professional, non-cluttered, **data-dense without visual noise**.
- Role-based workspaces with:
  - **My Queue** (SLA-sorted);
  - global search (customer, loan, PAN-masked, mobile, application ID);
  - a 360° customer/loan view with tabs;
  - keyboard shortcuts for power users;
  - bulk actions with maker-checker;
  - saved filters;
  - export controls by permission;
  - inline explanations of why data is requested;
  - clear error messages and recovery steps;
  - timeline views of every account.
- **Theming and white-labelling** through design tokens (colours, typography, spacing, radius, logo, density). I must be able to change the look without code changes.
- Maximum automation:
  - pre-fill from data pulls;
  - auto-generated documents;
  - auto-allocation;
  - auto-reconciliation;
  - auto-reminders;
  - auto-escalation;
  - straight-through processing where rules allow, with human review where rules or regulation require it.
- **Consistent component library and Storybook. Every screen must have** empty, loading, error and permission-denied states.
- **Menus, screens and settings (v1.5):** menus are generated from the module registry, roles and entitlements, and every module's screens and settings follow its `Menu and screens` and `Settings and options` subsections, consolidated in Appendix G. Standard patterns: list (saved views, filters, bulk actions under maker-checker, exports by permission), detail with timeline, create or edit wizard with inline validation, approval queue with SLA countdown, and dashboard with drill-down. Every block or refusal explains why (rule, citation, the screen that fixes it). Heavy back-office queues have keyboard shortcuts, and every action also has a button. Screens meet WCAG 2.2 AA; borrower-facing screens are vernacular. A setting classed as a regulatory floor can be tightened but never relaxed (`floor_violation`, Part 10.2 principle 42), and automation never takes a regulated decision without human approval.

## 10.6 Vendor obligations Finbyx must meet as a service provider to regulated lenders

Finbyx is an IT service provider to its tenants. Build these obligations into the product, the contracts and the evidence packs:

1. **Contract clauses** (OUT paras 33–34, 74(i)–(xix), 87–88, 97(xvi); CYB para 62 for BL tenants ≥ ₹500 crore). The standard Finbyx MSA/DPA carries all of them, with a clause matrix per tenant:
   - continuous monitoring by the NBFC;
   - data-protection systems;
   - access to books, records and information;
   - **retention of administrative audit trails and logs**, accessible on approved request;
   - audit rights for internal or external auditors;
   - copies of Finbyx's audit reports;
   - RBI access to data within reasonable time.
2. Maintenance and support under a formal agreement and SLA (CYB para 104).
3. **Source code of critical applications, or source-code escrow** with an independent agent. Deposit every release including fixes, with a verified build (CYB para 105; DPS para 31).
4. **Security certificate:** a written certificate that the software is free of known vulnerabilities, malware and covert channels.
   - Issue it at onboarding and on each material change, using an agreed materiality definition (CYB para 106).
   - For card issuers, issue it annually if the application changed.
   - Accept penal clauses (DPS para 32).
5. **Testing:** independent VA every 6 months and PT annually, and on major change. Share the reports and remediation status (CYB paras 121–126).
6. **Incidents:** the tenant's 6-hour RBI clock runs from **detection by Finbyx** (OUT para 61). Notify the tenant without undue delay (target ≤ 2 hours from Finbyx detection) for the contractually listed material adverse events (OUT 74(iii)); support forensics and RCA; take part in crisis drills; supply lessons-learned input (CYB paras 28, 140–146; ORM 99–101).
7. **BCP and DR:** geographically separated sites; half-yearly full-day DR drills; collaborative resilience tests against each tenant's RTO; proactive BCP assurance (CYB paras 59(5), 64, 102, 129–138).
8. **Staff and policy:** comply with tenant InfoSec and acceptable-use policies; background-screen privileged staff (CYB paras 21(4), 97).
9. **Disclosures to tenants:**
   - RCSA;
   - sub-processor list for concentration and supply-chain assessment;
   - SBOM;
   - EOS dates;
   - asset inventory and CIA classification for Finbyx-hosted assets (CYB paras 21(1), 91–92, 117; DPS para 16).
10. **Card data:** none stored in plain text; PCI confirmations where in scope (DPS para 69).
11. **Regulator and auditor access:** read-only RBI and auditor access to tenant data and MIS on request (CYB paras 46, 57, 62).
12. **Certifications:** pursue ISO/IEC 27001, SOC 2 (Type 1, then Type 2) and the other schemes per Part 7L EO5; never claim a certification, attestation or compliance status before the report or certificate is issued, and describe work in progress only as a readiness programme. They are not mandated, but a tenant may rely on globally recognised third-party certifications instead of its own audit, subject to its risk assessment (OUT para 79). Their scope must cover the OUT 97(xvii) heads. Offer pooled audits (OUT para 77).

**Finbyx's status under the Outsourcing Directions.** Hosted multi-tenant Finbyx is a cloud SaaS (OUT 96(1)(i)(c)) that delivers ASP, data-centre and cloud services (5(1)(iii)–(v)) and holds borrower data. For ML/UL tenants it is therefore **material IT outsourcing** (58(2)(i)–(ii)). The licence/subscription and OEM-maintenance exclusions (5(2)(v)–(vi)) can at most cover a dedicated deployment in the tenant's own account where Finbyx neither operates the system nor accesses its data; the tenant decides that (62(iii)) [interpretation]. BL tenants fall under CYB Ch III/IV instead of OUT Ch IV, and CYB 117 covers what OUT does not. **Design every deployment to the in-scope standard.** Existing contracts had to comply by renewal or 10 Apr 2026 (OUT 2), so all tenant contracts must comply now.

13. **Ownership/conflict declaration:**
   - Finbyx is not owned or controlled by a tenant's director, KMP, arrangement approver or their relatives, unless it is a group company or the tenant's Board grants an exception with disclosure (OUT 59, 13(iv)).
   - Infrabyx group tenants: Board policy, SLA, objective selection, arm's length and identical risk practice (90–92).
14. **Vendor assurance pack**, refreshed at least annually (OUT 30, 38, 71, 80):
   - financials, track record, reputation, litigation and complaints;
   - staff and subcontractor vetting;
   - security and internal controls, audit coverage and BCM;
   - infrastructure and DR;
   - conflicts and data-segregation capability;
   - cyber risk assessment;
   - enforceability;
   - evidence of operational resilience at least equivalent to the tenant's (ORM 73).
15. **Sub-processors and supply chain:**
   - tenant prior consent before appointing or changing a sub-processor, with the full supply-chain list (OUT 34(iv), 74(xi), 82);
   - Finbyx contractually liable for subcontractors and nth parties (74(xiii); ORM 76);
   - back-to-back terms with cloud providers and OEMs (74(xviii));
   - CIA assessment of subcontractors (97(x)(d)).
16. **Access:** unrestricted access to data, logs, alerts and premises, including subcontractors, for the tenant, its auditors, RBI and competent authorities (OUT 34(ii), (vii), 74(ii), (xii), 81). Support pooled audits (77).
17. **Data:**
   - India-only storage (OUT 74(vi));
   - data inventory of what is captured, processed and stored (74(vii));
   - permitted-sharing list (74(viii));
   - lifecycle through to permanent erasure (97(ii));
   - NDA, with confidentiality surviving termination (34(xi), 74(xix));
   - preservation per the tenant's legal obligations (34(xii)).
18. **Multi-tenant isolation:** only tenant-authorised personnel access tenant data (OUT 26–27, 70, 97(vii)(c)). Finbyx staff use break-glass, need-to-know access only, every access logged and visible to the tenant (24, 69(i)).
19. **Keys and access:**
   - tenant-controlled keys/HSM (OUT 97(vii)(b));
   - IAM with RBAC for user and privileged access, an SoD role-conflict matrix and least privilege;
   - **MFA** (97(viii)).
20. **SOC:** log and event export to the tenant's SOC (SIEM feed), with log retention (OUT 97(xi)). If Infrabyx offers a SOC service, meet para 95.
21. **SLAs:** a monitoring dashboard covering uptime, availability, performance and incident response, plus KRIs (OUT 74(v), 75, 64(4)).
22. **Incidents:** contractual list of material adverse events (OUT 74(iii)); notice measured from Finbyx detection (61); breach/leakage disclosure (25, 28, 69(iii)).
23. **BCP/DR:**
   - documented and tested, with joint tests (OUT 40, 83; ORM 79, 82);
   - CSP-level DR drills (97(xv));
   - "essential personnel" on site during exigencies (74(xvii)).
24. **Exit:**
   - orderly transfer (OUT 74(xv)) and full cooperation with the incoming provider (88);
   - **no erasure or alteration of data during the transition** (87);
   - **complete export in documented formats** (ledger, loans, documents, audit trail, configuration) within agreed turnaround times;
   - secure purge with an independent-assurance certificate (42, 97(xvi)(d)); the export, exit states and turnarounds are in Part 7J DP1–DP5.
25. **Continuity:** cooperation in the tenant's insolvency or resolution (OUT 74(xvi)). Records stay available even if Finbyx is liquidated (43, 53(iii); CYB 105 escrow).
26. **RBI directions:** comply with RBI directions on the outsourced service (OUT 74(xiv), 47(v)).
27. **No core management functions for tenants** (OUT 15):
   - no Finbyx-staff role can sanction loans, decide KYC compliance, perform internal audit or compliance, or manage investments;
   - BRE and auto-decisions run only on tenant-approved rule versions, attributed to the tenant's authority;
   - Udofin is bound by the same limits.
28. **Grievances:** Finbyx and Udofin route customer complaints to the tenant's GRO and never close them (OUT 54–57, 98–99).
29. **ORM inputs for tenants:**
   - RTO, RPO, data-loss and service-level metrics for each Finbyx-supported critical operation (ORM 33);
   - Finbyx RCSA;
   - post-incident lessons-learned reports (ORM 99–101).
30. **Certification scope** covers OUT 97(xvii) (OUT 79).

# PART 11 — WORKING METHOD, GIT DISCIPLINE AND DEFINITION OF DONE

## 11.1 For each module or sub-module

Work through these steps in order:

1. Explain the business objective in plain English.
2. Identify assumptions and ask only material unresolved questions.
3. Research the relevant legal, provider and technical requirements, and update the regulatory register and integration register.
4. Produce the functional specification and acceptance criteria (Given/When/Then), including negative cases. Save it to `docs/specs/<module>.md`.
5. Describe the data model, APIs, events, permissions, state machine and workflows.
6. Identify security, privacy, failure, performance and migration risks.
7. **Stop for my approval.**
8. Explain the logic in plain English, then implement only the approved scope, in small, reviewable commits.
9. Write and run the tests that apply:
   - unit;
   - property-based (money);
   - integration;
   - contract;
   - E2E;
   - tenant-isolation;
   - security;
   - Fineract differential tests.
10. Run linting, type checks, build checks, migration validation and security scans.
11. Review the diff for unrelated changes, secrets, PII in logs and security defects.
12. Update the docs: setup, configuration, migration, deployment and runbooks.
13. Summarise:
    - what changed;
    - the actual test results;
    - known limitations;
    - mock vs live integrations;
    - next steps.
14. Commit with a meaningful message on the feature branch, open a pull request, and merge only after my approval.

## 11.2 Financial integrity before financial features

Do not implement live financial operations until their transaction rules and acceptance tests are approved. This covers:

- schedules;
- allocation;
- accruals;
- reversals;
- reconciliation;
- accounting entries;
- classification;
- provisioning.

Maintain a **golden test-case library**, approved by me and our finance/compliance reviewers, of worked numerical examples (EMI, broken-period interest, prepayment, bounce, IRACP Illustration I day-end dates, NPA upgrade, borrower-level contagion, HP/lease provisioning, restructuring downgrade/upgrade, EIR, GST). Every release must pass it.

## 11.3 Git and environment rules

- First inspect the connected repository: current branch, existing files, Git status and available tooling.
- Do not overwrite existing work without understanding its purpose.
- Work on feature branches. **Never push directly to `main`.** Never deploy to production, rotate live credentials or modify production data without my explicit authorisation.
  - The original Udofin prompt asked for a direct commit to main in one place. For Finbyx we use pull requests only. Branch protection on `main` must be enabled.
- Never commit API keys, service-role secrets, private certificates, production credentials or real borrower data. Use `.env.example` files with placeholders. Keep local, test, staging and production configuration separate. Use synthetic test data only.
- If repository write access or commit capability is unavailable, provide the exact files and commands. Do not claim to have committed.
- Do not claim a test passed unless it was actually run and its output is available.
- Do not implement large unapproved features or silently expand scope. Do not create placeholder business logic that pretends to work. Mark mocks clearly.

## 11.4 Project documents to maintain

Keep these documents current:

- `README.md`
- `CLAUDE.md` (concise, stable; links to detail)
- `docs/00-master-prompt.md`
- `docs/architecture/` (system context, C4 diagrams, module map, data ownership)
- `docs/adr/`
- `docs/specs/`
- `docs/products/`
- `docs/data-model/` (ERD, migrations log)
- `docs/api/` (OpenAPI, AsyncAPI)
- `docs/integrations/register.md`
- `docs/compliance/requirements-to-controls.md` and `docs/compliance/regulatory-register.md` (dated)
- `docs/security/threat-model.md` and `docs/security/checklist.md`
- `docs/testing/strategy.md` and `docs/testing/golden-cases/`
- `docs/ops/` (deployment, rollback, DR, runbooks, SLOs)
- `docs/legal/third-party-notices.md` (including Apache Fineract attribution if any code is derived)
- `docs/status/modules.md` (module status and outstanding decisions)
- `docs/economics/unit-costs.md`
- `docs/regulations/return-registry/` (v1.5: return definitions and versions, cell maps, CEL validation packs, the RBI-list conflict log and filing acknowledgements index; Part 7B RR1–RR5)
- `docs/compliance/control-library.md` (v1.5: common control framework mapping each Finbyx control to CYB, OUT, DPS, CERT-In, DPDP, ISO/IEC 27001 and 27701, SOC 2 and PCI DSS; Part 7L EO5.3)
- `docs/compliance/certification-evidence-register.md` (v1.5: evidence item, control, period, collector, SHA-256, auditor request and status; Part 7L EO5)
- `docs/portability/archive-standard.md` (v1.5: folder tree, naming rules, formats, manifest schema and README template; Part 7J DP1)
- `docs/profiles/institution-catalogue.md` (v1.5: institution types, rule-pack bindings and guard-rail registry; Part 7G IP1)

## 11.5 Definition of done

1. A module is not complete just because its screen renders.
2. It is complete only when all of the following are true:
   - its approved acceptance criteria are met;
   - the relevant tests (including negative and tenant-isolation tests) have passed and their output is recorded;
   - authorisation and maker-checker have been checked;
   - failures, retries and reconciliation are handled;
   - accounting entries balance and reconcile;
   - audit events are emitted;
   - documentation and registers are updated;
   - the change is reviewable.
3. A mock or sandbox integration is always clearly distinguished from a production integration.
4. Our goal is a secure, maintainable, configurable, regulator-ready and commercially viable lending platform, not the largest number of features or files.

## 11.6 Additional quality gates

These come from the Udofin prompt and are extended here:

- **Independent security review** each phase (see 10.4).
- **Borrower consent and data lifecycle:** record what was consented to, why, when, for which lender and purpose, and the exact wording shown. Handle withdrawal, retention, deletion, correction and access logging, with legally required exceptions.
- **Disaster recovery:** test restoration of the database, documents, queues/workflows, and post-outage reconciliation. A backup is not proven useful until a restore has been tested.
- **Change and migration safety:** no deployment may leave web, field app, workers and database on incompatible versions. Use expand-and-contract migrations.
- **Regulatory change management:** keep a dated register. When a rule changes, assess the affected products, configurations, disclosures, workflows, tests and evidence.
- **Production monitoring:** SLOs for availability, latency, integration failure rates, queue delays, COB duration, reconciliation breaks and recovery. Alerts carry no sensitive data.
- **Commercial viability:** track per-application costs (verification, bureau, AA, eSign/eStamp, messaging, cloud, support) and revenue per tenant. A technically working product may still be commercially unviable.

# PART 12 — PHASED ROADMAP WITH CLAUDE CODE INSTRUCTIONS

Build a common platform first, then launch a **narrow MVP pilot** before expanding:

- **MVP product scope:** an unsecured Personal Loan + an unsecured MSME Term Loan, branch-assisted, for a single NBFC pilot tenant.
  - Development and staging use synthetic data only.
  - The pilot goes live only on India-region hosting (Part 10.1).
- **Next:** LAP/Home (secured property), Vehicle, Gold, LAS and co-lending.
- **Last:** the specialist products (13–16), after feasibility approval.

How to run the phases:

- Each phase ends with a review gate.
- Copy one **"Instruction to Claude"** block into Claude Code when you start that phase. Do not paste several phases at once.
- Split large phases into sub-modules.
- **Phase P (pilot go-live)** comes before the expansion phases (16–20, including 16b–16e, 17b–17d, 18b and 20b).
- **v1.4 phases:** 12 (Recovery Suite core), 12b (settlement and ADR with Equator) and 17b (secured enforcement and shared-exposure recovery) build Part 7A; 16b implements the Ecosystem Integration Specification. These phases are built once for the product; whether a tenant uses the suite is decided at runtime by licence and feature flag (Part 7A.0), so no phase is skipped.
- **v1.5 phases:** 13b (accounting frameworks, financial statements, GST and Income-tax Act 2025 outputs, the Tally agent and the statutory audit trail; Part 7C), 14b (RBI returns engine and supervisory portal workflows; Part 7B RR1–RR5 and RR8), 14c (credit bureau submissions; RR6–RR7), 14d (risk function, capital adequacy, ratio library, ICAAP, stress testing, PCA and leadership dashboards; Part 7E), 15b (data portability, archives, customer-controlled storage, customer-held backups and exit; Part 7J), 16c (audit and assurance suite with auditor and supervisor workspaces; Part 7D), 16d (corporate governance, listed-company compliance, client HRMS and workplace integration; Part 7F), 16e (plans, entitlements, billing and payments; Part 7K), 17c (institution profiles for credit co-operative societies, co-operative banks and microfinance; Part 7G IP1–IP4), 17d (ARCs, IFSC entities, the investment module and securitisation servicing; Part 7G IP5–IP6 and Part 7H), 18b (voice, AI contact-centre and Jio adapters; Part 7L EO6) and 20b (engineering-operations evidence and certification readiness; Part 7L EO1–EO5). Like the v1.4 phases, they are built once for the product and switched per tenant at runtime by institution profile (Part 7G IP1), licence and feature flag (Part 7K CM1), so no phase is skipped. Phases 13b, 14b, 14c, 14d and 15b come before Phase P because the pilot needs its books, returns, bureau files, capital and liquidity runs and exportable archive; 14b and 14c are built first for the returns and bureaus that apply to the pilot tenant. Phase 16e needs Operations Hub phase O6 (revenue catalogue, billing and Razorpay) to be live, because the Hub owns the catalogue, invoices and the Razorpay account; Phase 20b needs Operations Hub phase O12 (engineering console and control library). The Part 7L EO1 repository controls (rulesets, signed commits, CODEOWNERS, SBOM, pinned Actions) start in Phase 1, the statutory audit log and external-access role skeleton in Phase 2; Phase 20b completes and evidences them. Phase 16d's payroll needs the signed Labour Code rule pack 1.0 (Integration Spec 12.3). Order: 0 → 1 → 2 → 3 → 3b → 4 → 5 → 6 → 7 → 8 → 8b → 8c → 9 → 10 → 11 → 12 → 12b → 13 → 13b → 14 → 14b → 14c → 14d → 15 → 15b → P → 16 → 16b → 16c → 16d → 16e → 17 → 17b → 17c → 17d → 18 → 18b → 19 → 20 → 20b.
- **Menus, screens and settings (every v1.5 phase, and v1.4 modules when next touched):** each phase builds the navigation, screens and settings that the `Menu and screens` and `Settings and options` subsections of its Part specify, inside the Part 3.2 workspaces, and registers them in **Appendix G — Navigation, menus, screens and settings map**, so the menu is generated from the module registry and entitlements (Part 7K CM1) rather than hand-coded. Every setting carries its scope (tenant, legal entity, product or role), default, effective date, owner and class: a **regulatory floor** (cited; enforced server-side; any attempt to relax it fails `floor_violation`, or `RULE_LOOSENING_BLOCKED` for institution rule packs) or a **commercial choice** (effective-dated, maker-checked, audited). Screens follow Part 10.5: list, detail, create or edit wizard, approval queue and dashboard patterns; saved views, bulk actions with maker-checker, exports by permission, keyboard shortcuts on heavy back-office screens, explain-why messages, empty, loading, error and permission-denied states, and WCAG 2.2 AA; borrower-facing screens are vernacular. Automation may prepare, pre-fill, remind and route, but a regulated decision always waits for a human approval.
- Each phase also includes the v1.3 additions listed for it in **Part 8A.36.4**. Add them to the phase specification before approval.

> **Instruction to Claude:** "Before writing the specification, verify: (i) the RBC Third Amendment Directions, 2026 (RBI/2026-27/230, 6 Aug 2026, effective 1 Jan 2027) against the contact-policy rule pack built in Phases 3b and 11, recording that the official text is not yet in docs/regulations/rbi/; (ii) the current version of docs/ecosystem/infrabyx-integration-spec.md; (iii) the Part 7A module boundaries. Then build the Recovery Suite core as an attachable module pack, in the `packages/recovery-*` domain packages behind the stable contract of 7A.0:
>
> - **7A.0 attach and detach:** a `module.yaml` manifest per module (id, version, requires, capabilities, events produced and consumed, APIs, permissions, data categories, regulatory refs, retention class, licence SKU, UI slots, migrations); the lifecycle AVAILABLE → LICENSED → INSTALLED → CONFIGURED (maker-checker) → CERTIFIED → ENABLED → READ_ONLY → DETACHED (7A.0.3); entitlement and flag checks on the server for every call (flag keys `mod.[module].[capability]`); `ModuleAttached` and `ModuleDetached` events (Integration Spec Part 6.16, Platform). Detaching turns off writes and UI, produces a hashed export pack and keeps every record read-only under legal hold until closure plus the retention period. **Nothing is deleted on detach.**
> - **R1 case management and strategy engine:** case opening from M8 hand-off rules; strategy per product playbook key (Part 6.3); the **mechanism-selection engine**, which evaluates every mechanism on every material event and logs the permitted set with blocking reasons (for example SARFAESI blocked below the NBFC threshold or without CERSAI registration, s.26D; DRT blocked for an NBFC not notified under RDB s.2(h)(ii); arbitration blocked without a pre-named institution or post-dispute consent); the **limitation engine** (Limitation Act Arts. 19, 21, 55, 62, 136 and 137; rebase only on a written signed acknowledgment, s.18, or a documented part-payment, s.19; no reset on death, s.9; alerts at T−180, T−90 and T−30 days).
> - **R2 pre-legal recovery, field investigation and skip tracing:** lawful sources only, no disclosure of the debt to third parties, purpose LOCATE logged (DPDP Act s.17(1)(f) basis [VERIFY: wording and commencement]).
> - **R3 legal notices, letters and document automation:** clause library with statute citations; vernacular templates with human check (RBC 10); PDF/A with QR hash; DSC or eSign; outward register; dispatch adapters for India Post Speed Post with proof of delivery (Registered Post merged into Speed Post on 1 Sep 2025), couriers, email, DLT SMS and print-to-post; no WhatsApp channel for recovery or statutory notices (WhatsApp Business Messaging Policy prohibits debt-collection use; guard-rail 7A.0.6); a proof-of-service register per party per mode; **no deemed-served state without evidence** (*Sedhram Nilkanth Muglikar v M.R. Makhare*, Bom HC, 2026).
> - **R7 cheque and mandate dishonour:** NI Act s.138 and PSS Act s.25 — notice within 30 days of receiving information of dishonour, 15 days for payment, complaint within one month of the cause of action with a condonation flag (s.142(1)(b)), filed where the payee's bank branch is (s.142(2)); summons by electronic modes and payment link, early s.143A, compounding-cost tiers (*Sanjabij Tari v Kishore S. Borcar*, 2025 INSC 1158, 25 Sep 2025); if the drawer company is under moratorium, proceed against its officers.
> - **R9 litigation and proceedings tracker:** offensive and defensive matters in every forum (magistrate, civil and commercial courts, DRT and DRAT, NCLT and NCLAT, High Courts, Supreme Court, consumer commissions, arbitral tribunals, Lok Adalat and Permanent Lok Adalat, RB-IOS); CNR sync through the court-data adapter and daily cause-list matching; hearings, orders, directions as tasks, stays as holds on R1 actions; borrower-initiated matters (s.17 SARFAESI, Permanent Lok Adalat, writs) as a separate stream. SARFAESI, DRT and IBC matters are tracked manually here until Phase 17b.
> - **R11 counsel, agency and vendor management:** empanelment with outsourcing due diligence (OUT 30, 34) and conflict checks; agent police verification and IIBF certificate register (RBC 100I from 1 Jan 2027); agency list on the website updated within 7 days (RBC 100K); counsel portal limited to assigned matters; bills with RCM GST and TDS.

### Phase 12b — Settlement and ADR with Equator

> **Instruction to Claude:** "Before writing the specification, verify: (i) the Mediation Act 2023 commencement status (only ss.1, 3, 26, 31–38, 45–47, 50–54 and 56–57 in force by S.O. 4384(E) of 9 Oct 2023; Mediation Council of India established 27 Aug 2026; ss.4–25, 27–30 and 39–44 not yet notified); (ii) any RBI direction following *Shikha Ghosh v Axis Bank* (Del HC DB, 30 Sep 2026; next date 17 Nov 2026); (iii) the Equator API version, Integration Spec Part 6.9 (ADR) and Part 8 (Equator Resolution and other ODR/ADR providers). Then build R8, Settlement and ADR:
>
> - **Negotiation and compromise settlement:** NPV calculator; the Board settlement policy as a versioned object; approver at least one level above the sanctioning authority with sanctioning officials excluded (RSA 16(5)(i)); Board approval for fraud and wilful-defaulter cases, without prejudice to criminal proceedings and penal measures (RSA 16(5)(ii), 97–98); payment over more than 3 months, or a part settlement, treated as restructuring until paid (RSA 89–90); consent decree where judicial proceedings are pending (RSA 100); cooling period of at least 12 months (RSA 95); quarterly reporting (RSA 93–94); applies to NBFCs below ₹500 crore too (RSA 157); CIC "settled" only where a waiver was given for financial inability (CIR 12(2), 12(4)); LWD removal only on full payment of the compromise amount (WD 13). AI or agent offers only inside the pre-approved band; anything else goes to a human approver.
> - **Forum-selection rules,** logged with overrides: arbitration blocked for in-rem mortgage enforcement (*Booz Allen*, (2011) 5 SCC 532) and for claims within the RDB Act by banks and notified institutions (*Vidya Drolia*, 14 Dec 2020); all ADR on hold during an IBC moratorium; a pending consumer complaint cannot be forced into arbitration (*Emaar MGF v Aftab Singh*, (2019) 12 SCC 751); s.12A pre-institution mediation (3 + 2 months) before any commercial suit of ₹3 lakh or more without urgent relief (*Patil Automation*, 2022; *Dhanbad Fuels*, SC, 15 May 2025).
> - **Conciliation (default enforceable route today):** invitation under A&C Act s.62 (no reply in 30 days is a rejection); online sessions; s.73 settlement signed by the parties and authenticated by the conciliator; s.74 status of an arbitral award, enforceable under s.36.
> - **Mediation:** written consent to online mediation (Mediation Act s.30, once in force); recording hard-disabled (ss.22–23). Until s.27 is notified, a mediated settlement is only a contract, so the workflow converts it into a s.73 settlement or a consent decree.
> - **Arbitration:** only where the loan agreement pre-names Equator or another independent institution, or the borrower gives written consent after the dispute arises; otherwise a s.11 petition. Never a lender-selected or lender-vetoed arbitrator, and never a forced choice from the lender's panel (*CORE v ECI-SPIC-SMO-MCML (JV)*, SC Constitution Bench, 8 Nov 2024; *Perkins Eastman v HSCC*, (2020) 20 SCC 760; *L&T Finance v Jai Paras Material Store*, Cal HC, 14 May 2026). s.21 notice to every known address with delivery evidence; Sixth Schedule disclosure before acceptance; per-neutral, per-lender counts against Fifth Schedule items 22 and 24 (*Shikha Ghosh*); clocks for s.23(4), s.29A, s.29B, s.33 and s.34(3); award stamped at signing (*URC Construction v AAI*, Del HC, 1 Sep 2026); execution in the civil court where assets lie (*Sundaram Finance v Abdul Samad*, (2018) 3 SCC 622).
> - **Lok Adalat:** pre-litigation bulk referral under LSA Act ss.19–21 (next National Lok Adalat 12 Dec 2026), DLSA list export and award import, instalment awards over 3 months flagged as restructuring; Permanent Lok Adalat (ss.22A–22E) handled as borrower-initiated defensive matters in R9. The RBI ₹20 lakh Lok Adalat ceiling applies to banks and AIFIs only.
> - **Connectors:** the Equator connector and the generic `OdrProvider` adapter for other providers (Presolv360, Sama, Jupitice, CADRE; CSV fallback where no API exists), both implementing Integration Spec Parts 6.9 and 8: `ADRReferralCreated`, `ADRConsentRecorded`, `ADRNeutralAppointed`, `ADRHearingScheduled`, `ADRCaseStatusChanged`, `ADROutcomeRecorded`, `ADROutcomeComplianceUpdated`; and the settlement events `SettlementRequested`, `SettlementOfferIssued`, `SettlementOfferAccepted`, `SettlementApproved`, `SettlementBreached` (Part 6.8). Outcomes create an R1 settlement record or an R9 execution matter.
> - **Udofin (LSP scope):** relays `SettlementRequested`, shows RE-approved offers and Equator links (no separate app), and shows payment links to the RE's account only (CF 10(2)–(3)). Udofin never approves a settlement, never refers a dispute to arbitration and never holds funds.
>
> Tests and acceptance evidence:
>
> - a settlement proposed by the sanctioning officer cannot be approved by that officer or anyone below the next level;
> - a fraud-tagged settlement routes to the Board;
> - a 4-month instalment plan flags restructuring and blocks the closed-settled status until paid;
> - a fresh-exposure request inside 12 months of settlement is blocked;
> - referral without a pre-named institution or recorded post-dispute consent is rejected by the API;
> - the lender role has no endpoint to choose, rank or veto a neutral;
> - a mediation session cannot be recorded;
> - Pact tests pass against the Equator stub, and Equator outage leaves Finbyx operating.
>
> Show me the settlement policy object, the forum-selection table and the ADR state machine for approval before coding."

### Phase 14b — RBI returns engine and supervisory portal workflows

> **Instruction to Claude:** "Before writing the specification, verify: (i) the RBI (NBFC – Supervisory Returns) Directions, 2026, RBI/DoS/2026-27/466 of **31 Jul 2026** (SR) paras 4, 7 and 12–26 against docs/regulations/rbi/, and log the owner's superseded '28 Nov 2025' reference in docs/regulations/errata.md; (ii) the RBI list of returns and, for each pilot return, the current template, record cap and channel on CIMS/Sankalan (fetch date and template hash), recording every difference from SR as a `registry_variance` (RR1.4: the DNBS04A/04B ₹100 crore BL test, the DNBS08/09 qualifier, ARC rows, the Form A channel); (iii) that CIMS system-to-system (ADF) collection is not confirmed for NBFCs, so that adapter stays flagged off; (iv) FIU-IND formats and PML Rules r.8 clocks, the CKYCR 10/7-day and CERSAI 30-day clocks and ITA25 s.508 Forms 165 and 166; (v) the HFC, bank, UCB, StCB/DCCB, ARC and IFSCA rows, which load as `ACTIVE_UNVERIFIED`. Then build Part 7B 7B.0, RR1–RR5 and RR8 (bureau files follow in Phase 14c):
>
> - **7B.0 boundaries:** prepare, never file; no field for any regulator user ID, password, OTP, DSC PIN, cookie or token, and no RPA or scraping (a static scan fails the build if an HTTP client targets a regulator domain); a portal-user alias register only; email filing only as an RBI-advised contingency, followed by `ONLINE_RESUBMISSION_PENDING` (SR para 18).
> - **RR1 registry and applicability:** regulator → portal → definition → version → due instance → run; 21 return definitions (the 20 items of SR para 21, with item 4 split into DNBS04A and DNBS04B), with due rules `+21D`, `+15D`, `WED_NEXT_WEEK`, `+5WD_FROM_AUDIT_REPORT_CAP_31DEC`, `+14D_FROM_CLASSIFICATION` and `+6H_FROM_DETECTION`; CEL applicability rules with citations and a decision log; an applicability change closes future instances with `APPLICABILITY_CHANGED` and never deletes past ones; no other-institution row can generate a filing until a named reviewer verifies it.
> - **RR2 elements and lineage:** data elements with RBI harmonised-definition references, dimensions, unit and scale; source mapping to GL, loan, exposure, liquidity, capital, investment, fraud and DLA stores; a frozen `reporting_snapshot`; cell maps; per-cell lineage with masked drill-down (SR para 15); ad hoc subset queries (para 13); DQ metrics (para 17); independent approval of each cell-map version (para 7). DNBS03 and DNBS04A/04B map to the Phase 14 capital and ALM runs; Phase 14d swaps the source runs without changing the cell maps.
> - **RR3 generation and sign-off:** the RR3.1 state table (entry condition, owner, allowed actions, exit, failure and rollback for every state) with REPAIR, PORTAL_REJECTED, REVISION_REQUESTED and contingency branches; template hash check, only unprotected cells filled; versioned YAML/CEL validation rules (ERROR blocks; WARNING needs a maker comment and checker acceptance), including cross-return and portal rule packs; TB reconciliation with tolerance equal to the template rounding unit and an explained-variance register; the RR3.5 maker-checker-signatory matrix (the CRO and CCO are never makers; GOV para 21; CMP para 27); a signed package (`manifest.json`, detached JWS with the tenant KMS key); NIL returns with the same approvals.
> - **RR4 portal workflows:** guided checklists and acknowledgement capture for CIMS (above 2,000 records the web form is refused and file upload forced), DAKSH (6-hour cyber timer from detection; nomination coverage), PRAVAAH (application pack builder with a Board-resolution gate), NABARD ENSURE, IFSCA (USD), FIU-IND FINGate 2.0 (STRs hidden from non-AML roles; no tipping off), CKYCR, CERSAI satisfaction on closure and income-tax SFT.
> - **RR5:** the RR5.3 revision assessment (each trigger — RBI query, audit adjustment, back-dated posting into a filed period, DQ finding, re-approved statements — assessed as `REVISE` or `NO_REVISION` by the CCO with reasons); due instances 13 months ahead plus event-driven instances; alerts at T−7, T−3, T−1 and on breach; evidence vault in the Part 7J folder paths; `ACKNOWLEDGED` needs the uploaded acknowledgement and the confirmed reference; revisions as run n+1 with a cell diff, version n preserved; the `supervisory_item` register; retention 10 years from filing.
> - **RR8:** CRILC Main for borrowers with aggregate fund and non-fund exposure of ₹5 crore or more (union of SR para 21 item 5 and RSA para 20, tenant toggle and variance row); DNBS09 move-in and move-out from SMA-0 events reconciled to M6; LEF with immediate breach intimation; monthly WD/LD files to all four CICs (suit-filed and non-suit-filed separate; removal within 30 days below ₹25 lakh); FMR, FUA and FMR4-RBR from the fraud module (FRM paras 42, 45–49); no RFA category for NBFCs.
> - **Menus, screens and settings:** build workspace K (Compliance and Regulatory Reporting), with the signatory queue for workspace M exactly as the returns rows of the `Menu and screens` and `Settings and options` subsections of Part 7B (RR9) specify (navigation paths, list, detail, wizard, approval-queue and dashboard screens, actions, bulk actions, filters, exports, empty and error states, role visibility, and each setting with its scope, default and floor), and register every entry in Appendix G; the filing calendar is the landing screen of workspace K; due rules, validation packs and the sign-off matrix are versioned settings that can add checks or signatories but never loosen an SR timeline or remove a required signatory.

Return status metadata reaches the Operations Hub only where the tenant opts in, and never amounts.

> - **RR6.4–RR6.6 routing, packs and mapping:** individuals → Consumer; non-individuals and guarantors → Commercial with the Relationship segment; microfinance → MFI only, never also Consumer; each co-borrower in its own format; format packs as versioned data (segments, tag-length-value, catalogues, validations, file names, cycle codes DL/W1/W2/W3/ME/DC/AH/RR, `FINBYX` and the release version as MFI vendor identifier); generator-enforced mapping ('settled' only for a waiver for financial inability, CIR para 12(4); IBC admission as suit-filed 01 or 05 NCLT/NCLAT; wilful default only ML and above; DPD cap 900 consumer and 999 MFI; CKYC number as ID type 09; commercial written-off and settled amounts enforced from 1 Apr 2027).
> - **RR6.7 build and transmit:** freeze → extract → route → validate against the pack and the CICs' uniform data-acceptance rules (ERROR records to a repair queue, never silently dropped) → four outputs from one dataset → nodal-officer approval of counts by segment, status and DPD bucket → SFTP from a lender-controlled host or tenant agent, with SFTP and PGP keys in the tenant vault (BYOK; unreadable by Finbyx staff; CIBIL correction uploads unencrypted, other CICs per their own specification) → acknowledgement; the RR6.7 state machine with its exception paths (a nodal-officer rejection rebuilds all four outputs together; transmission failures retry with back-off for 2 hours, then alert bureau operations and the nodal officer, and escalate to the CCO at due − 1 day; a late file raises a compliance issue); `BureauFileGenerated`, `BureauFileSubmitted`.
> - **RR7 rejections, data quality and disputes:** rejection reports and file-level DQI ingested within 3 days into `bureau_rejection` keyed by uniform reason code; repair at source, never a hand-edited file; resubmission as cycle `RR` before or with the next reference-date file; ageing escalation to the nodal officer and the CCO; monthly CI-level DQI and the half-yearly review to top management within two months (CIR para 17); an SMS or email alert at submission of default data on 1600-series service headers that never delays the file (CIR para 34(1)(i)); the dispute state machine with the 21-day CI clock and 30-day overall clock (CICRA s.21(3); CIR para 35), ₹100 a day compensation apportioned per CIR para 35(4) by the RR7.4 formula, rounded to the paisa by largest remainder so that the shares sum to the total [owner to confirm the paisa rounding], and paid within 5 working days (CIR para 35(9)); `BureauRejectionReceived`, `BureauCorrectionRequested`, `BureauCorrectionCompleted`; nodal-officer changes notified to every CIC within 5 days. Disputes link to M15 grievances when Phase 15 delivers them; until then they run in their own register.

> - **CM1 entitlements:** fetch the signed catalogue, verify its JWS against the pinned Hub key and its schema, store it read-only, and keep the previous version live on failure; every SKU maps to modules whose `module.yaml` carries `licence_sku`; entitlements come only from the Hub; capacity, rate and environment limits with hard, soft or informational behaviour; server-side checks on every API call, workflow step, worker and UI slot returning `not_entitled`, `limit_reached`, `not_enabled`, `dependency_missing` or `read_only`; tenant flags only narrow; downgrades go through the Part 7A.0.5 detach workflow; a signed offline licence file for dedicated deployments; the last valid entitlement kept 30 days if the Hub is unreachable; **no kill switch and no remote deletion**.
> - **CM1.4 regulatory-continuity guard-rail:** no commercial state stops COB, accruals, classification, provisioning, close, already-sanctioned disbursement, servicing, receipts, refunds, document release, CIC files, returns, FIU-IND and incident notices, grievance and RB-IOS workflows, borrower statements, contact-policy controls, the audit trail, read access, export, or auditor and supervisor access; hard limits apply only to new non-regulated units.
> - **CM2 pages:** the CM2.2 menu `Settings › Plan and billing` (Overview, Compare plans, Add-ons, Usage with dispute, Invoices, Payment methods and mandates on hosted pages only, Billing contacts, Cancel or downgrade) and `Settings › Users and roles › Seats`; the CM2.4 plan-change workflow (DRAFT → PREVIEWED → SUBMITTED → APPROVED → ORDERED → SCHEDULED → EFFECTIVE) with a Hub-priced proration preview, the entitlement diff, a second approver for increases above threshold and every downgrade, and entitlements changed only on the signed `EntitlementChanged`; `billing_admin` (MFA on every change), `billing_viewer` and `tenant_admin`; plain-language explainers from the catalogue, with a downgrade explainer on every item; a CI content check rejecting 'guarantees compliance' or any certification claim without an EO5 issued-report or certificate record (the EO5 claims register is created empty in this phase and completed in Phase 20b); no dark patterns; cancellation no harder than purchase.
> - **CM3 metering:** `active_loans`, `aum_band` (own share only for co-lent loans), users, branches, `regulatory_runs` (re-runs not billed), `api_calls`, `storage_gb` and pass-through meters, computed from ledgers, idempotent on `(tenant, meter, source_ref, period)` and reconciled nightly; `UsageRecorded` carries aggregates and a statement hash only, never a loan, borrower, member or user identifier; a 7-day dispute window; no meter priced per recovered rupee, notice or connected call.
> - **CM4 payments:** redirect or payment links only, with no Razorpay script on Finbyx pages, plus CSP and a script inventory; Finbyx holds no Razorpay keys and never treats a browser return as proof of payment; strict separation from tenant loan-money rails (M7; CF paras 10(1)–(3)); recurring debits above ₹15,000 go to eNACH or bank transfer; a T−48-hour courtesy notice; GST invoices and TDS certificate upload; dunning ACTIVE → PAST_DUE → RETRY → GRACE → RESTRICTED (D+30 after 7 days' notice) → TERMINATION_NOTICE (D+45) → EXIT (Part 7J DP5), never a hard cancel.
> - **CM5 revenue streams:** read `revenue_stream_flags`; show a purchase option only if its stream has an approved legality-gate record; the vendor-announcements panel never appears inside lending workflows or borrower surfaces; sandbox self-serve rejects PAN- or Aadhaar-like uploads; a production tenant only after a signed MSA, DPA and customer due diligence. No fee from borrowers, no data monetisation, no paid ranking.
> - **Menus, screens and settings:** build workspace N (Tenant Administration: Plans, billing and membership) exactly as the `Menu and screens` and `Settings and options` subsections of Part 7K specify (navigation paths, list, detail, wizard, approval-queue and dashboard screens, actions, bulk actions, filters, exports, empty and error states, role visibility, and each setting with its scope, default and floor), and register every entry in Appendix G; downgrade, cancellation and exit are reachable in no more steps than purchase, and every plan item links to its plain-language explainer.
>
> Tests and acceptance evidence:
>
> - a catalogue signed with an unknown key is rejected and the previous version stays live; a SKU naming an unknown module fails import;
> - a tenant without the Investments SKU gets `403 not_entitled` on every Part 7H API even with the tenant flag on;
> - an expired subscription with an overdue invoice still runs COB, files the CIC file due on the 16th and lets a borrower download a statement; a RESTRICTED tenant still disburses a sanctioned loan but cannot create a user;
> - replaying a disbursement event three times yields one usage record; `UsageRecorded` passes the schema test forbidding identifiers;
> - the billing page HTML contains no third-party script; a 'success' redirect without Hub confirmation leaves the invoice unpaid;
> - an ₹18,000 recurring card debit is not set up as a no-AFA mandate;
> - an explainer claiming 'certified' without an EO5 record fails CI;
> - a navigation test walks each role through the Appendix G entries for this phase and finds every screen, action and setting with the stated visibility and nothing more; the cancellation path has no more steps than the purchase path.
>
> Show me the SKU-to-module map, the entitlement check matrix, the regulatory-continuity list written as tests, the meter definitions and the dunning timeline, with the menu tree and settings catalogue of this phase (Appendix G), for approval before coding."

### Phase 17b — Secured enforcement and shared-exposure recovery

> **Instruction to Claude:** "Before writing the specification, verify: (i) each pilot tenant's SARFAESI eligibility evidence (last audited assets and the NBFC thresholds of ₹100 crore of assets and ₹20 lakh of debt under S.O. 652(E), 12 Feb 2021) and any RDB s.2(h)(ii) notification for the tenant; (ii) IBC commencement notices after S.O. 2625(E) of 22 May 2026 (CIIRP, group insolvency and cross-border provisions not in force as of 19 Oct 2026); (iii) access to BAANKNET and to the Vahan financier services. Then build:
>
> - **R4 SARFAESI enforcement:** eligibility gate (NBFC thresholds; HFCs as notified financial institutions; s.31 exclusions including pledges, agricultural land and claims of ₹1 lakh or less or below 20% of principal plus interest); CERSAI registration gate (s.26D); limitation gate (s.36); state machine 13(2) notice → 13(3A) reply within 15 days → 60-day cure → possession notice and publication within 7 days (Rule 8(1)–(2)) → s.14 application → valuation and reserve → sale notice (Rule 8(6)) → auction no earlier than 30 days (15 for a re-sale; Rule 9(1)) → 25% deposit the same or next working day → balance within 15 days of confirmation, or up to 3 months by written extension (Rule 9(3)–(4); *M.R. Vasumathi v Authorized Officer*, SC, 9 Jun 2026) → sale certificate → s.13(7) appropriation → surplus or shortfall; redemption closing on publication of the sale notice (s.13(8); *Celir LLP v Bafna Motors*, SC, 21 Sep 2023; *M. Rajendran v KPK Oils*, 2025 INSC 1144); borrower's s.17 window of 45 days tracked in R9; possessed-asset website feed updated monthly (CIR 21).
> - **R5 civil and tribunal remedies:** DRT original applications only for RDB-eligible lenders (₹20 lakh threshold, S.O. 4312(E) of 6 Sep 2018); an NBFC is not eligible unless notified under s.2(h)(ii) (*Tata Motors Finance v Naushad Khan*, Bom HC, 2023; *Aditya Birla Finance v Anjali Nag*, Del HC, 2024); e-DRT filing for all pleadings from 23 Jun 2025; Order XXXVII summary suits; commercial suits with the s.12A gate from R8; execution under Order XXI; the forum for an un-notified NBFC's s.13(10) shortfall application [VERIFY].
> - **R6 insolvency (IBC):** NeSL information-utility record of default; s.7 applications for defaults of ₹1 crore or more within Art. 137 limitation, with admission tracked against s.7(5) as amended (14 days, from 26 May 2026); Form C claims by the public-announcement date and late-claim rules; CoC vote log; personal-guarantor applications at the NCLT (s.95; no interim moratorium against personal guarantors to corporate debtors, s.96(4) as amended); moratorium watcher that freezes R4, R7 and R10 actions against the corporate debtor; liquidation auctions on BAANKNET; CIIRP kept off in the rule pack until notified.
> - **R10 repossession, valuation, auction and sale:** vehicles (contractual notice period elapsed, daytime repossession by an authorised agent with ID and authorisation, signed possession memo and inventory, no force; RBC 26; *Hari Dutta Sharma v State of UP*, SC, 16 Sep 2026; Form 36 re-registration under MV Act s.51(5)); gold (RBC 60–66; reserve from the IBJA or exchange feed; surplus within 7 working days); LAS and LAMF invocation and sale (Part 6.4.7); SARFAESI immovable and movable sales; valuer panel and reserve worksheet; e-auction listings through the Phase 16b connectors; `AssetRepossessed`, `AuctionScheduled`, `AuctionConcluded`, `CollateralInvoked`, `SurplusRefunded` (Integration Spec Parts 6.5 and 6.8).
> - **R13 shared-exposure recovery:** co-lending decision matrix (servicer RE decides contact; each RE settles its own share under its own Board policy; joint SARFAESI needs secured creditors holding at least 60% by value, s.13(9)); classification sync by the end of the next working day (TDCR 124, `ClassificationSynced`); recoveries after DLG invocation kept off the loan account (CF 25(2)); transferred loans (each party resolves its own economic interest, TDCR 19(2); binding invocation mechanism for security held in trust, TDCR 21; servicer trust accounts and certified data, TDCR 29–30, 41–42); securitisation servicing (remit all cash flows, no commingling, SEC 95–96; servicer replacement, SEC 70); stressed-loan sale and ARC transfer (Board review, valuations, Swiss challenge, permitted transferees, s.29A check, cash only, cooling period; TDCR 56–94; substitution of the assignee in pending cases); consortium and ICA vote engine (75% by value and 60% by number; dissenters at least liquidation value; RSA 31–33, 45–48); `LoanTransferred` and `ServicerChanged` (Integration Spec Part 6.6).
> - **R16 product recovery playbooks:** one playbook per product code in Part 6.3 (and the co-lending overlay), each binding the mechanism profile, notice templates, clocks, conduct overlay and accounting map; tenant-editable within guard-rails.
>
> Tests and acceptance evidence:
>
> - SARFAESI is blocked for a tenant below the threshold, for a debt below ₹20 lakh and for a charge not on CERSAI;
> - a sale balance received on day 16 with no written extension blocks the sale certificate and opens the forfeiture workflow;
> - a vehicle repossession task cannot start before the notice period ends or without an authorised agent;
> - a gold auction reserve below 90% (85% after two failed auctions) is rejected;
> - an IBC admission for a corporate debtor freezes SARFAESI and invocation actions against it;
> - a 90:10 co-lent account cannot start SARFAESI on the 10% lender's vote alone;
> - an ICA decision with 76% by value but 55% by number fails;
> - every product code has an approved R16 playbook.
>

### Phase 18b — Voice, AI contact-centre and Jio adapters

> **Instruction to Claude:** "Before writing the specification, verify: (i) the TRAI Direction of 19 Nov 2025 and clarification of 10 Jul 2026 on 1600-series numbers (from 1 Jan 2026 for banks; 1 Feb 2026 for NBFCs above ₹5,000 crore, payments banks and SFBs; 1 Mar 2026 for other NBFCs, co-operative banks and RRBs; the 1601 sub-series), TCCCPR 2018 as amended 12 Feb 2025 (140-series, DND, auto-dialler notice), and whether credit co-operative societies can obtain 1600-series numbers; (ii) RBC paras 91(2), 100 and 100P, the Second Amendment para 101I (consent default 'No' from 1 Jan 2027) and the RBC Third Amendment pack (RBI/2026-27/230) already in Phases 3b, 11 and 12; (iii) RBI FREE-AI (13 Aug 2025) and the M20 controls; (iv) for each candidate provider (JioCX, Jio Business SIP and toll-free, Exotel, Ozonetel, Gupshup, Knowlarity; Sarvam AI or Bhashini for speech): DLT principal-entity support, 1600-series support, India residency for recordings, transcripts and call records, India inference, DPA and API documentation. JioCX publishes no API documentation, rates, residency statement or AI voice-agent product, and reports of a 'JioBrain' API are uncorroborated — do not rely on them. Then build Part 7L EO6 on M18 and R15:
>
> - **Interfaces:** `MessagingProvider` (SMS with DLT ids, RCS, email; WhatsApp never for collection, recovery or legal notices), `VoiceProvider` (number pools by series and circle, IVR, dialler and OBD, click-to-call with masking, recording, CDR webhooks), `SpeechProvider` (Indic ASR and TTS) and `LLMProvider` (the M20 India-region endpoint only); each passes connector certification (Integration Spec Parts 10.1 and 14.3) before production.
> - **Jio plan:** a stub `JioCxAdapter` with certification tests, and a request list to JioCX (API documentation, DPA, residency proof, DLT and 1600-series support, AI roadmap, rates); production enablement only after contract, residency proof and certification; other certified adapters serve tenants meanwhile. The owner's Jio requirement is met by the adapter, not by a dependency on Jio.
> - **Contact-policy checks (fail closed with a reason):** purpose category; the tenant as DLT principal entity and number holder, never Infrabyx; RE service, transactional and recovery voice only from the tenant's 1600-series numbers — no other number even with consent; promotional voice only through a 140-series registered telemarketer with DND scrub and explicit consent; non-RE tenants through telemarketer routes until 1600 eligibility is confirmed; consent default 'No' from 1 Jan 2027 and 90 days before re-seeking after opt-out; recovery 08:00–19:00, microfinance 09:00–18:00 until 31 Dec 2026 then the Third Amendment pack; a stricter borrower preference prevails; by default ≤ 3 attempts and 1 connected recovery call a day; auto-diallers pre-notified; a DLT template id on every SMS.
> - **AI contact centre:** the inbound assistant authenticates (registered mobile plus OTP, or IVR PIN) before disclosing anything, answers balance, due date, receipt and document-release status, raises service requests and M15 complaints and hands over to a human on request; outbound AI voice for reminders and receipt confirmations, and for recovery only under a Board-approved policy with CCO-approved scripts; AI never negotiates or approves settlements or waivers, changes terms, closes or rejects complaints, threatens, misstates dues, discloses to third parties or takes card data; it states that it is an automated assistant; each interaction logs model, model and prompt versions and the transcript reference; monthly QA and bias sampling; a recording announcement on every recorded call; recordings, transcripts and call records stay in India, and recovery recordings are kept at least 6 months and longer while sub judice (RBC para 100P).
> - **Residency gate and metering:** no adapter is enabled for a production tenant without proof of India storage and India inference; voice, SMS, WhatsApp and AI minutes are metered as CM3 pass-through with cost per call; records use the existing R15 entities, with no new ecosystem events.
> - **Menus, screens and settings:** build workspaces G (Collections) and F (Servicing and Customer Service) for calling and the assistant, and N for provider settings exactly as the `Menu and screens` and `Settings and options` subsections of Part 7L (EO6) specify (navigation paths, list, detail, wizard, approval-queue and dashboard screens, actions, bulk actions, filters, exports, empty and error states, role visibility, and each setting with its scope, default and floor), and register every entry in Appendix G; contact windows and attempt caps can only be tightened; the provider screen shows certification and residency-proof status before the production toggle is enabled.

> Tests and acceptance evidence:

> - a microfinance recovery call at 18:15 in December 2026 is refused;
