# APPENDIX A — CLAUDE.md SEED (keep concise and stable)

```markdown
# Finbyx — Claude Code Project Instructions

## What this is
Finbyx: multi-tenant web LOS + LMS + accounting + collections/recovery + risk +
regulatory reporting + compliance + audit + governance for Indian lenders (NBFC/HFC/UCB/banks,
co-operatives, ARCs, CICs and investment companies, IFSC entities).
Part of the Infrabyx ecosystem (Udofin LSP, LawDocsComply GRC, Equator ODR, Operations Hub) — integrate
only via versioned contracts. Full brief: docs/00-master-prompt.md.

## Non-negotiables
- Feature branches + PRs only. Never push to main, deploy to prod, touch prod data or
  rotate live credentials without explicit owner approval.
- Spec → approval → code. Explain logic in plain English before code. Small commits.
- Never claim a test passed unless run; paste results. Mark mocks vs live clearly.
- No secrets, real borrower data, Aadhaar/PAN/OTP/account numbers in code, logs or fixtures.
- Money: NUMERIC in DB, decimal.js in TS, strings in APIs. Never floats.
- Ledger is append-only and always balanced; corrections by reversal only.
- Every financial write is idempotent; state machines govern all lifecycle changes.
- Tenant/entity/branch isolation enforced in API, services AND Postgres RLS — and tested.
- Regulatory parameters live in versioned rule packs with guard-rails; tenants cannot
  override regulatory safeguards.
- Before any regulated workflow: verify the current RBI/other source and update
  docs/compliance/requirements-to-controls.md. Distinguish law vs interpretation.
- AI never approves/rejects/prices loans, moves money, rejects complaints or alters terms.
- Data stays in India (prod data, backups, logs, SaaS sub-processors). Railway or any non-India host:
  synthetic data only.
- KFS validity is not a waiting period; COB never accrues income on an account turning NPA.
- Part 8A citations are verified against the official RBI texts in docs/regulations/rbi/; prefer them
  over any other citation. ORM IDs are guidance, not Directions. Drafting slips: docs/regulations/errata.md.
- Ecosystem contracts: docs/ecosystem/infrabyx-integration-spec.md is canonical; propose new events,
  never invent them locally.
- Recovery Suite (Part 7A) is attachable: entitlement + flag checked server-side; detach =
  read-only + export pack; never delete regulated, legal or recovery records.
- Recovery: hard statutory gates before irreversible steps (SARFAESI eligibility and CERSAI,
  limitation, IBC moratorium, notice served with evidence); contact only in permitted hours;
  no one-sided arbitration (institution pre-named or written post-dispute consent); LSPs never
  approve settlements, issue legal notices in their own name or hold funds.
- Filings (RBI, NHB, NABARD, IFSCA, CICs, MCA, GST, income tax, exchanges): prepare → validate →
  reconcile → evidence; an authorised human approves and files. Never store or script portal
  credentials, OTPs, DSC tokens or PINs.
- Co-operative societies: no deposits from nominal/non-voting members (hard block); no co-lending
  with, or loan sale to, NBFCs (not REs).
- Investments: record, check, value, account and report. Never execute trades or give advice.
- Certifications are a readiness programme: never claim ISO/SOC 2/PCI status before issue.
- Archive exports must open without Finbyx (folders, XLSX/DOCX/PDF-A, manifest, README); export
  and read access never stop for non-payment.
- Menus and settings come from registries (Appendix G): no hand-coded tenant menus; regulatory-floor
  settings are enforced server-side and can never be relaxed; regulated decisions always need a human.
- v1.5 Parts 7B–7L and Part 8A.37; group operations live in the Operations Hub, not in Finbyx.

## Commands
(pnpm install / dev / test / lint / typecheck / db:migrate / db:test — fill in Phase 1)

## Where things live
docs/00-master-prompt.md (full brief), docs/architecture, docs/adr, docs/specs, docs/products,
docs/data-model, docs/api, docs/integrations, docs/compliance, docs/security,
docs/testing (golden-cases), docs/ops, docs/legal, docs/economics, docs/status.

## Definition of done
Acceptance criteria met; unit/integration/E2E/tenant-isolation/security tests run and
passed; ledger balances & reconciles; audit events emitted; docs and registers updated;
diff reviewed for secrets/PII/unrelated changes.
```

# APPENDIX E — REVISION LOG

## E.1 v1.0 → v1.1 (18 October 2026)

v1.1 corrects the errors found in an independent regulatory and technical review of v1.0. Claude Code must follow v1.1. The v1.0 statements listed below are withdrawn.

| # | Area | v1.0 statement (withdrawn) | v1.1 correction |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Usage | Paste Parts 1–13; save the prompt after approval | Commit the whole file (including the appendices) as `docs/00-master-prompt.md` before Session 1. Phase 0 reads it from the repository |
| 2 | KFS | 3/1 working-day "consideration period before execution" | KFS **validity** period under RBC para 29(2): the lender is bound for ≥ 3 working days (≥ 1 if tenor < 7 days). It is not a waiting period |
| 3 | COB | Accruals before borrower-level NPA classification; interest recalculation after accruals | Two-pass COB with a cross-loan classification barrier. Income derecognition happens before accrual on accounts that turn NPA |
| 4 | Hosting | Railway "Mumbai region" | Railway has no India region: synthetic data only. Real data only on India-region hosts. All SaaS sub-processors must pass a residency check |
| 5 | Aadhaar vault | UIDAI Circular 8 of 2025 | UIDAI Circular No. 14 of 2025 (4 Nov 2025): on-premises, GCC or ADV-as-a-service only; FIPS 140-2 L3+ HSM |
| 6 | Recovery agents | "Recovery-agent amendment"; visits only after failed contact attempts; MFI window 09:00–18:00 shown as permanent | RBC Third Amendment Directions, 2026 (paras 100A–100AB, from 1 Jan 2027). Visit conditions per para 100Y(5). Call recording per para 100P. Effective-dated MFI window. Separate marketing window 09:00–19:00 (para 101N(4)) |
| 7 | Gold loans | Release and auction cited to Credit Facilities Ch IV; release cited to RBC 35–41 | LTV, caps and bullet loans: CF Ch IV. Release and auction: RBC Ch III.G (paras 58, 60–66) |
| 8 | Loans against securities | 50% LTV and Group 1 for all NBFC LAS (shares, bonds, MF) | Applies only to loans against shares by NBFCs with assets ≥ ₹100 crore (CF para 106), with conditions. Para 105 prohibits loans against own shares |
| 9 | CIC | Rework rejected data "within 7 days"; dates marked as unverified | Effective-dated: fortnightly with 7-day rejection rework until 30 Jun 2026; reference dates 9/16/23/month-end and rework by the next submission from 1 Jul 2026 (RBI/DOR/2025-26/117). ₹100/day after 30 days, with a 21-day lender leg |
| 10 | eSign | DP note listed as eSign-capable | DP notes (negotiable instruments) and powers of attorney go to the physical-execution path (IT Act First Schedule) |
| 11 | GST | Penal charges "CBIC circular Jan 2025 [VERIFY]"; e-invoicing unclear | No GST on penal charges: CBIC Circular 245/02/2025-GST, 28 Jan 2025. NBFCs are exempt from e-invoicing (Notification 13/2020-CT) |
| 12 | Fraud | "EWS/RFA" | NBFC Directions use EWS (UL/ML) and have no RFA. Applies to UL, ML and BL ≥ ₹500 crore. Show-cause ≥ 21 days. FMR within 14 days |
| 13 | CFSS | Not mentioned | Core Financial Services Solution mandate (Misc. Supervisory Directions 2026, Ch II) added as a product requirement |
| 14 | Revolving credit | Flagged for Product 12 only | The Aug 2026 draft affects Products 1, 3, 7 and 12. Build term-loan structures by default |
| 15 | Co-lending | "Interest split by hurdle rate"; escrow unspecified | Single blended (funding-share-weighted) rate. Escrow held with a bank |
| 16 | Prepayment | Para 34 only; layer rules unspecified | Paras 33–34, with rules for all NBFCs, the Upper Layer and the Middle Layer (₹50 lakh) |
| 17 | DLG | 5% "of covered portfolio"; paras unverified | ≤ 5% of the amount disbursed out of the portfolio (para 24). Invocation within 120 days (para 27). DLG term ≥ longest tenor |
| 18 | Fineract | Wrong strategy codes; `rbi-india-strategy` as universal default; all reschedule strategies on all engines; partially disbursed ≠ Active; technical write-off = Closed; "reset" delinquency action; schema-per-tenant | Codes corrected. RBI order also expressed as an advanced-allocation rule set. Engine constraints stated. Lifecycle corrected. Database-per-tenant. PostgreSQL 18 |
| 19 | Fineract oracle | Run in CI on every PR | Nightly or on-demand on a large runner. PR CI uses golden fixtures |
| 20 | Money precision | `NUMERIC(9,6)` rates; decimal.js defaults | Rates `NUMERIC(12,8)`; APR/EIR `NUMERIC(14,10)`; decimal.js precision ≥ 40 |
| 21 | RLS | RLS stated without enforcement details | Non-owner role, `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY`, `SET LOCAL` context, zero-rows test |
| 22 | Roadmap | Pilot launch depended on all 20 phases; field app and communications had no phase; Udofin connector late; SARFAESI before secured products | Added Phases 3b, 8b, 8c and P (pilot go-live). SARFAESI, repossession and auction moved to Phase 17. Phases 17–20 split into separate instructions |
| 23 | Licences | AG Grid and Metabase embedding unqualified | AG Grid Community or TanStack by default; Superset for embedded MIS; open-source JDM editor (not the GoRules BRMS) |
| 24 | Coverage | No audit of the current Finbyx product; no competitor benchmark; grievance host switch missing; no SSO or app distribution | Added to Phase 0, M14, M19 and M22, with a concurrency target |
| 25 | Other | DPDP breach "Board within 72 hours"; Schedule III Div III only; Cyber VAPT/DR shown for all NBFCs; NSDL e-Gov naming | Intimation without delay, then the 72-hour report. Division I for non-Ind AS entities. Cyber obligations by chapter. Protean naming |

## E.2 v1.1 → v1.2 (18 October 2026): official RBI texts supplied by the project owner

v1.2 checks the prompt against the official text of 15 Directions: CF 347, CIR 349, CRM 350, CON 351, INV 354, BR 342, ALM 355, FS 359, CLM 364, AA 368, CMP 460, CYB 461, DPS 462, FRM 463 and AUD 468. Part 8A is new and holds the paragraph-level requirements. The corrections to earlier text are:

| # | Area | v1.1 statement (withdrawn) | v1.2 correction (source) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Cash recovery | Cash "must reach the lender's account the same day" | Must be reflected in full **in the borrower's loan account** on the same day, with no LSP fee deducted (CF 10(5)) |
| 2 | CIC default alerts | "Intimation **before** reporting default to CICs" | SMS/email alerts sent **while submitting** default/DPD data (CIR 34(1)(i)) |
| 3 | CIC timelines | Single regime | Effective-dated: fortnightly and 7-day rejection rework until 30 Jun 2026; 9/16/23/month-end and next-file rework from 1 Jul 2026 (CIR 10(2), 15). Sources link corrected to Id=13187 |
| 4 | Compliance function | "CCO certification"; CCO approval only for the payday template | No CCO certification is prescribed. Approval before launch applies to **every** new product and process for ML/UL, with 6-month monitoring (CMP 9(7), 15(2), 31). Applies to ML/UL only |
| 5 | Fraud | Summary only | Full lifecycle: three dates, natural justice, SCBMF, EWS (UL/ML), FMR per case, debarment, closure, legal audit, transfer gate, RBR (FRM 4–58). No RFA, no red-flag annex, no CIC reporting of fraud |
| 6 | DLG | Generic forms; "classification not affected" | Provider eligibility, precise forms, fixed DLG set, auditor-certified declaration, IRACP treatment, no set-off, no reinstatement, monthly LSP disclosure (CF 19–29) |
| 7 | Gold loans | Partial rules | Eligible collateral, prohibitions, valuation source and purity, slab basis, renewal/top-up, weight caps, para 47 money flows (CF 32–50) |
| 8 | Microfinance | "Unsecured" product | Every collateral-free loan to a household with income ≤ ₹3 lakh is microfinance, with a 50% household repayment cap and a block on new loans while above it (CF 51–62) |
| 9 | LAS | "Shares" | Listed shares only; Annex-III reporting; block on gold/silver ETF/MF collateral (CF 35(2), 106) |
| 10 | Products | No project finance or demand/call loans | Products 20 and 21 added; housing/CRE classification; PCE rules (CF 63–111) |
| 11 | Concentration | Generic limits [VERIFY] | Layer-wise limits, exposure computation, UL LEF with breach block and monthly return (CON) |
| 12 | Credit risk | Absent | Related-party lending (thresholds, routing, recusal), LEI gate, CDS, CERSAI types, own-debenture block (CRM) |
| 13 | CERSAI | "Within 30 days (s.23)" only | Four charge types filed on an ongoing basis (CRM 27–28); the 30-day period comes from SARFAESI/CERSAI Rules [VERIFY] |
| 14 | ALM | Generic | Buckets, tolerance limits, slotting rules, stock ratios, IRS, DNBS04A (quarterly) / 04B (monthly), daily LCR engine (ALM). "DNBS04A for BL ≥ ₹100 crore" withdrawn: the ₹100 crore test applies to every layer |
| 15 | Financial statements | Generic notes-to-accounts packs | FS disclosure engine (C.1/C.2/C.3), Impairment Reserve rules, Ind AS governance registers, LCR disclosure from daily values |
| 16 | Climate | Not covered | CLM is a green-deposit framework for NBFC-D and deposit-taking HFCs only |
| 17 | Investments; branches | Not covered | INV and BR requirements added (M10 item 7A; M1) |
| 18 | Cyber | Chapter thresholds partly right; repeal of the 2023 MD asserted | Ch III also covers all CICs; Ch V excludes CICs. Para 155 repeals via PPG.66 without naming the 2023 MD. Numeric RTO not prescribed. Vendor obligations (new Part 10.6), STP, regulator/auditor access, IPv6 |
| 19 | Digital payments | Not covered | DPS applies only to card-issuing NBFCs; adopted as the voluntary baseline for M7/M22/M23 |
| 20 | Account Aggregator | "TSP" list | Tenant is the FIU; AA and gateway recorded separately; FIP obligation for deposit-takers (AA 29); Finbyx is never an AA |
| 21 | Auditor's report | Not covered | Auditor evidence packs and DNBS10 support (AUD 6–11) |

## E.3 v1.2 → v1.3 (18 October 2026): further official RBI texts supplied by the project owner

v1.3 checks the prompt against the official text of 18 further Directions and 1 guidance note: IRACP 356, RSA 357, RBC 362, WD 358, KYC 361, TDCR 352, SEC 353, CAP 345, SBR 339, DIV 360, MISC 373, GOV 344, OUT 363, ORM (guidance note), MFI 371, IAF 464, SA 465, SR 466 and MSD 467. Part 8A.17–8A.35 hold the paragraph-level requirements; 8A.36 holds the consolidated build additions; Appendix F lists the drafting slips. The corrections to earlier text are:

| # | Area | v1.2 statement (withdrawn) | v1.3 correction (source) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | DPD | DPD = business date − oldest overdue due date | DPD = COB date − oldest unpaid due date + 1 (IRACP 19, Illustration I) |
| 2 | COB classification | Borrower-level classification across co-lending partners and group entities | Borrower-wise within the tenant, including NPI; co-lending sync per M11 (IRACP 23) |
| 3 | Settlements with wilful defaulters | "Settlement restrictions for wilful defaulters" [VERIFY] | Permitted, with Board approval in every case; criminal proceedings and penal measures continue; restructuring is barred (RSA 16(5)(ii), 83–85, 97–98) |
| 4 | CRILC scope | UL/ML and BL ICC/MFI/Factor ≥ ₹500 crore | NBFC-D and NBFC-ND ≥ ₹500 crore, and any NBFC-Factor; monthly ≥ ₹5 crore plus weekly Friday report (RSA 7, 20–21, 158) |
| 5 | HFC scope | Restructuring for all tenants per RSA | HFCs: only RSA paras 86–138; HFC restructuring per HFC Directions [VERIFY] (RSA 5) |
| 6 | OTS closure | "Closed: settled (OTS)" | Settlement paid over more than 3 months, or part settlement, is restructuring until paid (RSA 89–90) |
| 7 | Gold release compensation | "delay compensation [VERIFY amount and para]"; Ch III.G "paras 42–75" | ₹5,000/day beyond the 7-working-day timeline if attributable to the lender (RBC 69); para 42 deleted w.e.f. 1 Apr 2026; assay certificate, auction district rule, related-party bar, surplus refund within 7 working days, unclaimed after 2 years (RBC 43–75) |
| 8 | Penal charges | "RBC para 30 [VERIFY]" | Verified: only on the amount under default, no penal on penal, individual ≤ non-individual, shown in reminders (RBC 30) |
| 9 | Resets | Applies to EMI personal loans only | Also equated-instalment loans of any periodicity, external or internal benchmark; switch to fixed only where the Board policy offers it; quarterly statement contents (RBC 31–32) |
| 10 | Prepayment | Based on the 2 Jul 2025 Pre-payment Charges Directions; layer rules only | RBC 33–34 and 81 incl. source of funds, dual-rate, CC/OD, lender-initiated, undisclosed and waived charges |
| 11 | Document release | 30 days and ₹5,000/day for all loans | Personal loans (RBC 6(11)); 60-day clock for lost documents; choice of office; legal-heir procedure (RBC 35–41) |

It adds Phases 13b, 14b, 14c, 14d, 15b, 16c, 16d, 16e, 17c, 17d, 18b and 20b; Part 8A.37 (non-RBI and later RBI sources, superseded owner references and the v1.5 [VERIFY] register); pointers from M10–M21 and R11; Part 2, 3.1 and 3.2 updates (Operations Hub, new customer types, workspaces S–W); new rows in Parts 9.2 and 10.1; Part 10.2 principles 36–42; the reworded Part 10.6 item 12; and Appendix G (navigation, menus, screens and settings map). # APPENDIX F — DRAFTING SLIPS FOUND IN THE SUPPLIED RBI TEXTS

Seed `docs/regulations/errata.md` from this list (Part 8A.0.1 rule 5). For each slip, implement the evident intent, record the interpretation, and re-check it when RBI issues a corrected or amended text. The v1.2 examples are in Part 8A.0.1 rule 5.

**IRACP / RSA**

- IRACP para 32(2)(i) says "NBFC-BL" in a Chapter II (all-NBFC) rule.
- IRACP para 5 repeats "with these Directions".
- RSA para 23 table: the last row repeats "secured portion" (evidently "unsecured portion").
- RSA para 66 cites para 63 for the additional specific provisions (evidently para 64).
- RSA para 72 cites para 70 for the freeze period, which is set in para 69.
- RSA para 84 contains the artefact "_bookmark20".
- RSA para 108 says CRILC instructions "as per paragraph 107", which covers consortium intimation.
- RSA para 138 is truncated in the official PDF (text reads only "A").
- RSA Part B uses "compromise settlement" without defining it (definition is Part A para 10(2), not applied by para 157).

**RBC / WD**

- RBC para 37: "sanction letters issued on or December 1, 2023" (word "after" missing).
- RBC para 31(3) Note: "where such an option is provided by the bank" (should read NBFC).
- RBC para 43: unclosed parenthesis "(and timeline for serving an auction notice…".
- RBC para 6(9): defines microfinance loan by reference to an "NBFC – Microfinance Institution Directions, 2025", whereas microfinance rules sit in CF Ch V [VERIFY].
- RBC paras 89–97 (recovery and agent rules) sit under Section H (microfinance), while para 100 excludes microfinance loans; the general agent rules are in paras 98–100 only.
- WD Annex I field 10: valid values list "01 - Suit filed" and "– Non-Suit Filed" without the code "02" (Annex II shows 02).
- WD Annex I: field 11 uses "SUBST" and field 12 uses "SUBSTD".
- WD Annex II: field numbering skips 17 (16 → 18).
- WD para 5(15) requires non-whole-time/independent/nominee directors to be flagged in Annex II, but Annex II has no such field, and the Annex I note excludes them.
- WD para 3(1)(xii)(e): cites the SBR "Guidelines, 2025" (the instrument is a Directions).
- WD para 21(1): cites the "Fraud Risk Management in NBFCs Directions, 2024" (now RBI/DoS/2026-27/463, 2026).

**KYC**

- KYC para 23 proviso (v) and para 27(2)(vi)(c) refer to "paragraph 62" for CKYCR. CKYCR is para 63; para 62 is FCRA.
- KYC para 63(7) refers to "clauses (5) and (6)" for the 1 Apr 2017 / 1 Apr 2021 cut-off dates; they are in clauses (4) and (5). It also cites a "clause (10)" that does not exist (para 63 has nine clauses).
- KYC para 28(vi)–(vii) say "Directions (4) and (5)" where they mean clauses (iv) and (v) of para 28.
- Annex I (MHA UAPA Order) numbering skips para 3.3; the Order also cites "Para 4(i)" and "Paragraph 5 (i)", which do not exist in that form. These are reproduced Government text; no software impact.

**TDCR / SEC**

- **TDCR para 2, second proviso vs para 96:** para 2 defines existing CLAs as those "executed before August 06, 2025"; para 96 says "executed before the date of issuance of these Directions" (28 Nov 2025). Implement: CLAs entered into before the effective date follow the earlier rules, and record both dates.
- **TDCR para 83 proviso:** cross-refers to "sub-clause (a)", but the items are numbered (i)–(iv). It is a legacy 2021 transition running to FY 2025-26.
- **TDCR:** paras 1–2 read "Reserve Bank of India of India"; para 95 refers to "a RE"; para 92(2) has "perspective buyers".
- **SEC para 84(3):** reads "rest" for "reset".
- **SEC para 114:** omits "2025" from the FS Directions title.
- **SEC para 4(10) vs TDCR para 12(4):** the SEC AIFI list omits NaBFID; TDCR includes it. Treat as intended; do not harmonise.

**CAP / SBR / DIV / MISC**

- CAP 12(8)(iii) refers to "paragraph 8(i)" (para 8 is CET1 deductions); the intended cross-reference is within 12(8).
- CAP 18(9)(iii) refers to "8(i) and 8(ii)"; it means 18(9)(i)–(ii).
- CAP 50 refers to "paragraph 44" for the thickness adjustment; the formula is in para 45.
- CAP 18(1) places the Sr (2)(e) infrastructure loans under the "Investments" heading.
- DIV para 3 numbers item (x) twice; para 11 numbers item (i) twice; para 7 says "this Master Direction".

**GOV / OUT / ORM**

- CF para 62(2) cites a "Reserve Bank of India (NBFCs – Management of Third-Party Dependencies) Directions, 2025". No such Direction exists; the correct reference is OUT 363 ("Managing Risks in Outsourcing"; para 1), which CF para 6(6) cites correctly.
- GOV para 17(2) takes the IS audit periodicity from the Outsourcing Directions, which prescribe none. Use CYB para 56 for BL ≥ ₹500 crore (at least once a year, preferably before the statutory audit); ML and above set the periodicity in their IS Audit Policy (CYB para 150).
- OUT para 4(2)(i) and para 5(1) cross-refer to para 58(1)/(2) "above"; para 58 comes later.
- OUT para 6(2) defines "Group" by reference to the Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Concentration Risk Management) Directions, 2025, not the NBFC Directions. NBFC CON 351 contains no "group" definition [VERIFY the Commercial Banks text].
- OUT para 57(4) cites the RBI Integrated Ombudsman Scheme, 2021, which RB-IOS 2026 has superseded (effective 1 Jul 2026) [VERIFY: RB-IOS 2026 text not supplied].
- The ORM Guidance Note's RBI number is printed blank ("RBI/2025-26/") in the supplied copy.

**MFI / IAF / SA / SR / MSD**

- SA para 23: "the outgoing SCAs / SAs **of the bank**" in NBFC Directions.
- IAF para 29 uses a 3-level risk scale (high, medium, low). Para 34 uses 5 levels (low, medium, high, very high, extremely high). Make the scale configurable.
- ALM para 58 cites the "Reserve Bank of India (Filing of Supervisory Returns) Directions, 2024". Use SR 2026 instead.
- CON Annex I is headed "Return for the Month" and para 48(4) says "10 largest exposures". SR para 21 item 12 lists the LE Framework return as quarterly, with the "20 largest exposures".
- SR para 21 table: DNBS09 shares CRILC's merged applicability cell, and FUA and FMR4/RBR share FMR's merged cell. Plain-text extraction loses this; confirmed from the PDF (pp. 8, 10–11).

# APPENDIX G — NAVIGATION, MENUS, SCREENS AND SETTINGS MAP

This Appendix consolidates the `Menu and screens` and `Settings and options` subsections of Parts 7B–7L, designs menus for the v1.4 modules that have none (M1–M23, Part 7A R1–R16), and fixes the shell, screen patterns, settings hierarchy and notifications that every phase uses. Phase 0 confirms it (item 14); Phases 1 and 3 build the shell and settings framework; later phases register their entries here. A Part governs module behaviour; this Appendix governs menu keys, paths, placement and shared patterns (canonical paths in G.3.20). The owner approves the tree and commercial defaults (Appendix B item 48); regulatory floors are not owner choices.

## G.1 Design rules

### G.1.1 Navigation registry

- Each `module.yaml` (Part 7A.0.1) declares its `ui_slots` as `nav_item` records: `menu_key` (stable, never renamed, e.g. `compliance.returns.calendar`), `parent`, `label_key`, `route`, `workspaces[]`, `permission`, `capability`, `licence_sku`, `profile_condition` (IP1.4), `regulated` (carries a CM1.4 function), `order`, `phase`, `shortcut`.
- The server builds the tree per user, workspace and legal entity (`GET /me/navigation`), cached per session and invalidated on any role, entitlement, flag, profile or module-state change. The client never filters; an omitted item is never rendered, and a deep link to it opens the permission-denied or not-entitled page with the reason code.
- One canonical route per screen; a workspace (Part 3.2) is a curated view (landing page, pinned menus, queues). Three levels at most (sidebar › section › screen); deeper structure is tabs.
- CI fails on a `nav_item` without page test, permission or SKU, on an undeclared route, or on a `regulated` item unreachable in any commercial state.

### G.1.2 Visibility rules

| Condition | Menu | API |
|---|---|---|
| No SKU | Hidden; offered in `Settings › Plan and billing › Add-ons` | 403 `not_entitled` |
| Flag off for the entity, product or branch | Hidden there; tenant admin sees "Not enabled" in `Settings › Modules` | 403 `not_enabled` |
| Required module missing | Hidden; tenant admin sees "Needs" and the module | 403 `dependency_missing` |
| `CONFIGURED` or `CERTIFIED`, not `ENABLED` | Tenant admin and certifiers only, badge "Certification" | Writes refused except certification runs |
| `READ_ONLY` (detach, downgrade, cancellation; Part 7A.0.5, CM1.4) | Grey **Read-only** badge with date, reason and export link; create, edit and bulk actions removed; registers, reports and exports stay | Writes 403 `read_only` |
| `DETACHED` | Hidden except registers and export bundle in `Data › Exports` | Export only |
| No permission | Hidden, never shown disabled | 403 `forbidden` |
| ABAC scope (entity, branch, product, assignment, amount band) | Lists, counts and search filtered | Row-level security |
| Segregation of duties | Conflicting button absent; status line explains why | 403 `sod_conflict` |
| Quota, dunning or suspension | Never hides a `regulated` item (CM1.4); banner on new non-regulated units | `limit_reached` on creation only |
| Institution profile | Members, Microfinance, ARC, IFSC and Funds menus only where IP1 binds them to the selected entity | Guard-rail codes (IP1.6) |

### G.1.3 Vocabulary, language and locale

- Labels resolve `label_key` → vocabulary pack (IP1.5: `NBFC`, `COOP`, `COOPBANK`, MFI overlay, `ARC`, `IFSC`, `FUND`) → language pack; keys, routes, API fields, statutory documents, returns and CIC files never change.
- **Co-operative fold rule:** for `COOP` entities the `customers` menu is labelled **Members** and merged into `members` (CIF tabs inside member 360); `COOPBANK` shows both **Customers** and **Members**; the MFI overlay labels `customers` **Members**. No other menu may use "Members" (G.3.20).
- **Numbers:** Indian grouping (₹12,34,56,789.50); dashboards may show "₹12.35 lakh" or "₹1,234.56 crore" with the exact amount in the tooltip and accessible name; never million or billion for INR; USD tenants (IFSC) use international grouping and the currency code; 2-decimal percentages, rate moves in bps; negatives in parentheses in financial statements.
- **Dates:** DD-MM-YYYY on screens and user exports (30-09-2026); "30 September 2026" in letters; ISO 8601 in APIs and files; "FY 2026-27"; "tax year 2026-27" under the Income-tax Act 2025.
- **Time:** 24-hour with "IST" (UTC+05:30) on every displayed timestamp; stored in UTC; cut-offs, contact windows, COB and SLA clocks run in IST on the entity's holiday calendar (M1).

### G.1.4 Refusal codes

Every refusal returns a stable code, a plain reason, the rule or REQ-ID with citation and a link to the screen that fixes it.

| Code | Raised when |
|---|---|
| `floor_violation` (403) | A setting change relaxes a regulatory floor (Part 10.2 principle 42); replaces `regulatory_floor` in RR9 and AC8 |
| `RULE_LOOSENING_BLOCKED` | A rule-pack layer L2–L4 loosens a higher layer (IP1.3) |
| `not_entitled`, `not_enabled`, `dependency_missing`, `read_only`, `limit_reached` | Entitlement and module state (7A.0.2, CM1.3) |
| `forbidden`, `sod_conflict`, `step_up_required` | Permission, segregation of duties, fresh MFA |
| `GR-7G-nn`, `GR-7H-nn` | Guard-rails (IP1.6, Part 7H) |
| `stale_version` | Record or setting changed after submission; re-base required |

## G.2 Global shell

| Element | Behaviour and rules |
|---|---|
| Workspace switcher | Assigned workspaces only; last one remembered per device; external users (B, Q, R, V, W) have one workspace |
| Entity and branch switcher | Legal entity and branch set; "All entities" only with consolidated-view permission (Part 3.1 item 2); changing entity recomputes the menu (one profile per entity); IFSC and INR entities never share a view |
| Business-date chip | Business date and COB state; amber when it differs from the calendar date, red during COB (posting screens read-only) |
| Global search | Customers, loans, applications, cases, matters, documents, returns, tasks, users, settings (G.2.1) |
| Create (`c`) | Only the create actions the user holds in this workspace and entity; opens the module wizard; drafts autosave |
| Inbox (`g i`) | My tasks, Approvals, Team, Escalations, Mentions, Submitted by me (G.2.2) |
| Notifications | Unread count, filters, snooze of non-breach items for 24 hours at most (G.8) |
| Help | Context help in one fixed place; **Regulatory references** panel (REQ-IDs, citations, sources, last-verified dates from M14); release notes; support ticket with screen and correlation ID, never record data unless attached |
| User menu | Profile, language, theme (light, dark, high contrast), density, delegation and leave substitute (M19; never beyond the delegate's own limits), notification preferences, sessions and devices, MFA, "view as" grants (RK8), **My HR** (GV6), sign out |
| Banners | SANDBOX or STAGING watermark, open break-glass session, "viewing as", maintenance, offline; not dismissible while true |

### G.2.1 Global search

- Same row-level security and ABAC as list screens; unauthorised matches are neither counted nor hinted. Minimum 3 characters; mobile matches on the last 10 digits; PAN and mobile shown masked.
- **Pattern refusals** (browser and server): a Verhoeff-valid 12-digit number (Aadhaar) or 16-digit VID is refused with "Aadhaar numbers cannot be searched; use customer ID, mobile or Aadhaar reference"; a Luhn-valid 13–19-digit number (card) is refused; a PAN (`[A-Z]{5}[0-9]{4}[A-Z]`) is matched only as a keyed hash and only for roles holding `kyc.search_by_pan`. Such queries never enter history, analytics or logs (`[REDACTED_PATTERN]`).

### G.2.2 Inbox and maker-checker queue

- One queue fed by every module's `approval_request` (module, action, record, maker, reason, diff link, risk flags, SLA, step-up flag); module queues such as `Compliance › Returns › Approvals` show the same requests.
- A maker sees own requests only under **Submitted by me** (withdrawable before decision) and can never approve them (`sod_conflict`).
- Inline decisions only for items marked `inline_ok`; sanctions, settlements, sign-offs, filings, payouts and floor-class settings open the approval screen (G.6). Bulk approval only where the module allows it (e.g. NIL returns), each item logged.
- Requests expire after 10 working days by default (maker notified); a changed base version blocks approval as `stale_version`.

### G.2.3 Command palette and shortcuts

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `Ctrl+K` or `Cmd+K` | Palette: any permitted screen, create action, workspace or entity switch, recent record |
| `/`; `g h`, `g i`, `g n`, `g s`; `c`; `?` | Search; Home, Inbox, Notifications, Settings; Create; keyboard help |
| `j`, `k`, `x`, `Enter` | Next, previous, select, open (lists and queues) |
| `a`, `r`, `e`, `n`, `Shift+S` | Approve, reject with reason, export, new, save view (only where permitted) |
| Screen keys | Declared in `nav_item.shortcut` (`g c` returns calendar, GV2 vote keys, Part 7H blotter keys) |

Single-key shortcuts never fire in text fields, can be switched off or remapped per user (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.1.4), and every action also has a button.

## G.3 Sidebar and menu tree

Sidebar order is G.3.1–G.3.18; each workspace pins its subset (G.5). Keys in brackets; labels come from vocabulary and language packs. "As" rows repeat a Part's paths; the Part holds the detail.

### G.3.1 Home (`home`)

| Path | Screens and key actions | Owner | Phase | Roles |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Home` | Landing of every workspace; renders `Dashboards › My dashboard` (G.4) with queue counts, due today, alerts | RK8, M17 | 1; tiles 14d | All internal |

Kept deliberately: `Risk › Capital › Rule packs` (filtered view of `Settings › Rule packs`); `Compliance › Returns › Approvals` (same requests as the Inbox); `Audit › External access › Provider room` and `Settings › Security and trust` (one evidence set, two audiences); `Treasury › Limits` and `Risk › Limits` (one limit engine; Board limits edited in Risk).

## G.6 Standard screen patterns and states

| Pattern | Required elements and rules |
|---|---|
| List | Typed filters and chips; saved views (personal, team, tenant default); column chooser; exact counts to 10,000 then "10,000+"; bulk actions validated and authorised per item, with a result summary and one approval request listing all items when regulated; exports (XLSX, CSV; PDF for registers) by permission, watermarked, capped and logged; PII columns need `export.pii` and are masked by default |
| Detail | Header (identity, status, key amounts, next action); tabs; timeline of events, communications and approvals; field-level audit tab (before, after, who, when, where, reason); Regulatory references panel; optimistic locking (`stale_version`) |
| Wizard | Stepper; inline validation as the user types, server-authoritative per step; explain-why with citation and fix link; pre-fill with source badges and no re-entry (SC 3.3.7); autosave every 30 seconds; resume from the Inbox; declarations and summary step; submit creates an approval request where maker-checker applies |
| Approval | Side-by-side diff with effective date; impact preview (records, customers, amounts; simulation for rule packs and settings); maker, reason, attachments, comments; SoD and DoA result; step-up for regulated items; approve, reject (reason required) or return; decisions immutable, reversed only by a new request |
| Dashboard | Value, RAG with a text label, as-of date, metric version, certification badge; tile → segment → record in three clicks; "why this colour"; watermarked export; tiles arranged by buttons or drag |
| Settings page | Per setting: description; class badge (**Regulatory floor** with citation, **Commercial**, or **Fixed** read-only); effective value and source level; allowed range with the floor edge marked; pending change with date and approver; history; a floor setting offers only the stricter direction; "simulate impact" |

| State | Content and rules |
|---|---|
| Empty, first use | What the screen does, the missing prerequisite and one action ("No centre yet: run a village survey") |
| Empty, filtered | "No results for these filters" with clear-filters; never confused with no data |
| Loading | Skeleton after 300 ms; work over 2 seconds moves to the background and reports to the Inbox |
| Validation or error | Field messages plus a linked summary that takes focus; what failed, whether anything saved, correlation ID, retry; regulated submissions never silently retried |
| Partial failure | Counts, failure file, retry of failed items only |
| Permission denied or not entitled | Permission needed and who grants it, with a request-access task; for unlicensed modules a link to Add-ons for billing roles (never for `regulated` items) |
| Read-only, stale, outage | Read-only badge with export link; "Data as of 14:05 IST; feed delayed" (stale regulatory tiles cannot be certified); provider down with the fallback and the statement that regulated clocks keep running |
| Offline (web) and maintenance | Local draft kept, no regulated submission offline; maintenance per the EO1 release calendar |

## G.7 Settings catalogue

### G.7.1 Hierarchy and resolution

Levels, widest first: **platform floor → tenant → legal entity → product → branch → role → user**.

- `setting_definition` (Phase 3) also carries `levels_allowed[]`, `strictness` (`LOWER_IS_STRICTER`, `HIGHER_IS_STRICTER`, `SUBSET_IS_STRICTER`, `TRUE_IS_STRICTER`, `NONE`), `maker_checker` (none, one or two checkers), `checker_role`, `step_up`, `effective_mode` (immediate, next business date, next open period) and `ui_group`.
- `REGULATORY_FLOOR` settings resolve to the strictest value across applicable levels, never looser than the platform floor from statute or rule pack; `COMMERCIAL` settings take the most specific value within the range set above; the user level holds only preferences and tighter personal thresholds.
- Lifecycle `DRAFT → PENDING_APPROVAL → SCHEDULED → ACTIVE → SUPERSEDED`, plus `REJECTED` and `WITHDRAWN`; effective-dated and never retroactive for a closed period or past decision (a back-dated correction yields an impact report, as IP1.3); every regulated decision stores the setting versions used.
- Platform floors change only by release (Part 8.1) and show read-only; a narrower value made looser by a wider tightening is marked `superseded_by_floor`, ignored and tasked to its owner; onboarding imports pass the same checks.

### G.7.3 Fixed rules shown read-only

Audit trail on (CA13 rule 3(1)); NPA beyond 90 DPD; capitalised penal charges; prepayment fees on barred loans; another lender's data; WhatsApp for collection, recovery or legal notices; settlement approval by a sanctioning official; recovery contact outside the window; GR-7G-01 to GR-7G-07, GR-7G-13, GR-7G-14 and GR-7H-01; the CM1.4 continuity rule; prohibited employee monitoring (GV6); AI approving, rejecting or pricing a loan (M20); Aadhaar numbers outside the vault (M3); MFA off.

- Staff messages outside the app carry category, count and deep link only, never amounts, borrower names, PAN or UPSI (RR9.2, GV7). Daily digest at 09:00 IST; staff quiet hours 21:00–08:00 IST for non-mandatory classes; mandatory classes cannot be switched off.
- Regulatory-clock ladders can only be tightened; every notification and delivery result is logged; borrower templates are M18 templates with DLT IDs.

## G.9 Accessibility, languages and devices

WCAG 2.2 AA applies to every internal, external and borrower screen.

| Criterion | Rule |
|---|---|
| 1.4.1, 1.4.3, 1.4.11 | RAG always with text; contrast 4.5:1 for text, 3:1 for chips and focus rings |
| 1.4.4, 1.4.10 | 200% zoom; reflow at 320 CSS px (grids scroll inside their region) |
| 2.1.1, 2.1.4, 2.2.1 | Keyboard-operable flows; remappable single-key shortcuts; timeout warning 2 minutes ahead with extend, draft saved first |
| 2.4.11, 2.5.7, 2.5.8 | Focus never hidden by sticky headers or toasts; button alternative to every drag; targets at least 24 × 24 CSS px |
| 3.2.6, 3.3.7, 3.3.8 | Help in a consistent place; no re-entry; paste allowed in password and OTP fields, passkeys, no puzzles |
| 4.1.3 | Status changes announced through live regions |

- Keyboard-only E2E tests for onboarding, sanction, disbursement, return sign-off, meeting votes and every approval screen; NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver and TalkBack checks on the same flows each release; charts have table alternatives; axe-core on every story and page template from Phase 1 (serious and critical issues block); manual audit before Phase P and yearly.
- **Languages:** staff UI in Indian English, Hindi optional. Borrower outputs (KFS, sanction letter, loan card, notices, SMS, statements, portal) in the borrower's preferred Eighth Schedule language as template packs are approved (M18); microfinance KFS and loan card in the State languages of operation (IP4; RBC paras 77, 79); language recorded with consent (M4); Noto fonts for Indic scripts; right-to-left for Urdu; legal review and back-translation before a translation goes live [REC].
- **Breakpoints:** 1440 px and wider, dense three-pane back office; 1024–1439 px two-pane; 768–1023 px single pane with drawers (branch and verifier tablets); 360–767 px card lists without bulk actions [REC] (mobile approvals with step-up, director and borrower portals); 320 px reflow floor.
- **Field app offline** (M22):
  - offline: visits, FI and PD forms, document capture, collection sheets and receipts from a pre-allocated series, PTP, centre attendance; never offline: sanction, disbursement, registry KYC verification, settlement offers, approvals;
  - device-keystore encryption; wipe on remote command or after 5 failed unlocks [REC]; forced sync within 72 hours, then capture locks [REC];
  - idempotent sync; the server wins for masters and balances; visit and receipt conflicts go to human resolution and receipts are never dropped; offline cash receipts show "provisional, pending sync" and post in full the same day (CF para 10(5));
  - server-corrected time and geo-tag; low-bandwidth mode; read-aloud and large type (IP4); DPS para 68 controls.

## G.11 Acceptance tests

- Without the `Investments` SKU, `GET /me/navigation` returns no `treasury` node and a deep link shows `not_entitled`.
- After detaching the Recovery Suite, `recovery` items show the Read-only badge without create buttons, the NPA register exports, and a POST returns 403 `read_only`.
- Searching a Verhoeff-valid 12-digit number is refused and the string reaches no log, analytics event or history.
- Widening the recovery contact window returns 403 `floor_violation` with the citation; narrowing it applies after checker approval on its effective date.
- A `COOP` entity shows one **Members** entry with CIF and IP2 items, and no seats screen is labelled "Members".
- A maker sees his or her request only under Submitted by me; approving a request whose base changed returns `stale_version`.
- ₹12345678.5 renders as ₹1,23,45,678.50; dates show as DD-MM-YYYY with IST times; the keyboard-only suite completes onboarding to disbursement.

## G.12 Open points for the owner (Appendix B item 48)

- Hindi staff UI at Phase P or later; field-app offline limit (72 hours [REC]); approval-expiry default (10 working days); mobile approvals for Board members; whether `Funds` stays top-level or moves under `Treasury`.
